pages.title: Editing and files
pages.description: Editing and files — local application manual
pages.html:
Documents and transactions#

The native engine owns live text. Revisions and disk baselines are checked before saving; an external change may require review or Save as. Undo/Redo belongs to editor changes. Opening help does not create an editing transaction.

Encoding and readability#

Shared editor references describe UTF-8 and newline-preserving I/O. Do not assume Reader-specific extended encodings are all IDE services.

Windows, text size and themes#

Move detachable views to another display. Application controls own text size and themes. Layout restoration and complete historical Undo remain subject to the documented limits.

pages.title: Languages and highlighting
pages.description: Languages and highlighting — local application manual
pages.html:
Highlighting#

Syntax modes come from the shared CyUI catalogue. Choose Automatic or a specific mode. Shared modes include C/C++, C#, Rust, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, HTML/CSS, HLSL, GLSL and logs; the installed catalogue is authoritative for the complete list. Extensions can register syntaxes through the documented contracts.

Language services#

CyCode connects services to configured servers, with backend-specific capabilities. Build, diagnostics, completion, debugging and highlighting are separate. Unreal analysis also depends on engine/project context and compile commands. Consult Languages, Unreal and Roadmap for precise limits.

pages.title: Scope and limits
pages.description: Scope and limits — local application manual
pages.html:
Read capability claims carefully#

Original technical guides and their dates are preserved. Compilation does not prove execution of a GUI scenario, server or platform. Known gaps and remaining checks stay in Validation and specialized references.

Languages#

User guides have English and French versions with common IDs. Original English references and API schemas are retained; the reader falls back to English where a translation is missing. The translation report exposes missing/outdated pages. Translation is not automatic.

Local reader#

CyDoc’s theme selector includes light and dark themes. Initial appearance follows reader/system preferences. Minimal media controls remain available on hover, focus and touch. Escape reduces enlarged media. Reading positions and personal data depend on file-origin/browser storage behavior; no server receives them.

Source indexing is lexical and limited to selected application-owned files. It does not replace Doxygen, a compiler or Unreal macro analysis. The native Windows help URL converter does not support extended paths.

SDK / MCP companion#

The native application owns documents and revisions. CyToolsCore owns jobs, identities, permissions and MCP. Follow this application’s MCP reference for companion requirements and access modes. Keep instance descriptors and credentials in their local storage; they are not documentation resources.

Operation reference#

The API reference is generated from the actual shipped descriptor. It exposes input/output schemas without inventing C++ methods or server capabilities. Runtime availability depends on application state, tools and permissions.

pages.title: CyCode
pages.html:
CyCode#

A native IDE for C++/Unreal projects and multilingual development services.

Start here#

  • Open your first file or project
  • Visual tour
  • Edit and save safely
  • Find and navigate
  • Syntax and language services
  • Use extensions
  • SDK / MCP reference
  • Original technical guides

Platforms and scope#

Local Windows compilation is documented. Architecture, Validation and Roadmap retain the actual feature and acceptance status. Linux/macOS code or CI configuration does not establish validation on those platforms.

Help is shipped locally and opens through file:// without a server or connection. External reference links remain optional. The CyDoc reader provides language and theme selection.

Licensing#

The application is GPL-3.0-only. CyDoc is MIT. The MIT badges in the stock reader refer to CyDoc, not to the application. Dependency notices retain their own licences.

pages.title: Plugins
pages.html:
Extensions#

Open the extension manager to review available plugins and options. Native contracts are versioned and use the documented UTF-8/JSON formats. Callbacks and libraries must remain alive during calls; STL/ImGui objects do not cross the ABI boundary.

Develop a plugin#

Start with the preserved Plugins reference and indexed PluginAPI header. Check this application’s ABI version. Shipped examples demonstrate the actual contract; a descriptor alone does not implement behavior.

pages.title: Projects and tools
pages.description: Projects and tools — local application manual
pages.html:
Projects and tools#

CyCode can open supported workspaces, .sln solutions and Unreal descriptors. CMake/MSBuild, Cargo, npm, JVM and shaders have distinct workflows and prerequisites: read the specialized guide before executing. Tool discovery does not establish acceptance of every scenario. Native owners retain targets, arguments, output and cancellation.

Unreal#

Check engine version, project, targets and analysis data. Build, Live Coding and automation have different prerequisites. Unreal, UnrealLaunch and UnrealAutomation preserve their limits and validation status.

Distributable example#

Read the actual CMake file and C++ entry point of the minimal bundled project. Building it uses your own compiler; documentation generation does not run it.

pages.title: Quick start
pages.html:
First work session#

  1. 1

    Open CyCode and choose File > Open solution for a .sln, or Open workspace for a folder.

  2. 2

    For Unreal, select the .uproject or its solution. Inspect engine and target discovery before building.

  3. 3

    Open a file from Project. Language services require their installed/configured backend; highlighting is independent.

  4. 4

    Save with Ctrl+S. Review any conflict when a file changed externally.

Close deliberately#

Review Save / Discard / Cancel prompts. Cancelling closure does not authorize an update or save. Native application owners retain settings, documents and MCP lifetime.

pages.title: Advanced DAP inspection and breakpoints
pages.html:
Advanced DAP inspection and breakpoints#

Instruction breakpoints now share the native worker and disassembly snapshot. See Instruction breakpoints for session-only full-list edits, conditions/disabled entries, actual verification and pending acceptance.

Forward stepping options, reverse execution and frame restart now share this DAP worker. The controls respect advertised capabilities and actual execution events; see Execution controls for context guards and pending acceptance.

Capability-gated data breakpoint inspection/replacement now shares this owner. Handles expire with the pause; installed targets can remain across resume. See Data breakpoints for session-only persistence, full-list edits, revision/uncertainty guards and pending acceptance.

Paused variable/expression setters and guarded memory writes also use this worker. See Value and memory editing for capabilities, explicit context guards, read-back/uncertain outcomes and pending real-adapter acceptance.

Debugger's Scopes / Registers, Memory, Disassembly and Function / Exception breakpoints tabs use the existing native DAP owner. GUI, SDK/MCP and native plugin requests call the same service. No synthetic target values, separate debugger process implementation or UI dependency enters the native core.

Inspection#

debug.memory / debug_memory uses readMemory only when supportsReadMemoryRequest is advertised. A request has an opaque memoryReference, byte offset (±1 MiB) and count (1–4096). Native validation checks canonical base64, response byte limits and unreadable counts. The returned body contains the adapter's address/data plus decoded integer bytes and unreadableBytes. The GUI shows a read-only hexadecimal/ASCII view. Evaluate a pointer expression in Watch, then use its returned memory reference when the adapter supplies one. The separate explicit write controls require both read/write support and a current readable snapshot; see Value and memory editing.

debug.disassemble / debug_disassemble uses a capable adapter's disassemble request with bounded byte/instruction offsets and 1–200 instructions. The GUI can use the selected stack frame's instruction reference and shows addresses, bytes, instructions and symbols. Supplied source locations use existing registered-source navigation; they do not grant arbitrary disk access. Source/instruction breakpoint editing and reverse debugging are separate work.

debug.variables / debug_variables accepts start, count (1–200), optional filter (named or indexed) and the live variablesReference. Child trees have page controls. Scopes / Registers can explicitly read expensive scopes, including registers when the adapter supplies such a scope. There is no invented universal register request. A full page means another page may exist; an empty next page marks the end when the adapter does not report a total.

debug.exceptionInfo / debug_exception_info retrieves actual exception details for the selected stopped thread when supportsExceptionInfoRequest is advertised. All these operations require process.execute. Their output is persistent debugger state/data, not a job artifact or a workspace source document.

Stop generations and stale references#

Read/step operations accept stopGeneration from debug.status. Omitting it pins the current generation when the request is queued. Target value/memory setters instead require explicit session/stop generations. Inspection queued for an older stop is rejected before dispatch; memory, disassembly, exception, variable, evaluate and source responses are rejected if execution resumes/stops again while waiting. Resume clears GUI caches, and scopes/watches do not publish late stopped results. Step/continue requests also reject a mismatched observed stop.

These checks cannot roll back side effects of an Evaluate command already accepted by the target. Explicit evaluation retains its existing side-effect semantics.

Persistent breakpoints#

debug.functionBreakpoints / debug_function_breakpoints replaces up to 128 named function breakpoints. Entries support enabled, condition and hitCondition, with actual function/condition/hit-count capability checks. Only enabled entries bind; the UI distinguishes adapter verification and messages. Deferred breakpoint events update verification without fabricating a source location.

debug.exceptionBreakpoints / debug_exception_breakpoints selects filter IDs from the actual adapter's exceptionBreakpointFilters. filters:null uses advertised defaults, [] disables all, and an explicit list must contain known unique IDs. Both built-in and contributed adapters receive configuration before configurationDone. No universal C++/.NET exception names are guessed.

Both setters support an expected snapshot, require process.execute and workspace.write, and persist alongside source breakpoints/profile in .cycode/launch.json. A nonblocking native lease serializes competing writers; baseline-checked atomic writes reject a file changed since this instance loaded/saved it. Unsupported stored enabled functions/exception filters fail the next launch explicitly. Confirmed breakpoint locations are session-owned and cleared when the adapter closes. The plugin host exports these same guarded operations through its versioned JSON/C ABI.

Verification and boundaries#

Windows production app/core/CLI compilation and source-only MSVC /Zs checks passed. Added regression sources cover malformed base64, unreadable ranges, request/response bounds, variables, capability checks, function conditions, exception defaults and explicit filter selection. The existing DAP integration test also specifies stale-stop rejection and conditional actual memory/disassembly queries when the installed engine advertises them.

Those native/MCP/GUI tests have not been executed during the Kaspersky interruption. No debugger, debuggee or GUI acceptance was launched for this change. Actual CodeLLDB/NetCoreDbg/contributed-adapter behavior, themes/DPI/keyboard and Linux/macOS remain unverified. A capability branch and successful compilation are not runtime acceptance. Data breakpoints and value/memory setters now have shared native implementations with acceptance still pending. Dedicated machine-register commands, remote/core dumps and full Unreal visualizers/Live Coding remain separate. Reverse execution and frame restart now have shared paths with real-adapter acceptance still pending. Targeted step-in and set-next-statement also have shared guarded native/SDK/plugin paths with pending acceptance; see Targeted step-in and Set next statement. The latter skips code instead of executing through to a source position.

Run to cursor now has a shared native/SDK/plugin path with a verified temporary source breakpoint, one Continue and guarded original-list restoration. Actual adapter/cleanup/concurrency/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Run to cursor.

Primary contract: Debug Adapter Protocol specification.

These checks cannot roll back side effects of an Evaluate command already accepted by the target. Explicit evaluation retains its existing side-effect semantics. Persistent breakpoints # debug.functionBreakpoints / debug_function_breakpoints replaces up to 128 named function breakpoints. Entries support enabled, condition and hitCondition, with actual function/condition/hit-count capability checks. Only enabled entries bind; the UI distinguishes adapter verification and messages. Deferred breakpoint events update verification without fabricating a source location. debug.exceptionBreakpoints / debug_exception_breakpoints selects filter IDs from the actual adapter's exceptionBreakpointFilters . filters:null uses advertised defaults, [] disables all, and an explicit list must contain known unique IDs. Both built-in and contributed adapters receive configuration before configurationDone . No universal C++/.NET exception names are guessed. Both setters support an expected snapshot, require process.execute and workspace.write , and persist alongside source breakpoints/profile in .cycode/launch.json . A nonblocking native lease serializes competing writers; baseline-checked atomic writes reject a file changed since this instance loaded/saved it. Unsupported stored enabled functions/exception filters fail the next launch explicitly. Confirmed breakpoint locations are session-owned and cleared when the adapter closes. The plugin host exports these same guarded operations through its versioned JSON/C ABI. Verification and boundaries # Windows production app/core/CLI compilation and source-only MSVC /Zs checks passed. Added regression sources cover malformed base64, unreadable ranges, request/response bounds, variables, capability checks, function conditions, exception defaults and explicit filter selection. The existing DAP integration test also specifies stale-stop rejection and conditional actual memory/disassembly queries when the installed engine advertises them. Those native/MCP/GUI tests have not been executed during the Kaspersky interruption. No debugger, debuggee or GUI acceptance was launched for this change. Actual CodeLLDB/NetCoreDbg/contributed-adapter behavior, themes/DPI/keyboard and Linux/macOS remain unverified. A capability branch and successful compilation are not runtime acceptance. Data breakpoints and value/memory setters now have shared native implementations with acceptance still pending. Dedicated machine-register commands, remote/core dumps and full Unreal visualizers/Live Coding remain separate. Reverse execution and frame restart now have shared paths with real-adapter acceptance still pending. Targeted step-in and set-next-statement also have shared guarded native/SDK/plugin paths with pending acceptance; see Targeted step-in and Set next statement . The latter skips code instead of executing through to a source position. Run to cursor now has a shared native/SDK/plugin path with a verified temporary source breakpoint, one Continue and guarded original-list restoration. Actual adapter/cleanup/concurrency/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Run to cursor . Primary contract: Debug Adapter Protocol specification .

pages.title: Architecture
pages.html:
Architecture#

UpdateHistory adds explicit bounded metadata-only installation/recovery history within cycode_updates. Shared staging/outcome parsers, work/pending/receipt identity agreement and numeric guards produce advisory rows without payload hashes or filesystem mutation. UpdateHistoryUI owns one cancellable/joined future, cached CyUI filtering, twelve-row pages and snapshot selection. The native report excludes raw metadata/errors. No SDK/ABI, target, module or dependency is added. See Update history.

RecoveryProgress publishes single-attempt atomic phase/count/write observations bound to the native review's plan/transaction. UpdateRecovery retains validation, leases, copying, commit and postflight; internal typed cancellation preserves its ordinary exception contract. UpdaterRecoveryUI starts and joins that service worker from a thin system TaskDialog, keeps close requests cooperative and separates final results from optional technical errors. Native receipts and explicitly copied reports reuse the recovery owner and never authorize file changes. Only the Windows helper adds Comctl32/Common-Controls v6; core dependencies, SDK 227 / ABI2 and CyUI modules stay unchanged. See Recovery controls.

UpdateRecovery now owns bounded prepared-copy reuse through immutable work identity and source maps, with the existing mutable status as a discovery hint only. Native review revalidates source ownership/type/size/hash; execution recomputes reuse headroom under its lease, stages missing originals, rechecks all selected sources and commits from their verified paths. Mixed-directory maps survive further retries without a second history owner. Original backups remain required; SDK/ABI, modules and the core dependency boundary remain unchanged. See Recovery resumption.

UpdateRecovery now derives allocation-aware copy/retention headroom from its own verified scan. Preview space fields are observations; execution rechecks under exclusive ownership, stages all bounded copies, repeats the complete baseline and checks commit headroom before moving targets. Plan-bound space receipts and honest preparation/commit phases remain with the same recovery owner. EN/FR native helper feedback adds required/available capacity without SDL/ImGui/SDK dependencies. See Recovery preparation.

UpdatePackage now uses allocation-aware UpdateBudget installation estimates before extraction and before replacement. UpdateInstall supplies stable failure categories shared by helper/history; UpdateFiles removes pending markers through the verified Windows file handle. Ordinary-failure rollback verifies the full original baseline. These remain inside existing native/cache/recovery owners, with no SDK/ABI/module change. See Installation checks.

UpdateBudget supplies bounded download/staging headroom arithmetic, with native caller-available space probes in the existing worker. UpdateProgress defines release-bound atomic observations and a main-thread-only sampled rate/ETA meter. UpdateTransfer publishes preparation/receiving/hash/staging/readiness/failure phases; UpdatesUI reads counters without per-frame disk/network probes. Installation still requires full native verification. SDK/ABI/module/target ownership is unchanged. See Download observations.

Update retry now passes an explicit native resume/fresh mode. UpdateDownload owns bounded deterministic checkpoint selection; fresh mode bypasses inspection and uses a new owned directory. DownloadError carries fixed failure categories and UpdateFeedback supplies EN/FR display keys, independently of technical messages. UpdatesUI schedules one quiet local inspection after interruption/failure, retaining diagnostics and discarding replaced-release digests without network retry, restored consent or modal reopening. The existing owners/dependencies/SDK remain unchanged. See Download retry.

UpdateDownload owns exact asset/checkpoint binding and bounded partial discovery; UpdateRange supplies the actual constexpr HTTP response policy. UpdateTransfer uses native non-truncating file handles, per-copy download exclusion, validated ranges and one fresh-folder fallback while retaining interrupted data. UpdateCache exposes observed partial summaries separately from verified Prepared candidates; UpdatesUI keeps explicit network/install consent. No SDK/dependency/module owner is added. See Download resumption.

UpdateStorage adds explicit bounded cache inspection and receipt-backed reversible payload moves to the existing installation owner. UpdateStorageUI owns guarded asynchronous selection/acknowledgement and cancelled/partial results; no startup maintenance runs. Shared cache leases exclude download/helper/recovery races, while the existing file utility owns non-overwriting moves for recovery and storage. Metadata/history and installation backups remain with their existing owners. See Update storage.

Application updates have an installation-scoped owner outside the workspace Engine and MCP. UpdateRelease owns typed stable-version/asset/path policy; UpdateTransfer owns bounded WinHTTP/SHA-256 staging; UpdateCache owns bounded read-only staging discovery, shared candidate verification and helper outcome persistence through the existing atomic text writer. UpdatePackage owns manifest-checked replacement and retained transaction backup. UpdateManifest shares strict before/after file-set validation with UpdateRecovery. Immutable format-2 pending plans bind reviewed preimages; recovery owns an exclusive lease, exact review guards, non-overwriting copy/retain operations and final baseline postflight. The existing helper adds standalone EN/FR OS recovery dialogs, preserving its minimal dependency boundary. UpdatesUI owns asynchronous futures, atomic progress/cancellation, startup proposals and explicit post-close handoff. The native lease implementation is factored into one cycode_native_lease target shared with the core. cycode_updates and the production CyCodeUpdater avoid IDE/SDL/ImGui/SDK links. GUI/native-service leases exclude replacement until shutdown; the helper waits without killing processes. Existing save/session/Undo owners remain. The SDK stays at 227 operations. See Application updates.

OccurrenceCatalogue validates/deduplicates document highlights in cycode_core, using the existing source identity/revision/backend guards and SymbolTextBounds. OccurrencesUI owns one context-bound future, debounced ready-server queries and a cached dockable inspector. EditorOccurrences owns independent geometry and draws unfilled outlines through existing CodeEditor coordinates; it never overwrites native glyph annotations. EditorTextMap shares UTF-16/glyph conversion with DiagnosticAnnotations. Explicit multi-selection preflights all ranges before one SetSelections, preserving source/Undo ownership. GUI/SDK/ABI2 share the native read (227 SDK operations); no module/dependency/C ABI/target is added. See Document occurrences.

NavigationLocations now normalizes bounded source Location/LocationLink responses in the native core, with identity/revision/backend guards and live-source UTF-16 validation. It serves five navigation methods through GUI/SDK/ABI2 (226 SDK operations). NavigationUI owns ticketed result presentation and cached LocationModel filter/selection labels, reusing the existing document/history owner and References dock. No dependency, CyUI module, C ABI, process or Undo owner is added. See Source navigation.

SymbolCatalogue normalizes hierarchical/flat server results, snapshot-local node relationships, extents and deprecation in the native core. SymbolTextBounds indexes the validated buffer once for UTF-16 range checks. Engine symbol queries guard identity/revision and backend configuration epochs without invalidating document structure for unrelated edits. OutlineModel caches source/alphabetic order and CyUI-filter ancestor visibility. StructureUI and the existing palette share those native results, guarded document/history navigation and ticketed async replies. SymbolSession now retains bounded opaque workspace-symbol data for on-demand location resolution, with expiry/eviction, reply cache and pre/post workspace/ lifecycle/monitor/backend guards. The palette separates query and selection tickets, adds same-query refresh tickets and reuses the existing guarded source opener. SDK language_symbol_resolve and ABI2 language.symbolResolve share that owner. Existing Core/CodeEditor modules and ABI2 JSON services remain; no dependency, process owner, C ABI or executable target is added. See Symbol navigation.

LanguageService now pairs native document identity/revision with connection-wide monotonic LSP versions, including replacement lifetimes and reload. Editor annotations and ProblemModel navigation require current ownership; Problems shares severity/text selection and CyUI's diagnostic list/detail card. The CompilerLocation core parses bounded caller-supplied lines, resolving existing workspace files through Engine's guard. GUI log activation, SDK build_location and ABI2 share that service. No additional process/model owner, UI module, dependency, C ABI or executable target. See Diagnostics and Compiler locations.

Three related milestones share existing ownership. TaskOutput extracts the bounded journal in BuildOutput for both BuildOperations and ProjectTasks, retaining separate reservations/tokens. TaskOutputText frames Cargo display records while preserving the final parser. Project status/output bypass execution locks and reuse SDK/ABI2. BuildUI switches sources and protects captured cancellation; workspace switching observes remote task ownership. ProblemModel owns filtered/cyclic location selection, and ModuleUI/commands reuse guarded document opening and CyUI Diagnostics. No new dependency, process owner, CyUI module, C ABI or executable target is added. See Project output and Diagnostics.

BuildOperations owns a bounded, revisioned live output tail on its existing reservation. Internal ProcessOutputScope binds observation to a synchronous thread/token; adapters opt in only for user-facing main execution. BuildOutput repairs display text and rejects stale callbacks without affecting raw process results or cancellation. BuildUI polls the same lock-independent Engine service as SDK/ABI2 and uses CyUI Diagnostics. No new owner, module, dependency or C ABI; see Live build output.

UnrealArtifacts adds a bounded, read-only assessment of project Editor receipts, module BuildIds and recorded binary presence. It reuses native Unreal discovery and remains UI-free. Build results retain actual process data plus artifacts or postflight uncertainty. The existing debugger's ProfileCheck distinguishes profile configuration from actual process launch; only run/launch require fresh scoped artifact readiness. Desktop continuation also requires matching ready outputs. UnrealArtifactsUI reuses Core controls and virtualized file rows, and SDK/ABI2/ provider 1.5.0 use the same service. No new dependency, module or process owner; see Unreal outputs for excluded dependency/ABI coverage.

Unreal launch settings now persist an optional profile/request binding in the common debug profile. Debugger's internal ProfileCheck callback delegates bound configure/run/launch validation to UnrealProject; the core has no UI dependency. UnrealLaunchUI compiles the bound build context and captures a one-shot desktop continuation with immutable parameters, draft/saved-profile/build-ID guards and open document identities/revisions. Pure continuation/document helpers reject stale or uncertain results before using existing terminal/DAP owners. Saved edits during a build are covered; unrelated clean document opens remain allowed. Legacy/null profiles and explicit detachment preserve manual editing. SDK/ABI2 use the same profile model and validator; no new API operation, module, dependency, process owner or ABI. See Unreal launch.

UnrealLaunch prepares typed UE4/UE5 editor/game/uncooked-server profiles through the existing Unreal inspector. Map validation is shared with automation. Engine adds the observed debug profile for compare-and-swap; Debugger validates that snapshot on its existing job owner and retains atomic disk-baseline saving. UnrealLaunchUI guards its draft, uses CyUI Core and saves through debug.configure; actual Run/Debug retain the existing terminal/DAP owners. No extra process owner, profile store, module, dependency or ABI. SDK/ABI2 and provider 1.5.0 use the same implementation. See Unreal launch profiles.

UnrealAutomationModel validates typed cook/package/map/container controls and fixed argv. UnrealProject owns bounded issued previews, descriptor/rule/map/tool guards, exclusive output intent, actual process/archive inspection and persistent logs/results. Managed .NET tool discovery is shared with UBT. BuildOperations owns cancellation/status/events until work stops; Engine guards live documents. UnrealAutomationUI discards stale previews and reuses the build owner, CodeEditor logs and CyUI Core controls. SDK/ABI2 and bundled Unreal provider 1.5.0 use that same owner. No new dependency, target, CyUI module or ABI; acceptance remains pending. See Unreal automation.

GitReplayModel normalizes single-commit actions and derives start/continue/quit blockers from the common GitMerge inspector. GitReplay reuses its complete bounded index/metadata/document observations, verifies actual source objects, guards workspace metadata, persists exclusive intents and checks actual process/raw parent/tree/index outcomes. GitReplayUI binds history choices and stale-context guards to the same SDK/ABI2 service. No new dependency, target, CyUI module or ABI; acceptance remains pending. See Git replay.

GitMergeModel parses bounded parent/path/tree records and normalizes commit/quit requests. GitMerge owns operation metadata, full index/flag/intent state, document guards, reviewed effects, intent receipts and actual process/postflight outcomes through the VCS mutex. GitMergeUI preserves drafts, discards stale previews and shares Diff/conflict navigation with the same SDK/ABI2 service. Commit verifies actual parents/tree/index; quit retains working/index state and is separate from abort/reset. No dependency, executable target, CyUI module or ABI change. Runtime acceptance remains pending; see Merge workflow.

GitCheckout adds stage-zero/absent-index working-file plans and receipts to the native VCS owner. Resources owns bounded private binary payloads, file/permission guards, persistent trash/install journals and restoration, reusing exclusive moves and new exclusive binary creation. Engine document locking protects commit and closed source/trash roots. Generic resource calls cannot consume private Git plans; SDK/UI/ABI2 share native preview/index guards. Common events refresh image views. No dependency, executable target, CyUI module or ABI change; runtime/POSIX acceptance remains pending. See Git working files.

GitConflictModel parses bounded complete NUL index records and validates explicit portable path choices into fixed Git argv. GitConflicts owns selected-repository, HEAD/branch/index guards, blob inspection, deterministic previews and actual postflight through the existing VCS mutex. GitConflictsUI uses the same service as the typed SDK and four ABI2 exports, rejects stale async contexts, and preserves the existing three-way text editor. Resolution changes the index only; working files and document ownership/Undo remain untouched. No new target, dependency, CyUI module or ABI change is introduced. Native runtime acceptance is pending; see Git conflicts.

Three Git milestones extend existing ownership. Optional versioned Git selection metadata joins the existing per-instance WorkspaceSession and validates repository identity before restoration. GitWorktreeMaintenance shares Git selection/catalogues and the VCS mutex, but owns portable requests, local previews, pointer/index/HEAD/ directory guards and one move/repair process. Repair audits the complete linked set and common metadata; postflight preserves actual/uncertain outcomes for both target and reviewed siblings. GUI/SDK/ABI2 use the same service with stale-preview discard and explicit read/mutation permissions. No executable target, third-party dependency, CyUI module or C ABI change is introduced. See Git worktrees and Workspace sessions.

Submodule settings reuse the common address validator and add fixed URL/branch/ remote-default argv planning. The Engine binds both working and indexed metadata, parent branch context and relevant directories/pointers to a separate preview. An ordered config remainder verifies unrelated records independently of the one target key; the index and checkout are preserved. Unsafe old values are redacted, effective branch overrides are reported and already-configured branches are not dispatched. UI/SDK/ABI2 retain one owner and real/uncertain postflight outcomes. No dependency, executable target or CyUI module is added. See Git submodules.

Submodule deinitialization extends the same UI-free model and Engine owner with complete bounded index/flag validation, an explicit preview revision and one offline/no-force Git action. Parent-owned absorbed metadata, native documents, normal .gitmodules and complete cleanliness including ignored files are checked again before dispatch. Actual retained metadata and unregistration/removal are verified after Git, preserving uncertainty even on exit zero. UI cancellation and stale async results cannot apply a preview. ABI2 and SDK share the same service; no dependency, executable, CyUI module or source Undo transaction is added. See Git submodules.

Submodule addition extends the existing model/Engine with normalized fixed argv, local preview and a distinct clone/stage operation. Catalogue, parent HEAD/reference, destination/metadata directories and normal indexed .gitmodules bytes bind the preview revision; inputs/context are checked again before dispatch. UI discards cancelled/stale asynchronous previews. SDK and ABI2 share permission and process ownership, with no new dependency/executable/CyUI module. See Git submodules.

GitSubmoduleModel parses NUL-delimited path/index records and builds fixed argv. Engine owns catalogue fingerprints, filesystem/document guards and actual Git processes under its existing VCS mutex. GUI, real SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugins share one selected-repository service; raw URL/config values stay private. Update uses the recorded gitlink commit and preserves explicit uncertainty/refresh results. No dependency, executable target or CyUI module is added. See Git submodules.

RunToCursor owns one revisioned temporary source-breakpoint lease, independent of persisted project breakpoints. Engine supplies native document/disk guards; the existing DAP worker arms/verifies the complete replacement, resumes once and restores the original list on an actual stop. Tracked pending replies, actual stop confirmation and explicit guarded repair prevent blind continuation or restoration after uncertain outcomes. GUI, SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugins share this owner; no executable, dependency or CyUI module is added. See Run to cursor.

DebugTargets now owns both issued target families through one implementation. Goto queries use the actual selected frame source, privately preserve/compare bounded adapterData and expose only filtered metadata. Separate catalogues and markers expire through the existing DAP worker. Targeted goto reuses execution acknowledgements/epochs but awaits an actual stopped event with pendingStop, invalid inspection and a bounded unconfirmed deadline, without inventing resume or automatic retry. StepInTargets is a compatibility alias; both views share one stable target table. See Set next statement.

StepInTargets owns one bounded, pause/frame-bound catalogue with private signed adapter IDs and monotonic public handles. Debugger serializes queries and targeted stepIn on its existing DAP worker, rechecks response context, publishes the current catalogue ID and expires choices on context changes or execution submission. Targeted actions reuse DebugExecution acknowledgement/event ordering with public handle-only metadata. GUI, SDK and ABI2 requests share that owner; no dependency, executable or CyUI module is added. See Targeted step-in.

InstructionBreakpoints owns a bounded session-only replacement list, revisions, enabled-to-wire mapping, actual verification and deferred breakpoint events. Debugger retains DAP/session/execution ownership and explicit context guards. DebugInspection provides common verification parsing reused by data breakpoints; their existing bounds remain compatible. Disassembly views capture their pause, and instruction drafts retain stable UI row IDs. GUI, SDK and ABI2 host exports share this owner, with no persisted process addresses, dependency or new CyUI module. See Instruction breakpoints.

DebugExecution validates bounded forward/reverse/frame-restart plans, observed contexts and actual acknowledgement metadata without a UI dependency. Debugger serializes them on its existing DAP owner and records applying/accepted/unconfirmed outcomes. Queued legacy context is pinned; new operations require explicit guards. An execution epoch protects rapid new stopped events from a late acknowledgement without confusing ordinary cache invalidation with program execution. GUI controls, menus/keymaps, SDK and ABI2 host requests share this service, with no dependency or CyUI module added. See Execution controls.

DebugMutations validates bounded value/expression/byte operations and adapter results without UI dependencies. Debugger keeps those operations on its existing worker with explicit session/stop/frame guards, a separate execution epoch, expected-memory preflight/read-back and reference invalidation after attempts. DebugMutationsUI is only a captured-context form and byte preview. SDK/MCP and ABI2 host exports share the same process.execute service and retain its result after submission. No dependency or CyUI module is added. See Value and memory editing.

DataBreakpoints owns bounded pause-bound inspection handles, private DAP identities and reported watchpoint configuration without UI dependencies. Debugger retains transport/session ownership, revision-guards full-list replacement, marks uncertain mutations and adapts actual verification/invalidation events. UI, SDK and ABI2 host requests share that owner; data targets are session-only and the SDK mutation is noncancellable after submission. See Data breakpoints.

Java Hot Code Replace uses the existing Java language-service owner for a fixed incremental JDT build request and the same DAP connection for redefineClasses. Debugger owns per-call cancellation flags/IDs, bounded reply/custom-event parsing, session/backend checks and inspection invalidation; Engine supplies saved workspace document identity/revision snapshots. UI, SDK and ABI2 host exports share those services. The SDK retains its reservation until the native result after matched cancellation; imports, autobuild and VM restart remain explicit user choices. Runtime acceptance remains pending. See Java debugging.

JavaDebug validates typed Java launch options and converts literal argv to the Java DAP wire format. It also validates persistent JDWP endpoints and builds attach requests containing only endpoint/source context. ProjectTasks prepares actual main/runtime-classpath profiles; LanguageService issues the fixed JDT LS session command. Debugger retains DAP, breakpoint/inspection/terminal ownership through LanguageClient's framed transport and a bounded LoopbackStream connection. Java backend epochs invalidate sessions; native/plugin stdio owners remain unchanged. See Java debugging.

The reserved javaAttach profile field retains host/port/timeout separately from launch options. The existing Debugger performs launch or attach through the local JDT LS adapter, records requested attach targets, refuses target-terminal reverse requests for attached Java sessions and disconnects without terminating existing JVMs. Legacy profiles retain local defaults; SDK schemas preserve the native PID route and optional legacy outputs. Registration/configuration do not resolve DNS or connect to the endpoint. Runtime/network acceptance remains pending.

RustToolchain validates symbolic installed-toolchain names and supplies literal Rustup argv/environment plans. Cargo tasks and the existing language server owner consume the same helpers, without a discovery subprocess, installer, shell or second process owner. RustAnalysis retains unresolved names in local preferences and derives compatible sysroot/env settings. See Rust toolchains.

RustAnalysis supplies bounded typed Cargo-to-analysis profiles and derives both initialization and configuration settings without changing the user's base launch. ProjectTasks inspection exposes the data-only projection; LanguagePreferencesEngine validates enabled paths/settings before saves, and LanguageService retains server process/epoch ownership. Desktop, SDK and ABI2 plugins share the existing configure operation and preference locks. See Rust analysis.

CargoBuild validates typed Cargo options and adapts actual format-version 1 workspace metadata and compiler-reported executable identities. ProjectTasks retains process/cancellation/cache ownership; ProjectTasksUI adapts the shared model with CyUI Core. SDK and ABI2 plugin services forward to the same native adapter without a TOML parser, second process owner or new ABI. See Cargo workspaces.

ChangeAnnotations validates passive LSP annotation data, normalizes server IDs and retains only effective text-edit groups. The existing change store binds IDs to issued plans and checks required acknowledgements before mutation. SemanticUI adapts the same plan metadata with CyUI Core; SDK/native-plugin requests share the Engine guards and Undo without another parser or ABI. See annotated changes.

SessionViewsUI captures and restores the shared editor's wrap, public folded-line state and document scroll anchors without another folding engine. WorkspaceSession validates optional versioned editor/image metadata; ImageView adapts the existing CyUI canvas after asynchronous decode/viewport availability. Source fingerprints, capture budgets and input precedence guard replay. No source, Undo or process state is serialized. See workspace sessions.

SemanticTokens validates and reconstructs LSP full/delta integer arrays and owns bounded immutable LRU bases. LanguageService keeps that cache on the existing server worker; LanguageClient negotiates support and tracks server refreshes separately from document invalidation. Highlighting retains Unicode/range guards and the existing desktop/SDK/plugin output. See semantic updates.

CMakePresetActions extends the existing native reader with test/package and ordered workflow metadata. BuildSystem supplies reviewed plans and CTest/CPack/CMake argv execution under BuildOperations; CMakePresetsUI adapts the same services using CyUI Core. The real SDK and native plugin host share them without a Python parser, another process owner or C ABI layout change. See Preset actions.

Hierarchy validates the LSP call/type hierarchy data contract without a transport or UI dependency. HierarchyEngine owns bounded issued sessions, opaque server items and document/notification/backend guards; LanguageService retains the server processes and request queue. HierarchyUI adapts these read-only services with CyUI Core, and the real SDK/native plugin host expose the same operations. See Hierarchies.

GitRepositories supplies bounded filesystem discovery and explicit repository selection without another Engine/document model. GitWorktrees owns Git's NUL-delimited catalogue, identity/revision guards and bounded native mutations; GitWorktreesUI adapts those same services through CyUI Core. Documents and SDK file paths stay workspace-relative, while Git receives repository-relative literal pathspecs. No Python Git backend or new native-plugin ABI is introduced. See Git repositories and worktrees.

DocumentReference distinguishes issued untitled references from filesystem paths. DocumentDrafts keeps draft text/revisions in the existing Engine document model and commits Save as through the shared text writer. DocumentDraftsUI adapts the existing CodeEditor without replacing its Undo/window identity. Recovery and session metadata retain their current owners; the real SDK and ABI2 host route to the same native mutations. See Untitled documents.

PluginPackages owns signed local extension installation, publisher trust, immutable versions and guarded selection/rollback/cleanup outside workspaces. PluginPackageData provides bounded metadata/path/streaming-integrity operations with pinned Monocypher Ed25519/SHA-512. PluginPackagesUI uses common Core widgets; the SDK forwards to the same native service. Shared/exclusive NativeFileLease ownership prevents cleanup while a host retains a version. The loader and manager reuse PluginManifest validation; no UI, scheduler or plugin ABI is duplicated. See Plugin packages.

DebugInspection validates capability-gated DAP memory/disassembly, paged variables and function/exception breakpoint contracts. The existing Debugger owns transport, stop generations, saved profiles and process lifecycle; the desktop, MCP and plugin host share those services. See Advanced debugging.

JvmBuild supplies UI-free Java argv launchers and bounded real Maven/Gradle model readers to ProjectTasks. Build/test/run retain the common cancellation/deadline, workspace guards and terminal owner. See JVM builds. ShaderBuild supplies typed DXC/glslang argv, bounded artifact checks and workspace-mapped diagnostics to that same ProjectTasks process owner. Its desktop panel also works as an explicit secondary task view for C++/Unreal projects; see Shader compilation.

WorkspaceSession stores bounded per-instance tab/panel/layout metadata outside project sources; SessionUI adapts the common editor and ImGui models. NativeFileLease prevents concurrent session ownership and debug-profile writes. Text recovery and Undo retain their existing owners. See Workspace sessions.

cycode_process shares argv execution, bounded child ownership and installed-tool discovery between the native core and bundled SVN/Perforce/Mercurial providers. SVN uses the same XML library, provider descriptors/root mapping, live/disk guards and shared Diff/read-only Review views without linking IDE/UI services into its DLL. See Subversion. Perforce uses tagged JSON and the same project provider routes, with checked client mappings and file-scoped submit/revert. Typed SDK Git handlers explicitly select the built-in Git provider and an explicit workspace repository; generic plugin requests retain their own permissions/schema and longer transport wait. See Perforce. Mercurial reuses those provider routes and process utilities with structured JSON, exact file selectors, local repository identity and clean-update checks. Its DLL also remains independent of IDE/UI services; see Mercurial. Diversion also reuses those routes/process services, with documented CLI text, local/cloud sync metadata and guarded actions rather than Git staging/push/pull. See Diversion and the custom-provider contract.

DebugAdapters validates declarative ABI2 stdio-DAP definitions and request options. Engine publishes one active-plugin service snapshot to the existing LSP/DAP owners. The Debugger retains native transport/process ownership, explicit provider IDs, queued-launch epochs and revocation across disable/change/shutdown. GUI/MCP/plugin requests share this worker; no plugin callback owns a debugger process. See Plugin debuggers.

The native language owner maps versioned diagnostic publications back to live document revisions. DiagnosticsUI checks those revisions and uses the common CodeEditor squiggle/tooltip hook through DiagnosticAnnotations; the core keeps its UI-free boundary. See Editor diagnostics.

Events owns a bounded metadata journal with epoch/cursor paging. Engine emits committed changes; ABI2 subscribers run on a serial native worker outside document locks, with manifest permissions, read-only snapshot handshakes and error suspension. Shutdown joins event delivery before releasing plugins/services. See Workspace events for ordering, retention and native-code limits.

XmlSolution maps .slnx folders/projects/configuration rules into the shared solution/MSBuild model through a pinned UI-free XML reader. CMakePresets resolves bounded metadata, include/inheritance graphs and workspace binary paths; actual preset execution remains in CMake. GUI, MCP and plugins use those native services. See Project formats.

Application-owned LanguagePreferences stores unresolved per-workspace LSP launch and activation choices outside project configuration. OS locks, checked revisions and the shared atomic text writer guard multi-instance edits. Engine routes GUI, MCP and plugin controls to that same store and existing server owners; inspection does not activate saved servers. See Language preferences.

BuildOperations coordinates CMake, MSBuild and explicitly dispatched Unreal work with one native reservation and a matching cancellation ID. BuildEngine routes shared GUI/MCP/plugin requests. Status/cancel bypass execution locks; process ownership remains held through termination. GUI background Unreal analysis retains its independent token. See Build cancellation.

Installed plugin manifests are checked against the native host version and process platform before library loading. ABI2 retains its original host prefix, adds optional feature bits and serial activation notifications with no host requests. Guarded project activation commits precede notification; enabled dormant dependents initialize after their dependencies become active. Libraries stay pinned until reverse-order shutdown. See Plugins for the ABI and the distinction from native-code isolation.

Configured CTest discovery/execution, issued Git hunks, regex searches of unsaved buffers and plugin-owned LSP definitions share the UI-free native Engine. The language registry is workspace-local, with host-owned server workers and routing epochs; it does not modify the common syntax catalogue. See Development workflows for process ownership, cancellation, limits, GUI/MCP/ABI2 contracts and remaining scope.

The desktop selects Core, Code/CodeEditor, Diff, Commands, Diagnostics, DocumentViews, Inspector, Assets and Images/Canvas from modular CyUI. The Engine/core/CLI have no UI dependency. See CyUI migration for exact pins, view ownership, source adapters and limits.

Project creation uses the UI-free ProjectTemplates service. The desktop wizard renders native plans through CyUI Core/Code; MCP and native plugins call the same Engine routes within their workspace boundary. The desktop explicitly selects its parent directory without changing those permissions. The shared FileTransactions primitive provides exclusive renames for resources and project publication. See Project templates. ABI2 template contributions contain data only. TemplateDefinitions checks and expands bounded UTF-8 files/options; Plugins supplies an atomic active-registry snapshot and holds its activation lock through creation. Snapshot reads happen before the plan mutex; commit always locks the plugin host before the plan store, including requests from a plugin's callback. No plugin callback executes during template expansion or file publication.

Image tabs use the app-owned ImageLoader worker, bounded native decoders and deferred OpenGL textures, rendered by CyUI::Images. They are separate from Engine text documents and retain the shared tab/docking lifecycle. See Images.

CyCodeReader lives in its own repository. Its editor/ source module provides the same cycode_editor and cycode_fileicons targets to the IDE, at the revision in app/editor-source.lock.json or an explicit CYCODE_EDITOR_ROOT development checkout. CyCode does not build the Reader app. The Reader hosts dockable file editors without an Engine, language server, build adapter or Core companion. cycode_files owns UTF-8 validation, newline encoding, bounded reads, path conversion and guarded atomic saves used by both applications. The IDE retains workspace/revision permissions; Reader uses files selected directly by its user and keeps per-document disk baselines across directories. Its application-specific extensions are documented in the Reader repository.

Interactive execution uses the shared native Terminals and Debugger services. Terminals owns bounded libvterm screens/history and real ConPTY/POSIX PTY process trees, with separate read/write/supervisor threads. Only visible grid rows are copied for rendering. Debugger has one owner thread for DAP and a bounded command queue; the framed JSON transport is shared with LanguageClient without LSP initialization. Adapter reverse terminal requests create native terminals with explicit argv/env. DebugRuntime detects native/managed outputs and selects a compatible .NET host. CodeLLDB and NetCoreDbg share this DAP owner, inspection state and persistent profile; NetCoreDbg output uses the debug console, while interactive managed Run uses a PTY. Existing attached processes detach on stop; launched processes terminate. Persistent profiles/breakpoints use atomically replaced workspace metadata. See Execution.

CyCode starts with C/C++ and keeps language support, project/build adapters, editor views and revision-control providers as separate extension points. A workspace can eventually contain several project types. CMake, MSBuild and UnrealBuildTool are executable adapters; solution inspection does not evaluate MSBuild. Explicit MSBuild evaluation reads real target properties/items, produces managed clangd metadata and tracks local solution/project/import inputs. Builds share the same native adapter with MCP; source diagnostics feed the Problems panel.

ProjectTasks supplies Cargo metadata/compiler JSON, npm scripts and standalone javac compilation to both GUI and MCP. It owns one cancellable native task with bounded output/deadline and uses Terminals for persistent Run. The private IPC bridge accepts a bounded set of concurrent connections so cancellation remains receivable while a compiler is running. CyToolsCore continues to own scheduling, permissions and identities; matching native operation ids only correlate process cancellation. See Project tasks.

text
CyUI / SDL3 desktop                 External MCP clients        |                                  |        |                           official MCP SDK (stdio)        |                                  |        |                        CyToolsCore authenticated HTTP        |                        runtime, jobs, sessions, permissions        |                                  |        +-------- native Engine <--- private loopback command bridge                     |             documents / search / Git / CMake / Unreal / trusted plugins                     |             LanguageService router                +-- C++ owner thread <---- LSP transport ----> clangd                +-- C# owner thread  <---- LSP transport ----> csharp-ls/Roslyn

The native Engine has no UI dependency. Documents carry monotonically increasing revisions, UTF-8 content, original BOM/newline convention and disk baseline. Saves reject stale revisions and external modifications before atomic replacement. Workspace paths are canonicalized and checked by path components, including symlink resolution. New files use exclusive creation. A task cleanup never removes source files.

Resources owns bounded filesystem snapshots and issued plans, exclusive moves, guarded inverse actions and persistent project trash. Engine retains the live document model and gives text documents stable identities across path changes. Filesystem mutations emit bounded cursor events; the GUI rebases tabs/navigation without replacing editor Undo or native window identity. Deleted open buffers remain available with a missing marker. CyUI::Assets supplies the physical browser and its action requests. These operations are distinct from semantic symbol/file rename; see Resources for the SDK, limits and remaining integration gaps.

Documentation and signature requests use those same live document/revision guards. LanguageInfo normalizes display-only sections and UTF-16 signature parameter offsets into bounded UTF-8 labels. The GUI keeps one information request in flight and discards responses for obsolete cursors; it follows the visible panel with a small debounce. It never executes backend Markdown, HTML or documentation links.

The desktop polls document metadata, copies text on changes, indexes project paths off the UI thread and delegates content search to ripgrep. WorkspaceMonitor owns recursive Windows directory notifications with bounded buffers and overflow reconciliation; other systems currently use a bounded directory polling fallback. It publishes counters, never callbacks into UI or document services. Background workspace.poll reloads clean buffers and preserves dirty, missing or invalid files with a disk-conflict marker. A two-second reconciliation also covers open files in excluded directories. Replacing a search cancels its native process, and generation IDs suppress obsolete results. Dirty buffers supersede disk text in literal and regex searches; regex uses bounded private snapshots and native ripgrep cancellation. The path index is cached in memory, invalidated by structural/ignore-file events, and paged for clients (up to 200,000 indexed paths). Persistent path/symbol indexes, incremental symbol queries and large-file editing remain future work. See Workspace monitoring.

The extension host supports ABI1 and the instance-based C ABI2. It resolves manifest dependencies before loading, preserves libraries until callbacks have stopped, and exposes JSON descriptors for commands, menus, panels, syntax, language servers, project templates and VCS/project providers. Application owns the UI and CyUI syntax-registration lifetimes. Project activation and VCS root mappings have revision/disk guards and independent workspace metadata. Git remains built in; selecting another provider changes the available actions and does not silently fall back to Git if that provider disappears. The bundled Unreal extension uses existing native services rather than another project parser/build engine. The original Unreal project panel and backend remain in the application. See Plugin SDK for contracts and remaining extension boundaries.

Every native text editor is owned by CyUI::CodeEditor behind native document services. The GUI build prepares a patched copy in its build directory using prepare_texteditor.py; the checksum-pinned downloaded source is unchanged. The small adapter adds function, macro and reflection-attribute roles, a context tokenizer and a read-only token query for tests. EditorLanguage supplies bounded lexical C/C++/Unreal and C# rules; the widget retains incremental multi-line comment/string state. Preprocessor directives and their strings/comments are tokenized separately. Built-in keywords use one blue role; Unreal naming conventions supply types and reflection macros/metadata have dedicated roles. Function calls/declarations are recognized lexically. These fast rules remain available while project analysis loads or a backend is unavailable. EditorTheme owns the shared palette for editors, change previews and VCS views, with contrast checked against both editor grounds.

Highlighting.cpp requests full LSP semantic tokens through the existing C++/C# owner threads. It decodes each server's negotiated legend and relative UTF-16 positions, validates single-line/non-overlapping ranges and surrogate boundaries, and returns UTF-16 positions plus separate Unicode glyph indexes. The same revision-checked language.highlight operation serves GUI and MCP. Results are capped at 50,000 spans or a 4 MiB token payload, with explicit truncation. Edits to any live document, server restart and semantic refresh requests invalidate the backend generation. The GUI debounces requests by 300 ms and runs at most two color queries concurrently, prioritizing the active and visible detached editors. Closed-tab queries retire asynchronously rather than blocking tab closure.

The widget stores semantic display colors independently from lexical glyph roles. Its transaction version disables obsolete spans immediately, including after undo; normal keyword/string/comment state, identifiers and completion stay intact. Colors map actual aliases/classes, functions/methods, variables/parameters/fields, macros and enum members; clangd's inactive-code comment spans use a readable muted role. Unknown/dependent classifications retain lexical colors. C# uses the same adapter with Roslyn's legend. Delta/range streaming, advanced modifier styling and broader raw-string/preprocessor fallback coverage remain pending.

External buffer replacements are applied as editor transactions to retain undo. The LSP transport queues writes and delivers replies on a dedicated LanguageService owner thread. One clangd process serves both UI completion/navigation and MCP queries; Engine document opens, changes and closes synchronize its unsaved overlays. Requests never wait on the UI thread. A maximum of 32 outstanding requests and a 15-second deadline bound the queue, including initialization; expired requests send LSP $/cancelRequest. Restart/shutdown fails in-flight requests and joins the child. The transport bounds queued writes by count and bytes; document synchronization retries under backpressure and completes before semantic queries are sent. Engine checks the source revision and live-document generation before accepting semantic replies; UI completion also checks its generation and cursor. The editor uses 32-bit Unicode codepoints; LSP uses zero-based UTF-16 positions, and ripgrep columns are byte offsets. Navigation converts those coordinates explicitly and decodes percent-escaped file URIs. Results outside the canonical workspace are counted but omitted by default. With includeExternal, registered engine/compiler SDK roots issue opaque read-only source references; they do not extend workspace write permissions. This initial adapter launches clangd; other servers need their own launch settings, project configuration and integration validation.

Semantic.cpp normalizes workspace/document symbols and maintains bounded rename and formatting plans. TextEdits validates UTF-16 ranges, surrogate boundaries and non-overlapping replacements. Plans snapshot live revisions and text; apply/undo validate every affected buffer and its current disk baseline before changing any buffer. Saves remain explicit. The desktop and MCP use these same operations. SDK documents live in a separate registry, can be read only through issued handles, and cannot be passed to document write/refactor operations. See Semantic editing.

Commands are registered once for menus, the keyboard settings and action palette. The toolkit-independent Keymap resolves profile bindings, contexts, custom overrides and multi-stroke chords. The UI consumes matched keys before the editor widget's fixed shortcuts, preserving ordinary typing/caret handling. This prevents Rider's Ctrl+Y/Ctrl+B from invoking the widget's redo or the former build shortcut. Initial completion waits for the document's first diagnostics publication: clangd's initialized status alone can still produce unrelated index-only completions while its first preamble is being built.

BuildSystem owns tool discovery, CMake execution, cache compatibility checks, profile persistence and File API inspection. UI and MCP use the same native operations. Configure requests codemodel/toolchain replies and selects the native compilation database or derives one from File API metadata for Visual Studio. The active database directory initializes the shared clangd; successful reconfigure reloads it while retaining live overlays. Local profile state is .cycode/build.json; generated analysis databases stay in the build tree. See Build services.

Solution inspection accepts directories, .sln and .uproject entries and keeps the canonical document root at the project directory. Missing/external references remain metadata rather than new document permissions. UnrealProject discovers the associated engine and invokes UBT using argv. Database generation reloads the same LanguageService used by the GUI/MCP. See Unreal integration for tested scope.

SDL3 and the ImGui OpenGL3 renderer provide native platform viewports. Each document is a dockable window; detached editors and panels own distinct SDL/OS windows and GL contexts. Rendering restores the main context afterwards. Closing a panel hides it; View/sidebar actions restore it. Editor closes retain unsaved-document checks. Independent processes own their engines, buffers, descriptors and jobs. Layout filenames are keyed by canonical project entry; global preferences use unique temporary files and atomic replacement. File icons use original vector drawings, semantic palette colours and DPI-aware geometry without OS symbol-font assets.

CyToolsCore is installed as a real wheel into runtime/python. One companion per GUI instance shares the Core scheduler across MCP connections. Each instance has unique private native/Core descriptors. The native token protects local IPC; Core owns assistant authentication and operation permissions. The bridge is application IPC, not another MCP parser, scheduler or job registry. The service exits when its native descriptor is removed. Jobs and artifacts use the SDK lifecycle.

Source document paths are workspace references, not file-import fields: importing a copy would disconnect edits from the open editor. Temporary generated reports belong in JobContext.path; explicit source saves remain persistent operations.

Git mutations are serialized by the native Engine. Vcs.cpp provides structured repository metadata and guarded working-tree changes. Changed clean documents reload through the same revision/LSP service; dirty buffers survive concurrent operations. VcsUI consumes structured responses asynchronously and keeps conflict editing in normal document tabs. Providers continue to use the existing C ABI.

CyUI is an external configurable checkout, not a vendored fork. Platform-specific code includes process/IPC, Windows engine registration and the Unicode entry point; SDL3 supplies window/input/render integration. Portability of source is not a claim that Linux/macOS builds have run.

The shared editor library owns per-document incremental Tree-sitter parsers for Rust/Java/JS/TS/TSX/HTML/CSS, with display spans separate from lexical and semantic overlays. Both applications and refactor/conflict previews use this same layer. The SDL-free core routes language requests to independent server owners for C++, C#, Rust, Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Initialization options and workspace configuration are separate; the service respects advertised methods and maps LSP workspace-edit versions to native document revisions. See language support for runtime prerequisites and deliberate limits.

CompletionEngine.cpp holds bounded issued-item sessions tied to document revision, workspace generation and backend epoch. Resolve receives only cached server items; prepare turns the primary edit and additional imports into the existing ChangePlan transaction after checking UTF-16 ranges, overlaps and disk baselines. The MCP surface is read-only until changes_apply. The build-local editor patch intercepts acceptance without inserting a partial symbol. The GUI prepares asynchronously, checks cursor/revision/generation again, applies the native plan and mirrors it as one tab-preserving undo transaction. A headless actual widget test verifies the acceptance hook; complete desktop acceptance remains separate.

Snippet.cpp is an SDL-free bounded parser/expander linked by the core and editor. Completion preserves field byte offsets through indentation and additional imports. EditorSnippet converts them once to glyph coordinates and uses the widget's detailed transaction callback to track linked fields without rescanning document text for every keystroke. The build-local adapter adds validated multi-selections and a pre-key handler; ordinary multicursor edits supply atomic mirror typing. Finishing a session collapses only its recorded cursor history so undo/redo cannot revive temporary linked cursors. The widget's text extraction also preserves exact final newlines rather than implicitly appending one to nonempty files.

CodeActions.cpp owns separate bounded issued-action sessions and lazy resolution. LanguageService adds overlapping published diagnostics to code-action context, matches decoded file URI identities and maps versioned edits to native revisions. LanguageClient invalidates diagnostic eligibility for actions on edits while retaining the last displayed diagnostics and fast completion; versionless publications remain advisory. New target overlays must be synchronized before a fresh query, preventing an edit from adopting an unrelated disk baseline. Shared workspace-edit parsing and ChangePlan validation serve rename and context actions. GUI and MCP use those same plans; no code-action command is executed. Only the pinned TypeScript server's verified empty acknowledgement is ignored. Resource operations and annotated/snippet action edits remain explicitly unavailable.

RecoveryStore is UI-free and keeps per-instance, OS-locked UTF-8 checkpoints under .cycode/recovery. Engine owns a joined background worker that snapshots dirty document revisions and writes immutable payloads before an atomic index. Restore validates checkpoint/target/disk guards, installs a live buffer and transfers its backup before retiring the source. The GUI uses CyUI Code for bounded previews and the existing editor replacement transaction for Undo. Native documents remain the only mutable model shared with MCP; checkpoints never save project files. See Recovery for quotas, failure handling and explicit limitations.
pages.text: Architecture # UpdateHistory adds explicit bounded metadata-only installation/recovery history within cycode_updates. Shared staging/outcome parsers, work/pending/receipt identity agreement and numeric guards produce advisory rows without payload hashes or filesystem mutation. UpdateHistoryUI owns one cancellable/joined future, cached CyUI filtering, twelve-row pages and snapshot selection. The native report excludes raw metadata/errors. No SDK/ABI, target, module or dependency is added. See Update history . RecoveryProgress publishes single-attempt atomic phase/count/write observations bound to the native review's plan/transaction. UpdateRecovery retains validation, leases, copying, commit and postflight; internal typed cancellation preserves its ordinary exception contract. UpdaterRecoveryUI starts and joins that service worker from a thin system TaskDialog, keeps close requests cooperative and separates final results from optional technical errors. Native receipts and explicitly copied reports reuse the recovery owner and never authorize file changes. Only the Windows helper adds Comctl32/Common-Controls v6; core dependencies, SDK 227 / ABI2 and CyUI modules stay unchanged. See Recovery controls . UpdateRecovery now owns bounded prepared-copy reuse through immutable work identity and source maps, with the existing mutable status as a discovery hint only. Native review revalidates source ownership/type/size/hash; execution recomputes reuse headroom under its lease, stages missing originals, rechecks all selected sources and commits from their verified paths. Mixed-directory maps survive further retries without a second history owner. Original backups remain required; SDK/ABI, modules and the core dependency boundary remain unchanged. See Recovery resumption . UpdateRecovery now derives allocation-aware copy/retention headroom from its own verified scan. Preview space fields are observations; execution rechecks under exclusive ownership, stages all bounded copies, repeats the complete baseline and checks commit headroom before moving targets. Plan-bound space receipts and honest preparation/commit phases remain with the same recovery owner. EN/FR native helper feedback adds required/available capacity without SDL/ImGui/SDK dependencies. See Recovery preparation . UpdatePackage now uses allocation-aware UpdateBudget installation estimates before extraction and before replacement. UpdateInstall supplies stable failure categories shared by helper/history; UpdateFiles removes pending markers through the verified Windows file handle. Ordinary-failure rollback verifies the full original baseline. These remain inside existing native/cache/recovery owners, with no SDK/ABI/module change. See Installation checks . UpdateBudget supplies bounded download/staging headroom arithmetic, with native caller-available space probes in the existing worker. UpdateProgress defines release-bound atomic observations and a main-thread-only sampled rate/ETA meter. UpdateTransfer publishes preparation/receiving/hash/staging/readiness/failure phases; UpdatesUI reads counters without per-frame disk/network probes. Installation still requires full native verification. SDK/ABI/module/target ownership is unchanged. See Download observations . Update retry now passes an explicit native resume/fresh mode. UpdateDownload owns bounded deterministic checkpoint selection; fresh mode bypasses inspection and uses a new owned directory. DownloadError carries fixed failure categories and UpdateFeedback supplies EN/FR display keys, independently of technical messages. UpdatesUI schedules one quiet local inspection after interruption/failure, retaining diagnostics and discarding replaced-release digests without network retry, restored consent or modal reopening. The existing owners/dependencies/SDK remain unchanged. See Download retry . UpdateDownload owns exact asset/checkpoint binding and bounded partial discovery; UpdateRange supplies the actual constexpr HTTP response policy. UpdateTransfer uses native non-truncating file handles, per-copy download exclusion, validated ranges and one fresh-folder fallback while retaining interrupted data. UpdateCache exposes observed partial summaries separately from verified Prepared candidates; UpdatesUI keeps explicit network/install consent. No SDK/dependency/module owner is added. See Download resumption . UpdateStorage adds explicit bounded cache inspection and receipt-backed reversible payload moves to the existing installation owner. UpdateStorageUI owns guarded asynchronous selection/acknowledgement and cancelled/partial results; no startup maintenance runs. Shared cache leases exclude download/helper/recovery races, while the existing file utility owns non-overwriting moves for recovery and storage. Metadata/history and installation backups remain with their existing owners. See Update storage . Application updates have an installation-scoped owner outside the workspace Engine and MCP. UpdateRelease owns typed stable-version/asset/path policy; UpdateTransfer owns bounded WinHTTP/SHA-256 staging; UpdateCache owns bounded read-only staging discovery, shared candidate verification and helper outcome persistence through the existing atomic text writer. UpdatePackage owns manifest-checked replacement and retained transaction backup. UpdateManifest shares strict before/after file-set validation with UpdateRecovery. Immutable format-2 pending plans bind reviewed preimages; recovery owns an exclusive lease, exact review guards, non-overwriting copy/retain operations and final baseline postflight. The existing helper adds standalone EN/FR OS recovery dialogs, preserving its minimal dependency boundary. UpdatesUI owns asynchronous futures, atomic progress/cancellation, startup proposals and explicit post-close handoff. The native lease implementation is factored into one cycode_native_lease target shared with the core. cycode_updates and the production CyCodeUpdater avoid IDE/SDL/ImGui/SDK links. GUI/native-service leases exclude replacement until shutdown; the helper waits without killing processes. Existing save/session/Undo owners remain. The SDK stays at 227 operations. See Application updates . OccurrenceCatalogue validates/deduplicates document highlights in cycode_core, using the existing source identity/revision/backend guards and SymbolTextBounds. OccurrencesUI owns one context-bound future, debounced ready-server queries and a cached dockable inspector. EditorOccurrences owns independent geometry and draws unfilled outlines through existing CodeEditor coordinates; it never overwrites native glyph annotations. EditorTextMap shares UTF-16/glyph conversion with DiagnosticAnnotations. Explicit multi-selection preflights all ranges before one SetSelections, preserving source/Undo ownership. GUI/SDK/ABI2 share the native read (227 SDK operations); no module/dependency/C ABI/target is added. See Document occurrences . NavigationLocations now normalizes bounded source Location/LocationLink responses in the native core, with identity/revision/backend guards and live-source UTF-16 validation. It serves five navigation methods through GUI/SDK/ABI2 (226 SDK operations). NavigationUI owns ticketed result presentation and cached LocationModel filter/selection labels, reusing the existing document/history owner and References dock. No dependency, CyUI module, C ABI, process or Undo owner is added. See Source navigation . SymbolCatalogue normalizes hierarchical/flat server results, snapshot-local node relationships, extents and deprecation in the native core. SymbolTextBounds indexes the validated buffer once for UTF-16 range checks. Engine symbol queries guard identity/revision and backend configuration epochs without invalidating document structure for unrelated edits. OutlineModel caches source/alphabetic order and CyUI-filter ancestor visibility. StructureUI and the existing palette share those native results, guarded document/history navigation and ticketed async replies. SymbolSession now retains bounded opaque workspace-symbol data for on-demand location resolution, with expiry/eviction, reply cache and pre/post workspace/ lifecycle/monitor/backend guards. The palette separates query and selection tickets, adds same-query refresh tickets and reuses the existing guarded source opener. SDK language_symbol_resolve and ABI2 language.symbolResolve share that owner. Existing Core/CodeEditor modules and ABI2 JSON services remain; no dependency, process owner, C ABI or executable target is added. See Symbol navigation . LanguageService now pairs native document identity/revision with connection-wide monotonic LSP versions, including replacement lifetimes and reload. Editor annotations and ProblemModel navigation require current ownership; Problems shares severity/text selection and CyUI's diagnostic list/detail card. The CompilerLocation core parses bounded caller-supplied lines, resolving existing workspace files through Engine's guard. GUI log activation, SDK build_location and ABI2 share that service.
