No additional process/model owner, UI module, dependency, C ABI or executable target. See Diagnostics and Compiler locations . Three related milestones share existing ownership. TaskOutput extracts the bounded journal in BuildOutput for both BuildOperations and ProjectTasks, retaining separate reservations/tokens. TaskOutputText frames Cargo display records while preserving the final parser. Project status/output bypass execution locks and reuse SDK/ABI2. BuildUI switches sources and protects captured cancellation; workspace switching observes remote task ownership. ProblemModel owns filtered/cyclic location selection, and ModuleUI/commands reuse guarded document opening and CyUI Diagnostics. No new dependency, process owner, CyUI module, C ABI or executable target is added. See Project output and Diagnostics . BuildOperations owns a bounded, revisioned live output tail on its existing reservation. Internal ProcessOutputScope binds observation to a synchronous thread/token; adapters opt in only for user-facing main execution. BuildOutput repairs display text and rejects stale callbacks without affecting raw process results or cancellation. BuildUI polls the same lock-independent Engine service as SDK/ABI2 and uses CyUI Diagnostics. No new owner, module, dependency or C ABI; see Live build output . UnrealArtifacts adds a bounded, read-only assessment of project Editor receipts, module BuildIds and recorded binary presence. It reuses native Unreal discovery and remains UI-free. Build results retain actual process data plus artifacts or postflight uncertainty. The existing debugger's ProfileCheck distinguishes profile configuration from actual process launch; only run/launch require fresh scoped artifact readiness. Desktop continuation also requires matching ready outputs. UnrealArtifactsUI reuses Core controls and virtualized file rows, and SDK/ABI2/ provider 1.5.0 use the same service. No new dependency, module or process owner; see Unreal outputs for excluded dependency/ABI coverage. Unreal launch settings now persist an optional profile/request binding in the common debug profile. Debugger's internal ProfileCheck callback delegates bound configure/run/launch validation to UnrealProject; the core has no UI dependency. UnrealLaunchUI compiles the bound build context and captures a one-shot desktop continuation with immutable parameters, draft/saved-profile/build-ID guards and open document identities/revisions. Pure continuation/document helpers reject stale or uncertain results before using existing terminal/DAP owners. Saved edits during a build are covered; unrelated clean document opens remain allowed. Legacy/null profiles and explicit detachment preserve manual editing. SDK/ABI2 use the same profile model and validator; no new API operation, module, dependency, process owner or ABI. See Unreal launch . UnrealLaunch prepares typed UE4/UE5 editor/game/uncooked-server profiles through the existing Unreal inspector. Map validation is shared with automation. Engine adds the observed debug profile for compare-and-swap; Debugger validates that snapshot on its existing job owner and retains atomic disk-baseline saving. UnrealLaunchUI guards its draft, uses CyUI Core and saves through debug.configure; actual Run/Debug retain the existing terminal/DAP owners. No extra process owner, profile store, module, dependency or ABI. SDK/ABI2 and provider 1.5.0 use the same implementation. See Unreal launch profiles . UnrealAutomationModel validates typed cook/package/map/container controls and fixed argv. UnrealProject owns bounded issued previews, descriptor/rule/map/tool guards, exclusive output intent, actual process/archive inspection and persistent logs/results. Managed .NET tool discovery is shared with UBT. BuildOperations owns cancellation/status/events until work stops; Engine guards live documents. UnrealAutomationUI discards stale previews and reuses the build owner, CodeEditor logs and CyUI Core controls. SDK/ABI2 and bundled Unreal provider 1.5.0 use that same owner. No new dependency, target, CyUI module or ABI; acceptance remains pending. See Unreal automation . GitReplayModel normalizes single-commit actions and derives start/continue/quit blockers from the common GitMerge inspector. GitReplay reuses its complete bounded index/metadata/document observations, verifies actual source objects, guards workspace metadata, persists exclusive intents and checks actual process/raw parent/tree/index outcomes. GitReplayUI binds history choices and stale-context guards to the same SDK/ABI2 service. No new dependency, target, CyUI module or ABI; acceptance remains pending. See Git replay . GitMergeModel parses bounded parent/path/tree records and normalizes commit/quit requests. GitMerge owns operation metadata, full index/flag/intent state, document guards, reviewed effects, intent receipts and actual process/postflight outcomes through the VCS mutex. GitMergeUI preserves drafts, discards stale previews and shares Diff/conflict navigation with the same SDK/ABI2 service. Commit verifies actual parents/tree/index; quit retains working/index state and is separate from abort/reset. No dependency, executable target, CyUI module or ABI change. Runtime acceptance remains pending; see Merge workflow . GitCheckout adds stage-zero/absent-index working-file plans and receipts to the native VCS owner. Resources owns bounded private binary payloads, file/permission guards, persistent trash/install journals and restoration, reusing exclusive moves and new exclusive binary creation. Engine document locking protects commit and closed source/trash roots. Generic resource calls cannot consume private Git plans; SDK/UI/ABI2 share native preview/index guards. Common events refresh image views. No dependency, executable target, CyUI module or ABI change; runtime/POSIX acceptance remains pending. See Git working files . GitConflictModel parses bounded complete NUL index records and validates explicit portable path choices into fixed Git argv. GitConflicts owns selected-repository, HEAD/branch/index guards, blob inspection, deterministic previews and actual postflight through the existing VCS mutex. GitConflictsUI uses the same service as the typed SDK and four ABI2 exports, rejects stale async contexts, and preserves the existing three-way text editor. Resolution changes the index only; working files and document ownership/Undo remain untouched. No new target, dependency, CyUI module or ABI change is introduced. Native runtime acceptance is pending; see Git conflicts . Three Git milestones extend existing ownership. Optional versioned Git selection metadata joins the existing per-instance WorkspaceSession and validates repository identity before restoration. GitWorktreeMaintenance shares Git selection/catalogues and the VCS mutex, but owns portable requests, local previews, pointer/index/HEAD/ directory guards and one move/repair process. Repair audits the complete linked set and common metadata; postflight preserves actual/uncertain outcomes for both target and reviewed siblings. GUI/SDK/ABI2 use the same service with stale-preview discard and explicit read/mutation permissions. No executable target, third-party dependency, CyUI module or C ABI change is introduced. See Git worktrees and Workspace sessions . Submodule settings reuse the common address validator and add fixed URL/branch/ remote-default argv planning. The Engine binds both working and indexed metadata, parent branch context and relevant directories/pointers to a separate preview. An ordered config remainder verifies unrelated records independently of the one target key; the index and checkout are preserved. Unsafe old values are redacted, effective branch overrides are reported and already-configured branches are not dispatched. UI/SDK/ABI2 retain one owner and real/uncertain postflight outcomes. No dependency, executable target or CyUI module is added. See Git submodules . Submodule deinitialization extends the same UI-free model and Engine owner with complete bounded index/flag validation, an explicit preview revision and one offline/no-force Git action. Parent-owned absorbed metadata, native documents, normal .gitmodules and complete cleanliness including ignored files are checked again before dispatch. Actual retained metadata and unregistration/removal are verified after Git, preserving uncertainty even on exit zero. UI cancellation and stale async results cannot apply a preview. ABI2 and SDK share the same service; no dependency, executable, CyUI module or source Undo transaction is added. See Git submodules . Submodule addition extends the existing model/Engine with normalized fixed argv, local preview and a distinct clone/stage operation. Catalogue, parent HEAD/reference, destination/metadata directories and normal indexed .gitmodules bytes bind the preview revision; inputs/context are checked again before dispatch. UI discards cancelled/stale asynchronous previews. SDK and ABI2 share permission and process ownership, with no new dependency/executable/CyUI module. See Git submodules . GitSubmoduleModel parses NUL-delimited path/index records and builds fixed argv. Engine owns catalogue fingerprints, filesystem/document guards and actual Git processes under its existing VCS mutex. GUI, real SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugins share one selected-repository service; raw URL/config values stay private. Update uses the recorded gitlink commit and preserves explicit uncertainty/refresh results. No dependency, executable target or CyUI module is added. See Git submodules . RunToCursor owns one revisioned temporary source-breakpoint lease, independent of persisted project breakpoints. Engine supplies native document/disk guards; the existing DAP worker arms/verifies the complete replacement, resumes once and restores the original list on an actual stop. Tracked pending replies, actual stop confirmation and explicit guarded repair prevent blind continuation or restoration after uncertain outcomes. GUI, SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugins share this owner; no executable, dependency or CyUI module is added. See Run to cursor . DebugTargets now owns both issued target families through one implementation. Goto queries use the actual selected frame source, privately preserve/compare bounded adapterData and expose only filtered metadata. Separate catalogues and markers expire through the existing DAP worker. Targeted goto reuses execution acknowledgements/epochs but awaits an actual stopped event with pendingStop, invalid inspection and a bounded unconfirmed deadline, without inventing resume or automatic retry. StepInTargets is a compatibility alias; both views share one stable target table. See Set next statement . StepInTargets owns one bounded, pause/frame-bound catalogue with private signed adapter IDs and monotonic public handles. Debugger serializes queries and targeted stepIn on its existing DAP worker, rechecks response context, publishes the current catalogue ID and expires choices on context changes or execution submission. Targeted actions reuse DebugExecution acknowledgement/event ordering with public handle-only metadata. GUI, SDK and ABI2 requests share that owner; no dependency, executable or CyUI module is added. See Targeted step-in . InstructionBreakpoints owns a bounded session-only replacement list, revisions, enabled-to-wire mapping, actual verification and deferred breakpoint events. Debugger retains DAP/session/execution ownership and explicit context guards. DebugInspection provides common verification parsing reused by data breakpoints; their existing bounds remain compatible. Disassembly views capture their pause, and instruction drafts retain stable UI row IDs. GUI, SDK and ABI2 host exports share this owner, with no persisted process addresses, dependency or new CyUI module. See Instruction breakpoints . DebugExecution validates bounded forward/reverse/frame-restart plans, observed contexts and actual acknowledgement metadata without a UI dependency. Debugger serializes them on its existing DAP owner and records applying/accepted/unconfirmed outcomes. Queued legacy context is pinned; new operations require explicit guards. An execution epoch protects rapid new stopped events from a late acknowledgement without confusing ordinary cache invalidation with program execution. GUI controls, menus/keymaps, SDK and ABI2 host requests share this service, with no dependency or CyUI module added. See Execution controls . DebugMutations validates bounded value/expression/byte operations and adapter results without UI dependencies. Debugger keeps those operations on its existing worker with explicit session/stop/frame guards, a separate execution epoch, expected-memory preflight/read-back and reference invalidation after attempts. DebugMutationsUI is only a captured-context form and byte preview. SDK/MCP and ABI2 host exports share the same process.execute service and retain its result after submission. No dependency or CyUI module is added. See Value and memory editing . DataBreakpoints owns bounded pause-bound inspection handles, private DAP identities and reported watchpoint configuration without UI dependencies. Debugger retains transport/session ownership, revision-guards full-list replacement, marks uncertain mutations and adapts actual verification/invalidation events. UI, SDK and ABI2 host requests share that owner; data targets are session-only and the SDK mutation is noncancellable after submission. See Data breakpoints . Java Hot Code Replace uses the existing Java language-service owner for a fixed incremental JDT build request and the same DAP connection for redefineClasses. Debugger owns per-call cancellation flags/IDs, bounded reply/custom-event parsing, session/backend checks and inspection invalidation; Engine supplies saved workspace document identity/revision snapshots. UI, SDK and ABI2 host exports share those services. The SDK retains its reservation until the native result after matched cancellation; imports, autobuild and VM restart remain explicit user choices. Runtime acceptance remains pending. See Java debugging . JavaDebug validates typed Java launch options and converts literal argv to the Java DAP wire format. It also validates persistent JDWP endpoints and builds attach requests containing only endpoint/source context. ProjectTasks prepares actual main/runtime-classpath profiles; LanguageService issues the fixed JDT LS session command. Debugger retains DAP, breakpoint/inspection/terminal ownership through LanguageClient's framed transport and a bounded LoopbackStream connection. Java backend epochs invalidate sessions; native/plugin stdio owners remain unchanged. See Java debugging . The reserved javaAttach profile field retains host/port/timeout separately from launch options. The existing Debugger performs launch or attach through the local JDT LS adapter, records requested attach targets, refuses target-terminal reverse requests for attached Java sessions and disconnects without terminating existing JVMs. Legacy profiles retain local defaults; SDK schemas preserve the native PID route and optional legacy outputs. Registration/configuration do not resolve DNS or connect to the endpoint. Runtime/network acceptance remains pending. RustToolchain validates symbolic installed-toolchain names and supplies literal Rustup argv/environment plans. Cargo tasks and the existing language server owner consume the same helpers, without a discovery subprocess, installer, shell or second process owner. RustAnalysis retains unresolved names in local preferences and derives compatible sysroot/env settings. See Rust toolchains . RustAnalysis supplies bounded typed Cargo-to-analysis profiles and derives both initialization and configuration settings without changing the user's base launch. ProjectTasks inspection exposes the data-only projection; LanguagePreferencesEngine validates enabled paths/settings before saves, and LanguageService retains server process/epoch ownership. Desktop, SDK and ABI2 plugins share the existing configure operation and preference locks. See Rust analysis . CargoBuild validates typed Cargo options and adapts actual format-version 1 workspace metadata and compiler-reported executable identities. ProjectTasks retains process/cancellation/cache ownership; ProjectTasksUI adapts the shared model with CyUI Core. SDK and ABI2 plugin services forward to the same native adapter without a TOML parser, second process owner or new ABI. See Cargo workspaces . ChangeAnnotations validates passive LSP annotation data, normalizes server IDs and retains only effective text-edit groups. The existing change store binds IDs to issued plans and checks required acknowledgements before mutation. SemanticUI adapts the same plan metadata with CyUI Core; SDK/native-plugin requests share the Engine guards and Undo without another parser or ABI. See annotated changes . SessionViewsUI captures and restores the shared editor's wrap, public folded-line state and document scroll anchors without another folding engine. WorkspaceSession validates optional versioned editor/image metadata; ImageView adapts the existing CyUI canvas after asynchronous decode/viewport availability. Source fingerprints, capture budgets and input precedence guard replay. No source, Undo or process state is serialized. See workspace sessions . SemanticTokens validates and reconstructs LSP full/delta integer arrays and owns bounded immutable LRU bases. LanguageService keeps that cache on the existing server worker; LanguageClient negotiates support and tracks server refreshes separately from document invalidation. Highlighting retains Unicode/range guards and the existing desktop/SDK/plugin output. See semantic updates . CMakePresetActions extends the existing native reader with test/package and ordered workflow metadata. BuildSystem supplies reviewed plans and CTest/CPack/CMake argv execution under BuildOperations; CMakePresetsUI adapts the same services using CyUI Core. The real SDK and native plugin host share them without a Python parser, another process owner or C ABI layout change. See Preset actions . Hierarchy validates the LSP call/type hierarchy data contract without a transport or UI dependency. HierarchyEngine owns bounded issued sessions, opaque server items and document/notification/backend guards; LanguageService retains the server processes and request queue. HierarchyUI adapts these read-only services with CyUI Core, and the real SDK/native plugin host expose the same operations. See Hierarchies . GitRepositories supplies bounded filesystem discovery and explicit repository selection without another Engine/document model. GitWorktrees owns Git's NUL-delimited catalogue, identity/revision guards and bounded native mutations; GitWorktreesUI adapts those same services through CyUI Core. Documents and SDK file paths stay workspace-relative, while Git receives repository-relative literal pathspecs. No Python Git backend or new native-plugin ABI is introduced. See Git repositories and worktrees . DocumentReference distinguishes issued untitled references from filesystem paths. DocumentDrafts keeps draft text/revisions in the existing Engine document model and commits Save as through the shared text writer. DocumentDraftsUI adapts the existing CodeEditor without replacing its Undo/window identity. Recovery and session metadata retain their current owners; the real SDK and ABI2 host route to the same native mutations. See Untitled documents . PluginPackages owns signed local extension installation, publisher trust, immutable versions and guarded selection/rollback/cleanup outside workspaces. PluginPackageData provides bounded metadata/path/streaming-integrity operations with pinned Monocypher Ed25519/SHA-512. PluginPackagesUI uses common Core widgets; the SDK forwards to the same native service. Shared/exclusive NativeFileLease ownership prevents cleanup while a host retains a version. The loader and manager reuse PluginManifest validation; no UI, scheduler or plugin ABI is duplicated. See Plugin packages . DebugInspection validates capability-gated DAP memory/disassembly, paged variables and function/exception breakpoint contracts. The existing Debugger owns transport, stop generations, saved profiles and process lifecycle; the desktop, MCP and plugin host share those services. See Advanced debugging . JvmBuild supplies UI-free Java argv launchers and bounded real Maven/Gradle model readers to ProjectTasks . Build/test/run retain the common cancellation/deadline, workspace guards and terminal owner. See JVM builds . ShaderBuild supplies typed DXC/glslang argv, bounded artifact checks and workspace-mapped diagnostics to that same ProjectTasks process owner. Its desktop panel also works as an explicit secondary task view for C++/Unreal projects; see Shader compilation . WorkspaceSession stores bounded per-instance tab/panel/layout metadata outside project sources; SessionUI adapts the common editor and ImGui models. NativeFileLease prevents concurrent session ownership and debug-profile writes. Text recovery and Undo retain their existing owners. See Workspace sessions . cycode_process shares argv execution, bounded child ownership and installed-tool discovery between the native core and bundled SVN/Perforce/Mercurial providers. SVN uses the same XML library, provider descriptors/root mapping, live/disk guards and shared Diff/read-only Review views without linking IDE/UI services into its DLL. See Subversion . Perforce uses tagged JSON and the same project provider routes, with checked client mappings and file-scoped submit/revert. Typed SDK Git handlers explicitly select the built-in Git provider and an explicit workspace repository; generic plugin requests retain their own permissions/schema and longer transport wait. See Perforce . Mercurial reuses those provider routes and process utilities with structured JSON, exact file selectors, local repository identity and clean-update checks. Its DLL also remains independent of IDE/UI services; see Mercurial . Diversion also reuses those routes/process services, with documented CLI text, local/cloud sync metadata and guarded actions rather than Git staging/push/pull. See Diversion and the custom-provider contract . DebugAdapters validates declarative ABI2 stdio-DAP definitions and request options. Engine publishes one active-plugin service snapshot to the existing LSP/DAP owners. The Debugger retains native transport/process ownership, explicit provider IDs, queued-launch epochs and revocation across disable/change/shutdown. GUI/MCP/plugin requests share this worker; no plugin callback owns a debugger process. See Plugin debuggers . The native language owner maps versioned diagnostic publications back to live document revisions. DiagnosticsUI checks those revisions and uses the common CodeEditor squiggle/tooltip hook through DiagnosticAnnotations ; the core keeps its UI-free boundary. See Editor diagnostics . Events owns a bounded metadata journal with epoch/cursor paging. Engine emits committed changes; ABI2 subscribers run on a serial native worker outside document locks, with manifest permissions, read-only snapshot handshakes and error suspension. Shutdown joins event delivery before releasing plugins/services. See Workspace events for ordering, retention and native-code limits. XmlSolution maps .slnx folders/projects/configuration rules into the shared solution/MSBuild model through a pinned UI-free XML reader. CMakePresets resolves bounded metadata, include/inheritance graphs and workspace binary paths; actual preset execution remains in CMake. GUI, MCP and plugins use those native services. See Project formats . Application-owned LanguagePreferences stores unresolved per-workspace LSP launch and activation choices outside project configuration. OS locks, checked revisions and the shared atomic text writer guard multi-instance edits. Engine routes GUI, MCP and plugin controls to that same store and existing server owners; inspection does not activate saved servers. See Language preferences . BuildOperations coordinates CMake, MSBuild and explicitly dispatched Unreal work with one native reservation and a matching cancellation ID. BuildEngine routes shared GUI/MCP/plugin requests. Status/cancel bypass execution locks; process ownership remains held through termination. GUI background Unreal analysis retains its independent token. See Build cancellation . Installed plugin manifests are checked against the native host version and process platform before library loading. ABI2 retains its original host prefix, adds optional feature bits and serial activation notifications with no host requests. Guarded project activation commits precede notification; enabled dormant dependents initialize after their dependencies become active. Libraries stay pinned until reverse-order shutdown. See Plugins for the ABI and the distinction from native-code isolation. Configured CTest discovery/execution, issued Git hunks, regex searches of unsaved buffers and plugin-owned LSP definitions share the UI-free native Engine. The language registry is workspace-local, with host-owned server workers and routing epochs; it does not modify the common syntax catalogue. See Development workflows for process ownership, cancellation, limits, GUI/MCP/ABI2 contracts and remaining scope. The desktop selects Core, Code/CodeEditor, Diff, Commands, Diagnostics, DocumentViews, Inspector, Assets and Images/Canvas from modular CyUI. The Engine/core/CLI have no UI dependency. See CyUI migration for exact pins, view ownership, source adapters and limits. Project creation uses the UI-free ProjectTemplates service. The desktop wizard renders native plans through CyUI Core/Code; MCP and native plugins call the same Engine routes within their workspace boundary. The desktop explicitly selects its parent directory without changing those permissions. The shared FileTransactions primitive provides exclusive renames for resources and project publication. See Project templates . ABI2 template contributions contain data only. TemplateDefinitions checks and expands bounded UTF-8 files/options; Plugins supplies an atomic active-registry snapshot and holds its activation lock through creation. Snapshot reads happen before the plan mutex; commit always locks the plugin host before the plan store, including requests from a plugin's callback. No plugin callback executes during template expansion or file publication. Image tabs use the app-owned ImageLoader worker, bounded native decoders and deferred OpenGL textures, rendered by CyUI::Images. They are separate from Engine text documents and retain the shared tab/docking lifecycle. See Images . CyCodeReader lives in its own repository . Its editor/ source module provides the same cycode_editor and cycode_fileicons targets to the IDE, at the revision in app/editor-source.lock.json or an explicit CYCODE_EDITOR_ROOT development checkout. CyCode does not build the Reader app. The Reader hosts dockable file editors without an Engine, language server, build adapter or Core companion. cycode_files owns UTF-8 validation, newline encoding, bounded reads, path conversion and guarded atomic saves used by both applications. The IDE retains workspace/revision permissions; Reader uses files selected directly by its user and keeps per-document disk baselines across directories. Its application-specific extensions are documented in the Reader repository. Interactive execution uses the shared native Terminals and Debugger services. Terminals owns bounded libvterm screens/history and real ConPTY/POSIX PTY process trees, with separate read/write/supervisor threads. Only visible grid rows are copied for rendering. Debugger has one owner thread for DAP and a bounded command queue; the framed JSON transport is shared with LanguageClient without LSP initialization. Adapter reverse terminal requests create native terminals with explicit argv/env. DebugRuntime detects native/managed outputs and selects a compatible .NET host. CodeLLDB and NetCoreDbg share this DAP owner, inspection state and persistent profile; NetCoreDbg output uses the debug console, while interactive managed Run uses a PTY. Existing attached processes detach on stop; launched processes terminate. Persistent profiles/breakpoints use atomically replaced workspace metadata. See Execution . CyCode starts with C/C++ and keeps language support, project/build adapters, editor views and revision-control providers as separate extension points. A workspace can eventually contain several project types. CMake, MSBuild and UnrealBuildTool are executable adapters; solution inspection does not evaluate MSBuild. Explicit MSBuild evaluation reads real target properties/items, produces managed clangd metadata and tracks local solution/project/import inputs. Builds share the same native adapter with MCP; source diagnostics feed the Problems panel. ProjectTasks supplies Cargo metadata/compiler JSON, npm scripts and standalone javac compilation to both GUI and MCP. It owns one cancellable native task with bounded output/deadline and uses Terminals for persistent Run. The private IPC bridge accepts a bounded set of concurrent connections so cancellation remains receivable while a compiler is running. CyToolsCore continues to own scheduling, permissions and identities; matching native operation ids only correlate process cancellation. See Project tasks . text Copy CyUI / SDL3 desktop External MCP clients | | | official MCP SDK (stdio) | | | CyToolsCore authenticated HTTP | runtime, jobs, sessions, permissions | | +-------- native Engine <--- private loopback command bridge | documents / search / Git / CMake / Unreal / trusted plugins | LanguageService router +-- C++ owner thread <---- LSP transport ----> clangd +-- C# owner thread <---- LSP transport ----> csharp-ls/Roslyn The native Engine has no UI dependency. Documents carry monotonically increasing revisions, UTF-8 content, original BOM/newline convention and disk baseline. Saves reject stale revisions and external modifications before atomic replacement. Workspace paths are canonicalized and checked by path components, including symlink resolution. New files use exclusive creation. A task cleanup never removes source files. Resources owns bounded filesystem snapshots and issued plans, exclusive moves, guarded inverse actions and persistent project trash. Engine retains the live document model and gives text documents stable identities across path changes. Filesystem mutations emit bounded cursor events; the GUI rebases tabs/navigation without replacing editor Undo or native window identity. Deleted open buffers remain available with a missing marker. CyUI::Assets supplies the physical browser and its action requests. These operations are distinct from semantic symbol/file rename; see Resources for the SDK, limits and remaining integration gaps. Documentation and signature requests use those same live document/revision guards. LanguageInfo normalizes display-only sections and UTF-16 signature parameter offsets into bounded UTF-8 labels. The GUI keeps one information request in flight and discards responses for obsolete cursors; it follows the visible panel with a small debounce. It never executes backend Markdown, HTML or documentation links. The desktop polls document metadata, copies text on changes, indexes project paths off the UI thread and delegates content search to ripgrep. WorkspaceMonitor owns recursive Windows directory notifications with bounded buffers and overflow reconciliation; other systems currently use a bounded directory polling fallback. It publishes counters, never callbacks into UI or document services. Background workspace.poll reloads clean buffers and preserves dirty, missing or invalid files with a disk-conflict marker. A two-second reconciliation also covers open files in excluded directories. Replacing a search cancels its native process, and generation IDs suppress obsolete results. Dirty buffers supersede disk text in literal and regex searches; regex uses bounded private snapshots and native ripgrep cancellation. The path index is cached in memory, invalidated by structural/ignore-file events, and paged for clients (up to 200,000 indexed paths). Persistent path/symbol indexes, incremental symbol queries and large-file editing remain future work. See Workspace monitoring . The extension host supports ABI1 and the instance-based C ABI2. It resolves manifest dependencies before loading, preserves libraries until callbacks have stopped, and exposes JSON descriptors for commands, menus, panels, syntax, language servers, project templates and VCS/project providers. Application owns the UI and CyUI syntax-registration lifetimes. Project activation and VCS root mappings have revision/disk guards and independent workspace metadata. Git remains built in; selecting another provider changes the available actions and does not silently fall back to Git if that provider disappears. The bundled Unreal extension uses existing native services rather than another project parser/build engine. The original Unreal project panel and backend remain in the application. See Plugin SDK for contracts and remaining extension boundaries. Every native text editor is owned by CyUI::CodeEditor behind native document services. The GUI build prepares a patched copy in its build directory using prepare_texteditor.py; the checksum-pinned downloaded source is unchanged. The small adapter adds function, macro and reflection-attribute roles, a context tokenizer and a read-only token query for tests. EditorLanguage supplies bounded lexical C/C++/Unreal and C# rules; the widget retains incremental multi-line comment/string state. Preprocessor directives and their strings/comments are tokenized separately. Built-in keywords use one blue role; Unreal naming conventions supply types and reflection macros/metadata have dedicated roles. Function calls/declarations are recognized lexically. These fast rules remain available while project analysis loads or a backend is unavailable. EditorTheme owns the shared palette for editors, change previews and VCS views, with contrast checked against both editor grounds. Highlighting.cpp requests full LSP semantic tokens through the existing C++/C# owner threads. It decodes each server's negotiated legend and relative UTF-16 positions, validates single-line/non-overlapping ranges and surrogate boundaries, and returns UTF-16 positions plus separate Unicode glyph indexes. The same revision-checked language.highlight operation serves GUI and MCP. Results are capped at 50,000 spans or a 4 MiB token payload, with explicit truncation. Edits to any live document, server restart and semantic refresh requests invalidate the backend generation. The GUI debounces requests by 300 ms and runs at most two color queries concurrently, prioritizing the active and visible detached editors. Closed-tab queries retire asynchronously rather than blocking tab closure. The widget stores semantic display colors independently from lexical glyph roles. Its transaction version disables obsolete spans immediately, including after undo; normal keyword/string/comment state, identifiers and completion stay intact. Colors map actual aliases/classes, functions/methods, variables/parameters/fields, macros and enum members; clangd's inactive-code comment spans use a readable muted role. Unknown/dependent classifications retain lexical colors. C# uses the same adapter with Roslyn's legend. Delta/range streaming, advanced modifier styling and broader raw-string/preprocessor fallback coverage remain pending. External buffer replacements are applied as editor transactions to retain undo. The LSP transport queues writes and delivers replies on a dedicated LanguageService owner thread. One clangd process serves both UI completion/navigation and MCP queries; Engine document opens, changes and closes synchronize its unsaved overlays. Requests never wait on the UI thread. A maximum of 32 outstanding requests and a 15-second deadline bound the queue, including initialization; expired requests send LSP $/cancelRequest. Restart/shutdown fails in-flight requests and joins the child. The transport bounds queued writes by count and bytes; document synchronization retries under backpressure and completes before semantic queries are sent. Engine checks the source revision and live-document generation before accepting semantic replies; UI completion also checks its generation and cursor. The editor uses 32-bit Unicode codepoints; LSP uses zero-based UTF-16 positions, and ripgrep columns are byte offsets. Navigation converts those coordinates explicitly and decodes percent-escaped file URIs. Results outside the canonical workspace are counted but omitted by default. With includeExternal, registered engine/compiler SDK roots issue opaque read-only source references; they do not extend workspace write permissions. This initial adapter launches clangd; other servers need their own launch settings, project configuration and integration validation. Semantic.cpp normalizes workspace/document symbols and maintains bounded rename and formatting plans. TextEdits validates UTF-16 ranges, surrogate boundaries and non-overlapping replacements. Plans snapshot live revisions and text; apply/undo validate every affected buffer and its current disk baseline before changing any buffer. Saves remain explicit. The desktop and MCP use these same operations. SDK documents live in a separate registry, can be read only through issued handles, and cannot be passed to document write/refactor operations. See Semantic editing . Commands are registered once for menus, the keyboard settings and action palette. The toolkit-independent Keymap resolves profile bindings, contexts, custom overrides and multi-stroke chords. The UI consumes matched keys before the editor widget's fixed shortcuts, preserving ordinary typing/caret handling. This prevents Rider's Ctrl+Y/Ctrl+B from invoking the widget's redo or the former build shortcut. Initial completion waits for the document's first diagnostics publication: clangd's initialized status alone can still produce unrelated index-only completions while its first preamble is being built. BuildSystem owns tool discovery, CMake execution, cache compatibility checks, profile persistence and File API inspection. UI and MCP use the same native operations. Configure requests codemodel/toolchain replies and selects the native compilation database or derives one from File API metadata for Visual Studio. The active database directory initializes the shared clangd; successful reconfigure reloads it while retaining live overlays. Local profile state is .cycode/build.json; generated analysis databases stay in the build tree. See Build services . Solution inspection accepts directories, .sln and .uproject entries and keeps the canonical document root at the project directory. Missing/external references remain metadata rather than new document permissions. UnrealProject discovers the associated engine and invokes UBT using argv. Database generation reloads the same LanguageService used by the GUI/MCP. See Unreal integration for tested scope. SDL3 and the ImGui OpenGL3 renderer provide native platform viewports. Each document is a dockable window; detached editors and panels own distinct SDL/OS windows and GL contexts. Rendering restores the main context afterwards. Closing a panel hides it; View/sidebar actions restore it. Editor closes retain unsaved-document checks. Independent processes own their engines, buffers, descriptors and jobs. Layout filenames are keyed by canonical project entry; global preferences use unique temporary files and atomic replacement. File icons use original vector drawings, semantic palette colours and DPI-aware geometry without OS symbol-font assets. CyToolsCore is installed as a real wheel into runtime/python. One companion per GUI instance shares the Core scheduler across MCP connections. Each instance has unique private native/Core descriptors. The native token protects local IPC; Core owns assistant authentication and operation permissions. The bridge is application IPC, not another MCP parser, scheduler or job registry. The service exits when its native descriptor is removed. Jobs and artifacts use the SDK lifecycle. Source document paths are workspace references, not file-import fields: importing a copy would disconnect edits from the open editor. Temporary generated reports belong in JobContext.path; explicit source saves remain persistent operations. Git mutations are serialized by the native Engine. Vcs.cpp provides structured repository metadata and guarded working-tree changes. Changed clean documents reload through the same revision/LSP service; dirty buffers survive concurrent operations. VcsUI consumes structured responses asynchronously and keeps conflict editing in normal document tabs. Providers continue to use the existing C ABI. CyUI is an external configurable checkout, not a vendored fork. Platform-specific code includes process/IPC, Windows engine registration and the Unicode entry point; SDL3 supplies window/input/render integration. Portability of source is not a claim that Linux/macOS builds have run. The shared editor library owns per-document incremental Tree-sitter parsers for Rust/Java/JS/TS/TSX/HTML/CSS, with display spans separate from lexical and semantic overlays. Both applications and refactor/conflict previews use this same layer. The SDL-free core routes language requests to independent server owners for C++, C#, Rust, Java, TypeScript/JavaScript, HTML and CSS. Initialization options and workspace configuration are separate; the service respects advertised methods and maps LSP workspace-edit versions to native document revisions. See language support for runtime prerequisites and deliberate limits. CompletionEngine.cpp holds bounded issued-item sessions tied to document revision, workspace generation and backend epoch. Resolve receives only cached server items; prepare turns the primary edit and additional imports into the existing ChangePlan transaction after checking UTF-16 ranges, overlaps and disk baselines. The MCP surface is read-only until changes_apply. The build-local editor patch intercepts acceptance without inserting a partial symbol. The GUI prepares asynchronously, checks cursor/revision/generation again, applies the native plan and mirrors it as one tab-preserving undo transaction. A headless actual widget test verifies the acceptance hook; complete desktop acceptance remains separate. Snippet.cpp is an SDL-free bounded parser/expander linked by the core and editor. Completion preserves field byte offsets through indentation and additional imports. EditorSnippet converts them once to glyph coordinates and uses the widget's detailed transaction callback to track linked fields without rescanning document text for every keystroke. The build-local adapter adds validated multi-selections and a pre-key handler; ordinary multicursor edits supply atomic mirror typing. Finishing a session collapses only its recorded cursor history so undo/redo cannot revive temporary linked cursors. The widget's text extraction also preserves exact final newlines rather than implicitly appending one to nonempty files. CodeActions.cpp owns separate bounded issued-action sessions and lazy resolution. LanguageService adds overlapping published diagnostics to code-action context, matches decoded file URI identities and maps versioned edits to native revisions. LanguageClient invalidates diagnostic eligibility for actions on edits while retaining the last displayed diagnostics and fast completion; versionless publications remain advisory. New target overlays must be synchronized before a fresh query, preventing an edit from adopting an unrelated disk baseline. Shared workspace-edit parsing and ChangePlan validation serve rename and context actions. GUI and MCP use those same plans; no code-action command is executed. Only the pinned TypeScript server's verified empty acknowledgement is ignored. Resource operations and annotated/snippet action edits remain explicitly unavailable. RecoveryStore is UI-free and keeps per-instance, OS-locked UTF-8 checkpoints under .cycode/recovery. Engine owns a joined background worker that snapshots dirty document revisions and writes immutable payloads before an atomic index. Restore validates checkpoint/target/disk guards, installs a live buffer and transfers its backup before retiring the source. The GUI uses CyUI Code for bounded previews and the existing editor replacement transaction for Undo. Native documents remain the only mutable model shared with MCP; checkpoints never save project files. See Recovery for quotas, failure handling and explicit limitations. pages.title: CyCode branding
pages.html:
CyCode branding#

The owner-supplied assets live in the repository's icons/ directory:

  • CyCode.png: transparent application logo, used in the top bar and SDL window icons.
  • CyCode.ico: Windows executable application icon, resource ID 1 / icon index 0.
  • CyCode-document.ico: document icon, resource ID 2 / icon index 1.
  • CyCode-document.png: original document artwork, included in distribution.

Each ICO contains 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 96, 128 and 256 px images. CMake configures the Windows resource paths from the repository root; source code has no machine-specific path. Only the GUI executable embeds these icon resources. The UI-free CLI keeps its existing dependencies.

The desktop reads the PNG from its installation, decodes it with the existing native image decoder and prepares a display copy of at most 256 px. The original assets stay unchanged. The top bar uses the existing OpenGL texture owner and CyUI dimensions. The image retains its supplied colours in each theme.

SDL's Windows class-icon hints select resource 1 for large/small icons before initialization. The cached image is also applied when SDL shows a main or detached window. Its pixel/texture lifetime belongs to Application, including deferred GPU deletion. Missing/broken artwork cannot prevent project editing; the text title and embedded Windows resource remain available.

Windows packaging explicitly includes the four PNG/ICO files and records their hashes. Keep icons/, app/ and tools/ alongside CyCode.exe. The document icon is available to a future installer/file-association workflow; adding it does not register file extensions or change system defaults.

Windows x64 resource embedding and native icon/logo rendering have been verified. Linux/macOS runtime and native desktop/bundle packaging remain unverified; a Wayland desktop entry or a macOS application bundle is still separate work.

pages.title: C/C++ toolchains and CMake
pages.html:
C/C++ toolchains and CMake#

UpdateHistory.cpp joins cycode_updates and UpdateHistoryUI.cpp joins cycode_ui; UpdateHistory/UpdateHistoryPolicy are their native model/policy. The fixture source joins the existing opt-in core target only, with BUILD_TESTING=OFF in production. No new target, external dependency or CyUI module is introduced. Helper references and its manifest stay unchanged. See History.

Recovery progress adds UpdateRecoveryProgress/UpdateRecoveryFeedback to the existing native/helper sources. The Windows production helper links the system comctl32.lib and Threads::Threads. Its configured resource embeds Updater.manifest, requesting Common-Controls 6 and asInvoker, with the MSVC generated manifest disabled to avoid a duplicate resource. No downloaded runtime, executable target or CyUI module is added; helper references remain files/native-lease/updates only. BUILD_TESTING stays OFF. See Recovery controls.

Space/progress adds only the UpdateBudget and UpdateProgress headers to existing native/update/UI sources; it creates no target, dependency or CyUI module. Windows uses the existing system Kernel32 API for caller-available space; non-Windows transport remains manual. Thirty actual policy assertions are compiler-evaluated without a native test executable. See Download observations.

Retry adds only the internal UpdateFeedback header and extends the existing UpdateDownload/Transfer/Files and UpdatesUI/StorageUI sources. It adds no target, dependency, external adapter or CyUI module. Opt-in download/module contracts stay in their existing targets; production testing remains OFF. See Download retry.

UpdateDownload joins cycode_updates; UpdateRange is its shared constexpr response policy. Download regression sources join only the existing opt-in core target. BUILD_TESTING remains OFF for production. Nineteen actual policy assertions are compiler-evaluated by /Zs without generating/running native test executables. There is no new target, external dependency or CyUI module; see Download resumption.

UpdateStorage joins cycode_updates, UpdateStorageUI joins cycode_ui, and the cache fixture joins the existing opt-in core target. No target/dependency/module is added.

UpdateManifest/UpdateRecovery join the existing cycode_updates target; the existing production helper adds UpdaterRecoveryUI. There is no new target, third-party runtime or CyUI module; the current helper's additional Windows system dependency is described above. The recovery fixture source joins the opt-in core target only.

UpdateCache is part of the existing cycode_updates library; it adds no target or third-party dependency. It reuses cycode_files for atomic helper outcome records.

Application updating adds the production CyCodeUpdater on Windows as a dependency of CyCode. cycode_updates links only the shared file/lease implementation and system WinHTTP/BCrypt; it does not link the IDE, SDL, ImGui or SDK. NativeFileLease.cpp now has one cycode_native_lease target reused by the core/updater. Existing CyUI modules are unchanged. BUILD_TESTING=OFF still excludes all native fixtures. The Windows packager includes the helper and writes both the normal compressed ZIP and a stored -update.zip, with manifest format 1 and exact file sizes/hashes. It reads PE resources instead of launching a CLI, and requires clean source and matching executable/descriptor versions. See Application updates for release publication, private-access configuration and recovery limits.

Document occurrences add OccurrenceCatalogue to the existing core target and OccurrencesUI, EditorOccurrences and EditorTextMap to cycode_ui. Diagnostics reuse the latter coordinate adapter. The new occurrence regression source joins the existing semantic fixture; existing command/module/lifecycle fixture sources are extended. No new executable target, dependency, CyUI module, backend copy or notice is needed. Production keeps BUILD_TESTING=OFF; do not run native tests implicitly. Regenerate app/CyTool.json via app/contracts.py and locales/ui.json via scripts/write_locales.py. See Document occurrences.

Source navigation adds NavigationLocations.cpp to cycode_core and NavigationUI.cpp to cycode_ui, reusing the existing CyUI Core filter and result controls. The navigation regression source joins the existing opt-in semantic fixture; command, module and lifecycle sources extend existing targets. Production BUILD_TESTING=OFF does not build/run those fixtures. No new module, dependency, executable/test target or license notice is needed. Existing bridge/locale regeneration commands remain. See Source navigation.

Symbol navigation adds SymbolCatalogue to cycode_core and StructureUI to cycode_ui, using existing CyUI Core, its shared filter/folding and ImGui tree controls. Deferred symbol resolution extends the same native Semantic/LanguageService and existing Application/SemanticUI sources. No build integration or dependency change is needed; regenerate the bridge with python app/contracts.py and locales with python app/scripts/write_locales.py after contract/label changes. No new module or dependency is selected. Source regressions join existing semantic, module and lifecycle test targets; production BUILD_TESTING=OFF does not build or run them. No new executable/test target is introduced. See Symbol navigation.

Compiler source links add CompilerLocation to the existing native core. GUI reuses BuildUI/ModuleUI and the already selected CyUI Core/Diagnostics modules. The compiler-location regression source joins the existing opt-in build target; production BUILD_TESTING=OFF does not build/run it. Diagnostic lifetime tests extend the existing language fixture. No extra dependency, module or executable target. See Compiler locations.

TaskOutput now provides the shared journal implementation in BuildOutput; the new TaskOutputText core source frames Cargo display messages. Existing ProjectTasks, ModuleModels/ModuleUI, Commands and BuildUI provide status and diagnostic navigation. Existing CyUI Diagnostics/Core suffice. No new dependency or executable target; regression sources join the existing BUILD_TESTING-only build/project/module targets. Ordinary production remains BUILD_TESTING=OFF. See Project output.

Live build output adds BuildOutput to the existing core, extending the internal process observer and BuildOperations reservation. BuildUI reuses the selected CyUI Diagnostics module. No new library, module or executable target is required. Its regression source joins the existing build fixture, excluded from ordinary BUILD_TESTING=OFF production builds. See Live build output.

Instruction breakpoint support adds InstructionBreakpoints to the native core and InstructionBreakpointsUI to the UI, reusing DebugInspection, JSON and CyUI Core. Its source assertions join the existing debugger target; normal BUILD_TESTING=OFF production builds do not generate or run that test executable. No extra library, adapter, runtime executable or dependency is introduced.

Advanced execution adds DebugExecution to the existing native core and DebugExecutionUI to the UI. It reuses JSON, the DAP worker, commands and CyUI Core. The new regression source joins the existing debugger test target. Production BUILD_TESTING=OFF does not build/run it or a new test executable. No recording, debugger or reverse-execution dependency is installed by this feature.

Debugger value/memory editing adds DebugMutations to the native core and DebugMutationsUI to the existing UI target. It reuses JSON, the DAP worker and CyUI Core widgets; no new library, module or executable is required. Its regression source joins the existing debugger test target, which stays excluded from ordinary BUILD_TESTING=OFF production builds. See Value editing.

Java debugging adds only JavaDebug/LoopbackStream core sources, reusing existing JSON, threading and Windows ws2_32 dependencies. No additional CyUI module, native test executable, Python backend or external library is compiled. JDT LS and its separately installed Microsoft java-debug JAR are runtime prerequisites, not build dependencies. CYCODE_JAVA_DEBUG supplies the JAR to default server initialization, with explicit remembered profiles remaining authoritative. See Java debugging; ordinary builds retain BUILD_TESTING=OFF.

JDWP attach reuses those same sources/dependencies. No JDWP client library, remote helper, new binary or CyUI module is added. Its network connection is performed by the existing local JDT LS/java-debug owner only on explicit attach.

CMake test/package/workflow presets now have a separate ordered preview and reviewed execution path, sharing the ordinary native cancellation/deadline reservation. View > CMake preset actions and the Build menu expose them; see Preset actions. These project commands are distinct from this repository's opt-in developer test builds, which remain disabled in ordinary application builds.

The application build also produces bundled Subversion, Perforce and Mercurial providers. SVN reuses cycode_process, cycode_files and the already pinned TinyXML2 dependency without linking UI/Engine services into its library. BUILD_TESTING=OFF keeps the separate svn_provider regression executable out of production builds. Git remains built in; SVN is an optional installed CLI resolved through PATH or CYCODE_SVN. Perforce links the shared process/file utilities and JSON, without additional dependencies; resolve its separately installed p4 through PATH or CYCODE_P4. The separate perforce_provider regression also remains opt-in. See Subversion and Perforce. Mercurial also reuses the shared process/file utilities and JSON, without new dependencies. Its production target is cycode_mercurial; resolve the separately installed hg with PATH or CYCODE_HG. The mercurial_provider regression is opt-in behind BUILD_TESTING, like the other provider regressions. See Mercurial. No external VCS client or credentials are packaged. Diversion adds cycode_diversion using the same process/file/JSON dependencies; its external CLI is resolved through PATH or CYCODE_DV. The separate diversion_provider regression is also gated by BUILD_TESTING. No external client is launched as part of compiling it. See Diversion.

Configure/build presets are available in the CMake panel and native/MCP/plugin services. CMake applies their cache/toolchain/environment/condition semantics; CyCode reads bounded metadata and guards include/binary paths. See Project formats for inheritance, selection and validation limits.

Visual Studio solution/project builds have a separate native MSBuild adapter. Unreal solutions retain their UnrealBuildTool workflow.

Open Build > CMake settings, or start the desktop with --show-cmake. The CMake panel selects source/build directories, toolchain, generator, configuration and target. Configure applies those settings; Build compiles the selected target, or the default target set when All targets is selected. Output remains in Build. Build > Cancel build and the Build panel request owned process-tree termination. The same services cover MSBuild and explicit Unreal operations, including MCP and plugin host requests. See Build cancellation for IDs, reservation lifetime, scope and the current unexecuted regression checks.

Detection runs off the UI thread. It queries CMake capabilities, compiler versions and installed Visual Studio instances through vswhere. Standard Clang/GCC pairs are found on PATH; Windows also checks LLVM and CMake/Ninja bundled with Visual Studio. A generator listed by CMake is a supported generator format, not proof that every prerequisite for that generator is installed. GCC is detected by the same portable path but was not installed or exercised on the local Windows machine. The initial adapter offers installed Visual Studio generators, Ninja (single configuration), and Unix Makefiles when their build tools are found. Ninja Multi-Config, Xcode and other generator integrations remain future work.

Automatic selects a discovered compiler for a new tree and preserves the compiler and generator of an existing tree. On Windows, MSVC uses a Visual Studio generator, x64 host/target and the detected MSVC tools version. This milestone does not use MSVC with Ninja: localized showIncludes/dependency handling needs separate validation. Clang/GCC use Ninja when available, otherwise Unix Makefiles. Presets can supply custom toolchain/compiler/generator options through CMake. Broader cross-toolchain validation and automatic MSVC/Ninja environment setup remain work items.

A compiler or generator change requires a new build directory. CyCode does not delete CMake caches. Existing trees without compiler metadata can be configured with Automatic first, or replaced by an explicitly chosen new build directory. Source and build paths must remain in the workspace; in-source builds and build directories containing the source tree are rejected. Build configuration choices are Debug, Release, RelWithDebInfo and MinSizeRel. A single-configuration generator must be reconfigured before building a different configuration.

Project metadata and code analysis#

CyCode requests codemodel-v2 and toolchains-v1 using its own CMake File API client query directory. It reads targets, artifacts and actual compiler information from the referenced replies. It never evaluates CMake scripts to inspect a configured project. Configure/build operations execute trusted project code as normal CMake operations do. Inspect validates reply references and source/build identities.

For Ninja/Makefiles, the IDE uses CMake's native compile_commands.json. Visual Studio generators do not export it, so CyCode derives a database from the selected configuration's CMake File API compile groups: compiler, command fragments, definitions, includes and reported implicit include directories. Only workspace C/C++ translation units are exported. The generated database lives under BUILD/.cycode/clangd/CONFIGURATION and is labelled cmake-file-api in the UI/API. It describes analysis commands rather than a replacement build system. CMake still owns the actual build. Advanced module/PCH/unity/framework and cross compilation workflows have not been validated by this adapter.

The shared clangd receives the selected database directory through its initialization options. A successful configure restarts it and resynchronizes live unsaved buffers, including when flags change at the same database path. CyCode does not copy a database over the workspace's root compile_commands.json or edit the user's .clangd. Failed configure operations keep the previously active profile/database selection.

Successful operations save the active local profile in .cycode/build.json, schema version 1. It contains source, buildDirectory, configuration, toolchain, generator and target. Toolchain IDs may contain machine paths; this is local state, ignored in CyCode's own repository. Invalid profiles are reported and preserved. They can be repaired or removed explicitly; CyCode will not overwrite an unrecognized format. The build tree gets a .gitignore if none exists, and .cycode metadata is excluded from project text/file search. Existing ignore files are preserved.

Primary references: CMake File API, compilation database export, clangd compilation settings.

The advanced DAP, JVM build-model, shader-task and workspace-session services introduce no new downloaded library. Maven XML reuses the pinned UI-free TinyXML2 target; the native lease uses Windows/POSIX system APIs. JVM distributions/JDKs remain separate tools; DXC/glslang are also separate installed prerequisites. Opening a project does not install them. Contract regression sources join the existing opt-in core, debugger, project-task and extension test targets. Ordinary app builds retain BUILD_TESTING=OFF; MSVC /Zs checks those sources without generating a test executable. See Testing.

Signed local packages add Monocypher 4.0.3, pinned by release/archive checksum in dependencies.lock.json. fetch_dependencies.py --core-only now includes its sources. cycode_crypto is a private static C99 dependency of the native core, with hidden ELF/Mach-O visibility; no extra runtime crypto DLL is packaged. Its optional Ed25519/SHA-512 source is compiled with the library, without upstream tests/demos. The full third-party notice is in licenses/Monocypher.txt. Package authoring's Python cryptography dependency is separate and optional; it is not required by the app's native verifier. See Plugin packages.

The expanded Cargo workspace/feature/profile/target adapter adds no build dependency or CyUI module. Cargo is a separate installed/private tool used only by explicit project tasks, not to compile CyCode. Existing application builds keep native tests disabled; the new regression source joins the opt-in project-task target. See Cargo workspaces for exact controls and validation limits.

RustAnalysis adds no external dependency, runtime or CyUI module. It derives a typed overlay inside the native language service and uses the existing server process owner, preference store and project-task inspection. Regression sources join the existing opt-in lifecycle target, not the production build. See Rust analysis.

Named Rustup selection is optional at runtime, not a dependency for compiling CyCode. Install/configure Rustup separately (PATH or CYCODE_RUSTUP) and use an already installed toolchain/component. RustToolchain adds only native planning helpers; no installer, proxy executable, downloaded library or CyUI module is packaged by this change. See Rust toolchains.

Installation headroom/failure policies use existing updater sources and Windows volume/handle APIs; no new dependency or CyUI module is selected. The new regression source joins the existing opt-in core target. Keep ordinary builds/testing OFF; see Installation checks.

Recovery headroom/staging extends existing updater sources and Windows volume/handle utilities, without a dependency/module/target change. Tests stay OFF; existing opt-in core sources carry budget and guarded-staging contracts. See Recovery preparation.

Prepared recovery resumption stays in existing UpdateRecovery/UpdateBudget sources, with the already-linked atomic text utility and no new target, dependency or CyUI module. Immutable work/source records are application metadata, not build inputs or published payload. Production tests stay OFF; see Recovery.

GUI builds also generate the bundled offline manual with Node.js 22+ / npm and the pinned private CyDoc source. See Documentation for cache, checkout, regeneration and validation options. Core-only builds do not need Node.

pages.title: Cancelling native build operations
pages.html:
Cancelling native build operations#

Reviewed Unreal cook/package execution now uses this same reservation, operation-ID matching and owned process tree. Its reviewed deadline can be 1..86400 seconds; partial archives/logs remain persistent on cancellation. No Unreal acceptance ran during the Kaspersky suspension; see Unreal automation.

Build > Cancel build, the command palette and the Build panel stop an active CMake, MSBuild or explicit Unreal operation. A custom binding can be set in Options > Keyboard shortcuts. Cargo/npm/standalone Java retain their separate Project tasks > Cancel task service.

The UI tracks the issued operation ID while an asynchronous task enters native execution. An old request cannot cancel the next operation. Cancel build also signals the existing background Unreal analysis cancellation token. Closing the application requests cancellation before waiting for owned task/plugin futures; trusted native plugin work outside exported services must cooperate with its own lifecycle contract.

Shared Engine, MCP and plugins#

Reviewed CMake test/package/workflow execution through build.presetRun also uses this reservation and its existing ID/deadline/cancellation contract. See Preset actions.

One BuildOperations reservation per Engine covers:

  • build.configure, build.run;
  • msbuild.build/rebuild/clean/restore/evaluate/prepare;
  • unreal.generate/database/build/prepare when explicitly dispatched.

build.status / MCP build_status returns running, operationId, method and cancelling. It describes the native reservation, including waiting for an adapter lock. The separate build.output/build_output service supplies a bounded, revisioned live tail; see Live build output. Background GUI Unreal analysis retains its independent token/status rather than creating a second reservation. The GUI's Working indicator includes native builds started by the MCP/plugin host; workspace switching waits for them to finish or be cancelled.

build.cancel / MCP build_cancel accepts optional operationId and returns requested. Omit the ID to stop the current native build intentionally; supply it to require an exact match. requested:true acknowledges the request, not completed termination. running remains true until native work and cleanup return. A second explicit native build is rejected while that reservation is held. Cancellation/status bypass plugin, document and adapter execution locks.

The facade gives each direct build request a fresh internal ID. SDK job cancellation repeatedly signals only that ID and keeps receiving its native response before the handler returns. Failed cancellation notifications do not release the SDK reservation; the client retries while waiting on the original call. build_cancel requires process.execute and has no workspace-mutation exclusive group, so it can run while a build owns that group. build_status is read-only. IDs correlate operations; they are not authorization tokens. An authorized operator can explicitly cancel the shared workspace's current build.

ABI2 host requests export build.inspect/status, build.configure/run/cancel, msbuild.inspect/build/rebuild/clean/restore/evaluate/prepare and the existing Unreal services. Process/mutation services require the manifest's process.execute permission and a mutating callback. Explicit build cancellation can stop these host-owned builds while a plugin callback is waiting. Generic plugin-job cancellation does not propagate an outer job ID through arbitrary plugin callbacks; use build_cancel for their active host-owned build. Arbitrary native plugin work cannot be interrupted by this service.

Execution and persistence#

The token reaches toolchain probes, native execution and MSBuild's per-project evaluation loop. Waiting for an adapter/detection lock is cancellable. Interrupted discovery does not publish a partial tool cache. Cancelled, timed-out or truncated results cannot be reported as successful builds. Profile and analysis publication checks cancellation; files already written or committed before observing it remain. No build tree, project source or cache is deleted, and no automatic retry occurs.

Windows children are created suspended, assigned to an owned Job Object and then resumed. If ownership cannot be established, the child is terminated before tool code runs and the operation fails. On completion/stop, remaining owned workers are terminated and the job is checked for an empty process set. Output draining is bounded even for a process continuously writing output.

Linux/macOS use an owned POSIX process group. The parent observes child exit with waitid(..., WNOWAIT) before stopping remaining group members and reaping it, avoiding use of an already-reaped/reusable child PID for group cleanup. A process deliberately escaping its group or using an existing shared daemon is outside this ownership contract. This is process lifecycle management, not an OS sandbox. References: Linux waitid documentation, Apple's wait API header.

The main CMake/MSBuild/Unreal build/generation subprocess accepts timeoutSeconds from 1 to 86,400. Native defaults remain 180 seconds for CMake/Unreal and 150 for MSBuild. Desktop Options remembers a 1,800-second default and supplies it to these operations, including background Unreal analysis. This preference is included in the existing configuration save/load. CLI/MCP/plugin callers can set their own request deadline; it is not stored in project/compiler profiles or index stamps.

The real CyToolsCore facade extends its build response wait to the requested native deadline plus 60 seconds (minimum 200), retaining correlated cancellation handling. Other RPC waits remain 200 seconds. Tool probes and 15-second structured MSBuild evaluations (up to eight projects) retain their independent bounds. The output cap remains 8 MiB. Explicit build execution now has a separate 256 KiB live tail; project tasks now share this implementation through project.status/project.output, with their existing separate owner and captured GUI cancellation IDs. See Project output. Background-analysis streaming and semantic request cancellation remain future work.

Validation boundary#

Windows application/core/CLI compilation and source checks are the local checks for this change. New C++ assertions cover ID matching, native ownership after a cancel acknowledgement, exclusion of a second build, reset for the next build, exception cleanup and pre-cancelled process requests. A new official MCP test exercises cancellation inside a CMake configure subprocess and a subsequent job. These scenarios have not been executed during the Kaspersky interruption; GUI interaction and Linux/macOS execution are unverified. See Testing and Validation.

pages.title: Cargo workspaces, features and targets
pages.html:
Cargo workspaces, features and targets#

Project tasks exposes the same native adapter to the desktop, MCP and the permission-checked project.* plugin host. Cargo owns TOML parsing, resolution, profile inheritance and compilation; no second Rust backend or ABI is added.

Open a workspace folder or Cargo.toml, then View > Project tasks. Configure refreshes packages, targets and declared features through cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps. Read-only inspection uses the saved model without invoking Cargo. Configure can resolve dependencies/update Cargo.lock; offline and locked also apply to metadata.

Saved controls#

Field Behavior
cargoToolchain Empty preserves automatic selection; a named installed Rustup toolchain wraps Cargo through rustup run, without requesting installation. See Rust toolchains.
cargoWorkspace --workspace builds/tests all members. Mutually exclusive with a nonempty package. False preserves Cargo's normal selected-manifest/default-member rules.
package Exact package name/specification forwarded as one --package argument. Wildcards and leading option markers are rejected. The menu selects reported names.
cargoTargetKind bin (default), example, lib, test or bench. Named targets use the corresponding Cargo selector; libraries use --lib.
target Optional exact target name. Empty bin preserves default Cargo targets; empty example/test/bench selects --examples/--tests/--benches. Libraries ignore the name.
cargoProfile Optional --profile, up to 128 UTF-8 bytes; overrides Debug/Release. Empty preserves Configuration. Cargo validates existence/inheritance.
cargoFeatures Up to 128 unique names, 256 UTF-8 bytes each, one per line. package/feature is supported; the declared-feature menu adds that form. No whitespace/comma bundles or option markers.
cargoAllFeatures --all-features.
cargoNoDefaultFeatures --no-default-features.
cargoLocked --locked: Cargo rejects missing locks or resolution changes.
offline --offline; combined with locked gives Cargo's frozen behavior.

Metadata receives feature/offline/locked options, without build-only package, target or profile switches. It lists all workspace members. Packages retain opaque IDs, workspace-relative manifests, declared feature names and Cargo's default-member status. Targets retain package IDs, kinds and required features. Required features are displayed, never silently enabled. This model does not claim transitive enabled-feature state.

Example SDK/native parameters for an executable example:

json
{  "system": "cargo",  "directory": ".",  "package": "render-tools",  "cargoWorkspace": false,  "cargoTargetKind": "example",  "target": "preview",  "cargoFeatures": ["render-tools/gpu"],  "cargoNoDefaultFeatures": true,  "cargoProfile": "development-fast",  "cargoLocked": true}

Executables and cache#

Run/debug build first and use Cargo's actual reported executable. It must match a known workspace package ID, target name and selected kind, and exist inside the opened workspace. Dependency executables, custom-build scripts, test harnesses and example libraries are excluded. Equal target names remain distinguished by package and kind; several eligible executables require narrower selection. Libraries/tests/benchmarks cannot run as applications. project_test still invokes Cargo test; no benchmark runner or structured framework result tree is added.

The cache includes every new option, workspace/member manifests, the workspace lock file, and config/toolchain files from the selected directory through the opened workspace root. Changed options/inputs invalidate cached targets/artifacts. Failed, cancelled, timed-out or truncated configure/build operations leave an incomplete cache with no runnable artifacts. Legacy profiles gain defaults; old Cargo caches require refresh. Every build still runs Cargo. Existing buffer, deadline, cancellation and terminal lifecycle guards remain shared.

Workspace roots, member manifests and target sources must fit inside the opened IDE workspace. Open the enclosing workspace instead of an isolated member whose Cargo root is outside it. Global/user Cargo config, external dependencies/toolchains and external source edits are not watched; the next real invocation evaluates them. Named installed Rustup selection is available; toolchain listing/management, arbitrary toolchain paths and cross-target execution/custom runners remain separate work. Trusted project build rules/macros execute on explicit tasks; language-server defaults remain unchanged. The explicit Apply Cargo options and restart Rust action synchronizes manifest/features/default-feature/offline/locked settings; it can remember a snapshot in local application preferences. Later task changes require applying again. Package/target/custom profiles remain build controls. See Rust analysis for the mapping, removal and validation limits. Builds are not sandboxed project execution.

Validation#

See Validation for Windows production compilation, SDK schemas and syntax-only checks. New regression assertions extend the existing task target; they have not run while native acceptance is suspended after antivirus removals. No Cargo invocation, generated Rust executable, debuggee or GUI run validated this addition. Actual workspace/feature resolution, example run/debug, menus/keyboard, themes/DPI and Linux/macOS remain unverified. Advanced Rust debugging and framework test discovery remain broader work.

References: Cargo build, metadata, compiler JSON.
