pages.title: Annotated language-server edits
pages.html:
Annotated language-server edits#

Language-server fixes, refactorings and symbol renames can now attach passive labels/descriptions to text edits. These remain ordinary guarded native change plans: prepare, inspect, apply to live buffers, then Save separately. The common Engine serves the desktop, real SDK/MCP and permission-checked native plugin host.

The protocol distinguishes descriptive annotations from annotations requiring confirmation. See the official LSP text edit contract and workspace edit capabilities. The client now advertises changeAnnotationSupport and honorsChangeAnnotations for code actions and rename. It supports version-mapped text document changes, line-ending normalization and textOnlyTransactional handling; resource-operation capabilities remain absent.

Desktop review#

Annotated plans always open Refactoring before applying, including corrections requested with Enter/Apply correction and ordinary automatic formatting paths. Unannotated actions retain their existing behavior. Change annotations lists each label; expand its row for the description and affected files. Each required label has its own confirmation checkbox. Apply changes stays disabled until all required labels are confirmed. Closing the view does not apply or save source changes.

Confirmations survive redraws of the same plan and clear when the plan ID or workspace changes. The existing before/after Diff, live-buffer application and guarded Undo remain in use. Annotated and plain edits can share one transaction; annotations do not introduce individual per-file commits or a second Undo model.

Native ownership and bounds#

ChangeAnnotations validates definitions/references and substitutes native IDs for opaque server IDs. storeChange qualifies those IDs with the issued plan ID. An acknowledgement from another plan, an unknown ID or a duplicate is refused. Required confirmations are checked before any buffer mutation, followed by the existing all-document revision/text/disk checks. Failed confirmation leaves the plan available for review; a later source/disk change still invalidates applying it.

Only annotations on effective edits survive. No-op edits and unused definitions do not request confirmation. Global plan metadata lists the actual affected files; changes.preview retains the same IDs but filters each annotation's files to the requested preview. Normalized text edits retain annotationId alongside their range, oldText and newText. Undo needs no new acknowledgement.

Bounds: 128 definitions, raw server IDs up to 512 bytes, labels up to 2,048 bytes, descriptions up to 4,096 bytes and 512 KiB of annotation metadata, including final issued IDs/file lists. Labels are nonempty; descriptions are optional. NUL text, invalid confirmation flags and unknown references fail explicitly. Empty raw server IDs remain valid and are replaced with ordinary nonempty issued IDs. The existing 100-document, 16 MiB before/after preview, per-file text and UTF-16/ overlap limits still apply. Plans remain process-owned and expire/evict through the existing change store. No annotation is interpreted as a command, path grant, Markdown/HTML program or executable plugin contribution.

SDK and plugins#

Prepared plans now include annotations (an empty array for plain plans). Each entry has id, label, description, needsConfirmation and files. The output field is optional in the published schema so old plain-plan examples remain compatible. No operation ID or permission changed; there are still 170 SDK operations.

After inspecting the plan/preview, an SDK caller supplies the required issued IDs:

json
{  "id": "change-issued-plan",  "confirmedAnnotations": ["change-issued-plan:annotation-1"]}

This is the parameter object for changes_apply, not a raw LSP edit. The optional confirmedAnnotations array holds at most 128 unique strings (1–256 characters). Omitting it remains valid for plans without required confirmations; the native Engine enforces which IDs must be present. workspace.write and the existing SDK workspace-mutations group remain required. The actual CyToolsCore owns identities, jobs and permissions; no Python editor/parser or alternate scheduler is added.

Native plugins now also receive the refactoring prepare/preview/apply/undo services through the existing JSON host entry point, with the same metadata/acknowledgements and workspace permission. Provider read callbacks cannot apply/undo. No C ABI layout changed.

Limits and verification#

Executable server commands, resource create/delete/rename edits, snippet code-action edits and writes outside the workspace remain unsupported. The existing pinned TypeScript empty acknowledgement remains the sole passive command omission; no additional command is executed. This feature enables annotated text edits from available backends, not every refactoring offered by Rider or an Unreal asset tool.

Assertions extend existing core, code-action, extension and workflow-UI test targets, with no additional runner. They cover definition/size/reference guards, effective-edit grouping, plan-specific confirmations, versioned annotated actions, apply/undo and GUI approval reset and native-plugin export/permission/read-callback guards. Current verification is MSVC /Zs plus production compilation and real SDK schema examples. Native assertions, actual backend/MCP/plugin calls, checkbox/keyboard/focus behavior, themes/densities/DPI and Linux/macOS remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky interruption. See Validation.

pages.title: Test, package and workflow presets
pages.html:
Test, package and workflow presets#

View > CMake preset actions opens the secondary panel. Build and the command palette also expose CMake test/package/workflow presets. Select a workspace source directory and preset, preview its steps, then run the reviewed preset. Inspection does not invoke CMake, CTest, CPack or project scripts. The action selection is transient; panel visibility uses the existing workspace session metadata, while the ordinary saved build profile remains separate.

The preview shows the linked configure preset, binary directory, configurations, ordered steps, declared output paths and process deadline. CPack retains multiple configurations. Public paths remain workspace-relative. Ordinary configure/build selectors and the successful saved build profile keep their existing ownership.

Kind Native command Prerequisite
Test ctest --preset NAME Matching configured binary tree; command needs CMake/CTest 3.20+
Package cpack --preset NAME Matching configured binary tree and project packaging setup; CMake/CPack 3.25+
Workflow cmake --workflow --preset NAME Configure first, then build/test/package steps linked to that same configure preset; CMake 3.25+

The installed tools must also support the file schema and chosen options. Conditions, filters, dependencies, generators and project/package commands remain owned by the real tools. References: official presets, workflows, CTest and CPack.

Metadata and review#

The existing native reader now loads all five preset families. It retains hidden bases, local includes, earlier-parent inheritance, environment/cache/output/ CPack-variable maps and defining-file macro origins. Action environments insert configure variables after inherited action variables and before explicit action variables. Workflows have no inheritance/hidden mode; all step references must be visible from their defining file and use the initial configure preset.

Includes, binary roots, explicit CTest log/JUnit paths, CPack config paths and declared package directories pass the workspace resolver. In-source/ancestor binary roots and caches belonging to another source tree are refused. Complex conditional availability remains a CMake execution check; the selector does not evaluate every condition or project-defined output.

Execution requires expectedRevision from the preview. The token covers loaded preset contents, root-file presence and the normalized plan. New/changed/deleted root or included preset files require another preview. Snapshots are checked before and after execution. This is an optimistic concurrency check, not authentication or a freeze of sources, process environment and installed tools. Filesystem races are not a transaction.

Bounds: 64 files / 8 MiB source metadata, 512 entries per family, 64 JSON/ inheritance levels, 256 KiB per resolved preset / 16 MiB combined, 16 MiB public catalogue, 2 MiB plans, 64 workflow steps, 64 CPack configurations and 32 KiB path expansion. Invalid paths, steps and limits produce explicit errors.

Execution and cancellation#

The common BuildOperations reservation owns build.presetRun alongside ordinary CMake/MSBuild/Unreal work. The adapter uses argv and the source directory as cwd; CTest/CPack infer their binary tree from the native preset. Companion tools are selected beside detected CMake when present, then through the usual tool resolver.

Workspace buffers must be saved. The GUI retains the preview if saving is cancelled. Cancel build, app closing and SDK cancellation signal the same correlated operation ID; process-tree ownership and the reservation remain until native work stops. The main deadline covers the whole workflow: 180 seconds for direct calls, the configured desktop value in the GUI, or a 1–86,400 second override. Tool discovery retains separate bounded probes. Output is capped at 8 MiB.

No fresh/force-clean option is added. Failure/cancellation can leave compiled files, reports, packages and completed steps. There is no automatic rollback, deletion or invented per-step success parsed from console text. Successful workflows can refresh existing File API/C++ analysis for the last explicit build configuration without replacing the saved profile. A later metadata/snapshot failure is returned as inspectionError separately from the actual process result.

Project/test/package scripts are trusted executable code. Guards cover known metadata fields, not every output a script or generator might create. Configured CTest's structured test tree remains separate; this view returns preset output, not a fabricated per-test tree or installer artifact browser.

Shared SDK and plugins#

build_preset_plan accepts source (default "."), kind (test/package/workflow) and preset; it is read-only. build_preset_run additionally requires expectedRevision, accepts timeoutSeconds and requires process.execute plus the existing SDK workspace-mutations group. Callers cannot supply arbitrary commands/arguments. The real SDK owns jobs, identities, permissions and cancellation.

Native plugins export build.presetPlan/run through the existing JSON host request and process permission. No C ABI layout, CyUI module or Python process/parser implementation is added. Paths remain persistent workspace references.

pages.title: Commands and keyboard profiles
pages.html:
Commands and keyboard profiles#

View > Application updates opens the installation update view; Check for updates is also available there and through Find Action, with no new default shortcut. Startup checking is configurable and enabled by default. A newer stable release gets an EN/FR proposal with Later and Skip this version. Download and Install update and restart are separate actions; the latter uses the existing document save/discard/cancel close flow. Native test/smoke sessions disable I/O and handoff. See Application updates.

Navigate / Find Action includes Highlight occurrences at caret (Rider Ctrl+Shift+F7), Next/Previous reported occurrence and Clear occurrence highlights. Edit includes Select reported occurrences; View > Occurrences opens its dockable inspector. Other profiles/actions have no new default binding. Existing F3 find and lexical occurrence selection are unchanged. All action availability is tied to the current native report/provider. Selection rejects incomplete, overlapping, empty or oversized reports before replacing cursors. See Document occurrences for source references and scope differences.

Navigate adds Go to declaration, Go to type definition and Go to implementation, using the real backend capability. The Rider defaults add Ctrl+Shift+B for type and Ctrl+Alt+B for implementation; Ctrl+F9 remains build and the former extra Ctrl+Shift+B build alias is removed to avoid a conflict. VS/VS Code add Ctrl+F12 for implementation. Declaration and other missing defaults remain assignable. The References dock adds shared filtering, cyclic keyboard/result selection, Enter/click activation, Copy locations and Refresh at caret; stale source/backend snapshots remain inspectable but do not navigate. See Source navigation for source references and limits.

View > Structure opens a dockable persistent panel without a new default shortcut. Rider/Visual Studio/VS Code member/symbol bindings and @/# palette prefixes remain. Structure row clicks or focused-row Enter use existing source/history navigation; disclosure arrows keep tree behavior. The symbol/type/everywhere palette can select one available enabled server, including contributed IDs; document members always follow their own backend. Picker navigation does not activate a result. URI-only symbol rows display “Location on selection”; click/Enter waits in the palette for a current resolved position. Progress/errors remain visible. Refresh symbols creates a new request ticket even with unchanged text. Query/server/mode/selection changes or popup dismissal discard obsolete resolution replies; existing bindings remain. See Symbol navigation.

Previous/Next diagnostic commands now navigate reported workspace or current-file locations with the Problems text/severity filters and wrap behavior. Unverified positions in open documents are retained for inspection/copy and excluded from navigation. The selected message has its own detail card. Rider uses F2/Shift+F2 in file and Alt+F2/Alt+Shift+F2 across reported locations; Visual Studio/VS Code use F8/Shift+F8 for the latter, keeping VS Code F2 for Rename. CyUI icon controls and guarded document opening share the same model. See Diagnostic navigation for scope and pending acceptance.

The command catalogue is shared by menus, keyboard dispatch and the action palette. Run > Run to cursor resumes once toward a verified destination in the active saved workspace document. It keeps existing breakpoints/exceptions and restores the original source list on the next actual stop. Rider uses Alt+F9 and Visual Studio Ctrl+F10; VS Code has no new default binding and custom bindings retain priority. Run > Restore source breakpoints is an explicit recovery action, available only with a confirmed pause and settled replies. See Run to cursor for guards and pending real-adapter/GUI acceptance.

Run > Step back / Continue backward / Restart selected frame are capability-gated commands with user-assignable shortcuts and no new default binding. Debugger > Execution controls sets the common stepping granularity and selected-thread mode; existing step shortcuts and Continue use those same native options/context guards. Frame restart is an explicit program action, separate from document Undo. See Execution controls for capabilities and pending acceptance.

Run > Choose step-in target opens the Debugger target list and reads actual adapter choices for the selected paused frame. Select a function explicitly, then use Step into selected target; ordinary Step into keeps its existing behavior. The new query command has no default binding and can receive a custom shortcut. See Targeted step-in for captured context and pending acceptance.

Run > Set next statement queries destinations in the selected frame source and opens the Next statement tab. Reading/selecting a destination does not move the instruction pointer; Set next statement here is a separate explicit action. It skips intervening code and does not run to the cursor. No default shortcut is added; see Set next statement for pending adapter/GUI acceptance.

Run > Apply Java code changes / Cancel Java reload use the same catalogue and native JDT/DAP service. They have no assigned shortcut by default; keyboard preferences can bind them. Application is manual and requires an active Java session with correctly imported JDT sources/output. See Java debugging. Navigate > Call hierarchy / Type hierarchy and View > Hierarchy now use the same catalogue. Rider uses Ctrl+Alt+H / Ctrl+H, Visual Studio Ctrl+Alt+K for calls and VS Code Shift+Alt+H for calls; other bindings remain user-assignable. These inspect actual capability-gated LSP relationships with lazy navigation, not string references. See Hierarchies for scope and pending runtime acceptance. Options > Keyboard shortcuts selects Rider / ReSharper (default), Visual Studio or Visual Studio Code. --keymap rider|visualstudio|vscode overrides the startup profile. These are Windows/Linux keyboard schemes. Dedicated macOS schemes remain pending.

The user-requested bindings are present in every preset:

Shortcut Action
Ctrl+Shift+F Workspace text search
Ctrl+F Current document find/replace
Ctrl+Alt+F File name lookup
Double Shift Search Everywhere: files, actions, C++ types/symbols and members

Search Everywhere provides files, actions, recent files, C++ workspace symbols/types and current-file structure. Results are selectable with Up/Down and opened with Enter. The Actions tab or a > query searches commands; @ selects members and # symbols. Symbol results come from the live clangd index and can be incomplete while indexing. Only commands implemented by the application are registered; unavailable actions are disabled. A key binding is not an implementation of a debugger or refactoring.

The Rider profile uses Ctrl+B/F12 for definition, Alt+F7/Shift+F12 for references, Ctrl+F9 for build, Ctrl+D for duplication, Ctrl+Y for line deletion and Ctrl+Shift+Z for redo. Ctrl+Shift+N searches file names; New window is available from File or Find Action. Visual Studio/VS Code use their separate editing/navigation mappings, including Ctrl+K, Ctrl+C to comment and Ctrl+K, Ctrl+U to uncomment. Those actions are idempotent. Chords time out after 1.5 seconds and cancel on Escape or focus change. Caret movement, ordinary typing and completion are still supplied by the editor. Editor editing shortcuts do not modify a document while typing in another field.

Interactive completion snippets have contextual Tab/Shift+Tab parameter navigation and Escape to finish, in all three profiles. Ctrl+Space leaves the snippet and requests a fresh completion. These contextual widget keys are currently fixed; the parameter badge shows them and a choice field offers its alternatives in a dropdown. See Languages for mirror behavior and current limits.

The catalogue also provides document close/reopen, save, undo/redo, clipboard, duplication/deletion/movement, indentation, comments, selection growth, occurrences, case conversion, whitespace trimming, go to line, recent files, navigation history, tab switching, folding, view toggles, panels, builds and refresh commands. Saves and closures retain revision/conflict/unsaved-document checks.

Semantic commands use actual language services:

Action Rider Visual Studio VS Code
Types Ctrl+N Ctrl+1, Ctrl+T Types tab
Symbols Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N Ctrl+1, Ctrl+S Ctrl+T
File structure Ctrl+F12 Ctrl+1, Ctrl+M Ctrl+Shift+O
Rename symbol Shift+F6 Ctrl+R, Ctrl+R F2
Format document Ctrl+Alt+L Ctrl+K, Ctrl+D Shift+Alt+F
Format selection Ctrl+Alt+Shift+L Ctrl+K, Ctrl+F Ctrl+K, Ctrl+F
Quick fixes / context actions Alt+Enter Ctrl+. or Alt+Enter Ctrl+.

Context actions use the live cursor/selection and actual server proposals. The Code actions panel offers filtering, arrow selection, Enter/Apply correction and Preview changes. Unsupported actions show a reason. Apply edits unsaved buffers; refactoring undo and explicit saving retain the native revision/disk guards.

Rename opens a multi-file preview before applying; Apply refactoring and Undo refactoring are also executable through Find Action. Applying changes preserves the originating editor and loads affected documents as unsaved buffers. Formatting uses the project's .clang-format and normal editor undo. SDK tabs are read-only and disable editing/refactoring commands. See Semantic editing for limits.

Select an action in the keyboard settings to edit its bindings. Separate alternatives with ;, and chord strokes with , (for example Ctrl+K, Ctrl+C; Ctrl+Slash). An empty list disables the binding. Duplicate or ambiguous prefix bindings are rejected while retaining the previous valid map. Settings keep overrides separately for each profile. Reset command/profile restores defaults. Menus/tooltips use the selected bindings.

The presets cover implemented commands. Remaining Rider functionality is tracked in Roadmap; full Rider, Visual Studio and VS Code feature parity is not claimed.

Primary references used to establish the schemes: Rider predefined keymaps, Visual Studio shortcuts, VS Code keybindings.

pages.title: Compiler output source links
pages.html:
Compiler output source links#

The Build panel's live and final logs reuse CyUI Diagnostics. Clicking a row with a recognized source location opens that file through the normal guarded document service. Ordinary rows remain selectable. Opening a source does not edit it, replace its buffer, save it or add an Undo transaction.

The native build.location service is also exported through the existing ABI2 JSON host callback and SDK/MCP operation build_location. It receives supplied text only, needs no permissions or mutation group, runs no compiler and reads no source contents. Retrieving compiler output still requires process.execute. No new dependency, CyUI module, C ABI or executable target is introduced.

json
{"text":"src/main.cpp(42,7): error C2065: missing identifier","directory":"."}

Successful results contain mapped:true, a workspace path, one-based line and column, format (parentheses or colon) and an empty reason. An ordinary unmapped line returns mapped:false and a reason without coordinates. Invalid requests raise an error. The working directory defaults to the workspace root and must already exist inside the workspace.

Recognized forms include explicit file(line,column):, file(line):, file:line:column:, file:line: and Rust --> file:line:column / ::: .... Quoted paths, spaces, UTF-8 filenames, Windows drive letters, numeric MSBuild 1> prefixes and GLSL ERROR: / WARNING: file prefixes are supported. Numeric GLSL source IDs such as ERROR: 0:12: have no file mapping. The parser is bounded to one 16 KiB UTF-8 line; NUL, newline and other controls except tab/CR are rejected. Line numbers are bounded to 10 million and columns to 1 million.

Only an existing regular file inside the current workspace can map. Missing, external, symlink-escaping, drive-relative and URI paths are not source links. Paths are checked again when opening. No basename search or guessed directory is used: live project logs use their validated recorded task directory; native live logs and combined final logs use the workspace root. Relative paths emitted from an unrecorded subdirectory can therefore remain unmapped.

Compiler columns are reported coordinates. Their byte/display/Unicode conventions vary by tool; exact Unicode columns, ANSI/terminal decoding, source maps, caret inference and external SDK links are not implemented here. Compiler lines are last-run observations, not proof of the current source revision. This parser does not replace structured compiler diagnostics or LSP UTF-16 conversion.

Regression source joins the existing opt-in build fixture: formats, nested working directories, quoted/Unicode/absolute names, missing/external/symlink paths, bad numbers, controls and request bounds. Sources pass MSVC /Zs only. Actual native filesystem/parser execution, row activation, focus, Unicode columns, themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending under the Kaspersky test suspension. See Validation.

pages.title: C# language services
pages.html:
C# language services#

CyCode routes C# documents to Roslyn through csharp-ls and C/C++ to clangd. Each backend has its own owner thread, process and queue; both use the same native Engine documents, revisions, edit transactions and bounded LSP transport. The GUI starts a server when a supported document is opened. It passes the selected .sln explicitly; direct .csproj workspaces use server discovery. Project references, references restored by the .NET SDK and unsaved open documents feed semantic results. For the pinned C# backend, didOpen starts lazy workspace loading after initialization; the server serializes these notifications and retains their overlays. Semantic queries wait for its loading progress to finish. The initialize response alone does not mean Roslyn has loaded the workspace. Unsaved documents are replayed on restart.

The local package is checksum-pinned csharp-ls 0.28.0, targeting .NET 10, with a private .NET SDK 10.0.403 under runtime/tools/csharp-dotnet. build.py or scripts/setup_csharp.py installs both only under this project. The SDK archive has its official SHA-512 locked per platform; the server package has a locked SHA-256. No global dotnet tool or SDK is installed or changed. Builds retain their existing MSBuild/dotnet selection. The project's own target SDK/targeting packs and restored dependencies must be available; the private analysis SDK does not replace every SDK requested by global.json. Exact URLs/hashes and upstream source are in language-tools.lock.json. CYCODE_CSHARP_LS can select an absolute server executable or DLL; CYCODE_CSHARP_DOTNET can select its absolute .NET host. Missing components and project-load failures appear in Problems.

The desktop uses the ordinary completion menu, definition/reference navigation, type/symbol search and file structure, Shift+F6 rename preview/apply/undo and document/selection formatting commands. Workspace symbol search follows the active document's language. Rename edits are prepared by Roslyn, then validated and applied to live buffers by Engine; Save all remains explicit. C# formatting uses Roslyn and .editorconfig. Revision changes during a query reject stale results.

Starting a C# server evaluates trusted MSBuild projects/imports. A native CLI/MCP Engine keeps C# disabled until language_configure is called with process.execute. Reading documents or language_status does not enable it. The desktop's normal language-service activation and Restart language server action enable both backends; capture-only mode starts neither. language_configure accepts enabled and an optional executable and affects only the current process. An enabled server starts lazily on an open C# document/request. It can be disabled or restarted without losing buffers.

MCP operations language_complete, language_definition/references/document_symbols, language_rename and language_format select a backend from the document extension. language_symbols accepts language=cpp (default) or csharp. language_status includes servers.cpp/servers.csharp and merged diagnostics. Completion returns standard LSP items; coordinates are zero-based UTF-16, including supplementary characters. The GUI filters Roslyn items against the typed prefix and tracks editor transactions after popup insertion, so accepting a suggestion immediately updates the shared live buffer and dirty revision. The shared issued-item resolve/prepare path handles server-provided additional imports and interactive numbered snippet parameters. Symbol/import insertion forms one undoable editor transaction; linked fields use the shared snippet session. Arbitrary server commands remain unsupported. See Languages. Server requests to apply workspace edits are refused: use the revision-checked preview/apply API. No C# server metadata URI grants arbitrary filesystem access.

Roslyn semantic tokens now augment the ordinary lexical colorizer through the same revision-checked language_highlight service used for C++. Cross-project C# semantic colors are exercised in a hidden native desktop; no separate editor model is used. Edits/restarts discard old spans while lexical colors remain immediately available.

Each backend allows 32 outstanding requests. C# has a 60-second request deadline, including project loading; C++ retains 15 seconds. Framed messages, stderr and queues are bounded. Process-tree shutdown is tied to workspace/IDE shutdown, disable and restart. Filesystem watchers/dynamic registration are not implemented; restore/build the project, then restart the server after changing project references or SDKs.

Managed run/debug uses NetCoreDbg through the shared native DAP service, including portable PDB source breakpoints, conditions, locals, objects/arrays, watches, evaluation, stepping and attach/detach. Select the built executable assembly from MSBuild evaluated artifacts and use the ordinary Debugger panel and Rider bindings. See Execution for the tested .NET 8 scope and adapter limitations.

The shared code-action service now routes advertised Roslyn edit-only fixes and lazy resolution through native previews, apply and undo. Server commands and resource operations remain unsupported; broader Roslyn action acceptance is pending.

Remaining work includes complete Roslyn action coverage, snippet variables/transforms and a user catalogue, rich documentation rendering, metadata decompilation/source-generated views, Razor, test discovery and broader framework/SDK/project-load coverage. External project files outside the workspace remain outside editable document permissions. Windows is validated locally; Linux/macOS execution remains unverified.

Documentation/signature requests and the Code information panel share the native language service and MCP. csharp-ls 0.28.0 omits its active parameter after the last comma; CyCode preserves that as unknown and still shows actual overloads/parameters. See Languages. Current GUI acceptance remains pending; compilation and native/MCP results are recorded separately.

Reproduce with scripts/build.py, private Python's test_mcp.py suite, then scripts/verify_csharp.py and scripts/verify_csharp.py --preview-only. Tests use owned workspaces, two .NET 8 projects and the locally installed target SDK/packs; they restore with empty NuGet package sources and leave source files unsaved.

pages.title: Adding a revision-control provider
pages.html:
Adding a revision-control provider#

CyCode's provider boundary is independent of Git, SVN, Perforce, Mercurial and Diversion. The owner's future revision-control system can use that same boundary once its protocol is defined; no implementation or protocol for it is invented here. A provider does not have to imitate Git commands, staging or remotes.

Implement a native ABI2 plugin against PluginAPI.h. The bundled Diversion adapter is a concrete example of registering a vcs contribution and calling an existing CLI through the shared native process owner. Its client/descriptor remains free of CyUI, ImGui and Engine. An adapter can instead use its own SDK/service, retaining application path, data, persistence and process ownership rules.

Descriptor and result contract#

Use an independent stable plugin ID, provider ID, contribution/action IDs and local library basename. Declare only implemented capabilities. For example, a system that publishes changes and manages file leases can describe its own actions:

json
{  "id":"example.revisions.provider", "title":"Example revisions",  "capabilities":["status","diff","log","publish","lease.acquire"],  "actions":[    {"id":"diff","title":"Working differences","scope":"repository","fields":[]},    {"id":"log","title":"Revision history","scope":"repository","fields":[]},    {"id":"publish","title":"Publish changes","scope":"repository",     "fields":[{"id":"message","title":"Description","required":true}]},    {"id":"lease.acquire","title":"Acquire file lease","scope":"file","fields":[]}  ]}

This is a documentation example, not a registered provider or simulated backend. The host generates provider menus/forms and palette actions from the descriptor. Labels require English/French translations; IDs remain stable and untranslated. Fields are bounded text inputs with optional default/required. File actions receive the active document path. Providers can contribute separate native model panels, commands and event subscriptions for advanced workflows beyond these forms; see Plugins and Events for the implemented limits.

Callbacks receive {action, parameters}. The host owns the injected absolute workspace and workspace-relative root; validated file path stays within that mapping. Validate again against the backend's own repository/client/workspace identity. An independent ID/protocol must never cause an unimplemented operation to fall back to Git. Return a nonempty JSON error on failure, or preserve the native operation's exitCode/output/timedOut/truncated/cancelled metadata.

status returns at least:

json
{"provider":"example.revisions.provider","repository":true,"branch":"main", "files":[{"status":"M","path":"Game/Source/Main.cpp"}],"message":""}

path values are workspace-relative, not backend IDs, URLs or temporary artifacts. Additional backend metadata can be returned without inventing Git state. diff returns a unified patch in output, consumed by the common CyUI Diff view; log and blame return read-only Review text. Unsupported binary/conflict/history representations require an explicit panel/contract rather than fabricated text.

Routing, permissions and lifetime#

Installed plugins are loaded from application extension locations. A project selects a provider using revision-checked .cycode/vcs.json root mappings; the deepest matching root drives native GUI/CLI/MCP routes. Explicit selection is also available. The built-in default stays Git. An unavailable mapped provider remains unavailable until reenabled/reinstalled or explicitly remapped.

Generic MCP access uses vcs_provider_action; its conservative permissions include plugins.execute, process.execute, workspace.write and vcs.write. Typed Git SDK methods keep their existing Git-only schemas and permission boundaries. Recognized read actions are status/inspect/diff/log/history/show/blame. Other action IDs are conservatively treated as mutations, including custom read-like actions until a versioned access contract exists. They therefore also receive dirty-buffer/disk-baseline guards and reconciliation. This limitation is explicit.

The versioned C ABI transports UTF-8 JSON and callbacks, without STL/ImGui objects or cross-library allocators. Calls are serial, outputs are plugin-owned until the next invocation and exceptions must be caught before returning across the ABI. Activation/dependency/version/platform checks and disable/shutdown ownership apply to VCS providers just as to other extensions. Native plugins are trusted code; the ABI is not a process sandbox. Process-wide application data belongs to the host, and backend history/Undo/persistence semantics belong to the backend.

Acceptance for a future adapter#

Specify read/write operations, repository identity, exact path encoding, conflict states, authentication, background work and cancellation before exporting actions. Use argv with bounded owned children for CLI integration; never shell-concatenate project input. Validate complete metadata before a destructive or broad operation. Document which commands change disk, publish remotely or schedule asynchronous work. Do not imply that stopping a waiter cancels accepted server work.

Runner/ABI regressions should cover actual backend contracts, path identities, partial/error responses, dirty-buffer protection, routing and lifecycle; real-client and GUI acceptance must be recorded separately. Current local validation follows Testing: source checks and production builds only during the antivirus interruption. Windows production compilation does not validate Linux/macOS.

pages.title: CyCode modular CyUI integration
pages.html:
CyCode modular CyUI integration#

CyCode now consumes the shared editor API at the exact commit in app/editor-source.lock.json and CyUI at the exact commit in app/cyui-source.lock.json. The Reader application itself is not compiled. Neither developer checkout is modified by configuration or compilation.

Modules and migrated views#

Module CyCode use
Core Existing themes, fonts, icons, docking, notifications; shared locale catalogues and filters for menus, project files, diagnostics and settings
Code / CodeEditor Editable documents, read-only SDK/debugger sources, Git source versions, project-template source previews and wrapped refactoring previews; common 101-mode syntax catalogue including HLSL, GLSL and logs; version-checked diagnostic squiggles through the existing native annotation hook
Diff Unified/split Git review and refactoring comparisons, synchronized scrolling, inline differences and hunk navigation
Commands Action palette with stable command IDs and keyboard navigation; common ranking plus the IDE's abbreviation matching inside Search Everywhere
Diagnostics Bounded build output with shared log severity classification, filtering and follow; build/LSP problem list and source navigation
DocumentViews Native Markdown documentation from language servers; literal code sections use Code and plain text remains literal
Inspector General settings with stable property IDs, validation, drafts and commit/cancel phases
Images / Canvas Read-only image tabs with transparency, fit/zoom/pan and reload; the application owns decoding and GPU resources
Assets Lazy physical file/folder browser, common selection/filter/grid/list/navigation and action requests; native Engine owns preview/apply/undo and persistent project trash

The IDE retains its project/symbol search tabs, asynchronous symbol requests, keymaps, document permissions/revisions, multi-file refactoring transactions, LSP/DAP/Unreal services, SDK/MCP bridge, Git actions, project configuration and persistence. Its portable file icons remain shared with Reader. Native plugin contracts continue to use their existing C ABI; no ImGui/STL objects cross it. The app's Graphite theme is a shared palette adaptation, not a second widget set.

The old raw TextEditor-owned document/preview views, local refactoring marker renderer, unstructured build-output textarea, diagnostic rows and settings form have been replaced. Every native editor now belongs to CyUI::CodeEditor. Native hooks remain necessary for Unreal completion, Tree-sitter/LSP overlays, snippets, breakpoint gutters and guarded external buffer replacements. Those services and their Undo history have not moved into CyUI.

Dependency/build contract#

sh
python app/scripts/fetch_dependencies.pypython app/scripts/build.py --no-install

The default CyUI source is a separate commit-specific cache under runtime/deps. Alternatively pass --cyui PATH for a clean Git checkout matching the lock. --editor-root PATH explicitly selects a development Reader checkout with shared source API 1. Production uses the pinned Reader source. During local validation that Reader commit was obtained from the owner's local Git repository. Its remote availability was not verified or changed. A fresh machine needs read access to the exact dependency commits; the explicit local checkout option remains available while those commits are unpublished.

CyCode validates its own newer CyUI lock before selecting the shared editor's explicit host-source mode (CYCODE_CYUI_DEVELOPMENT). This does not relax the host's revision or cleanliness checks. Reader's standalone lock remains intact. Direct CMake configuration performs the same validation.

CYCODE_EDITOR_UI_MODULES is set before the shared editor's add_subdirectory; that provider sets CYUI_MODULES before adding CyUI. The app links explicit CyUI::<Module> targets. Audio, Gallery, Demo, CEF and library tests are disabled; Canvas is selected automatically by Images. Plots/Nodes/Timeline/Assets/Viewport/Web are not required. Dependencies between the selected modules are resolved by CyUI.

One host cycode_imgui target (Dear ImGui >= 1.92) is supplied through CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET. One cyui_texteditor backend serves all app and library views. The shared adapter prepares its advanced hooks in the build directory; it never changes upstream sources. The obsolete standalone TextEditor archive is no longer a dependency. Tree-sitter and its grammars remain required for richer language overlays. Lexilla/Scintilla are selected by Code for the built-in syntax catalogue. The native core/CLI/file services still compile without any UI dependency. C++20 is required by CodeEditor; platform backends remain SDL3/OpenGL.

Preserved interactions and limits#

Settings change only on commit. Filtering, closing or collapsing the settings window cancels active drafts. Loading a configuration advances the model revision. Menu IDs and problem destinations do not depend on translated labels or filtered row indices. Ctrl/Cmd+F belongs to the focused filter panel; the document editor keeps its own find/replace. Ctrl+Shift+F keeps the IDE workspace search binding. Search Everywhere retains files, actions, types, symbols, members and recent files.

Diff does not implement editable three-way merges or file writes. CyCode retains its three read-only conflict versions and guarded working-document resolution. Diff also has no wrapped split renderer; the refactoring view retains a selectable wrapped CodeEditor presentation. Its bounded comparison can be approximate on large inputs; full before/after buffers remain available.

DocumentViews implements a Markdown subset, not HTML/CommonMark or a browser. Links emitted by language-server documentation remain inert. Literal code is sent directly to Code so fence syntax and all catalogue languages survive this subset's limits. Large sections have their own scrollable view. No CEF engine is added.

Diagnostics is not an interactive terminal emulator. CyCode's bounded libvterm grid, PTY processes, ANSI input, selection, clipboard and shell key ownership stay in its terminal adapter. General project/debug/plugin panels with specialized service interactions retain Core widgets rather than being forced into generic properties. The migration does not add new LSP or debugger backends.

Validation#

ui_modules exercises the actual app adapters and views with headless ImGui frames, without SDL/native windows: editing/Undo/Redo and explicit save through Engine, catalogue selection, filtering/draft cancellation, diagnostics identities, log severities and action dispatch. View checks cover six themes, both densities, 100/150/200% DPI and English/French. This verifies generated drawing data and interactions; it is not a native desktop screenshot/renderer acceptance test.

See Validation.md for the executed build/test results. Windows/MSVC is the local validation platform. Linux/macOS builds and native multi-monitor acceptance have not been executed for this migration. No application window is opened or old quarantined executable restored by the headless checks. Release validation and publication are tracked separately in the project changelog and Validation.md.

pages.title: Data breakpoints
pages.html:
Data breakpoints#

Debugger > Data breakpoints uses the common native DAP owner, SDK and ABI2 host exports. It requires the active adapter's supportsDataBreakpoints capability; no support is inferred from a language or project type. Actual adapter/hardware/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Validation.

Desktop workflow#

Pause the program, select a stack frame, then enter a variable/expression using Selected stack frame, or a child name within a displayed variable scope. Inspect data breakpoint target requests actual dataBreakpointInfo. Its description explains the target or why it is unavailable. Choose an advertised read/write mode or Adapter default, which omits accessType on the wire instead of inventing a write fallback. Conditions/hit conditions require their capabilities.

Add every desired inspected target to the Replacement list, then Replace data breakpoints. This replaces the entire list rather than appending implicitly. Rows can be removed locally; New replacement list discards the draft and captures the latest configuration revision. Clear data breakpoints submits an empty list. All mutations require a paused target and actual adapter support.

The status table retains the adapter's verified flag/message, including refused targets and hardware limits. Changed/removed breakpoint events update verification. A data-breakpoint stop uses the common stack, variables and stepping views.

Native and SDK contract#

Both operations require process.execute and observed sessionGeneration / stopGeneration from debug_status:

  • debug_data_breakpoint_info / debug.dataBreakpointInfo: name plus optional positive variablesReference from a current scope. Without a container, the owner supplies the selected frameId. Caller-supplied frame IDs/range flags/raw dataId are not accepted. Output: available, issued id, name/description, accessTypes, canPersist and both generations. A null adapter dataId returns available:false.
  • debug_data_breakpoints / debug.dataBreakpoints: complete breakpoints array (empty clears), expectedRevision from debug_status.dataBreakpointRevision and both generations. Entries use an issued id and optional advertised accessType, condition and hitCondition. Output includes actual dataBreakpoints, dataBreakpointRevision and dataBreakpointsSynchronized.

Example after actual status/inspection calls (replace these illustrative values):

json
{  "breakpoints": [{"id": "data-3-1", "accessType": "write"}],  "sessionGeneration": 3,  "stopGeneration": 7,  "expectedRevision": 4}

Raw adapter IDs remain private to the registry/wire plan. Bounds: 128 handles and 1 MiB of stored text payload per pause, 32 replacement entries, 64 KiB info replies, 512 KiB verification replies and bounded names/messages. Duplicate targets, unadvertised modes and unknown/expired handles are rejected before mutation.

Lifetime and failure#

Resume, another stop, DAP invalidation, termination and disconnect expire inspection handles. Already installed targets can survive resume and remain visible. Inspect every desired target again at a later pause before submitting a new full list. canPersist is adapter metadata: CyCode keeps data targets within this session and does not save or restore them through launch.json.

An expectedRevision guard rejects an older draft. Before submitting replacement, the owner marks the list unsynchronized. Timeout, rejection, malformed verification or a changed pause may leave target-side effects; the old list is retained only as the last known configuration with dataBreakpointsSynchronized=false. Re-inspect and replace/clear while paused to establish a new confirmed list. The operation has no Undo or cancellation once submitted; the SDK retains its native outcome rather than discarding a mutation due to a late cancellation token. Inspection can involve target expression evaluation. No target/server is restarted or installed.

See the upstream DAP contract. Address/range/mode controls, automatic re-resolution and persisted targets remain separate work. New regression assertions were compiled with /Zs, not executed. Real native/.NET/JVM, MCP/plugin, hardware, keyboard/theme/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain unexecuted while native tests are suspended after antivirus removals.

pages.title: Stepping, reverse execution and frame restart
pages.html:
Stepping, reverse execution and frame restart#

The Debugger Execution controls tab and Run commands share the existing native DAP worker with SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugin requests. DebugExecution validates plans and acknowledgements without UI dependencies. No target process owner, recording engine, CyUI module or external dependency is added.

Desktop controls#

Pause the program and select its thread. Stepping granularity offers Adapter default, Statement, Source line and Machine instruction when supportsSteppingGranularity is advertised. Default omits the wire field. Only selected thread requires supportsSingleThreadExecutionRequests; otherwise the normal adapter behavior applies. Unavailable options reset on status polling. These settings are local to this application instance and are not saved in launch.json.

The existing Step over / Step into / Step out shortcuts use those options too. Continue uses the thread option and never receives a stepping granularity. Run > Step back, Continue backward and Restart selected frame also appear in the action palette and can receive user-defined keyboard bindings. They have no new default shortcut that would replace an existing Rider/VS/VS Code binding.

Step back and Continue backward require supportsStepBack. The external debugger must actually support the required execution history. CyCode does not emulate reverse execution through document Undo or repeated launches. Restart selected frame requires supportsRestartFrame, a current inspected selected frame and canRestart other than false. It sends one restartFrame request and uses the actual subsequent stopped event. It does not issue an automatic stepIn or restart the VM. Re-executing code can repeat its I/O and other effects; it does not undo them.

Last execution request distinguishes submission, adapter acknowledgement and an unconfirmed outcome. When supplied, the actual allThreadsContinued value remains visible, including false. The current host still uses one selected execution context: independent simultaneous inspection of every suspended thread while other threads run is not implemented by these controls.

Native and SDK contracts#

All seven execution operations require process.execute. Their SDK handlers retain the native result after submission and are noncancellable. Source files and source Undo/Redo are unaffected.

SDK operation / native method Context Options
debug_continue / debug.continue optional sessionGeneration, stopGeneration, threadId singleThread
debug_next / debug.next optional same context granularity, singleThread
debug_step_in / debug.stepIn optional same context granularity, singleThread
debug_step_out / debug.stepOut optional same context granularity, singleThread
debug_step_back / debug.stepBack required sessionGeneration, stopGeneration, threadId granularity, singleThread
debug_reverse_continue / debug.reverseContinue required same context singleThread
debug_restart_frame / debug.restartFrame required sessionGeneration, stopGeneration, frameId none

For the four existing forward operations, omitted context is captured under the native queue lock when submitted. Explicit guards are preserved. New reverse/frame operations require explicit observed context, including through the plugin host. The GUI always captures its observed context for all seven commands. A changed session, pause, selected thread or selected restart frame is rejected before dispatch. Thread/frame IDs are bounded signed 32-bit references, with positive threads and nonnegative frames. A restart frame must occur in the inspected stack; its canRestart hint is respected, defaulting to true only with advertised support.

Options require their own capabilities even when an explicit singleThread=false or granularity=statement is provided. Continue/reverse Continue reject granularity; frame restart rejects thread/granularity flags. Unknown fields, arbitrary commands, targetId overrides, malformed booleans and unadvertised options are rejected. Selected-target step-in and run-to-position are separate workflows, rather than unchecked extra fields in this API.

Example after reading actual debug_status:

json
{  "sessionGeneration": 3,  "stopGeneration": 7,  "threadId": 11,  "granularity": "instruction",  "singleThread": true}

That request can be used with debug_step_back only when all three required capabilities are advertised; it does not enable recording or install a backend.

Events and uncertain results#

Optional debug_status.lastExecution records method, applying/accepted/unconfirmed status, observed session/stop generations, actual wire arguments, message and a bounded validated result. A new launch clears it. It is the last submitted attempt, not a complete execution history. Pre-dispatch validation errors can leave the previous record unchanged. Failed calls still leave their attempted outcome available through debug_status; no automatic retry is issued.

accepted means the adapter acknowledged the request. It does not manufacture a completed step, a restarted frame or target values. After acknowledgement, the original paused inspection transitions to running while awaiting real events. An actual stopped event then supplies a new inspection generation and stack. If that event arrives before the acknowledgement is consumed, it remains stopped; a late response does not overwrite that new pause. A separate execution epoch allows same-pause invalidated/memory cache events without mistaking them for a new stop. A continued or exited event also remains authoritative.

Failed, malformed or timed-out submitted requests may already have changed the target. They invalidate inspection and record unconfirmed without automatic rollback or replay. Native error state is still reported. DAP results are bounded to 64 KiB; absent optional thread-continuation reports are not fabricated. Target events, not a returned empty acknowledgement, establish the next paused state.

Verification and remaining acceptance#

Source-only MSVC /Zs checks cover native/UI code and regression assertions for legacy defaults, capabilities, context/frame changes, per-frame restart hints, granularity/thread options, acknowledgement shapes, empty/partial thread reports and immediate-stop versus same-pause-invalidation ordering. The existing module test source specifies GUI context capture and preservation of explicitly supplied guards. These assertions were compiled as syntax only, not executed or linked.

The actual CyToolsCore manifest loader and all schemas accept 180 operations. Data examples cover legacy and required contexts, field isolation, bounds, typed acknowledgement states, permissions/noncancellable handlers, plugin/menu methods and English/French labels. See Validation for production checks.

Actual CodeLLDB/NetCoreDbg/java-debug/contributed adapter capabilities, recording, frame restart behavior/side effects, mixed thread states, timeouts/late events, SDK/plugin runtime and keyboard/themes/DPI remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky native-test suspension. Linux/macOS compilation/execution remains pending. Instruction breakpoints now have a separate shared service with pending acceptance; see Instruction breakpoints. Targeted step-in now has a shared guarded catalogue and execution service with pending acceptance; see Targeted step-in. Remote/core dumps and full per-thread non-stop UI remain separate work.

Set next statement now has a separate guarded goto catalogue and pending-stop flow sharing this owner. It skips code, does not resume or run to the cursor, and accepts no stepping options. See Set next statement.

Run to cursor now uses one ordinary Continue after verifying a temporary source breakpoint and restores the original source list at the next stop. It shares this worker's execution epoch/actual acknowledgement handling, with separate lease, pending-reply and restoration guards. Real adapter/GUI acceptance is pending; see Run to cursor.

pages.title: Debugger value and memory editing
pages.html:
Debugger value and memory editing#

Paused target edits use the existing native DAP worker. Desktop views, SDK/MCP operations and ABI2 plugin host requests call the same service. Support comes from the active adapter's capabilities, rather than the file language. No additional CyUI module, external dependency, executable or debugger implementation is added.

Desktop workflow#

Right-click a value in the Variables tree or Scopes / Registers table and choose Change value. The Edit value tab retains the displayed value and lets you enter an adapter/language expression before Apply value change. An empty value is passed through, since its meaning belongs to the adapter. A readOnly presentation hint disables this action. Registers can be assigned only when the adapter exposes them as writable variables; no universal register-write API is invented.

When supportsSetExpression and evaluateName are available, assignment uses setExpression in the selected frame, as recommended by DAP. Otherwise a named child uses setVariable when supported. Edit watched expression captures the current Watch text and frame without automatically evaluating it or treating an earlier Watch result as its current value. Target expressions can invoke code. The form is discarded when its pause, frame or session changes.

In Memory, first read the target reference and offset. Enter replacement hexadecimal byte pairs, such as 00 FF 2A, under Write target memory. A preview shows old and new byte values. Write these bytes replaces a prefix of the read range; it requires enough actually readable bytes and both read/write capabilities. Changing the reference, offset or execution context requires another read. There is no implicit write on typing, focus loss or read refresh.

All changes affect the debuggee. They are separate from source-document editing and its Undo/Redo history; there is no automatic target Undo, rollback or retry.

Shared contracts#

Each operation requires process.execute and explicit positive sessionGeneration and nonnegative stopGeneration from debug_status. Native host requests require these too; target setters do not silently pin a missing stop at dispatch time. The target must still be paused in that session when the queued operation runs.

SDK operation / native method Additional input Advertised capability
debug_set_variable / debug.setVariable positive variablesReference, name, value supportsSetVariable
debug_set_expression / debug.setExpression expression, value, observed selected frameId supportsSetExpression
debug_write_memory / debug.writeMemory memoryReference, optional offset, bytes, expectedBytes supportsReadMemoryRequest and supportsWriteMemoryRequest

Names/expressions are nonempty and bounded to 4096 UTF-8 bytes, values to 8192 bytes, references to 8192 bytes; embedded NUL and unknown parameters are rejected. Frame/container references are bounded signed 32-bit values. An expression's frame must match the selected frame, rather than silently using a newly selected one. Memory accepts 1–4096 integer bytes in 0–255 and offsets within ±1 MiB. expectedBytes must have exactly the replacement length. Schema bounds validate individual arrays; native code also checks their matching lengths and live context.

Illustrative memory request, after inspecting actual status and bytes:

json
{  "sessionGeneration": 3,  "stopGeneration": 7,  "memoryReference": "adapter-issued-reference",  "offset": 0,  "expectedBytes": [1, 2, 3],  "bytes": [0, 255, 42]}

The owner reads the range again and rejects mismatched/unreadable expected bytes before submitting writeMemory with canonical base64 data and allowPartial=false. This comparison is not an atomic compare-and-swap: other target threads or actors may still change memory between requests. A second read checks the resulting bytes. Only an actual adapter-provided bytesWritten/offset is exposed; a successful reply without a byte count does not fabricate one. Malformed, oversized or inconsistent replies are rejected.

Outcomes and reference lifetime#

debug_status.lastMutation is optional until a validated attempt starts. It records method, sessionGeneration, status, message and result. It remains the last observed attempt, not a mutation history; a new launch clears it. A pre-dispatch validation failure may leave that previous record unchanged.

Status Meaning
checking Memory preflight read is pending; no write submitted yet.
applying The target setter is being submitted or awaited.
applied A valid value/type reply was acknowledged, or memory read-back matches.
partial The adapter explicitly reported fewer bytes written than requested.
rejected Memory preflight/context check prevented submitting the write.
unconfirmed A submitted operation failed, timed out, changed execution context, or could not be verified. Effects may already exist.

Value results contain actual returned value and optional type. Memory results contain requestedBytes, optional actual bytesWritten/offset, and readBackVerified only when a read-back completed. An explicit partial count remains partial even if the remaining requested bytes already happen to match. A failed call still leaves its lastMutation outcome available through debug_status.

After every validated attempt, including failure, inspection generations/caches and data-breakpoint inspection handles expire and the shared owner refreshes the paused stack/scopes. Returned setter references are validated but omitted from the published result because they would immediately expire. DAP invalidated/memory events also expire inspection. A separate execution epoch prevents a resume/new pause from being mistaken for normal same-pause cache invalidation during a setter.

SDK operations are noncancellable after submission; the bridge retains the native outcome instead of discarding it on a late cancellation token. Errors never trigger an automatic second setter, JVM restart or target rollback.

Verification and remaining acceptance#

The new pure native contract regression source belongs to the existing debugger test target; it is checked with MSVC /Zs without objects or execution. It specifies capabilities, guards, frame mismatch, readOnly preference, wire bytes/base64, partial/missing counts, malformed responses, bounds and stale-reference omission. Actual CyToolsCore manifest/schema examples check all 177 operations, typed mutation states, required context, permissions and noncancellable handlers. See Validation for production build and delivery checks.

Actual CodeLLDB/NetCoreDbg/java-debug/plugin adapters, target expression evaluation, memory protection/partial writes, timeouts/late events, concurrent clients and GUI/keyboard/themes/DPI remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky test suspension. Linux/macOS compilation and runtime acceptance remain pending. Source/data checks and successful compilation do not establish those runtime behaviors.

Status Meaning checking Memory preflight read is pending; no write submitted yet. applying The target setter is being submitted or awaited. applied A valid value/type reply was acknowledged, or memory read-back matches. partial The adapter explicitly reported fewer bytes written than requested. rejected Memory preflight/context check prevented submitting the write. unconfirmed A submitted operation failed, timed out, changed execution context, or could not be verified. Effects may already exist. Value results contain actual returned value and optional type. Memory results contain requestedBytes, optional actual bytesWritten/offset, and readBackVerified only when a read-back completed. An explicit partial count remains partial even if the remaining requested bytes already happen to match. A failed call still leaves its lastMutation outcome available through debug_status. After every validated attempt, including failure, inspection generations/caches and data-breakpoint inspection handles expire and the shared owner refreshes the paused stack/scopes. Returned setter references are validated but omitted from the published result because they would immediately expire. DAP invalidated/memory events also expire inspection. A separate execution epoch prevents a resume/new pause from being mistaken for normal same-pause cache invalidation during a setter. SDK operations are noncancellable after submission; the bridge retains the native outcome instead of discarding it on a late cancellation token. Errors never trigger an automatic second setter, JVM restart or target rollback. Verification and remaining acceptance # The new pure native contract regression source belongs to the existing debugger test target; it is checked with MSVC /Zs without objects or execution. It specifies capabilities, guards, frame mismatch, readOnly preference, wire bytes/base64, partial/missing counts, malformed responses, bounds and stale-reference omission. Actual CyToolsCore manifest/schema examples check all 177 operations, typed mutation states, required context, permissions and noncancellable handlers. See Validation for production build and delivery checks. Actual CodeLLDB/NetCoreDbg/java-debug/plugin adapters, target expression evaluation, memory protection/partial writes, timeouts/late events, concurrent clients and GUI/keyboard/themes/DPI remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky test suspension. Linux/macOS compilation and runtime acceptance remain pending. Source/data checks and successful compilation do not establish those runtime behaviors. Primary contract: DAP requests and capabilities . { "sessionGeneration": 3, "stopGeneration": 7, "memoryReference": "adapter-issued-reference", "offset": 0, "expectedBytes": [1, 2, 3], "bytes": [0, 255, 42] }

pages.title: Development workflows and language extensions
pages.html:
Development workflows and language extensions#

The native Engine owns these operations; the desktop, CLI, CyToolsCore MCP and permission-checked plugin host call the same services. No additional CyUI module or second editor implementation is introduced.

Configured CTest projects#

View > Tests and Build > Discover CTest tests inspect a configured build directory using the actual CTest --show-only=json-v1 model. The build directory and configuration come from the CMake panel. Discovery executes trusted project test definitions but does not compile or execute the listed tests.

The panel provides a name filter, labels, multi-selection, per-test results, durations and expandable output. Run selected tests and Cancel tests are also commands available to the palette and custom key bindings. The panel docks with the build tools and can become a separate native window like other panels.

tests.discover issues one current catalogue. tests.run accepts its ID and zero-based selected indices, verifies the current CTest definitions and refuses unsaved source buffers. CTest runs selected tests serially using native numeric selection, without shell interpolation. CTest fixture dependencies may execute additional setup/cleanup tests. Disabled entries are reported separately.

Limits: 5,000 discovered tests / 4 MiB JSON; 1..128 selected tests; per-test timeout 1..120 seconds (60 by default), 180 seconds for the native run including discovery; 64 KiB output per test and 2 MiB combined. Cancellation terminates the owned process tree. Output limits/timeouts/cancellation do not count as success, and entries that were not executed remain not-run. Source files and test executables remain project-owned; no task cleanup deletes them. Normal CTest logs remain in the build.

MCP operations tests_discover, tests_run, tests_cancel require process.execute. Core retains its job reservation until native execution stops. The private bridge correlates cancellation with a unique operation ID, preventing a queued cancelled job from stopping another actor's run. Native plugins can request the same services with their declared process.execute permission.

This is a CTest integration. Discovery for .NET test frameworks, Unreal Automation, Maven/Gradle and framework-specific debugging/coverage remains separate work.

Partial Git staging#

Version control > Hunks offers working-tree and staged previews for the active file. The Diff button's context menu also opens either preview. Select one or more blocks and choose Stage selected hunks or Unstage selected hunks. Rendering uses the shared CyUI Diff model and theme palette.

vcs.hunks / MCP vcs_hunks issues a read-only preview containing numbered blocks. vcs.applyHunks / vcs_apply_hunks accepts only a preview ID and issued indices; it never accepts a client-supplied patch. Apply requires vcs.write. Both operations require selecting the actual repository root. File paths remain workspace-relative for nested repositories; previews are bound to that repository's identity. Dirty/conflicted buffers, unresolved merge conflicts, changed selected-file index contents/diff, unknown/duplicate indices and expired/consumed plans are refused. Git owns the atomic index lock and validates the patch's old text. Working files are not rewritten. Temporary host-created patches are removed.

Unrelated staged files are preserved and do not invalidate the preview. The host queries only the selected index entry instead of listing an entire large repository. The newest 16 plans live for five minutes; each diff/index listing is limited to 2 MiB and 1,000 blocks. Added/deleted, binary and mode-changing files use whole-file staging. Arbitrary line selection, complex conflict handling, interactive rebase and production third-party VCS acceptance remain work items. Nested roots and linked-worktree controls are implemented with new native/GUI acceptance pending; see Git worktrees.

Search live buffers#

Global literal and regex search both prefer unsaved text over disk contents. Regex matching uses the same native ripgrep engine through private temporary numeric snapshots, with cancellation and cleanup. Original filenames/paths are mapped back into the results; project files are never saved by search.

Unsaved regex snapshots are limited to 128 buffers / 64 MiB. Exceeding that bound reports an error rather than silently excluding edits. Search output/match limits remain explicit. Literal case folding is still ASCII-oriented; regex case handling uses ripgrep. Columns remain one-based UTF-8 byte offsets.

Python and shaders#

Install optional servers without global installation or package lifecycle scripts:

sh
python app/scripts/setup_languages.py --python --glsl

The exact archives and SHA-256 values are in language-tools.lock.json: Pyright 1.1.411 (Node.js required) and GLSL Analyzer 1.7.1. The installer retains upstream package notices. GLSL archives are pinned for Windows/Linux/macOS x64 and ARM64; only Windows x64 execution has been tested.

Python .py/.pyi/.pyw uses LSP language ID python. GLSL .glsl/.vert/.frag/.geom/.tesc/.tese/.comp uses glsl. Python provides the actual Pyright completion/navigation/rename/diagnostics surface. GLSL Analyzer advertises completion, hover, definitions and formatting, but no document/workspace symbols, references, rename or semantic tokens; unavailable commands are disabled/rejected.

HLSL .hlsl/.hlsli/.fx/.fxh now has a separate configurable hlsl backend, rather than being routed through ordinary C++. Its external server is not installed or runtime-validated here. Separate typed DXC/glslang compilation is now implemented through ProjectTasks; its actual compiler/GUI acceptance is pending. GPU preview remains separate work; see Shader compilation.

Problems > Configure language server accepts a full argv JSON array and settings object, with local per-workspace persistence and session-only opt-out. See Language preferences for storage, revision guards, activation, reset/forget and shared SDK/plugin contracts. It does not execute a shell. Explicit empty arguments/settings restore the installed defaults; ordinary enable/disable/restart preserves the current argv and settings. An installed additional server starts on first file opening in the trusted desktop workspace unless its saved preference disables it. Core/MCP inspection never enables an additional server; use language_configure with process.execute. Stderr traces appear under Server log, independently from explicit protocol/initialization failures.

Upstream sources: Pyright, GLSL Analyzer.

ABI2 language-server contributions#

A trusted native plugin with process.execute may call host->contribute during initialization with kind languageServer, this UTF-8 JSON descriptor, and a null callback:

json
{  "id": "vendor.dialect.analysis",  "title": "C++ dialect analysis",  "arguments": ["clangd", "--background-index", "--header-insertion=never"],  "settings": {},  "languages": [    {"id": "cpp", "extensions": [".dialect"], "filenames": ["Dialectfile"]}  ]}

The contribution ID uses the plugin namespace; selectors cannot overlap built-in backends or another plugin. Extension/name matching folds ASCII case. LSP language IDs are separate from the plugin's backend ID. The application must supply valid project analysis flags (for example -xc++ in compile_commands.json for a dialect). Lexical fallback colors still come from the shared catalogue or a separate syntax contribution; registering a language server does not install a grammar. ${pluginDir} and ${workspace} tokens expand in argv values only, without a shell. The native host owns processes, transport, queues, live-buffer versions, completion sessions, diagnostics, semantic overlays and guarded edit transactions.

Limits: 32 plugin servers, 128 KiB per descriptor, 1..128 argv values of at most 8,192 bytes, settings at most 64 KiB; 1..32 language selectors with at most 128 extensions/names each. Registration cannot have a callback or contextual when. No process is launched by registering/inspecting the contribution. Enable through the common controls or language_configure using its namespaced backend ID.

Disabling the plugin removes routing, stops/joins its server owners and invalidates completion epochs. Reactivation creates a disabled owner and resynchronizes open documents. Unchanged definitions retain their owners. Each workspace has its own registry; no process-global extension map is modified. The binary C ABI2 layout is unchanged and no STL/ImGui object crosses its boundary.

Plugins also have read-only host requests for language.status, language.complete, language.hover, language.signature, language.definition, language.references, language.symbols, language.documentSymbols, language.highlight. language.configure requires process.execute. Existing document/resource/edit permissions continue to apply. These additions do not provide plugin DAP registration, arbitrary GPU/editor widgets, an installer or a marketplace.

pages.title: Diagnostic keyboard navigation
pages.html:
Diagnostic keyboard navigation#

Navigate and Find Action expose Next/Previous diagnostic and their current-file variants. Problems provides previous/next icon buttons with translated action and current shortcut tooltips, plus the selected source location. Navigation opens through the existing guarded document service, preserving edit/Undo ownership.

Problems also has Errors, Warnings and Information toggles. Both the list and keyboard navigation use the same severity mask and text filter. The selected diagnostic has a scrollable, wrapped detail card and Copy diagnostic action, including its complete message and location. Interface colors and dimensions come from CyUI Core; the list remains CyUI Diagnostics.

The source is the current reported build/project diagnostics and LSP publications already used by Problems. No extra analysis engine, compiler run or solution-wide index is created. Unmapped messages remain visible but cannot be navigation targets. Existing compiler coordinates and LSP UTF-16 conversion are retained; build diagnostics remain last-run observations and may refer to edited sources.

Language publications carry the native document identity and revision in language.status.diagnosticRevisions (and each server's equivalent). Every Engine sync, including reload/recovery/rename, supplies the identity. LSP wire versions increase across documents and close/reopen within one connection; replacement identities trigger didClose/didOpen even if a queued close was coalesced. Versions are reused only after the old server connection is stopped. Exhaustion stops synchronization and reports an error rather than wrapping.

Squiggles and navigation in open documents require enabled/ready servers and an explicitly versioned publication matching both live identity and revision. The Problems cache includes those document changes, not just diagnostic payloads. Unchanged frames compare borrowed diagnostic payloads instead of copying the whole catalogue; only real diagnostic/ownership/availability changes rebuild the model. During desktop Unreal analysis preparation, C++ positions are temporarily inactive. Old/unversioned positions in open documents remain visible and selectable for inspection/copy, labeled Position not verified, but do not navigate. Inactive server entries are similarly retained without navigation. Closed-file reports are advisory positions and can still open the file, subject to workspace guards; their position is labeled unverified. Build reports are labeled Last build result. This does not transform ranges or infer freshness for unversioned servers.

Both directions honor the Problems filter and wrap. Workspace navigation follows the filtered Problems order. Current-file navigation sorts mapped entries by line/column; without a selected entry it starts at the current editor line in the requested direction, then wraps. Subsequent steps cycle stable selected IDs. A removed or filtered-out selection is resolved against the new candidate list. Closing/switching workspaces clears selection and cached Problems state.

CyCode profile Current file Reported workspace locations
Rider F2 / Shift+F2 Alt+F2 / Alt+Shift+F2
Visual Studio Available through commands/custom bindings F8 / Shift+F8
VS Code Available through commands/custom bindings F8 / Shift+F8

VS Code F2 retains Rename. Existing keyboard overrides remain in the same keymap store. Bindings follow the relevant defaults documented by JetBrains, its current-file navigation guide, Visual Studio and VS Code. The candidate/severity scopes above describe CyCode's current implementation, not full inspection parity with those IDEs.

The selected editor destination and Problems header are updated. CyUI's current diagnosticList API returns clicked IDs but exposes no programmatic selected-row or scroll-to-row input. That list limitation is retained explicitly instead of copying a divergent diagnostic widget into the app.

Source assertions specify severity/text filtering and cache changes, non-current positions, unmapped entries, wrapping, file ordering, line anchors, keymap/rename preservation and LSP close/reopen identity/version lifetimes. They are syntax-checked only under the Kaspersky suspension. Actual keyboard/mouse, Unicode destinations, focus, themes/DPI and Linux/macOS behavior remain unverified; see Validation.
