pages.title: Diversion provider
pages.html:
Diversion provider#

The bundled native ABI2 extension cycode.diversion contributes cycode.diversion.provider. Enable it in Extensions, choose Diversion in Version control and map the exact directory containing .diversion/. Git remains the default for unmapped projects. Install Diversion separately, log in and clone/init with its own client before using this provider. Tool discovery checks an absolute CYCODE_DV, managed tool locations and PATH; CyCode does not redistribute the CLI or collect credentials. No dependency or API subscription is added to the build.

Operations#

Diversion tracks working changes and synchronizes through its own agent. There is no staging area or push/pull action. The provider follows the documented agent workflow and uses dv subcommands, never its interactive shell. Mapping/refresh does not invoke init, clone, login, browser launch, preference changes or an explicit write command. The installed client's normal network/agent behavior remains in effect.

The ten menu actions use the existing common provider forms and Review views:

Action Behavior
diff Working-copy patch through shared CyUI Diff, with color disabled. Native requests can select one file.
log / history Read-only CLI history, default 50 and maximum 200 records, ISO dates; optional exact local file operand. No structured commit fields are guessed from display text.
blame Read-only annotations of one selected file.
commit Commit all changes with an explicit nonempty message; a native request with path commits that file only. The client's automatic synchronization publishes the result. Hooks remain enabled.
revert Reset one file after entering REVERT. Never reset all, clean added files, or select a forced conflict policy. Disk restoration belongs to Diversion and is not an editor Undo transaction.
branch.create Create a named branch with --no-checkout, preserving the current branch.
branch.switch Checkout a simple branch/ref only with a clean, fully synced working copy. Do not carry, shelve or discard local changes, or apply the target shelf.
update Update a clean, fully synced workspace using manual conflict resolution and wait for local synchronization.
lock / unlock Acquire/release a lock on one selected file without force/admin release. Hard-lock availability is controlled by the installed Diversion service/plan.

Status/inspect exposes repository/workspace/branch IDs, cloud and local base commits, sync readiness and changed paths. Added/modified/deleted records are mapped directly; a recognized two-path rename becomes old-deleted/new-added. Status is a cloud workspace comparison; an unsynced agent can still have pending local changes. An incomplete sync state is shown explicitly and refuses mutations.

Parsing and guards#

The public CLI reference documents text output, not a JSON/porcelain option. The provider parses the documented identity lines from status --nowait --no-limit and diff --name-status --color never. It never invents an undocumented JSON flag. Unsupported identity, quoted/ambiguous path/rename formats, invalid UTF-8, duplicate records, excessive output and incomplete responses fail explicitly instead of becoming a clean project. Real-client format/version compatibility remains to be established.

Mutation preflight requires matching local/cloud base commits and no reported pause, transfer, queued events, offline state, conflict or error. Update/checkout also require an empty change summary. A second status checks repository, workspace, branch and base identities before dispatch. Concurrent daemon/server/filesystem changes are not an atomic transaction; the client's own checks remain authoritative. Unrecognized/omitted conflict states and other client versions need runtime acceptance rather than a claim of complete conflict coverage.

The mapped root must contain a local, nonsymlink .diversion/ directory. Parent traversal, administrative paths, symbolic links and nested-workspace file targets are rejected. Paths remain inside the CyCode workspace. File selectors use ./ prefixes to avoid option interpretation; pattern metacharacters, control characters and ambiguous quoting are rejected rather than expanded. Branch/ref forms use bounded simple ASCII names; existing Unicode branch names can be displayed. Tracked symlinks, unusual filenames and submodule-specific editing remain outside this provider's contract.

The shared native process owner receives argv vectors, fixed cwd and color hints (NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR, TERM). Diff explicitly requests --color never. Only SGR color sequences are stripped from read metadata; other control sequences fail. Each process has a 512 KiB output cap. Status/diff/history/annotation reads have 30-second deadlines and final mutations 180 seconds. Generic SDK transport allows 600 seconds for sequential preflight and execution. No undocumented exit code is converted to success. A timeout stops the CLI waiter; it cannot roll back or stop work already accepted by the independent Diversion agent/cloud service.

Common native host guards refuse mutations with dirty/open disk-conflicted buffers and reconcile clean documents afterward while retaining concurrent editor changes. Provider disable never falls back to Git silently. Generic MCP calls use vcs_provider_action with its existing plugin/process/workspace/VCS permissions; typed SDK Git operations remain Git-only. See Plugins.

Reference contracts: commit, branch, checkout, reset, update, annotations, locks, syncing and conflicts.

Validation and remaining scope#

Windows production compilation and MSVC /Zs source checks pass. The opt-in native regression source specifies fake-runner identities, literal/Unicode operands, sync/merge/error/partial-output guards, changed preflight identities, clean update/ checkout, commit/reset/lock scope, deadlines and missing tools. It also specifies actual production-DLL registration, mapping, dirty-buffer refusal and disable behavior. The existing MCP inventory/permission assertions include Diversion.

These native/MCP/GUI regressions are not executed during the current Kaspersky interruption. No dv process, login, cloud request, app window or test executable was launched. See Validation for actual checks. Client/agent/service versions, authentication, hooks, text formats, branches, conflicts, locks and large repositories remain runtime-unverified; Linux/macOS and clean installation have not been tested. This is an implemented CLI integration, not full Diversion-client or Rider parity.

pages.text: Diversion provider # The bundled native ABI2 extension cycode.diversion contributes cycode.diversion.provider . Enable it in Extensions, choose Diversion in Version control and map the exact directory containing .diversion/ . Git remains the default for unmapped projects. Install Diversion separately, log in and clone/init with its own client before using this provider. Tool discovery checks an absolute CYCODE_DV , managed tool locations and PATH; CyCode does not redistribute the CLI or collect credentials. No dependency or API subscription is added to the build. Operations # Diversion tracks working changes and synchronizes through its own agent. There is no staging area or push/pull action. The provider follows the documented agent workflow and uses dv subcommands, never its interactive shell. Mapping/refresh does not invoke init, clone, login, browser launch, preference changes or an explicit write command. The installed client's normal network/agent behavior remains in effect. The ten menu actions use the existing common provider forms and Review views: Action Behavior diff Working-copy patch through shared CyUI Diff, with color disabled. Native requests can select one file. log / history Read-only CLI history, default 50 and maximum 200 records, ISO dates; optional exact local file operand. No structured commit fields are guessed from display text. blame Read-only annotations of one selected file. commit Commit all changes with an explicit nonempty message; a native request with path commits that file only. The client's automatic synchronization publishes the result. Hooks remain enabled. revert Reset one file after entering REVERT . Never reset all, clean added files, or select a forced conflict policy. Disk restoration belongs to Diversion and is not an editor Undo transaction. branch.create Create a named branch with --no-checkout , preserving the current branch. branch.switch Checkout a simple branch/ref only with a clean, fully synced working copy. Do not carry, shelve or discard local changes, or apply the target shelf. update Update a clean, fully synced workspace using manual conflict resolution and wait for local synchronization. lock / unlock Acquire/release a lock on one selected file without force/admin release. Hard-lock availability is controlled by the installed Diversion service/plan. Status/inspect exposes repository/workspace/branch IDs, cloud and local base commits, sync readiness and changed paths. Added/modified/deleted records are mapped directly; a recognized two-path rename becomes old-deleted/new-added. Status is a cloud workspace comparison; an unsynced agent can still have pending local changes. An incomplete sync state is shown explicitly and refuses mutations. The provider parses the documented identity lines from status --nowait --no-limit and diff --name-status --color never . It never invents an undocumented JSON flag. Unsupported identity, quoted/ambiguous path/rename formats, invalid UTF-8, duplicate records, excessive output and incomplete responses fail explicitly instead of becoming a clean project. Concurrent daemon/server/filesystem changes are not an atomic transaction; the client's own checks remain authoritative. Unrecognized/omitted conflict states and other client versions need runtime acceptance rather than a claim of complete conflict coverage. The mapped root must contain a local, nonsymlink .diversion/ directory. Parent traversal, administrative paths, symbolic links and nested-workspace file targets are rejected. Paths remain inside the CyCode workspace. File selectors use ./ prefixes to avoid option interpretation; pattern metacharacters, control characters and ambiguous quoting are rejected rather than expanded. Branch/ref forms use bounded simple ASCII names; existing Unicode branch names can be displayed. Tracked symlinks, unusual filenames and submodule-specific editing remain outside this provider's contract. pages.title: Local documentation with CyDoc
pages.html:
Local documentation with CyDoc#

CyCode's Help menu, action catalogue and panel help buttons open the complete local manual in the system browser. Ctrl+F1 opens the manual, Shift+F1 opens context help. F1 opens help in the Rider and Visual Studio profiles; the VS Code profile retains its existing F1 action palette. Quick documentation for source symbols remains a language-service action.

Generate#

From the repository root, with Python 3.11+, Git access to the public CyDoc repository, and Node.js 22+ / npm:

text
python app/scripts/build_documentation.pypython app/scripts/verify_documentation.py runtime/documentation/site

An optional --cydoc-source PATH accepts a clean local checkout at the exact revision in app/documentation/cydoc.lock.json. Preparation uses a separate Git archive or detached cache under runtime/deps; it never changes that checkout. The lock pins CyDoc 0.1.0 at 774f2a7eabf7dd181a98ffc5add115b580b67f42. The generator uses CyDoc's checked export and resource providers, without copying or changing its viewer sources.

Open runtime/documentation/site/index.html directly from disk. The exported reader uses classic local scripts, selected media bundles, CSS, compiled page data and local images. No server, CDN, account, Node installation or network is required to read it. Ordinary external source/licence links are optional.

Build and distribution#

GUI CMake builds generate documentation by default. CyCode_documentation publishes the full export under the build directory's help/ and next to the executable as app/help/. The Windows packager includes this complete tree and the documentation lock. Installation copies help to app/help/ too. CYDOC_DIR is the optional clean checkout override. A fresh dependency fetch requires GitHub and npm access; prepared caches work offline.

CYCODE_BUILD_DOCUMENTATION=OFF is an explicit development-only opt-out: help actions report that help was disabled. Core-only builds do not need CyDoc or Node. A distributable GUI package must contain the generated help export. The normal app build keeps BUILD_TESTING=OFF.

Authoring and migration#

  • app/documentation/manual/en and fr: paired user guides, stable page IDs and explicit section IDs. Increase the English revision and update French sourceRevision after reviewing the matching translation.
  • app/documentation/assets: layout illustrations and favicon. These are labelled diagrams, not screenshots of an untested desktop session.
  • app/documentation/project.json: imported original documents, local media, page aliases and the explicit distributable source allow-list.
  • Existing README, French README, technical guides, code examples and notices remain authoring inputs. Markdown links are rewritten to stable CyDoc routes; source links outside the small lexical index point to the recorded source revision. No runtime/dependency tree is indexed.
  • API reference comes from the real app/CyTool.json operation schemas. CyDoc's neutral API import and C++/Python source index do not parse a compiler AST. Bilingual native help annotations demonstrate source-driven documentation.

The export contains migration-report.json, including original-file/page mapping and unresolved legacy references, and translation-report.json. English is the default/fallback language; original English technical pages and operation schemas are not presented as completed French translations. Historical validation pages retain their dates and are marked as historical evidence.

Only image and gallery are selected: diagrams, logos and collections need these. Static diagram blocks compile to SVG, so graph is unnecessary. No video, GIF, mesh or Three.js runtime is shipped. CyDoc and its selected compiler dependency notices are retained in the exported licenses/ directory.

The upstream reader provides themes, keyboard navigation, in-window media enlargement and browser-local reading positions. Initial theme follows the reader/system preference; the stock exporter does not propagate the app's CyUI theme or density. File-origin storage behavior varies by browser. Windows help uses the platform file-URL converter; extended paths are not supported by that API. Linux/macOS URL branches and desktop help interaction need platform testing.

Verification scope#

The optional component check uses the pinned CyDoc development dependencies:

text
node app/scripts/verify_documentation_dom.mjs runtime/documentation/site runtime/deps/cydoc-774f2a7

It loads compiled manual data into a DOM fixture with resource/script loading disabled. It checks guide routes, language fallback, search, light/dark themes, gallery navigation, in-window enlargement/Escape and reading/navigation position restoration. This is not a browser or native desktop acceptance test. Real file-URL rendering, menu clicks, DPI, touch and Linux/macOS builds remain separate checks. The stock reader’s MIT badges describe CyDoc; the application remains GPL-3.0-only.

The migration was compiled in Windows Release. Export integrity/link checks and DOM component fixtures passed. Native tests were not executed. The source-comment extractor in the pinned CyDoc version does not propagate translation revision metadata: the bilingual help-routing annotation is explicitly reported as untracked. Authored guide translations have matching explicit revision metadata.

The repository-root launcher receives the same generated export in app/help/. These generated directories are ignored by Git; edit the authoring sources instead.

Published reader#

English documentation · Documentation française

.github/workflows/documentation.yml regenerates the same complete export on every main-branch push or manual dispatch, using the pinned CyDoc revision and only the image/gallery modules. Node.js 22 and Python 3.11 are build tools; the published reader needs neither. Hash routes preserve pages, sections, languages and media under the Pages project URL. Offline file:// help remains bundled. Only the verified export is uploaded, never application data or dependency caches.

Regenerate and verify the publication artifact from the repository root:

text
python app/scripts/build_documentation.py --output runtime/pagespython app/scripts/verify_documentation.py runtime/pages

The private source repository cannot use Pages on the current GitHub plan. The existing public MrMybal/CyCodeReader repository hosts both manuals. Its cycode-docs branch contains only the generated CyCode export in site/. The CyCode source workflow updates that branch using DOCS_DEPLOY_KEY, a write deploy key scoped to CyCodeReader, with no access to private CyCode source. The Reader workflow builds its own manual from main, checks the generated branch, and composes the Pages artifact: Reader at /, CyCode at /cycode/. No extra repository, private source checkout or local application data is needed. The publication helper refuses unknown or locally modified generated files. Keep the deploy secret configured when transferring CI.

pages.title: In-editor language diagnostics
pages.html:
In-editor language diagnostics#

CyCode connects the shared CyUI CodeEditor's native squiggle/tooltip API to actual language-server diagnostics. The application owns revision validation and mapping; the library owns rendering, folding/scrolling, font metrics and hover behavior. No editor/library source is copied or changed for this integration.

language.status.servers.<backend> now supplies diagnosticGeneration and diagnosticRevisions. The latter maps a workspace-relative path to its native id/revision and the server publication's uri. The native owner includes an entry only when the publication explicitly names the current LSP overlay version and the sent overlay still matches the document identity and revision. The combined status also contains eligible mappings from its child servers. These are display metadata, not permission to change/save text.

The desktop compares that native identity/revision pair with its tab, converts UTF-16 positions to editor glyphs and rejects out-of-range/reversed ranges and surrogate splits. Errors, warnings, information and hints use CyUI palette roles; the message and optional source appear in the existing editor tooltip. Errors retain precedence over overlapping hints. A zero-length range marks the adjacent real glyph, where one exists; an empty line has no artificial character added to it.

Annotations are cleared after local edits and when the tab's revision, backend availability or publication is no longer eligible. External/recovery/refactoring changes use those same ownership checks. Close/reopen or a replacement identity starts a new LSP lifetime with a higher wire version, even when queued close/open updates coalesce; reload resynchronizes its retained identity. A fresh publication or theme change rebuilds this annotation family. Search/other native annotation families are preserved. Annotation changes add no text edits or Undo entries.

The LSP allows servers to omit publication versions. Those diagnostics remain in Problems and in the existing native/MCP status response, but are not underlined: their range cannot be proven to belong to the current buffer. This is a deliberate limit of this display adapter. Problems labels unverified open-document positions and excludes them from keyboard/source navigation; closed-file reports remain advisory navigation destinations. See Diagnostic navigation. It does not fabricate a revision or wait for diagnostics before supplying completion. Pull-diagnostic providers and missing version information need further backend work.

Editor annotation work is bounded to 512 considered diagnostics, 64 lines per range, 2,048 painted line segments and 131,072 glyphs total (4,096 per segment). Messages are capped at 4 KiB on a UTF-8 boundary. The editor reports that additional diagnostics are available in Problems when a display budget is exceeded. All server diagnostics remain available there; full backend catalogues are not replaced with this bounded display subset.

Source assertions cover astral Unicode and invalid surrogate boundaries, multiline/point ranges, malformed ranges, preservation of another annotation family, display budgets, current/stale/unversioned publication routing and theme refresh. These checks have not been executed after the Kaspersky interruption; MSVC syntax-only validation generates no test executable. See Validation for the actual build/runtime evidence.

pages.title: Workspace events and native subscriptions
pages.html:
Workspace events and native subscriptions#

The native Engine owns one bounded event journal per workspace instance. GUI, MCP and ABI2 plugins observe that same stream. It reports committed document, resource and build metadata; it is not an alternative document model or an Undo log. Events contain no buffer text. Services such as documents.read remain the authority for a fresh snapshot and for revision-checked changes.

Reading the journal#

events.read (MCP events_read) is read-only and does not activate language servers, refresh plugins or acquire the document/build execution locks. Example:

json
{"tail":true}

This returns an empty page and the current epoch / nextSequence. Take that cursor before reading a snapshot, then resume with:

json
{"epoch":"<issued epoch>","afterSequence":42,"limit":128,"types":["document.*","build.finished"]}

The response contains epoch, oldestSequence, latestSequence, nextSequence, gap, hasMore and events. Each event has sequence, type, origin, timestampMs and data. Sequences are monotonic within the issued epoch; they are not document revisions. An empty origin means a host operation. Plugin host requests record the owning plugin ID. excludeOrigin can omit one such owner.

Always advance to nextSequence, including an empty filtered page. Read additional pages while hasMore is true. Filtering accepts up to 16 exact types or trailing wildcards (each at most 64 bytes). The page limit is 1–512, default 128. A nonzero resume cursor requires its issued epoch; foreign epochs and future cursors are errors. Omit the cursor to inspect retained history, or use tail to start now.

Retention is at most 512 entries / 4 MiB. Entries larger than 64 KiB are dropped with a gap marker; allocation/serialization failure also marks a gap. A consumer that falls behind must take a new snapshot when gap is true. Epochs change on workspace replacement/restart and on sequence rollover. Nothing is persisted, and there is no guarantee of replay after a consumer crashes.

Current event families:

Type Metadata and meaning
workspace.opened Root and selected entry of this native instance
workspace.changed Filesystem reconciliation summary; rescan affected resources
document.opened/changed/saved/reloaded/closed Relative path, stable document ID and revision; dirty/conflict state where applicable
transaction.committed Applied/undone shared semantic change set; refresh its affected documents
resources.changed Committed resource operation; refresh resource/document snapshots
build.started/finished Native operation ID, method and completion/cancellation/failure metadata

Multi-document change events are published after the complete in-memory transaction has been applied. Resource/reload operations retain existing document identities. The journal provides ordering and change notification, not a multi-service snapshot transaction. A later mutation may already have occurred when a consumer reads.

ABI2 automatic subscriptions#

Check the optional host tail size and CYCODE_HOST_FEATURE_EVENT_SUBSCRIPTIONS_V2 before registering an events contribution during init:

cpp
host->contribute(host->context, "events",    R"({"id":"example.tools.observe","types":["document.*","build.finished"],"maxBatch":32})",    on_events);

The callback uses the normal CyCodeCommandV2 signature and returns plugin-owned JSON, for example {"ok":true}. IDs must belong to the plugin namespace. No when/GUI context is supported; maxBatch is 1–32 and the host accepts at most 32 subscriptions. A separate CYCODE_HOST_FEATURE_EVENTS_V2 bit advertises the read-only events.read host request without requiring automatic callbacks.

The native worker calls active subscribers serially with all other callbacks for that plugin host, outside Engine document locks. It attempts delivery every 100 ms, skips a busy host and fairly limits each pass to eight callback deliveries. This is not a real-time notification deadline. Callback envelopes have the journal page fields plus subscription and event:

  • subscribed: initial empty page, cursor at the current tail, gap:true. Read the needed state through host services. Mutating host requests are denied during this initial snapshot handshake.
  • events: a normal filtered batch. Host requests use the plugin manifest's permissions and the existing native revision/path/process guards.
  • gap: empty page advanced to the latest tail. Rebuild the snapshot with read-only host requests; mutations are denied during this callback too.

The callback's successful return acknowledges that page. A thrown/returned error pauses only this subscription and is displayed in Extensions and plugins.list.eventSubscriptions. Disable/re-enable the plugin to retry from a new snapshot; failed callbacks are not retried automatically. Activation changes reset subscription cursors. Disabling removes future delivery; libraries remain pinned until shutdown.

Events produced synchronously by the subscribing plugin's own host requests are excluded from its automatic stream. This prevents the ordinary self-edit loop; it does not prevent two plugins reacting to each other, or identify filesystem writes performed directly by native code. Plugins must coalesce work, check revisions and bound their callbacks. Follow-up work on plugin-owned threads cannot call host services; use a later host callback.

Engine shutdown rejects new work, stops delivery, cancels owned work until the current callback returns, then deactivates/releases plugins while host services are still alive. Lifecycle/shutdown hooks themselves cannot call the host. Native code is trusted: an unreturning callback, native crash or arbitrary OS access is not isolated or preempted. There is no separate plugin process sandbox.

The bundled Unreal extension observes workspace/resource/build changes and shows the last event and count in its existing overview. These events do not implement Blueprint asset analysis, Live Coding or UnrealEditor automation.

Validation#

Windows x64/MSVC production application/core/CLI and bundled plugins compile with tests disabled. Journal paging/overflow/origin/ordering assertions, automatic subscription/permission/error/activation fixtures and an official SDK/MCP test are present; they have not been executed after the Kaspersky interruption. MSVC syntax-only checks generate no test objects or executables. GUI acceptance, shutdown under runtime load and Linux/macOS execution remain pending. See Validation and Testing.

Retention is at most 512 entries / 4 MiB. Entries larger than 64 KiB are dropped with a gap marker; allocation/serialization failure also marks a gap. A consumer that falls behind must take a new snapshot when gap is true. Epochs change on workspace replacement/restart and on sequence rollover. Nothing is persisted, and there is no guarantee of replay after a consumer crashes. Current event families: Type Metadata and meaning workspace.opened Root and selected entry of this native instance workspace.changed Filesystem reconciliation summary; rescan affected resources document.opened/changed/saved/reloaded/closed Relative path, stable document ID and revision; dirty/conflict state where applicable transaction.committed Applied/undone shared semantic change set; refresh its affected documents resources.changed Committed resource operation; refresh resource/document snapshots build.started/finished Native operation ID, method and completion/cancellation/failure metadata Multi-document change events are published after the complete in-memory transaction has been applied. Resource/reload operations retain existing document identities. The journal provides ordering and change notification, not a multi-service snapshot transaction. A later mutation may already have occurred when a consumer reads. ABI2 automatic subscriptions # Check the optional host tail size and CYCODE_HOST_FEATURE_EVENT_SUBSCRIPTIONS_V2 before registering an events contribution during init: cpp Copy host -> contribute ( host -> context , "events" , R"({"id":"example.tools.observe","types":["document.*","build.finished"],"maxBatch":32})" , on_events ) ; The callback uses the normal CyCodeCommandV2 signature and returns plugin-owned JSON, for example {"ok":true} . IDs must belong to the plugin namespace. No when /GUI context is supported; maxBatch is 1–32 and the host accepts at most 32 subscriptions. A separate CYCODE_HOST_FEATURE_EVENTS_V2 bit advertises the read-only events.read host request without requiring automatic callbacks. The native worker calls active subscribers serially with all other callbacks for that plugin host, outside Engine document locks. It attempts delivery every 100 ms, skips a busy host and fairly limits each pass to eight callback deliveries. This is not a real-time notification deadline. Callback envelopes have the journal page fields plus subscription and event : subscribed : initial empty page, cursor at the current tail, gap:true . Read the needed state through host services. Mutating host requests are denied during this initial snapshot handshake. events : a normal filtered batch. Host requests use the plugin manifest's permissions and the existing native revision/path/process guards. gap : empty page advanced to the latest tail. Rebuild the snapshot with read-only host requests; mutations are denied during this callback too. The callback's successful return acknowledges that page. A thrown/returned error pauses only this subscription and is displayed in Extensions and plugins.list.eventSubscriptions . Disable/re-enable the plugin to retry from a new snapshot; failed callbacks are not retried automatically. Activation changes reset subscription cursors. Disabling removes future delivery; libraries remain pinned until shutdown. Events produced synchronously by the subscribing plugin's own host requests are excluded from its automatic stream. This prevents the ordinary self-edit loop; it does not prevent two plugins reacting to each other, or identify filesystem writes performed directly by native code. Plugins must coalesce work, check revisions and bound their callbacks. Follow-up work on plugin-owned threads cannot call host services; use a later host callback. Engine shutdown rejects new work, stops delivery, cancels owned work until the current callback returns, then deactivates/releases plugins while host services are still alive. Lifecycle/shutdown hooks themselves cannot call the host. Native code is trusted: an unreturning callback, native crash or arbitrary OS access is not isolated or preempted. There is no separate plugin process sandbox. The bundled Unreal extension observes workspace/resource/build changes and shows the last event and count in its existing overview. These events do not implement Blueprint asset analysis, Live Coding or UnrealEditor automation. Validation # Windows x64/MSVC production application/core/CLI and bundled plugins compile with tests disabled. Journal paging/overflow/origin/ordering assertions, automatic subscription/permission/error/activation fixtures and an official SDK/MCP test are present; they have not been executed after the Kaspersky interruption. MSVC syntax-only checks generate no test objects or executables. GUI acceptance, shutdown under runtime load and Linux/macOS execution remain pending. pages.title: Run, terminal and debugging
pages.html:
Run, terminal and debugging#

Bound Unreal run/launch now checks ordinary Editor output receipts, module BuildIds and recorded project files before dispatching a terminal or DAP launch. Configure still works before compiling. Desktop build-before-debug also requires a matching ready artifact assessment; actual process success and output readiness are distinct. Existing attach and unbound manual profiles are unchanged. This does not validate every dependency, source freshness or binary ABI; see Unreal output inspection and its pending actual acceptance.

Bound Unreal profiles now retain their project/engine/target/platform/configuration and normalized launch options. Desktop compilation before debugging uses that context, then checks the captured profile/draft/build ID, matching successful result and open document identities/revisions before launching captured parameters. Cancellation, uncertainty or concurrent changes stop automatic launch. The native owner revalidates bound program/cwd/argv/runtime for configure and actual launch. Null detachment preserves manual profiles; SDK launch still does not compile. See Unreal launch for scope and pending actual acceptance.

The Unreal Engine panel now prepares UE4/UE5 editor, standalone game and uncooked server launch settings with map/listen/port/resolution/log options. Applying saves the common run/debug profile with an observed-profile conflict guard; no process starts until existing Run/Debug is used. Other saved environment/watch settings remain. SDK preparation/configuration share that owner and do not compile; actual Unreal execution remains unverified. See Unreal launch.

ABI2 plugins can contribute stdio-DAP adapters to the same native debugger, selected explicitly in Launch configuration or through debug_adapters and adapterId/adapterOptions. Disable/change revokes their owned session. See Plugin debuggers for manifests, payloads, process ownership and current runtime/adapter limits. The bundled Unreal extension supplies a CodeLLDB entry; this does not establish UnrealEditor debugging acceptance.

The desktop and MCP use the same native Terminals and Debugger services. Windows x64 has been exercised with actual PowerShell/cmd, a C++ PDB executable, CodeLLDB, and a .NET 8 console assembly with portable PDBs through NetCoreDbg, the official MCP SDK and real GUI key input. Linux/macOS implementations and pinned adapter archives are present; their execution remains unverified.

Terminal#

Alt+F12 opens/focuses the terminal. Its toolbar creates shells, switches between up to eight sessions, clears scrollback or closes the selected session/process tree. Closing the docked panel hides it; the session stays alive. Panels can be detached into native windows using the existing docking system. The normal Windows profile uses installed PowerShell (pwsh when found, otherwise Windows PowerShell); cmd is also available. POSIX profiles use the user's shell, bash or zsh. The startup option --terminal-profile cmd selects the profile for subsequently created terminals.

These are real PTYs: ConPTY on Windows and forkpty on POSIX. libvterm 0.3.3 handles UTF-8, cell widths, ANSI/VT state, alternate screens, cursor/device queries, paste and resize/reflow. Read/write threads and a process supervisor keep synchronous PTY I/O off the UI thread. ConPTY output continues draining during teardown. Only visible rows are copied for GUI rendering. Standard terminal colours follow the active theme and foreground contrast is adjusted; explicit 256/RGB colours remain terminal data.

The focused terminal owns shell editing keys, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+F and Tab. Ctrl+Shift+C copies a mouse selection; Ctrl+Shift+V pastes with bracketed-paste support. Paste is capped at 64 KiB and rejects escape bytes; raw authorized MCP input can send controls. Scrollback is bounded to 2,000 lines and 200,000 cells per session; input queues are bounded to 256 KiB. Terminal snapshots use display-cell coordinates, not UTF-16. The renderer supports bold, underline, strike and reverse video; italic style is retained in native cells but does not select a separate italic font. Full mouse reporting, terminal tabs with separate split panes, shell integration and IME/font coverage on other platforms need broader work/validation.

Run and debug#

Run > Run without debugging launches the selected executable or .NET assembly with argv/env in a native terminal. A persistent profile is stored in .cycode/launch.json. The Debugger panel edits executable, working directory, arguments (one argv element per line), environment, runtime (automatic/native/.NET), .NET host, adapter and stop-on-entry. Environment entries are KEY=VALUE; a line -KEY removes an inherited variable. Working directories remain within the workspace; an explicitly selected executable can be external, including UnrealEditor.

Build before debugging saves modified documents and runs the configured CMake, MSBuild or Unreal build before launching. Build failure prevents launch. CMake target artifacts can populate the executable selection. For discovered Unreal projects, the installed UnrealEditor executable/project arguments are suggested. UnrealEditor debugging itself has not been exercised; the executed debugger evidence is an owned C++ fixture.

The adapter speaks the actual Debug Adapter Protocol over private child-process stdio. One owner thread handles requests/events and refreshes stopped-thread stack, scopes, locals and watches. The framed JSON child transport is reused from the language client without sending LSP initialization. Requests have a 15-second deadline; commands, incoming messages, output and variable pages are bounded. MCP cancellation waits for native work to finish; immediate cancellation/streaming is not provided.

Click the editor gutter or use Toggle breakpoint. Breakpoints persist and include adapter-verified locations. The Breakpoints tab supports conditions, hit conditions, log messages and enabled flags; an expected-breakpoint snapshot rejects conflicting edits. Stack/thread selection refreshes variables and jumps to source. Registered SDK sources open read-only. Adapter-issued disassembly/source references open as separate read-only debug:// views and are valid only for the current debug session.

The Variables tab expands children, bounded to an initial 200-item page per reference and eight display levels. Additional collection-page controls are pending; MCP can request further pages. Watch expressions persist (up to 32), are reevaluated on stops and report individual failures. Evaluate uses the selected frame. Expression/debugger commands may have side effects in the target. No synthetic variable values are used.

Stop terminates a launched debuggee and its owned terminal. Attach takes an explicit process ID; stopping that session detaches and leaves the existing process running. Native acceptance verifies this distinction. Process ownership is tied to native shutdown/workspace changes. Always use matching symbols and sufficiently unoptimized code. MSVC incremental-link thunks can produce disassembly-only stops; the source-level fixture disables incremental linking. Capability-gated function/exception breakpoint controls, paged scopes/variables, register scopes, read-only memory and disassembly now use the same stopped-session guards. See Advanced debugging for contracts and currently unexecuted runtime acceptance. Data breakpoints, memory writes, remote/core-dump workflows, reverse debugging and full Unreal visualizers/Live Coding integration remain pending.

C#/.NET runtime#

runtime=automatic detects PE/CLI assemblies and native apphosts with a matching managed DLL/runtimeconfig. The managed backend uses NetCoreDbg. MSBuild evaluated artifacts offer runnable managed DLLs as well as executables; class libraries without a runtimeconfig are not offered as runnable targets. Select the actual built output, with matching portable PDBs. Automatic .NET host discovery probes installed runtimes and the private analysis host; an explicit host can be selected. Missing target framework runtimes produce an error rather than silently enabling major roll-forward. Standalone .NET 8 console debugging is validated; .NET Framework, Mono, Unity, other target frameworks, ASP.NET/browser and remote workflows remain unverified.

The same source markers, stack/threads, locals, object/array children, watches, evaluation, step into/over/out, pause and attach/detach are used for C# and C++. Inspection identifiers are cleared on resume/stop/relaunch; stop generations stay monotonic across sessions. Deferred managed breakpoint verification updates markers. NetCoreDbg supports conditional breakpoints; it does not advertise logpoints or hit counts. Unsupported enabled options are rejected before changing a live saved list. Unverified, disabled or unbound breakpoints remain visibly distinct.

Managed program output appears in the Debug console. NetCoreDbg does not implement runInTerminal or debuggee stdin; use Run without debugging for interactive console programs. UTF-8 program output is tested (the console fixture selects UTF8Encoding); other Windows output encodings and environment values outside the active Windows code page need broader adapter coverage. Unicode paths, accented environment values and arguments containing spaces, embedded quotes and shell punctuation are tested. The Windows adapter's argv builder drops empty arguments; CyCode rejects those and unrepresentable quote/tab-plus-trailing-backslash cases with a clear error. Native terminal Run preserves ordinary argv directly. Advanced adapterArgs persist in launch.json/MCP as separate argv elements, not a shell command; leave logging off for normal use. Environment overrides/removals are applied to the adapter's native environment to avoid NetCoreDbg's JSON-to-ANSI override corruption on Windows.

Keyboard profiles#

Action Rider Visual Studio / VS Code
Debug / Continue Shift+F9, F5, F9 F5
Run Shift+F10 Ctrl+F5
Toggle breakpoint Ctrl+F8 F9
Step over F8 F10
Step into F7 F11
Step out Shift+F8 Shift+F11
Stop Ctrl+F2 Shift+F5
Terminal Alt+F12 Alt+F12

Keyboard settings can override these bindings. A focused PTY owns its function keys; focus the editor/debugger before invoking debug function-key bindings.

Dependencies and reproduction#

libvterm is pinned in dependencies.lock.json and fetched for GUI/core builds. The GUI build runs setup_debugger.py, installing official CodeLLDB 1.12.3 and its bundled LLDB 22.1.8 under runtime/tools. Its platform archives/digests are locked in debugger-tools.lock.json. This avoids relying on an installed LLVM adapter whose Python DLL dependencies may be absent. For native debugging, automatic prefers bundled CodeLLDB, then an installed lldb-dap; a custom adapter path can be selected. Only the bundled CodeLLDB backend was exercised for native debugging. setup_debugger.py also installs official NetCoreDbg 3.2.0-1092 for managed debugging, with platform SHA-256 hashes in the same lock file. Upstream provides Windows x64, Linux x64/arm64 and macOS arm64 archives for this release. Other architectures need an installed adapter; only Windows x64 is validated here. Dependency licenses remain in app/licenses; CyCode's original source is licensed under GPL-3.0-only (see the root LICENSE).

The native terminal and debugger CTests use owned fixtures. The debugger test reports a skip if no adapter is installed in a core-only environment. GUI scripts:

text
python app/scripts/verify_terminal.pypython app/scripts/verify_debugger.pypython app/scripts/verify_managed_debugger.py

Run the private Python integration suite for SDK permission/schema checks and actual CMake-built C++ debugging over MCP. Every terminal_* and debug_* operation requires process.execute, including inspection, because process data can extend beyond source documents. Persisted profile/breakpoint changes also require workspace.write. Native sessions belong to the IDE and survive job/task completion until explicitly stopped; they are persistent runtime state rather than task-file artifacts.

Primary implementation references: Microsoft ConPTY lifecycle, redirected-parent handle behavior, libvterm, CodeLLDB configuration. Managed adapter references: NetCoreDbg release, DAP implementation.

pages.title: Git conflict catalogue and reviewed index resolution
pages.html:
Git conflict catalogue and reviewed index resolution#

CyCode now has three related conflict workflows: structural catalogue/inspection, reviewed binary or missing-side index resolution, and explicit grouped path choices for rename conflicts. They share the native Git owner across desktop, SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugins. The existing three-way working-text editor is retained.

After index resolution, a separate reviewed working-file service now installs raw stage-zero bytes or physically removes an absent-index path, with persistent backups and guarded Undo. It handles one file per transaction, without automatic rename inference or Git filters/EOL conversion. See Git working files for effects and pending runtime validation.

Inspect actual Git stages#

Open Version control > Conflicts, or Resolve conflict in Changes. The Git catalogue shows all unresolved paths from complete ls-files --stage -z records. It retains mode/OID/stage records, including SHA-1/SHA-256 object names, and absent base/ours/theirs entries. An absent side is distinct from an empty file. Paths in the new service are relative to the selected repository; documentPath maps each entry to the workspace for the existing text editor.

Inspect versions classifies each stage as text, binary/unsupported encoding, large, absent or unsupported, with its byte count. Valid UTF-8 text is returned only up to 4 MiB per stage and 16 MiB of encoded response overall. Binary bytes never enter editor buffers or JSON strings. Large blobs retain their metadata; they are not downloaded/read into a text preview. Native blob output must match its recorded byte count. Files in the working directory are not read by this inspection. Open working text conflict retains the earlier working-buffer editor; the working file must exist and satisfy the ordinary text-document guards.

The catalogue uses actual Git status codes for stage presence: DD, AU, UD, UA, DU, AA and UU. These codes do not reconstruct a rename topology. Ours/theirs refer to stages 2/3; rebase can reverse the branch roles a user expects from those names.

Choose and review index changes#

For each path choose Stage ours, Stage theirs, Stage base, Stage deletion, or Keep unresolved. A missing selected side produces an explicitly reviewed index deletion. Preview index resolution displays the exact selected objects and deletions before Apply reviewed index resolution is enabled.

For rename/rename or rename/delete conflicts, select each affected original and destination path explicitly in the same batch. For example, retain the ours stage at the chosen destination and stage deletion of the original and unwanted destination. Up to 32 paths are submitted together. CyCode never guesses which unrelated files belong to a rename, invents a destination, or uses --replace to erase a conflicting directory/file entry. Case aliases and overlapping requested paths are refused. Symlink/gitlink/sparse-directory conflicts remain visible but require an external resolver.

This is index-only resolution. The selected local blob OIDs and recorded executable modes are staged directly without text normalization or clean filters. Deletion removes the index entry only. Working files, unsaved documents and their Undo/revisions stay intact. Consequently, the editor can still show conflict markers or a different binary version after the index is resolved, and a deleted index path can remain as a local/untracked file. Review staged and working diffs before committing. There is no automatic checkout, physical rename/deletion, merge continuation or editor Undo for this action.

Shared native and extension contracts#

SDK operation Native / ABI2 host method Required inputs/effect
vcs_conflict_list vcs.conflict.list Selected repository; complete catalogue and revision
vcs_conflict_inspect vcs.conflict.inspect Repository-relative path and expectedRevision; nullable text/metadata
vcs_conflict_plan vcs.conflict.plan Choices, expectedRepository and expectedRevision; exact preview
vcs_conflict_apply vcs.conflict.apply Same choices/guards plus expectedPlanRevision; actual process result and catalogue or catalogError

These typed SDK operations select built-in Git and reject an external provider. External VCS plugins retain their provider-specific contracts. Read/preview exports have no mutation permissions; apply requires vcs.write, workspace.write and process.execute, with the existing workspace mutation group. The native VCS mutex serializes GUI/MCP/plugin operations. Native ownership remains noncancellable and the bridge keeps its existing bounded 600-second wait policy. ABI2 stays unchanged; no additional dependency, executable target or CyUI module is needed.

Guards, bounds and uncertainty#

The preview binds selected repository identity, Git administrative directory identity, HEAD, symbolic branch, complete listed index records and normalized choices. Apply rechecks these values and locally available blobs before dispatching one fixed-argv git update-index command. An existing regular index file is used as the hooks path, preventing hook discovery below a directory. Fsmonitor, prompts, lazy fetch and transport are disabled for these calls. No shell, filter, checkout, commit or source-file write is requested.

Git owns its index lock. The preflight is not an atomic compare-and-swap with other Git applications, so external-writer races remain possible. Postflight compares all selected and unselected mode/OID/stage records against the reviewed result, and rejects unstable catalogue snapshots. It does not promise byte-identical index extensions/stat caches or an OS sandbox. Preserve the actual exit code/timeout/ truncation result: even exit zero can carry catalogError when the observed index cannot be confirmed. Inspect and refresh after uncertainty; there is no automatic retry, cleanup or rollback.

Bounds are an 8 MiB listing, 100,000 index records, 512 unresolved paths, 4,096 bytes per path and 12,000 aggregate requested path bytes. Each subprocess has a 15-second timeout, checked against a local 45-second inspection budget; a call already in progress can finish after that budget. Truncated/incomplete records fail explicitly.

Validation status#

Windows x64 production compilation, MSVC syntax checks and real CyToolsCore manifest/JSON Schema data validation are used during the current Kaspersky native execution suspension. After index resolution, a separate reviewed working-file service now installs raw stage-zero bytes or physically removes an absent-index path, with persistent backups and guarded Undo. It handles one file per transaction, without automatic rename inference or Git filters/EOL conversion. See Git working files for effects and pending runtime validation. Inspect actual Git stages # Open Version control > Conflicts , or Resolve conflict in Changes. The Git catalogue shows all unresolved paths from complete ls-files --stage -z records. It retains mode/OID/stage records, including SHA-1/SHA-256 object names, and absent base/ours/theirs entries. An absent side is distinct from an empty file. Paths in the new service are relative to the selected repository ; documentPath maps each entry to the workspace for the existing text editor. Inspect versions classifies each stage as text, binary/unsupported encoding, large, absent or unsupported, with its byte count. Valid UTF-8 text is returned only up to 4 MiB per stage and 16 MiB of encoded response overall. Binary bytes never enter editor buffers or JSON strings. Large blobs retain their metadata; they are not downloaded/read into a text preview. Native blob output must match its recorded byte count. Files in the working directory are not read by this inspection. Open working text conflict retains the earlier working-buffer editor; the working file must exist and satisfy the ordinary text-document guards. The catalogue uses actual Git status codes for stage presence: DD, AU, UD, UA, DU, AA and UU. These codes do not reconstruct a rename topology. Ours/theirs refer to stages 2/3; rebase can reverse the branch roles a user expects from those names. Choose and review index changes # For each path choose Stage ours , Stage theirs , Stage base , Stage deletion , or Keep unresolved . A missing selected side produces an explicitly reviewed index deletion. Preview index resolution displays the exact selected objects and deletions before Apply reviewed index resolution is enabled. For rename/rename or rename/delete conflicts, select each affected original and destination path explicitly in the same batch. For example, retain the ours stage at the chosen destination and stage deletion of the original and unwanted destination. Up to 32 paths are submitted together. CyCode never guesses which unrelated files belong to a rename, invents a destination, or uses --replace to erase a conflicting directory/file entry. Case aliases and overlapping requested paths are refused. Symlink/gitlink/sparse-directory conflicts remain visible but require an external resolver. This is index-only resolution . The selected local blob OIDs and recorded executable modes are staged directly without text normalization or clean filters. Deletion removes the index entry only. Working files, unsaved documents and their Undo/revisions stay intact. Consequently, the editor can still show conflict markers or a different binary version after the index is resolved, and a deleted index path can remain as a local/untracked file. Inspect and refresh after uncertainty; there is no automatic retry, cleanup or rollback. pages.title: Reviewed merge completion and quit
pages.html:
Reviewed merge completion and quit#

Version control > Merge now joins conflict resolution, working-file review and final merge actions through one native/UI/SDK/ABI2 owner. Starting a merge retains the existing branch workflow. This view inspects and completes an already active merge, or explicitly quits its tracking while retaining local work.

Inspect and review#

Refresh merge state reads actual operation markers, HEAD/branch/admin identity, complete staged mode/OID/stage records, index flags and native document revisions. It lists unresolved paths, incoming merge parents, staged paths/stat and blockers. Review merge conflicts opens the existing conflict view; Review staged merge diff uses the common Diff review. Working files can then be synchronized through the separate working-file service.

Completion requires one incoming parent, all conflicts resolved, tracked working files matching the index, saved/reconciled repository buffers and closed Git metadata/managed receipt documents. Skip-worktree, assume-unchanged and intent-to-add entries block this reviewed completion. Autostash and another active rebase/apply/cherry-pick/revert/sequencer operation block both actions; handle those through their actual Git workflow. A changed merge-origin HEAD is also refused. Inspection is read-only and refresh is explicit.

Complete the merge commit#

Choose Complete merge commit, edit the message and Preview merge action. The first MERGE_MSG line seeds an editable subject; user edits survive a refresh within the same merge. Preview binds the current repository/state, complete staged index, ordered expected parents, message, hooks policy and effects. The whole index is included, including unrelated paths staged intentionally or accidentally; review the full list. Untracked files are not added.

Apply reviewed merge action writes an intent receipt, rechecks the snapshot and executes a fixed Git commit command with a message file, verbatim cleanup and explicitly disabled signing. The message is valid UTF-8 up to 16 KiB; nonempty content is required. This workflow currently creates unsigned commits. It never uses a project-derived shell command, starts an editor or performs a push.

Configured commit hooks default to disabled. Run configured Git commit hooks is an explicit reviewed choice and requires repository documents to be closed. Those trusted hooks may run tools, change files/index/message, access the network or fail. They are not an OS sandbox. Their actual process status and any changed postconditions remain visible. Native Git transport, fsmonitor, automatic maintenance, rerere and editor requests are disabled for this owner.

Postflight checks that no operation is still active, then reads the raw commit object to verify actual ordered parents independently of log signature/notes settings or grafted history. Replacement refs are disabled for this owner. It compares the committed recursive tree and current index mode/OID/stage/flag records against the preview. A zero exit code can still carry inspectionError when the reviewed outcome cannot be confirmed. The result retains the actual process status and available new commit identity rather than inventing success.

Quit merge tracking while retaining local work#

Choose Quit merge tracking, preview its effects and apply explicitly. This executes Git's merge --quit. It clears merge bookkeeping while retaining working files and indexed content; unresolved entries and unsaved source buffers may remain. The next ordinary commit will no longer use those recorded merge parents. The original merge message/parents are copied into the intent receipt first.

This is distinct from merge --abort, which attempts to restore pre-merge state. No reset or reconstruction is performed here. Autostash is refused because Git's quit operation can otherwise alter the stash list. Postflight verifies the removed active state and retained HEAD/index records and flags. Working-file preservation follows the requested Git operation; it is not a bytewise snapshot of every local or untracked file.

Ownership, receipts and limits#

SDK operation Native / ABI2 host method Inputs/effect
vcs_merge_state vcs.merge.state Selected built-in Git repository; actual blockers/revision
vcs_merge_plan vcs.merge.plan action, expectedRepository, expectedRevision; commit message and optional hooks
vcs_merge_commit vcs.merge.commit Matching commit request plus expectedPlanRevision
vcs_merge_quit vcs.merge.quit Matching quit request, empty message/no hooks, same guards

State/preview are read-only. Apply requires vcs.write, workspace.write and process.execute, shares the SDK workspace mutation group and retains noncancellable native ownership. The bridge keeps its existing 600-second wait. Typed contracts reject external VCS providers; plugin actions retain their separate permissions. The native VCS mutex serializes local callers. No C ABI, dependency, executable target or CyUI module changes are needed.

Intent receipts/message files are persistent workspace metadata under .cycode/merge-receipts, separate from temporary SDK task artifacts. Files are created exclusively before Git dispatch; they are not automatically removed or exported. A retained intent is evidence of a request, not proof of completion and not an automatic resume/Undo handle. Commit/quit have no editor Undo, automatic retry or rollback. External Git/editors/hooks can race preflight; no global lock or atomic compare-and-swap is claimed. Inspect actual state after uncertainty.

Each inspection uses a checked 45-second budget and 15-second subprocess timeouts; a running call can finish after the budget. The mutation timeout is 120 seconds, followed by a fresh postflight inspection budget. Listings are bounded to 8 MiB/ 100,000 index records, 2 MiB/2,048 changed paths and a 1 MiB stat. Merge-parent metadata supports 16 OIDs, with completion limited to one incoming parent. Metadata files are capped at 16 KiB, except 4 KiB HEAD/MERGE_HEAD, 32 KiB COMMIT_EDITMSG and 64 KiB MERGE_RR. The edit-message allowance covers Git's appended newline at the accepted request limit. Ordinary Git filesystem layouts are required. Exceeding bounds fails explicitly.

Validation and remaining scope#

Windows production compilation, MSVC /Zs and actual CyToolsCore/JSON Schema data checks are used during the existing Kaspersky native-execution suspension. Existing opt-in VCS fixture sources now specify parent/path/tree parsing, stale index/message rejection, intent-to-add blocking, dirty-buffer/index/disk preservation on quit, open metadata guards, configured hook failure/default suppression, exact-limit messages and actual raw committed parents/tree outcomes. These assertions have not run.

Actual Git/receipt/hook/filesystem/concurrency behavior, SDK/plugin/GUI keyboard/ themes/DPI and Linux/macOS remain unverified. Signed completion, autostash resolution, octopus completion, abort/reset recovery and interactive rebase remain outside this owner. See Testing, Validation and Roadmap.

Operation semantics follow Git's primary merge documentation, commit documentation and diff documentation. Object verification uses the documented raw cat-file output with replacement objects disabled.

pages.title: Reviewed cherry-pick and revert
pages.html:
Reviewed cherry-pick and revert#

Version control > Replay now provides single-commit cherry-pick, revert, continuation after conflict resolution and quit tracking. These actions share one native owner across desktop, CyTools/MCP and ABI2 plugins. The existing Merge and Conflicts views retain their separate responsibilities.

Choose and review a source#

Right-click a built-in Git History commit and choose Cherry-pick commit or Revert commit. The same view accepts a complete lowercase 40/64-character object ID. Branch names, shortened IDs, ranges, options and arbitrary argv are rejected. The object is verified as that exact commit, without replacement refs. Root/ordinary commits are supported; merge commits requiring mainline selection remain external. Source messages must be valid UTF-8 without NUL, up to 16 KiB.

Preview replay action binds repository/state identity, source object, source message/parents, paths/stat, previous HEAD, action and fixed arguments. Review source commit patch opens the common Diff review. These source changes describe the original commit, not a simulation of the resulting worktree. Revert reverses their effect. Context differences can produce conflicts, empty changes or failure.

Start requires a committed HEAD, no active operation, a clean tracked tree/index, ordinary index flags and closed repository documents. Untracked files are not added or included in an exact workspace snapshot; Git protects colliding paths. Previews reject changes that rewrite the active workspace's .cycode or Git administrative metadata. No force, reset, automatic stash or implicit push is used.

Conflicts, continue and quit#

After a failed cherry-pick/revert, refresh the actual state. A single pending CHERRY_PICK_HEAD or REVERT_HEAD exposes Review replay conflicts, actual conflict paths and separate blockers. Resolve/stage through the common conflict services, synchronize working files where needed and close repository documents.

Continue resolved replay reviews the whole current staged index, including unrelated staged changes. Review staged replay diff opens the shared Diff view. Continuation requires resolved conflicts, tracked files matching the index and ordinary index flags. The eventual committed tree must match this reviewed index exactly. Empty changes are not automatically skipped or forced into an empty commit; inspect Git's actual result.

Quit replay tracking previews an explicit Git cherry-pick/revert --quit. It clears operation bookkeeping while retaining working files and index entries; unsaved source buffers and unresolved index stages may remain. This does not restore pre-operation files. It differs from --abort/--skip/reset, which are not provided by this owner. Multiple-commit sequencers, rebase, concurrent operation markers, autostash and open administrative/managed receipt documents block the applicable workflow. External mainline/merge-commit replay remains external even when stopped.

Execution and outcomes#

Apply rechecks repository/state/plan revisions and index/flags before dispatch. A persistent, exclusive-created JSON intent is written under .cycode/merge-receipts/replay-*.json, sharing the common closed-metadata guard. It records the request and reviewed context before the command. An intent is not proof of success, an automatic resume token, a full backup or an editor Undo. It is not automatically removed or exported as a temporary SDK task artifact.

Commits are unsigned. Configured hooks, editor requests, rerere, automatic Git maintenance and Git transport are disabled. Trusted configured filters/merge drivers can still run project tools, including during read-only inspection. This is not an OS sandbox. Repository document closure protects native live buffers during writing operations; it does not coordinate other editors/processes.

The mutation has a 120-second native-owned process limit and bounded actual output. Actual exitCode, output, timedOut and truncated are retained. Conflicts can leave a valid pending operation with a nonzero process status. After success, postflight verifies removed operation state, exactly one new commit parent equal to reviewed previous HEAD, actual raw commit/tree/current index and synchronized tracked files. Continue additionally verifies the exact reviewed staged tree. Quit checks retained HEAD/index records/flags. Working-file retention on quit follows Git's operation semantics, not a bytewise snapshot of every file.

An inspectionError keeps uncertainty explicit even after exit zero. There is no automatic retry, rollback or success inference from a receipt. External Git/tools can race preflight; the native VCS mutex serializes local callers only, without global compare-and-swap. Inspect actual state before another mutation.

Shared contracts and bounds#

SDK operation Native / ABI2 method Effect
vcs_replay_state vcs.replay.state Actual kind/source/conflicts/index and start/continue/quit blockers
vcs_replay_plan vcs.replay.plan action + observed repository/state; commit ID for start, empty for continue/quit
vcs_replay_apply vcs.replay.apply Same reviewed request and expectedPlanRevision

State/plan have no write permissions. Apply requires vcs.write, workspace.write and process.execute, shares the existing workspace mutation group and retains noncancellable native ownership. The bridge waits up to 1,200 seconds to cover the repeated guarded inspections plus mutation/postflight; it does not release ownership merely on a cancellation request. Typed Git services reject alternative VCS providers, whose plugins retain their own actions/permissions.

The common inspector is reused rather than duplicating index/document snapshots. Each replay snapshot checks two common observations around actual marker reads. Common inspection budgets are 45 seconds, checked before each 15-second command; a running command can finish later. Other inspection commands have 15-second limits. Raw objects/index listings are bounded to 8 MiB, index to 100,000 records, changed paths to 2 MiB/2,048 records and stat to 1 MiB. Common metadata bounds and ordinary-layout requirements follow Merge workflow. No new dependency, executable target, CyUI module or C ABI is introduced.

Validation and remaining work#

Windows MSVC /Zs and production builds with BUILD_TESTING=OFF, actual SDK manifest loading and JSON Schema data checks are distinct from acceptance execution. Opt-in existing VCS fixture sources specify invalid IDs, stale/open-document guards, default hook suppression, successful cherry-pick/revert, conflict continuation and dirty-buffer/index/disk preservation on quit. These native assertions have not run during the existing Kaspersky suspension.

Actual Git/filter/driver/hook/receipt/filesystem/concurrency, SDK Runtime/plugin/ GUI/keyboard/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS remain unverified. Multi-commit/range/ mainline replay, interactive rebase, abort/skip recovery, configurable signing/ hooks and result-tree simulation remain outside this owner.

Semantics follow Git's primary cherry-pick, revert and diff-tree documentation.
