pages.title: Git submodules
pages.html:
Git submodules#

The Git Submodules tab inspects configured top-level modules in the selected repository. It joins .gitmodules paths with actual index gitlinks, then reads each available child's HEAD, branch and Git working-tree status. Spaces, UTF-8 and NUL-delimited records are preserved; object IDs support SHA-1 and SHA-256. It distinguishes absent checkouts, index conflicts, non-gitlink paths, matching or different commits and unavailable inspection. Unknown dirtiness remains null.

Choose Version control > Submodules, refresh, and filter by path/name/state. Each action opens a review section. Escape or Cancel submodule action discards that review without calling Git. Actions affect one selected module:

  • Register submodule uses git submodule init to register its URL locally.
  • Synchronize submodule URL uses git submodule sync for a registered module.
  • Update to recorded commit uses update --init --checkout --jobs=1. The destination is the commit recorded in the parent index, with a detached HEAD. This does not stage a new gitlink or commit the parent project.

Clone/fetch requires an explicit checkbox. Without it, update requires an existing checkout, passes --no-fetch and sets a Git protocol allow-list containing no protocol names (GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=:). The nonempty value survives Windows environment handling. With clone/fetch enabled, normal inherited Git protocol and credential configuration applies. URL values and raw Git configuration are not returned by the catalogue. Git hooks/helpers still execute with the user's normal privileges; this protocol control is not an OS network/process sandbox.

Add a module#

Choose Add submodule, enter a repository address and a new repository-relative folder, then choose Preview submodule addition. The destination parent must already exist. An optional logical name defaults to the path; an optional literal branch defaults to the remote HEAD. The form uses the current selected Git root. Changing fields, refreshing/changing repositories or cancelling clears the preview; cancelled or obsolete asynchronous results cannot reopen it.

The preview reads local metadata without clone/fetch or staging. It shows the normalized address/name/branch/destination and the effects of the action. remoteCommit stays null: Git resolves the remote commit during the later clone. Clone and stage submodule is a distinct action. It creates a checkout and stages .gitmodules plus the new gitlink, preserves unrelated staged entries and creates no commit. No source Undo, automatic retry or cleanup is provided for this action. Partial clones/configuration/index changes remain available after failure.

Both preview and execution require a new ordinary destination in the selected repository, unoccupied metadata/config names, no overlapping module path/name, and closed .gitmodules/destination documents. Existing .gitmodules must be a normal, unchanged tracked file. Staged/untracked/conflicted changes and hidden skip-worktree/assume-unchanged flags are refused. Its bytes are compared with the indexed blob, allowing normal CRLF/LF conversion; custom transformed metadata is unsupported. New metadata is allowed when the file is absent. Ignored destinations, existing empty folders/repositories and orphan metadata are not adopted or forced.

The separate preview revision captures normalized inputs, parent directory and metadata identities, relevant index/blob bytes, catalogue and parent HEAD/reference. The last guard also detects switching between parent branches with identical trees, since relative URLs depend on that context. The execution owner recalculates these guards before one git submodule add --name ... [--branch ...] -- URL PATH. External writers and remote branch changes remain outside an atomic transaction.

HTTPS/HTTP, SSH, Git and file URLs, SCP-style SSH and local/relative addresses use normal Git protocol/credential policy. Embedded user-info credentials, query tokens, fragments, custom helper-command addresses and checkout-history branch aliases are refused; use Git credentials or SSH authentication. No remote commit is invented or pinned by a local preview. Read queries deny Git transports, including lazy object fetch; trusted local Git helpers are not OS-sandboxed.

Edit a module URL or tracking branch#

Choose Edit submodule settings, select Repository address or Tracking branch, enter the new value, then choose Preview submodule settings. The separate Apply submodule action button requires that preview. Changing the value/type, refreshing, cancelling or switching repositories discards it; stale asynchronous responses do not restore it.

URL changes use fixed submodule set-url --quiet -- PATH URL argv. The shared address validator supports the same forms as addition and refuses embedded credentials, query tokens/fragments and helper-command URLs. Git may also synchronize local URL configuration according to its active-submodule rules. Relative addresses retain Git's parent/default-remote resolution semantics. These metadata operations deny Git transports; they do not clone or fetch.

Tracking branches use submodule set-branch --branch VALUE -- PATH. An empty value uses --default, removing the project setting in favor of remote HEAD; . uses the current parent branch name when a remote-tracking workflow later uses it. Literal names are checked with Git. Local/effective Git configuration overrides are reported and preserved. An already-configured project branch is shown without allowing a redundant action or inventing a process result. The existing Update to recorded commit still checks out the parent gitlink commit; editing the tracking branch does not introduce remote-tip checkout.

Both operations write project metadata without staging, committing, changing the checkout or creating an editor Undo transaction. Previously staged and unstaged .gitmodules edits may coexist: the file must have one ordinary stage-zero index entry without hidden flags/conflicts, but need not match its indexed blob. The observed working bytes and indexed content are captured separately. Other config records and their order, duplicates and valueless entries are retained and checked after applying; the .gitmodules index entry remains unchanged. Metadata documents must be closed. URL changes also require closed child documents and ordinary parent-owned absorbed metadata for a populated checkout. Independent/embedded or custom Git-directory layouts are unsupported for URL synchronization.

The preview shows the previous configured value, the new request, exact argv and effects. Sensitive/unsupported previous values stay null with previousRedacted; raw config is not returned. The revision binds the request, catalogue, metadata working/indexed bytes, parent HEAD/reference, directories and applicable Git pointer. It is rebuilt immediately before one action. Bounds are 16 KiB per native request, URL/value 4096 UTF-8 bytes, branch 256 bytes, 1 MiB .gitmodules, 20,000 config records, 2 MiB per query and a 30-second preflight. Postflight inspects the requested value, unrelated records, unchanged metadata index and checkout/pointer state. A process exit zero with an unconfirmed outcome still has catalogError. No atomic lock against external processes, automatic rollback or retry is provided.

Deinitialize a checkout#

Choose Review submodule deinitialization on a clean, registered checkout at the recorded gitlink commit. A local preview precedes the separate danger action Remove reviewed submodule checkout. It shows the number of tracked files to remove and explicitly states the retained data. Escape/cancel, refresh or a repository change discards the preview; cancelled/stale asynchronous results are not applied. No default shortcut performs this removal.

Execution uses only git submodule deinit --quiet -- PATH, without force, all, recursion or allowed Git transports. This removes the checkout and local module registration, while preserving .gitmodules, the parent gitlink and the absorbed repository under the parent's module metadata. It creates no commit/staging or editor Undo transaction. Reinitialization is a separate operation.

Both preview and action refuse tracked changes, untracked and ignored files, hidden skip-worktree/assume-unchanged flags, conflicted index entries and nested gitlinks (including unpopulated ones). This intentionally blocks ignored build outputs until the user preserves/manages them. Native documents under the module and .gitmodules must be closed. .gitmodules must be normally tracked and equal to its index blob, allowing CRLF/LF normalization. Independent repositories, embedded .git directories, custom Git-directory mappings, redirected metadata and non-parent-owned Git pointers are unsupported; no automatic absorption or migration is performed.

The preview revision additionally binds the complete child index/flags, .git pointer bytes, ordinary metadata/parent directory identities and metadata blob. At most 20,000 index records, 2 MiB per query, 256 directory levels and 30 seconds of preflight are accepted. Every check is repeated before the one Git action. Inspection disables optional Git locks and fsmonitor/untracked cache shortcuts for the complete cleanliness query. No filesystem-wide lock is claimed against external writers or later document opens.

The owner retains actual exit/timeout/output information, then inspects checkout and registration state, unchanged gitlink/metadata and retained repository identity. Git can report exit zero despite incomplete directory removal; that becomes a catalogError instead of a success notification. Partial outcomes are retained for inspection, with no automatic cleanup, rollback or retry.

Native ownership and guards#

GitSubmoduleModel parses bounded config key\nvalue\0 and ls-files --stage -z records and constructs fixed argv lists. Engine::gitSubmodules owns real Git queries/actions through the existing native process service and VCS mutex. The GUI, SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugins use this same owner; there is no Python repository model, new dependency, executable target or CyUI module. UI colors/styles/filtering use CyUI Core and English/French controls.

A mutation requires the observed repository identity and catalogue revision. The revision fingerprints .gitmodules, effective parent settings, selected gitlinks, child HEAD/branch/status, directory identities and private child repository/config identities. It is recalculated before acting. Linked/nested repository selection keeps the existing workspace boundaries. Symlinks/reparse points, absolute/traversal/ metadata paths, duplicate or overlapping module paths, invalid records and unresolved gitlinks are refused. .gitmodules must be saved and reconciled with open buffers.

Update refuses reported tracked/untracked child changes and any open child document at preflight. Original branches/commits remain Git-owned; there is no IDE source Undo for checkout. Ignored files follow Git's own checkout rules and are not part of the reported dirty check. No filesystem-wide lock is acquired against external Git processes, hooks, later file edits or another app instance. These are observed state/preflight guards rather than an atomic transaction over all external writers.

There is no force, recursive update, remote-tip update, merge/rebase or custom update command in this service. The explicit --checkout overrides configured custom update modes. Local URL registration/synchronization still follows Git's semantics. Failures/timeouts may leave changed configuration or a partial checkout; refresh and review that state. The response retains actual process status and a new catalogue, or a separate catalogError. The owner invalidates the path index; UI document reconciliation keeps the existing conflict/dirty-buffer protections.

Bounds: 16 KiB native request, 64 configured modules, 1 MiB .gitmodules, 2 MiB per command output, 4096 UTF-8 bytes per relative path, 512 bytes per module name/ branch. Complete catalogue work has a 30-second deadline after repository selection; addition-preview inspection has its own 30-second deadline and at most 256 parent directory levels, URL/path 4096 bytes, name 512 bytes and branch 256 bytes; an action has 180 seconds. SDK waiting allows 600 seconds for the native inspection, revalidation, action and refresh. Git terminal prompting is disabled. The operation is noncancellable while native process ownership is retained; timeout is reported after the existing process owner handles termination, with no automatic retry.

SDK/MCP and plugins#

vcs_submodules / vcs.submodules returns repository, identity, revision and typed entries. Entries expose name/path/workspace root, expected commit, actual HEAD/branch, registration/checkout flags, nullable dirty state, status/error and opaque directory/repository identities. It is a read operation with no mutation permission or exclusive group. Select a module from its actual returned path.

vcs_submodule_init, vcs_submodule_sync and vcs_submodule_update map to the corresponding vcs.submodule.* methods. For example, after an actual inspection:

json
{"repository":"project","provider":"git","path":"vendor/math", "expectedRepository":"observed-repository-identity", "expectedRevision":"observed-catalogue-revision","fetch":false}

fetch belongs only to update. Each existing-module mutation requires path, expectedRepository and expectedRevision; repository defaults to the workspace root. Paths refer to persistent project repositories, not SDK task artifacts. SDK mutations require vcs.write, workspace.write and process.execute, use the existing workspace mutation group and declare noncancellable behavior. These typed methods always target built-in Git; other providers retain their own actions. ABI2 host->request exports the same four methods and enforces all three mutation permissions, including rejection from read-only provider callbacks. C ABI unchanged.

vcs_submodule_add_plan / vcs.submodule.addPlan additionally takes url, path, optional name/branch and observed expectedRepository/expectedRevision. It is noncancellable local inspection with no mutation permissions/group. Its result contains repository/identity/catalogRevision/revision, normalized request, workspace root, bounded argv, createsCheckout/stagesGitmodules/stagesGitlink/ mayContactRemote flags and remoteCommit:null.

Pass the same inputs and expectedPlanRevision from that preview to vcs_submodule_add / vcs.submodule.add. It uses the three mutation permissions, workspace mutation group and noncancellable native ownership, returning the same actual process/catalogue result as other submodule writes. ABI2 exports both methods with the same read/mutation distinction. No URL/repository is a temporary SDK input artifact and no Python Git owner is added.

vcs_submodule_deinit_plan / vcs.submodule.deinitPlan takes the observed repository/catalogue guards and path. Its typed result adds the actual entry, trackedFiles, fixed argv and explicit removesCheckout/unregistersLocally/ preservesGitlink/preservesGitmodules/preservesRepository/mayContactRemote effects. Pass its revision as expectedPlanRevision, with the same guards/path, to vcs_submodule_deinit / vcs.submodule.deinit. Preview has no mutation permission or exclusive group; execution uses all three permissions and the workspace mutation group. Both are noncancellable while the existing native owner runs. ABI2 exports the same methods without changing the C ABI or adding a Python owner.

vcs_submodule_settings_plan / vcs.submodule.settingsPlan takes the observed repository/catalogue guards, path, setting (url or branch) and value. The typed plan returns request/entry, previousValue/previousRedacted/hasConfiguredValue, hasLocalBranchOverride/alreadyConfigured, argv, writesGitmodules/ maySynchronizeLocalUrl and false staging/checkout/transport effects. Apply the same inputs plus expectedPlanRevision through vcs_submodule_settings / vcs.submodule.settings. Preview has no mutation permission/group; application requires VCS/workspace/process permissions and the workspace mutation group. Both retain noncancellable native process ownership. ABI2 exports both methods.

Verification and remaining work#

MSVC /Zs checks the pure parser/argv planner, Engine, GUI, routing/plugin code and regression sources without linking/running test objects or executables. Assertions specify NUL/Unicode/newline paths, conflict stages, SHA formats, duplicate/overlapping paths, limits, disabled unsafe modes and exact single-module argv. The actual SDK manifest loader/schema data checks validate 200 operations, typed null/actual state, required guards, permission/cancellation contracts and the real pure parameter adapter. Addition assertions extend the same pure/VCS fixture sources with fixed argv, address/name/branch bounds, read-only previews, context/parent/index/metadata changes, hidden index flags and open-document rejection. They are syntax-checked only. These checks do not execute Git, filesystem guards or async GUI behavior. Deinitialization assertions extend the existing sources with fixed quiet argv, normal index/flag checks, nested/conflicted rejection, ignored/untracked/hidden files, open documents, unrecorded commits, stale preview and successful retention postconditions. These assertions are compiled with /Zs, not executed. Settings assertions cover shared URL validation, exact branch/default/dot argv, unrelated configuration records/order, staged/unstaged preservation, stale parent branch/preview, hidden flags, open documents, local overrides, unsupported old URL redaction and actual URL/branch/default outcomes. They are also source-only.

Real local/remote clone/fetch/checkout/sync, partial failures, transport restrictions, external races, SDK/plugin Runtime, keyboard/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky native-test suspension. Permanent removal, local branch-override editing, recursive bulk workflows and submodule-specific source Undo are not implemented. Select a checked-out module as a repository to inspect its own configured children. See Validation and Testing.

Primary references: git-submodule, Git config output, Git protocol allow-list, Git deinitialization implementation, Git transport implementation.

pages.title: Working files after Git conflict resolution
pages.html:
Working files after Git conflict resolution#

The conflict resolver stages selected versions without changing local files. Version control > Conflicts > Synchronize working file adds the explicit next step: install exact staged bytes or remove a working file already absent from the index. Binary files never enter editor buffers or JSON text strings.

Review, apply and Undo#

Choose a reviewed conflict path or enter another repository-relative file. Copy staged bytes requires one normal stage-zero blob; unresolved paths, symlinks and gitlinks are refused. Remove untracked working file explicitly requires no index entry. Close affected text documents and documents inside .cycode/trash. Preview working-file action shows original/replacement byte counts and whether open documents block the action. Closing them requires a fresh preview. Parent directories must already exist.

This copies raw staged bytes, without Git attributes, filters, textconv or line-ending conversion. A CRLF file can become LF when its blob contains LF. The Git index is retained. The latest GUI receipt offers Undo working-file synchronization. It requires unchanged installed content/permissions or expected absence, an intact original backup and closed affected text/trash documents. Current content moves to another trash entry before restoration through the existing resource service. Undo of a creation also retains displaced bytes. It never changes the Git index or silently overwrites newer content. After successful Undo, the original backup reference is cleared because that payload is back at its path; the displaced backup remains.

Git retains at most 16 in-memory receipts; the resource owner retains at most 32 issued plans. Other file operations can evict old receipts. Previews expire after ten minutes, with at most 64 MiB of retained binary preview bytes; older payload previews can be invalidated to stay within that budget. Persistent backups have no automatic expiry. Direct receipt Undo does not survive restart.

Open project trash displays original/displaced payloads after restarting too. Restore through the existing reviewed resource operation to an empty original or alternative destination. If the original path is occupied, preserve that newer file through a separate move/trash operation first; restoration never replaces it.

It reads local blob sizes/bytes with cat-file, with fsmonitor, prompts, lazy fetch and transport disabled. It performs no Git mutation, checkout command or configured hook/filter request.

Resources owns ordinary-path/disk/permission guards, private binary payloads and persistent trash/install journals. It reuses exclusive moves and adds exclusive binary creation (Windows CREATE_NEW; POSIX O_CREAT/O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW). Entries live under .cycode/trash/<receipt>/. The existing five-field record.json identifies an original payload; install.json records installation intent before source moves. The backup and installation/restoration are separate filesystem moves. They are not globally atomic or a compare-and-swap against external writers. state: partial retains available payloads and returns an error/backup references. pages.title: Multiple Git repositories and linked worktrees
pages.html:
Multiple Git repositories and linked worktrees#

The native Engine now accepts an explicit Git repository inside the workspace. Version control offers Automatic (active file) and a discovered repository selector. Automatic mode follows the nearest ordinary .git directory or gitdir pointer within the workspace; a more specific external-provider mapping still takes precedence. An explicit Git folder is now stored with its observed marker identity in the existing per-workspace, per-instance desktop session. Restoration requires the same ordinary repository identity; missing/replaced repositories fall back to Automatic with a visible warning. Automatic mode and the workspace root are distinct saved choices. Old sessions remain valid. The Restore last workspace session option also controls restoring this selection. This does not change .cycode/vcs.json or the SDK's explicit per-request repository selection.

Status, index actions, history, branches, remotes, stashes, text conflicts and issued hunk previews use the same selection. Paths in documents and returned status remain workspace-relative; only the Git argv uses repository-relative paths. Hunk application rejects previews from another repository or identity. Repository-wide actions require the selected directory to be the actual Git root, rather than requiring that root to equal the workspace. Unrelated repositories' dirty buffers do not block the selected Git working-tree action.

Discovery is explicit/background UI work, not a recursive scan on every frame. It executes no Git process or provider callback. Bounds are 20,000 visited directories, 200,000 inspected entries, depth 32 and 256 repositories; truncation and up to 16 errors are reported. Common metadata/generated/cache directories (.git, .cycode, runtime, data, node_modules, .vs, .idea, .cache, target, Binaries, Intermediate and Saved) and redirected directories are skipped. A repository under an excluded folder can still be selected by activating its file. Discovery recognises both submodule and linked-worktree pointer files; this does not implement submodule lifecycle management.

Linked worktree controls#

Version control > Worktrees uses Git's complete NUL-delimited porcelain catalogue, including paths/lock reasons containing newlines. Entries show branch, detached HEAD, primary/current, lock and pruning metadata. Catalogue bounds are 2 MiB and 256 records; incomplete, duplicate or unsupported fields fail explicitly.

  • Create a new local branch, check out an existing local branch, or detach at a verified commit. The new directory must not exist and its parent must already exist inside the workspace. Git enforces branch availability; there is no force, branch reset or remote-tracking guess.
  • Lock/unlock another available linked checkout using Git's administrative lock. This is not a source-file lock. An optional lock reason is limited to 512 bytes.
  • Remove a reviewed clean linked checkout after a desktop confirmation. The branch remains. The main checkout, selected checkout, workspace root/ancestors, .git/.cycode destinations, locked/unavailable trees and open destination documents are refused. Normal Git remove also refuses tracked modifications, untracked files and submodules; no force or automatic pruning is offered.
  • Open a listed checkout in a new application window using the existing launcher. External paths are catalogue-only: their existence is not probed and this workspace cannot create/remove/lock/unlock them. Opening is an explicit action.

Source/admin/common-directory identities and a catalogue revision guard every mutation. The revision is an optimistic concurrency token, not authentication or a cryptographic integrity claim. Target/parent identities are checked again before dispatch. An exclusive new-directory reservation is removed after failure only if it is still the same empty directory. Nonempty/partial checkouts and any branch Git already created are retained for inspection.

Reviewed move and link repair#

Move linked worktree selects another available, unlocked linked checkout. Enter a new workspace-relative folder whose parent already exists, choose Preview worktree maintenance, then Apply worktree maintenance. The main checkout, selected checkout, metadata paths, overlapping registered locations, occupied destinations, redirected directories and open native source/destination documents are refused. Open common worktree-metadata documents also block either action. Git uses a directory rename; local, staged, untracked and ignored files accompany the checkout without checkout, staging or commit. Cross- filesystem copying is not implemented, and no force is used. Submodule index entries or retained submodule metadata block maintenance.

Repair moved worktree is available on a missing registered linked path. Select the existing folder that was moved manually. Its intact .git pointer must identify this common repository's ordinary worktrees/<id> metadata, with the reciprocal backlink still naming the missing old path. A changed/corrupt or independent pointer is not adopted or guessed. Missing old parent directories are supported; the existing ancestor identities are captured. Request repair from an ordinary main checkout inside the workspace. Moving/copying the main repository, bare/separate-Git-dir layouts and arbitrary damaged metadata remain outside this supported repair workflow.

Git repair can inspect/update other linked checkouts even with one destination argument. Accordingly every registered checkout must be inside the workspace; all other checkouts must be available, unlocked and have correct ordinary reciprocal links. Their native documents must be closed. The common worktree directory is audited for unlisted/orphan metadata. The preview lists every verified linked path; an external, additional missing, locked, redirected or unreviewed record blocks the whole action. Git uses absolute linking policy; repair can normalize otherwise-correct relative links in the reviewed set.

Both actions use a separate preview revision binding request, catalogue, directory identities, affected pointer/HEAD/index bytes and sibling link/index fingerprints. Editing inputs, refreshing/cancelling or changing repositories discards the preview; stale asynchronous replies cannot apply it. The native VCS owner rechecks all guards and closed documents immediately before one fixed Git argv. Git transport protocols and terminal prompting are disabled. There is no source Undo, automatic cleanup/retry/rollback or filesystem-wide transaction.

Postflight checks actual source absence, retained directory identity at the destination, unchanged affected HEAD/index, reciprocal links and fresh catalogue branch/commit. Repair also checks the reviewed sibling identities, HEAD/index fingerprints and reciprocal links. Exit zero with an unconfirmed result remains catalogError and produces no success notification. Partial outcomes stay visible for inspection. These are observed guards, not a lock on external writers or other app instances.

Bounds: 16 KiB native request, 4096 UTF-8 bytes per portable relative input path, 256 directory levels/worktree records, 200,000 index mode records, 2 MiB per Git query and 64 MiB total reviewed index bytes. Metadata reads are bounded even if a file grows while being read. Local maintenance inspection has an observed 45-second budget; each command has at most 15 seconds, and apply has 180 seconds. Selected-repository/catalogue queries retain their existing separate bounds.

Native commands use argv, literal pathspecs, bounded output and deadlines (180 seconds for add, 30 for remove/lock/unlock; inspection calls have separate 15-second bounds). Git owns its checkout/index/administrative locks and may run configured hooks. There is no shell assembled from project data.

Each Engine serializes VCS requests. Git coordinates its own cross-process locks; the IDE's open-document check covers this Engine, not all independent processes. A transport error/timeout can follow partial Git work: refresh and inspect before retrying. A post-operation catalogue error is reported separately from the command result. OS crashes and arbitrary filesystem races are not a filesystem transaction.

Shared SDK contract#

All typed Git operations accept optional repository (workspace-relative folder, default ".") and expectedRepository (the observed context identity). They always select the built-in Git provider. File parameters remain workspace-relative. Missing explicit folders fail instead of falling back to another root.

Operation Purpose Permissions
vcs_repositories Workspace repository discovery without Git/provider execution None
vcs_worktrees Selected Git catalogue and revision None
vcs_worktree_add / vcs_worktree_remove Guarded checkout creation/removal vcs.write, workspace.write, process.execute
vcs_worktree_lock / vcs_worktree_unlock Guarded Git administrative lock vcs.write
vcs_worktree_plan Local move/repair preview and issued observed revision None
vcs_worktree_move / vcs_worktree_repair Reviewed directory move / administrative link repair vcs.write, workspace.write, process.execute

Mutations require expectedRevision from vcs_worktrees and are noncancellable once dispatched. The real CyToolsCore scheduler retains the existing workspace-mutations exclusive group; transport waits up to 600 seconds. There is no second Python Git implementation. New maintenance operations require observed expectedRepository, expectedRevision, path/destination and, for execution, expectedPlanRevision. The preview also takes action (move or repair); apply derives it from the method. Its typed result returns request/entry, fixed argv, checkedRoots and explicit move/repair/local-file/index/transport effects. ABI2 exports catalogue, preview, add/remove/move/repair and lock/unlock with the same permission distinction; read-only provider callbacks cannot invoke mutations. C ABI is unchanged. Typed worktree methods always select built-in Git; external providers keep their own descriptor/action contract. Repository-redirect environment variables (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES) must be unset for the built-in Git service; the application does not alter them.

Verification and remaining work#

Windows production compilation, MSVC syntax-only checks, real SDK manifest/schema checks and source/secret checks are recorded in Validation. New assertions extend the existing opt-in cycode_vcs_tests target, not a new executable: NUL parsing, nested path translation, unrelated dirty buffers, cross-repository hunk rejection and actual nested index-conflict rejection, catalogue revisions, lock/removal guards, untracked-file preservation, retained branches and external-worktree refusal. Move/repair assertions add portable path/command boundaries, read-only preview, stale preview/parent identities, occupied destinations, open documents, staged/ untracked/ignored payload preservation, manual relocation, external/orphan/sibling guards and retained index/link outcomes. Session assertions cover automatic/root/ explicit selection, version/identity/path bounds and legacy compatibility. Their native execution remains suspended during the Kaspersky interruption.

GUI selection/focus/scrolling, themes/densities/DPI, actual worktree Git execution, hooks, cross-instance behavior and Linux/macOS remain unexecuted. No new runtime acceptance is claimed. Still pending: cross-window open-document coordination, arbitrary external-root writes, worktree removal with populated submodules, worktree pruning, arbitrary main/bare/custom-layout repair, credential UI, interactive history editing and complex binary/delete/rename conflicts.

Configured-module inspection and guarded init/sync/recorded-commit update now have a separate shared service and view, with pending runtime acceptance; see Git submodules.

Command semantics follow the official Git worktree documentation and Git rev-parse documentation. The Git repair implementation explains the complete linked-set audit; index mode formatting provides bounded submodule detection without printing every path.

pages.title: Set next statement
pages.html:
Set next statement#

CyCode can ask a capable debug adapter for valid destinations in the selected frame's source, then move that thread's next instruction to one explicit choice. This is DAP gotoTargets / goto, guarded by supportsGotoTargetsRequest. The intervening code is skipped, and moving backward can repeat side effects. This does not implement Run to cursor, resume the program or undo source edits.

Desktop#

Choose Run > Set next statement, the same Find Action command, or the action in Debugger > Execution controls. The Next statement tab opens a query at the selected frame's line. It shows that frame's source path/name/reference; enter another Destination line and optional Destination column in that same source, then choose Read next-statement targets. Lines/columns are one-based; column 0 in the form means unspecified and is omitted from the request. Columns count UTF-16 code units, rather than visual indentation/display columns.

Select an actual returned destination and choose Set next statement here. There is no automatic first selection or execution on row selection. Changing the form clears its previous choices. A real empty result is displayed explicitly. The shared target table preserves stable issued row IDs, actual labels/start positions and delayed full-label/instruction-reference tooltips. This UI does not accept an arbitrary second source or infer that another open tab matches the selected frame. It does not validate that an edited source still matches the compiled program; actual valid destinations remain the adapter's responsibility.

Common owner and lifecycle#

DebugTargets replaces the step-in-only implementation with one common native catalogue implementation. Separate step-in/goto instances retain independent counters and markers; StepInTargets remains a source-compatible alias selecting the original default family. The shared table also replaces duplicate row logic. There is one DAP worker, no new executable/dependency/CyUI module and no C ABI change.

Both query and execution require explicit observed sessionGeneration, stopGeneration, threadId and frameId. They must match the current inspected pause and actual selected frame. Query inputs add line and optional column; caller paths, source descriptors, raw target IDs, arbitrary commands and stepping options are rejected. The native owner filters the actual frame source descriptor and passes bounded opaque adapterData back to that same adapter when present. That opaque data remains private and is compared again before issuing a response and before dispatching a selected target. A changed source cannot silently reuse a captured response. Public source metadata contains only path/name/reference.

A query replaces the goto catalogue, even within the same pause. Each returned target has an issued string ID, the actual label and required actual line, optional range coordinates and instructionPointerReference. Signed int32 adapter IDs stay private. Handles expire on refresh, resume/new stop/invalidation/memory events, frame/thread/capability/session changes or execution submission. Neither catalogue nor process instruction references are persisted. debug_status.gotoTargetCatalog is the current issued catalogue ID, or ""; stepInTargetCatalog stays independent.

Executing a choice consumes both families' catalogues before sending exactly one DAP goto. lastExecution.method is debug.gotoTarget; its public arguments contain the issued handle and captured frame/thread, never the raw adapter ID. singleThread and granularity are not accepted or injected from UI preferences. The existing applying/accepted/unconfirmed outcomes and execution epoch preserve a new stopped event that arrives before acknowledgement. There is no automatic retry, continuation, reverse operation or source Undo.

If acknowledgement arrives first, the old stack is invalidated and pendingStop is set. The public state remains stopped, with empty inspection and zero selected thread/frame; no resumed program state is fabricated. Debugger operations other than stopping the session are blocked, while status/profile/adapters remain readable. Actual stopped/continued/termination events remain authoritative. Invalidation events preserve the pending wait. A missing stopped event after 15 seconds marks the outcome unconfirmed and leaves the wait blocked; it does not inspect stale references, resume, retry, kill or disconnect the program automatically. Wait for the adapter's event or explicitly stop the debugging session.

SDK/MCP and plugins#

debug_goto_targets maps to debug.gotoTargets. For an observed session 3, stop 7, selected thread 11 and frame 9:

json

json

ABI2 plugins use the same methods/guards through host->request. Source references belong to the debug session, not SDK task artifacts, and are not staged or copied by the SDK.

Limits: 4 KiB public request, coordinates 1..10000000 on input, 64 KiB selected frame source descriptor including adapter data, 128 destinations / 512 KiB adapter reply, 4096 UTF-8 bytes per label and 8192 per nonempty instruction reference. Malformed/duplicate signed IDs, NUL/oversized text, missing destination lines, invalid or reversed explicit ranges fail without publishing a partial catalogue. Returned coordinates preserve DAP integer bounds 0..9007199254740991; zero remains unknown and missing optional fields remain absent. Extra adapter target fields are ignored. Distinct IDs with duplicate labels remain distinct.

MSVC /Zs checks the common native implementation, worker/UI/SDK plugin exports and regression sources without linking or running native tests. Assertions specify frame/source/context changes, opaque-data isolation/comparison, virtual sources, pending-state rejection, signed/issued identity isolation, bounds, exact goto wire fields, actual empty results, refresh/expiry and GUI option capture. Existing step-in and execution-epoch assertions remain in the same debugger target. Actual CyToolsCore loading and schema data examples validate all 185 operations, typed goto/pending outcomes, field isolation, permissions and translated controls. See Validation for completed build/source checks.

Actual adapters and VM behavior, unsupported destinations, event/deadline races, SDK/plugin runtime, keyboard/scrolling/themes/DPI and graphical acceptance remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky native-test suspension. Linux/macOS compilation and execution remain pending. Run to cursor now has a separate temporary-breakpoint/Continue/restoration workflow with pending runtime acceptance. Full per-thread non-stop debugging remains separate work.

pages.title: Call and type hierarchies
pages.html:
Call and type hierarchies#

Navigate > Call hierarchy / Type hierarchy inspects the symbol under the caret. View > Hierarchy reopens the dockable panel. Both commands are also available in the command palette and editable keymaps:

Profile Call hierarchy Type hierarchy
Rider (IntelliJ-style) Ctrl+Alt+H Ctrl+H
Visual Studio Ctrl+Alt+K Menu/palette; user-assignable
VS Code Shift+Alt+H Menu/palette; user-assignable

These defaults follow the official Rider keymap, Visual Studio shortcuts and VS Code C++ navigation. They describe these profiles, not every keymap supported by those products.

Desktop workflow#

Place the caret on a function or type in an editable workspace source document, then inspect it. The panel switches between callers/callees or base/derived types. Expand a row to request that branch from the original language server. Only the first root expands initially. Further descendants load when opened; recursive relationships and depth limits remain visible rather than recursing indefinitely.

Select a row to inspect its call sites. Open symbol, double click or Enter on a focused tree row navigates to its declaration through the existing UTF-16-aware document/SDK navigation service. Select a call site to visit that individual call: incoming sites are in the caller, while outgoing sites are in the expanded source function, not in the callee's declaration. Opening a clean file does not itself invalidate the browsing session.

Refresh at caret starts a new hierarchy from the current document/cursor. It is also the recovery path after edits, filesystem notifications or a backend change. The panel uses CyUI Core controls/theme roles, stable nested tree IDs, DPI-scaled dimensions and EN/FR messages. It adds no UI-library copy or dependency. This is a read-only graph inspection; source text, editor Undo/Redo, saves and refactoring transactions keep their existing owners.

Actual language-server contract#

The common LanguageService advertises static call/type hierarchy support and checks callHierarchyProvider/typeHierarchyProvider before sending a request, including for C++ and C#. Status exposes both methods for command enablement. No disabled backend is enabled by inspecting a hierarchy. The configured server may start on the explicit request through its ordinary owner.

Preparation uses textDocument/prepareCallHierarchy or prepareTypeHierarchy. Expansion uses callHierarchy/incomingCalls or outgoingCalls, and typeHierarchy/supertypes or subtypes. The native cache preserves the server's opaque data and exact item on follow-up requests. GUI, SDK and native plugins receive only issued session/node IDs and validated display locations; callers cannot inject a URI, opaque data or a server command.

The source must be a workspace document with expectedRevision. Descendants/sites can use workspace locations or, when includeExternal is true, already registered read-only SDK roots. Unsupported metadata/non-file URIs and unregistered external locations are omitted with an explicit count. Starting at an SDK/untitled document, arbitrary external browsing, Blueprint calls, runtime/dynamic call completeness and unsupported server methods are not implemented by this view.

This uses the official LSP call hierarchy and type hierarchy contracts. Results depend on the enabled server, project configuration and index; there is no text-search or inferred fallback presented as a semantic hierarchy.

Sessions, bounds and concurrency#

  • Eight native sessions, five-minute lifetime from preparation, 8 MiB combined payload; at most 512 nodes / 2 MiB per session, including raw and public data.
  • At most 2 MiB per server response, 256 returned relationships and 256 call sites per relationship. A raw item is limited to 64 KiB; names/details to 4/16 KiB. Truncation and omitted locations are exposed; malformed data fails explicitly.
  • A desktop session caches up to 64 branches / 8 MiB, draws at most 4,096 rows per frame and limits a visible chain to 32 levels. Start from another symbol to continue after reaching a limit.

Sessions pin document identity/revision, native document-event generation, workspace notification revision and backend epoch. Edits, saves, closes, reloads, conflicts and resource/recovery changes invalidate the context. Status checks perform no LSP request or synchronous filesystem rescan. The visible panel polls validity at most twice a second and checks again before cached navigation. Expansion verifies the context before and after the server response.

Cache additions are staged under the Engine lock. Concurrent expansions reject conflicting issued-node additions so a returned ID cannot silently refer to a different server item; retry the branch. Queries release the document lock while waiting on the existing bounded language worker. Deadlines and the 32-request per-backend queue remain owned by LanguageService. New hierarchy-specific cancellation is not provided.

Validity reflects events already observed by the application. Notification lag, external unopened-file changes on polling backends and the language server's asynchronous index can still affect results; status does not prove a complete or synchronously refreshed call graph. Explicit refresh remains necessary.

SDK and plugin surface#

language_hierarchy_prepare accepts path, zero-based UTF-16 position, expectedRevision, kind (call/type) and optional includeExternal. language_hierarchy_expand accepts sessionId, issued item and direction (incoming/outgoing or supertypes/subtypes for the corresponding session kind). language_hierarchy_status accepts sessionId and returns valid/reason, including valid:false for unknown/expired sessions.

All three are read-only real CyToolsCore operations without mutation permissions or an exclusive mutation group. The existing native plugin JSON host request exports the same three language.* methods, without changing the C ABI or exporting STL/ImGui objects. Native plugins retain their existing trusted-code boundaries. Paths are persistent workspace/issued SDK references, not imported task artifacts.

Acceptance#

See Validation for checks actually completed in this milestone. Pure range/item/routing and keymap regression assertions extend the existing opt-in cycode_tests target; no new executable/runner is introduced. Current local verification uses MSVC /Zs and production builds with tests disabled. Actual LSP preparation/expansion, plugin/MCP execution, cache concurrency/expiry, keyboard/scroll/focus, themes/densities/DPI and Linux/macOS remain unexecuted while the Kaspersky interruption is unresolved. Compilation and schema examples do not establish runtime acceptance or complete support by every language backend.

pages.title: Image previews
pages.html:
Image previews#

CyCode opens image files in read-only document tabs using CyUI::Images and its automatically selected Canvas dependency. Tabs share the normal docking, detachment, close/reopen and next/previous-document actions with code editors. There is no image decoder or renderer copied from CyUI.

Open an image from Project, Go to file/Search Everywhere, File > Open image, drag-and-drop, or --open within the active workspace. A positional image path starts CyCode with that image's parent folder as its workspace. Explicit file selection/drop also permits an image outside the workspace: only that canonical file receives read access. This does not extend Engine document permissions or permit writes outside the workspace. Reopening a tracked external image uses the same selected source; reloading rejects a retargeted symlink.

The view provides:

  • Wheel zoom around the pointer; middle-button or Space+drag panning.
  • Fit image, actual pixels (100%), zoom buttons and double-click to fit.
  • Theme-aware transparency checkerboard and optional nearest-neighbor sampling.
  • Dimensions, displayed zoom, input file size and pixel coordinates under the pointer.
  • Explicit reload, preserving the previous valid preview if decoding/upload fails.

Formats and scope#

Format Preview
PNG, JPEG/JFIF, BMP, TGA RGBA preview; PNG transparency and progressive JPEG included
WebP Static lossy/lossless images with transparency
GIF First frame, with a visible first-frame label; animation playback remains pending
PSD Flattened/composited image; no layer editing
Radiance HDR Converted to 8-bit display using stb_image's default conversion; original bytes unchanged
Softimage PIC, binary PGM/PPM Supported by stb_image
SVG Remains editable XML; no raster preview yet
TIFF, ICO, DDS, AVIF, EXR, animated WebP No preview yet; binary formats show an explicit unsupported message

This is a viewer, without painting, cropping transactions, image exports, EXIF orientation transforms or ICC color management. Code/language services, VCS, Engine text documents and the MCP text API remain separate. Save, text editing, document find and breakpoints are disabled for image tabs. File/source permissions are checked before reading, including again on the decoder worker.

Ownership, responsiveness and dependencies#

The application owns binary input, decoding and OpenGL texture lifetimes. One worker decodes off the UI thread; at most one completed RGBA result waits for consumption. Reload/close cancels stale requests. GPU upload and deletion run on the UI's existing shared OpenGL context. Texture deletion is deferred until the next frame so detached platform viewports finish using the previous draw lists. CPU pixel buffers are released after upload.

Inputs are bounded to 64 MiB, 32768 pixels per side and 64 x 1024 x 1024 pixels (including 8192 x 8192 textures). GPU limits are checked before allocation, and open previews have a 512 MiB texture budget. Oversized/invalid files report an error instead of being passed to the code editor.

app/dependencies.lock.json pins stb and libwebp by full commit and archive SHA-256. Only webpdecoder is linked; encoders, demux/mux tools and viewers are not built. Both decoders are desktop-only dependencies: --core-only does not fetch or build them. MIT/Unlicense (stb) and libwebp's BSD/patent/authorship notices are preserved under app/licenses. No additional decoder DLL or Python package is needed at run time.

Validation#

Workspace sessions now retain Fit mode or manual zoom/image-space center plus pixelated filtering. Settings wait for decoding/viewport availability, and changed image dimensions fall back to Fit. External grants do not restore. New native/ graphical acceptance is pending; see Workspace sessions.

The images CTest uses real PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF/BMP/TGA/PSD/HDR/PGM/PPM fixtures, Unicode paths, malformed/oversized inputs, cancellation and actual app views with headless ImGui frames. Its injected renderer verifies RGBA handoff, draw-list texture IDs, delayed deletion, reload failures, zoom/pan, image/text command routing and workspace/external-file permissions. The rendering checks cover six themes, English/French and 100/150/200% DPI.

Native OpenGL upload/display and detached multi-monitor image windows have not been run in this session, to avoid reopening the desktop app. The renderer adapter is compiled for Windows and its resource contract is exercised headlessly; this is not evidence of GPU screenshot acceptance. Linux/macOS remain unexecuted.

pages.title: Instruction breakpoints
pages.html:
Instruction breakpoints#

The Debugger Instruction breakpoints tab uses the shared native DAP owner, SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugin service. It requires supportsInstructionBreakpoints from the active adapter. No dependency, CyUI module, process owner or new test executable is added. Actual adapter/GUI acceptance remains pending.

Desktop workflow#

Pause the target and read Disassembly. Right-click an address and choose Add instruction breakpoint, or Copy instruction address. The add action requires the result's original session/pause and rejects rows marked invalid. Late disassembly results do not repopulate an expired inspection. Address-scoped popup IDs prevent a refreshed row from silently becoming another target.

The instruction tab also accepts an explicit adapter instruction/memory reference with a byte offset; Use selected frame instruction copies the actual frame reference. New instruction replacement list copies the entire last known configuration into an editable draft. Adding the first entry starts such a draft, so an existing list is not silently dropped. Rows retain stable local IDs while others are added/removed. Edit references, offsets, enabled flags, conditions and hit conditions, review the whole list, then Apply instruction breakpoints. Typing or closing the tab does not submit a change.

Clear instruction breakpoints explicitly sends an empty list. Resuming, changing pause/session, inspection invalidation or successful application discards the draft. A competing configuration revision disables the old draft until a new list is prepared. These actions affect the debuggee and are separate from source-document Undo.

Native and SDK contract#

debug_instruction_breakpoints / debug.instructionBreakpoints requires process.execute and all four fields:

json
{  "sessionGeneration": 3,  "stopGeneration": 7,  "expectedRevision": 4,  "breakpoints": [    {"instructionReference": "adapter-reference", "offset": 0,     "enabled": true, "condition": "counter > 1", "hitCondition": "3"}  ]}

Use observed debug_status generations and instructionBreakpointRevision, with references reviewed for that target. Native/plugin requests also require explicit context; an omitted stop is not silently filled. The owner rejects stale contexts and configuration revisions before mutation. Conditions/hit conditions on enabled entries require their advertised capabilities. Disabled entries remain local with verification:null and are omitted from the DAP request, rather than inventing a negative adapter verification for them.

References remain opaque strings. CyCode does not infer a symbol, pointer origin, byte width or address rebase from them. The manual API validates their shape and observed context, not that the caller obtained them from a particular adapter reply. The backend determines whether a reference actually resolves and can be bound. Disassembly addresses are passed unchanged; offsets are in bytes, not instructions.

Bounds are 128 entries / 1 MiB serialized request data, references of 1–8192 UTF-8 bytes, offsets within ±1 MiB and condition strings up to 4096 bytes, without NUL. Exact duplicate reference/offset pairs and unknown fields are rejected. Different strings that alias the same address are not canonicalized locally. Breakpoint modes and instruction logpoints are not exposed by this contract.

Verification, events and lifetime#

debug_status exposes instructionBreakpoints, instructionBreakpointRevision and instructionBreakpointsSynchronized. Entries retain requested reference/offset and options, plus real verification: verified, message, optional signed 32-bit id, actual instructionReference/offset and pending/failed reason. Requested locations are not substituted for missing actual locations. Signed IDs and optional reported offsets preserve their DAP ranges. Verification parsing is shared with data breakpoints, whose existing ID contract is preserved.

Reply counts must match enabled entries in order, with unique returned IDs. Replies are limited to 512 KiB. Changed/removed events update actual verification. During a pending replacement, up to 256 events / 1 MiB are retained and reconciled by ID after the acknowledgement; individual events are bounded to 64 KiB. Missing/ambiguous verification, malformed events or exhausted event budgets leave uncertainty visible. An adapter coalescing alias targets into repeated IDs requires an explicit corrected list; the host does not guess their identity.

Before submission the revision advances and synchronization becomes false. A rejected, malformed, timed-out or execution-expired request can already have side effects. The old list remains only the last known configuration. Inspect status, then explicitly replace or clear while paused to establish a confirmed list again. The SDK handler is noncancellable after submission and retains the native outcome. There is no automatic retry, rollback or replay.

Already installed points can remain across resume. Target termination, disconnect or a new launch resets this session configuration; no instruction addresses are written into launch.json or automatically reinstalled in another process. Same-pause cache invalidation does not falsely classify an acknowledgement as a different execution stop. A real new pause/resume while waiting leaves the mutation uncertain.

Verification performed#

MSVC /Zs checks the native/UI/regression sources without executing assertions or producing test objects/executables. Source assertions cover enabled mappings, conditions, exact references, duplicate/revision rejection, pre-ack events, relocated/removed/pending verification, signed IDs, uncertainty, clear/reset, count/byte/event bounds, invalid disassembly markers and captured GUI drafts. Actual CyToolsCore manifest/schema examples check all 181 operations, typed disabled/verified/uncertain outputs, guards, bounds, permissions, cancellation metadata and English/French controls. See Validation for delivery.

Real CodeLLDB/NetCoreDbg/java-debug/plugin behavior, protected or unloaded code, aliases/ID reuse, instruction-byte patching, conditions/hit semantics, late events, concurrency, MCP/plugin runtime and keyboard/themes/DPI remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky test suspension. Linux/macOS compilation and execution remain pending.

pages.title: Java debugging
pages.html:
Java debugging#

The built-in builtin.java provider connects the existing native Debugger to Microsoft's Java Debug Server add-on for Eclipse JDT LS. Launch and JDWP attach share the native debugger. Windows production compilation and schema/source verification are recorded in Validation; actual Java/DAP and graphical acceptance remain pending while native runs are suspended.

Prerequisites#

Install a compatible JDK, JDT LS and the Microsoft java-debug plugin JAR separately. CyCode does not download, build, install or redistribute that JAR. Keep its separate EPL licence and notices when supplying it. Resolve the application JDK through PATH or CYCODE_JAVA; standalone builds also need CYCODE_JAVAC/javac.

Enable Java in language settings. For the installed default server, set CYCODE_JAVA_DEBUG to the absolute plugin .jar path before starting CyCode. The default Java settings add that file to $initializationOptions.bundles. This lookup reads paths only. An explicitly configured server/settings profile remains authoritative: edit its existing JSON and include, for example:

json
{  "$initializationOptions": {    "bundles": ["/absolute/path/com.microsoft.java.debug.plugin-version.jar"]  }}

Merge this into the existing initialization options; retain other settings. Save/remember the Java profile and restart its backend. Merely changing the environment after startup does not replace a remembered profile. Java server configuration is shared by desktop, MCP and the native plugin host.

The add-on integration follows the upstream java-debug usage contract and Java launch fields. CyCode checks for the advertised vscode.java.startDebugSession command. Missing, disabled, incompatible or unresponsive servers fail explicitly. No adapter, compiler or server starts merely by listing adapters or saving a debug profile.

Build and launch#

Select a standalone Java, Maven or Gradle project and its main class in Project tasks, then Debug / Continue (F5). project.debug uses the existing cancellable build owner, selects one actual class-file main method and returns debugProfile. Maven resolves runtime dependencies for Debug as it already does for Run; Gradle uses its exported runtime model. This operation prepares a profile without starting a debugger. The GUI applies its main class, runtime classpaths, Java executable, working directory and arguments, preserving optional Java VM/source settings, then uses debug.configure and debug.launch. Cargo retains its native executable output and switches back to the native provider. Unsaved buffers must be saved before building/debugging.

For SDK/plugin clients, take debugProfile from a successful project.debug result, configure it, then launch. Check success/cancellation before proceeding. The existing operation permissions and host service remain in force; no second Python debugger model or plugin ABI was added. All 170 operations remain present.

Manual profiles select Java / JDT LS under Adapter provider. Adapter options are a bounded JSON object with these supported fields:

Field Meaning
mainClass Fully qualified class name, required at launch; up to 4096 bytes
classPaths Explicit runtime directories/JARs, required and nonempty at launch
javaExec Optional actual Java executable path; Project tasks supplies it
projectName Optional JDT project identity to disambiguate sources
sourcePaths Optional additional source roots, with standalone source root supplied by Project tasks
vmArgs Literal JVM arguments as an array

Each array is limited to 128 entries, each string to 8 KiB, and options to 16 KiB overall. Unknown/common transport/request fields are rejected. Main class names cannot be source paths, shell text or contain ASCII whitespace/control characters. Classpath/source entries are literal paths resolved relative to the working directory and canonicalized before the request. Additional source roots must exist. Missing classpath directories (for example Gradle resources with no files) stay in the array, matching JVM behavior. $Auto, wildcards, variables and JPMS module-path inference are not expanded. Large dependency graphs over these limits require further work; entries are never silently dropped.

Arguments, environment, cwd, stop-on-entry and terminal selection remain common profile fields, rather than duplicated Java options. The host sends DAP type java, request launch, noDebug=false and the integrated terminal or internal debug console. External terminals are rejected. Run without debugging uses the existing Project tasks Run command; debug.run remains native/.NET.

The host converts argument arrays to the Java server's actual string fields, using its platform-specific quoting rules, without a shell. Empty strings, spaces, quotes and trailing backslashes retain their intent. Environment removals require the integrated terminal: the adapter's internal-console environment path does not provide the same removal semantics. See the upstream wire fields and argument parser.

Attach to an existing JVM#

Start the target with JDWP enabled, using the target project's own launch method. For example, the following JDK command listens locally and waits for the debugger before executing the main class (illustrative only, not executed by validation):

text
java -agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=y,address=127.0.0.1:5005 -cp out demo.Main

Select Java / JDT LS in the Debugger's Launch configuration tab. Set JVM host, JDWP port and Attach timeout (ms), then Attach to JVM. The same configured JDT LS/java-debug add-on used for launch is required. The local adapter connects to the existing JVM; CyCode does not compile a project, launch that JVM or create a program terminal. Existing source roots and optional projectName come from Adapter options; mainClass, classPaths, javaExec, vmArgs, program arguments/environment and stop-on-entry are not sent in attach requests. Source paths still resolve against the guarded workspace working directory.

Save debug profile persists the endpoint independently of launch options in .cycode/launch.json. Per-call attach overrides do not implicitly save it. Existing profiles without an endpoint retain 127.0.0.1:5005 / 5000 ms. Successful project Debug target preparation preserves this endpoint while replacing its launch class/runtime options. Profiles and current debug status use the same typed javaAttach object:

json
{  "adapterId": "builtin.java",  "javaAttach": {    "hostName": "127.0.0.1",    "port": 5005,    "timeout": 5000  }}

For SDK/MCP/plugin host debug.attach, explicitly select adapterId=builtin.java and pass this endpoint, or omit javaAttach to use the saved/default endpoint. An empty adapterOptions is sufficient for attach and replaces any unrelated saved vendor options. Java rejects pid; native/.NET and contributed adapters continue to require a positive PID. Typed endpoint fields are reserved host configuration and cannot be smuggled through vendor adapterOptions. The existing process.execute permission remains required; saving also requires workspace.write.

The host is bounded to 253 ASCII characters and accepts hostnames, IPv4 and unbracketed IPv6 addresses with optional scope IDs. Port is 1–65535; timeout is 100–10000 milliseconds, within the common DAP response deadline. URLs, combined hostname:port values, spaces, control characters and unknown fields are rejected. Host/IP validity, DNS resolution, routing and reachability are determined by the installed Java adapter/JDK, rather than probed while editing or inspecting a profile. Unicode hostnames require their ASCII/punycode form. Remote endpoints are reached by the local JDT LS process; its DAP connection with CyCode stays on loopback. Target JDWP availability, networking or an existing tunnel are supplied by the user; CyCode does not provision them or search for targets automatically.

After attach, the shared breakpoint, thread, stack, scope, watch and stepping views apply. The panel shows the session's actual requested target separately from the editable profile draft, and identifies Java rather than C/C++. Stop, shutdown or backend reconfiguration sends disconnect with terminateDebuggee=false / suspendDebuggee=false. The adapter detaches from the existing JVM. A Java attach session refuses reverse runInTerminal requests and never takes ownership of the existing target process. Runtime acceptance of detach/resume, network failures and reconfiguration remains pending. Other owners retain their own lifetimes: workspace-owned Run terminals, for example, still close their processes when that workspace shuts down.

See the upstream Java attach handler, disconnect behavior and Oracle JPDA invocation guide.

Ownership and boundaries#

The Java language-service owner issues the fixed LSP command with a ten-second request deadline. The Debugger waits without holding its state mutex, checks the backend generation and validates the returned integer port (1–65535). Its framed JSON transport connects only to IPv4 127.0.0.1, without DNS, configurable remote addresses, a listener, shell, bridge process or separate JVM debug implementation. Connect is bounded to two seconds; socket writes to five seconds. Existing DAP message/queue limits, stop generations and inspection capability checks apply. Changing/disabling the Java backend invalidates the active session. Disconnect asks the adapter to terminate the launched debuggee and closes owned program terminals; the shared JDT LS backend remains under LanguageService ownership.

Breakpoints, stepping, threads, stack, scopes, watches, sources, exception filters and available inspection commands reuse the same Debugger/UI services. Their actual availability depends on the installed Java adapter and debug symbols; standalone Debug uses javac -g, while Release omits symbols. Maven/Gradle retain their own project compiler settings. Default JDT imports/autobuild remain disabled; configure project import/source roots explicitly when source resolution needs it.

Local/remote JVM attach is implemented with pending runtime acceptance. Manual Hot Code Replace is also implemented as described below. JPMS/Android, child sessions, automatic project import/build synchronization and Java-specific exception UI remain separate work, along with virtual JDT/JAR-source navigation beyond the shared file/source-reference views. There is no claim of tested Java/Rider parity, GUI/theme/DPI acceptance or Linux/macOS execution from a production Windows build.

Manual Hot Code Replace#

Run > Apply Java code changes, the Java debugger toolbar and the command palette share debug.hotReload. This action saves desktop buffers first, then requests an incremental JDT workspace build (java/buildWorkspace with the boolean false, encoded as JSON-RPC positional params: [false]). It never launches javac/Maven/Gradle as a substitute for that build. The JDT result must be ordinal 1 (success); failed, cancelled, erroneous or malformed results prevent sending redefineClasses.

The debuggee must use the same project/source and class output mapping as the imported JDT model. Configure the needed JDT project import and source/output roots explicitly, including adapterOptions.projectName when needed. The normal task-generated standalone javac directory is not automatically synchronized with a JDT project's output. Merely opening a Java file, compiling externally or having syntax coloring does not establish this mapping. Defaults still disable JDT Maven/Gradle import and autobuild. This action does not enable them, install tools, download dependencies or change the saved project build profile. An explicit JDT build can execute that imported project's configured builders.

debug_hot_reload takes sessionGeneration from the current debug_status snapshot and an optional unique operationId (ASCII letters/digits/underscore/ hyphen/dot, at most 128 characters). The generation identifies the active DAP session and rejects queued requests from earlier launch/attach sessions. It is zero while disconnected/tearing down, and a new nonzero value is issued only when starting a new session. The native owner also checks Java backend epochs and the saved/conflict-free open workspace document identity/revision snapshot before and after compilation. Editing/replacing a captured native document or leaving it dirty during the build requires a retry. This is not an atomic external filesystem snapshot: save and resolve external changes and keep the debuggee/JDT source mapping consistent.

javaReload in debugger status reports building, applying, applied, unchanged, failed or cancelled, with operationId, changedClasses and message. A successful DAP envelope containing errorMessage is still a failure. An empty class list is unchanged, never a successful application of changes. The reply is bounded to 256 KiB and 2048 class names of at most 4096 bytes. The native view lists the actual returned names. Adapter ERROR/WARNING diagnostics remain visible separately; STARTING/END/BUILD_COMPLETE notifications do not themselves establish successful replacement and never trigger automatic application. No invented standard DAP HCR capability is assumed; an older or incompatible add-on's request rejection remains an explicit error.

Cancel Java reload signals the pending compilation through debug.cancelReload; SDK debug_cancel_reload can match the same operationId, including a reload still queued in the native debugger. The SDK's own job cancellation sends this matched signal and retains its reservation until the native call returns. Cancellation is checked before application, with a 120 s build deadline and JDT request cancellation. The callback remains pending until JDT responds or that deadline expires; cancelRequested identifies this wait in status/the desktop. The compiler can finish before acknowledging cancellation, but its result will not trigger replacement. If a server ignores cancellation or the deadline expires, its compiler may still be active; CyCode does not claim to terminate it or kill the shared language server. A Stop request also interrupts that pre-application wait and then performs normal launch/attach disconnect semantics. Cancellation never stops the JDT language server or an attached JVM. Once redefineClasses has been sent, the 30 s adapter wait runs to an outcome or timeout; cancellation cannot undo a VM change. Failed, interrupted or timed-out application may have partially applied changes; inspect status and restart the session explicitly when needed. There is no automatic restart or Undo operation.

Reload attempts and Java stack invalidation events expire cached frame/scope/ variable/source-reference generations. Actual continued/stopped events retain execution state, and paused inspection refreshes asynchronously. Existing native, .NET and contributed stdio DAP adapters do not accept this Java-specific action.

On a standard JVM HCR primarily supports method body changes; adding/removing members or changing signatures may require a JVM restart. The installed VM and adapter remain authoritative. See the upstream HCR handler and reply semantics, JDT build protocol, JSON-RPC positional parameter encoding, build implementation and VM limitations. Windows compilation/schema checks do not establish actual JVM reload acceptance; real build/redefine/partial failure/cancellation, remote attach mapping, graphical interaction and Linux/macOS remain unexecuted while native tests are suspended.
