Runtime acceptance of detach/resume, network failures and reconfiguration remains pending. Other owners retain their own lifetimes: workspace-owned Run terminals, for example, still close their processes when that workspace shuts down. See the upstream Java attach handler , disconnect behavior and Oracle JPDA invocation guide . Ownership and boundaries # The Java language-service owner issues the fixed LSP command with a ten-second request deadline. The Debugger waits without holding its state mutex, checks the backend generation and validates the returned integer port (1–65535). Its framed JSON transport connects only to IPv4 127.0.0.1, without DNS, configurable remote addresses, a listener, shell, bridge process or separate JVM debug implementation. Connect is bounded to two seconds; socket writes to five seconds. Existing DAP message/queue limits, stop generations and inspection capability checks apply. Changing/disabling the Java backend invalidates the active session. Disconnect asks the adapter to terminate the launched debuggee and closes owned program terminals; the shared JDT LS backend remains under LanguageService ownership. Breakpoints, stepping, threads, stack, scopes, watches, sources, exception filters and available inspection commands reuse the same Debugger/UI services. Their actual availability depends on the installed Java adapter and debug symbols; standalone Debug uses javac -g , while Release omits symbols. Maven/Gradle retain their own project compiler settings. Default JDT imports/autobuild remain disabled; configure project import/source roots explicitly when source resolution needs it. Local/remote JVM attach is implemented with pending runtime acceptance. Manual Hot Code Replace is also implemented as described below. JPMS/Android, child sessions, automatic project import/build synchronization and Java-specific exception UI remain separate work, along with virtual JDT/JAR-source navigation beyond the shared file/source-reference views. There is no claim of tested Java/Rider parity, GUI/theme/DPI acceptance or Linux/macOS execution from a production Windows build. Manual Hot Code Replace # Run > Apply Java code changes , the Java debugger toolbar and the command palette share debug.hotReload . This action saves desktop buffers first, then requests an incremental JDT workspace build ( java/buildWorkspace with the boolean false , encoded as JSON-RPC positional params: [false] ). It never launches javac/Maven/Gradle as a substitute for that build. The JDT result must be ordinal 1 (success); failed, cancelled, erroneous or malformed results prevent sending redefineClasses . The debuggee must use the same project/source and class output mapping as the imported JDT model. Configure the needed JDT project import and source/output roots explicitly, including adapterOptions.projectName when needed. The normal task-generated standalone javac directory is not automatically synchronized with a JDT project's output. Merely opening a Java file, compiling externally or having syntax coloring does not establish this mapping. Defaults still disable JDT Maven/Gradle import and autobuild. This action does not enable them, install tools, download dependencies or change the saved project build profile. An explicit JDT build can execute that imported project's configured builders. debug_hot_reload takes sessionGeneration from the current debug_status snapshot and an optional unique operationId (ASCII letters/digits/underscore/ hyphen/dot, at most 128 characters). The generation identifies the active DAP session and rejects queued requests from earlier launch/attach sessions. It is zero while disconnected/tearing down, and a new nonzero value is issued only when starting a new session. The native owner also checks Java backend epochs and the saved/conflict-free open workspace document identity/revision snapshot before and after compilation. Editing/replacing a captured native document or leaving it dirty during the build requires a retry. This is not an atomic external filesystem snapshot: save and resolve external changes and keep the debuggee/JDT source mapping consistent. javaReload in debugger status reports building , applying , applied , unchanged , failed or cancelled , with operationId , changedClasses and message . A successful DAP envelope containing errorMessage is still a failure. An empty class list is unchanged , never a successful application of changes. The reply is bounded to 256 KiB and 2048 class names of at most 4096 bytes. The native view lists the actual returned names. Adapter ERROR/WARNING diagnostics remain visible separately; STARTING/END/BUILD_COMPLETE notifications do not themselves establish successful replacement and never trigger automatic application. No invented standard DAP HCR capability is assumed; an older or incompatible add-on's request rejection remains an explicit error. Cancel Java reload signals the pending compilation through debug.cancelReload ; SDK debug_cancel_reload can match the same operationId , including a reload still queued in the native debugger. The SDK's own job cancellation sends this matched signal and retains its reservation until the native call returns. Cancellation is checked before application, with a 120 s build deadline and JDT request cancellation. The callback remains pending until JDT responds or that deadline expires; cancelRequested identifies this wait in status/the desktop. The compiler can finish before acknowledging cancellation, but its result will not trigger replacement. If a server ignores cancellation or the deadline expires, its compiler may still be active; CyCode does not claim to terminate it or kill the shared language server. A Stop request also interrupts that pre-application wait and then performs normal launch/attach disconnect semantics. Cancellation never stops the JDT language server or an attached JVM. Once redefineClasses has been sent, the 30 s adapter wait runs to an outcome or timeout; cancellation cannot undo a VM change. Failed, interrupted or timed-out application may have partially applied changes; inspect status and restart the session explicitly when needed. There is no automatic restart or Undo operation. Reload attempts and Java stack invalidation events expire cached frame/scope/ variable/source-reference generations. Actual continued/stopped events retain execution state, and paused inspection refreshes asynchronously. Existing native, .NET and contributed stdio DAP adapters do not accept this Java-specific action. On a standard JVM HCR primarily supports method body changes; adding/removing members or changing signatures may require a JVM restart. The installed VM and adapter remain authoritative. See the upstream HCR handler and reply semantics , JDT build protocol , JSON-RPC positional parameter encoding , build implementation and VM limitations . Windows compilation/schema checks do not establish actual JVM reload acceptance; real build/redefine/partial failure/cancellation, remote attach mapping, graphical interaction and Linux/macOS remain unexecuted while native tests are suspended. { "$initializationOptions": { "bundles": ["/absolute/path/com.microsoft.java.debug.plugin-version.jar"] } } java -agentlib:jdwp=transport=dt_socket,server=y,suspend=y,address=127.0.0.1:5005 -cp out demo.Main { "adapterId": "builtin.java", "javaAttach": { "hostName": "127.0.0.1", "port": 5005, "timeout": 5000 } }

pages.title: Maven and Gradle project tasks
pages.html:
Maven and Gradle project tasks#

The shared native ProjectTasks adapter now detects pom.xml, build.gradle, build.gradle.kts and settings-only Gradle roots before standalone Java fallback. The existing panel, build/test/run shortcuts, configured deadlines, process-tree cancellation, persistent profile and SDK/MCP operations use these adapters. Inspection only reads descriptors/cache; it does not evaluate rules, resolve dependencies, execute wrappers or install tools.

Tool selection#

Install a suitable JDK and build tool, or supply the project's existing wrapper jar. CYCODE_JAVA/PATH selects Java using existing tool discovery. Explicit CYCODE_MAVEN_HOME or CYCODE_GRADLE_HOME selects an installed distribution. Otherwise the adapter searches ancestors within the workspace for .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.jar or gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar; installed MAVEN_HOME/M2_HOME/GRADLE_HOME is the fallback. Missing jars/tools produce errors. No wrapper jar or distribution is downloaded by opening/inspecting a project.

Explicit Configure/Build/Test/Run executes trusted Java build tooling and project rules, which may download distributions/plugins/dependencies as usual. Offline mode passes the tool's --offline; it does not promise that an uncached wrapper distribution is available offline. CyCode invokes wrapper main classes or installed Java launchers with argv vectors, never a project-derived shell command. Maven 3 uses its ClassWorlds bootstrap; Gradle supports the older launcher and newer gradle-gradle-cli-main layouts. Other layouts require adaptation/runtime acceptance.

Shell startup files, MAVEN_OPTS/JAVA_OPTS and shell parsing of .mvn/jvm.config are not reproduced. The selected JVM honors its own supported environment options; project build configuration remains owned by Maven/Gradle. If a Maven wrapper requests shell-side wrapperSha256Sum, the adapter refuses to bypass that check: use the official wrapper externally or select an installed Maven distribution explicitly. Jarless/script-only wrapper distributions need an installed tool here.

Tasks and runtime models#

Operation Maven Gradle
Configure Nonrecursive effective POM through pinned Maven Help Plugin 3.5.2 Application-owned init task exports actual Java source-set model as bounded JSON
Build package -DskipTests build with normal project test/dependency semantics
Test test, using project framework configuration test, using project framework configuration
Run build task One simple goal/phase such as clean/verify/install; preserves its test semantics One simple task, optionally scoped to a selected module
Run Build, resolve runtime dependencies through Maven Dependency Plugin 3.11.0, then run the selected actual main class Build, export runtime source-set classpath, then run the selected actual main class

Gradle's package field selects a module (app normalizes to :app; empty builds all). Maven selects its module through Project directory. A reactor-root package build may build its modules, but runtime metadata describes the selected POM only; choose a runnable module directory and ensure reactor dependencies are available. This is not a complete Maven reactor dependency/import model.

Runnable entry points are read from actual compiled class-file main methods, not source regexes. Class output/build paths are workspace-guarded. Runtime dependency classpath entries may reference installed external jars; they are runtime inputs, not newly editable workspace documents. Gradle Java source sets supply their actual runtimeClasspath; Maven uses its effective output directory and resolved runtime dependencies. A failed/incomplete operation does not publish runnable artifacts.

Java Run uses a fresh quoted argument file with disabled further @file expansion, preserving empty arguments, quotes, line breaks and shell punctuation while avoiding Windows command-line length limits. This launch path requires Java 9+; UTF-8 argument-file behavior on supported JDK/platform combinations still needs runtime verification. Java module-path applications and custom main launchers are not inferred from a classpath. Debug/Release labels do not invent project-specific Maven profiles or Gradle variants.

Project profiles include timeoutSeconds (1–86400; default 180). This is one total process budget across build/model/dependency steps. The GUI exposes it and the SDK retains ownership/cancellation while waiting for a saved long deadline. Increase it explicitly for a first large dependency resolution. Results/logs remain bounded; source/class scanning has entry/depth/class/artifact limits and observes cancellation.

Validation and remaining work#

Windows production compilation and MSVC /Zs source checks cover the adapter, panel and model/argument regression sources. Regressions specify Maven XML entities and unresolved properties, Gradle modules/outside outputs/dependencies, classpath bounds, exact argument-file encoding, wrapper argv and checksum refusal. They are added to the existing opt-in project test executable, without a new test binary.

No Java, Maven, Gradle, wrapper, generated Java fixture, test executable, debugger or app window was launched for this change during the Kaspersky interruption. Actual builds/tests/dependency resolution/interactive output, client/JDK versions, cross-module runtime behavior and GUI acceptance remain pending. Linux/macOS and clean-machine installation are untested. A subsequent implementation connects launch debugging through JDT LS; see Java debugging for setup and separately pending acceptance. This does not claim per-test JUnit/TestNG result discovery, Android/JPMS support, Maven reactor parity or full Gradle Tooling API coverage.

References: Maven Wrapper, effective POM, runtime classpath, Gradle initialization, source sets, Java argument files.

pages.title: Language-server preferences
pages.html:
Language-server preferences#

Rust adds an optional typed cargoProject selection alongside raw argv/settings, including a symbolic installed Rustup toolchain name when selected. Project tasks can apply the current manifest/features/offline/locked snapshot and remember it through this same revision-guarded store. Omission preserves it; explicit null removes it. See Rust analysis for supported mapping, restart behavior, path guards and build-profile limitations.

Problems > Configure language server edits the native server's unresolved argv and settings. Remember for this project is selected in an ordinary desktop session. Apply and restart saves that choice and enables the server. Enable, Disable and Restart also remember the current launch and activation choice. Unchecking Remember applies a session-only change. No shell command is assembled.

Use installed defaults sets arguments to [] and settings to {}. The host resolves the current bundled/system tools and default settings on preparation. Java's private data/OSGi paths and Rust's derived tool environment are not serialized as a saved default launch. An explicit argv remains an explicit user-selected override. The legacy single-executable/C# DLL setting is retained when its fields are left unchanged.

Reload saved settings replaces the modal's draft and revision with the current saved choice. A revision conflict leaves the draft intact until that action. Forget saved settings removes the persisted choice without changing the current server; the next session returns to installed defaults. Applying again with Remember checked saves the draft again.

Storage and activation#

The desktop and CLI supply an application-owned directory to the UI-free Engine. Files live under the installation's ignored data/settings/language-servers/<workspace-key>.json, with an adjacent persistent lock file. The key hashes the canonical workspace directory (not a solution's filename); the file verifies the complete workspace identity to reject collisions. Windows uses invariant Unicode case folding; POSIX retains case. Moving a project or portable installation does not migrate profiles. Profiles are not included in the existing UI configuration export or project templates.

The host does not load executable preferences from .cycode, a solution or a cloned project's files. Read/inspection refreshes stored data but never enables saved servers. An embedding using Engine(workspace) without an explicit preferences directory cannot persist settings. Desktop smoke/test sessions omit it; source-only verification does not create profiles.

On desktop opening, saved C++/C# choices override the global default executable. Unreal retains its initial analysis pause; restoring analysis does not undo an explicit Disable or reset another backend's current configuration. Installed additional servers still start on the first relevant document opening, using the saved launch unless that backend was explicitly disabled for the project. Core/CLI/MCP additional servers require explicit language.configure permission, even if a saved profile says enabled. Reading a profile does not start it.

Plugin profiles use the contributed backend ID. They remain stored while the plugin is disabled or absent; registration/inspection does not execute them. Reactivation retains the existing disabled-owner policy. An explicit Enable or the normal first-document desktop policy restores the saved launch. There is no implicit plugin installation or native-code sandbox.

Shared native, MCP and plugin contract#

  • language.preferences / MCP language_preferences: refresh local preferences; return available, revision, error and profiles. Read permission only.
  • language.configure / MCP language_configure: existing process-authorized launch control. Omitted launch fields preserve the current explicit choice or use the saved profile; explicit empty arguments/settings select installed defaults. enabled defaults to true. save defaults to false; true requires expectedPreferencesRevision from the preferences read.
  • language.preferencesForget / MCP language_preferences_forget: remove one saved backend with the expected revision; requires process.execute because it changes future executable configuration. It does not stop/reconfigure the current server or mutate project files.
  • language.status includes compact cached preference metadata and each current server's unresolved configuration, separately from resolved runtime arguments/settings. Frame-by-frame status does not reread the file or copy the full saved catalogue. Explicit reads refresh other instances' changes without applying them to current servers.

The existing permission-checked native plugin host exports all three operations. GUI, MCP and plugins share one store and the actual native server owners; Python does not maintain a second configuration model. Read-only identities cannot change future executable preferences.

Guards and limits#

Saves hold a nonblocking OS file lock across a fresh read, revision check and guarded atomic replacement. A competing/stale writer is rejected before changing the current server. Forget uses the same guard. A crashed owner releases the OS lock; the filename stays in place to avoid replacing the locked inode. Invalid/mismatched files report errors and are never silently overwritten. Write failures leave current server configuration unchanged. If a successful save is followed by a server-preparation failure, that distinction is reported and the saved configuration remains available for correction.

Limits: 42 saved backend IDs per workspace (10 built-ins plus 32 plugin slots), 160 ASCII letters/digits/._- per ID, 128 argv values of at most 8,192 bytes, 64 KiB settings, 4 MiB per file, integer revisions through 2^53-1. NUL arguments, an empty argv program, unknown fields, ambiguous executable/argv/settings and unsupported readiness notifications are rejected. Custom executables are trusted user preferences, not a sandbox.

Windows/MSVC compilation and source checks cover this change. New native assertions cover reopening, restoration, default intent, stale revisions, unavailable plugins, invalid files and a host without storage. The existing MCP web test adds permission and save/forget checks. Those runtime tests and graphical interaction remain unexecuted while native validation is suspended following the Kaspersky removals. Linux/macOS locking, filesystem and desktop behavior remain unverified. See Validation.

headings.text: Shared native, MCP and plugin contract

pages.title: Language support
pages.html:
Language support#

Java launch/attach debugging now uses JDT LS with the separately installed Microsoft java-debug bundle and shared DAP services. Project tasks provides explicit actual main/runtime-classpath launch profiles, while JDWP attach uses independent saved host/port/timeout fields and detaches existing JVMs. Manual Hot Code Replace builds the imported JDT model then requests redefineClasses with guarded session/documents and matched cancellation. JVM support and matching source/output mappings are required; runtime/network/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Java debugging.

CyCode and CyCodeReader share a native, incremental Tree-sitter syntax layer for Rust, Java, JavaScript/JSX, TypeScript/TSX, HTML and CSS. HTML script/style blocks use the JavaScript/CSS parsers. Strings, nested Rust comments, raw strings and JavaScript template substitutions have dedicated syntax handling. Existing C/C++/Unreal, C#, shader, JSON, Python, Lua and Markdown lexers remain available. Syntax runs on document changes, with byte/glyph conversion for UTF-8, a 4 MiB document limit, parser/walk deadlines and bounded display spans. Semantic overlays take precedence over syntax while protecting strings/comments.

Language services belong to CyCode's native core; Reader hosts the shared syntax layer, not project analysis or language servers.

Semantic coloring now negotiates full/delta transport for any connected server advertising it, with bounded per-worker bases and a full-request fallback. Existing Unicode/revision and display guards remain. Backend/GUI acceptance is pending; see semantic token updates.

Versioned diagnostics now feed CodeEditor squiggles and message tooltips with native revision/UTF-16 guards and theme roles. Unversioned advisory reports remain in Problems. See Editor diagnostics for provider limits, display budgets and unexecuted runtime acceptance.

Python/Pyright and GLSL Analyzer now use the same native service router, and ABI2 plugins can add file selectors/LSP backends without a process-global registry. Problems includes editable per-project argv/settings, session-only opt-out and separate server logs. See language preferences. See Development workflows for the installer, exact pins, supported methods and the configurable but unverified HLSL backend.

Files Native language server Connected operations
C/C++/Unreal clangd Completion, diagnostics, semantic colors, definitions/references, symbols, rename, formatting
C# csharp-ls/Roslyn Completion, diagnostics, semantic colors, definitions/references, symbols, rename, formatting
Rust rust-analyzer Completion, diagnostics, semantic colors, definitions/references, symbols, rename, formatting with rustfmt
Java Eclipse JDT LS Completion, diagnostics, semantic colors where advertised, definitions/references, symbols, rename, formatting
JavaScript/JSX, TypeScript/TSX typescript-language-server + TypeScript Completion, diagnostics, semantic colors where advertised, definitions/references, symbols, rename, formatting
HTML VS Code HTML server Completion, formatting, document structure and definitions where provided; no workspace symbol/reference/rename method advertised
CSS VS Code CSS server Completion, diagnostics, formatting, document structure, selector definitions/references and rename; no workspace symbol method advertised

The Problems panel shows the availability, state and enable/restart/disable controls for each server. The IDE starts installed additional servers when their files are first opened, preserving saved disables. The core/CLI/MCP starts those backends only after an explicit language_configure operation authorized with process.execute. Inspection and read-only queries never enable them. Servers are independent child processes with bounded queues/output and owned process-tree lifetimes. Rust and Java wait for their workspace readiness notifications before initial requests. Java receives separate data and OSGi configuration directories per instance.

Navigation and refactoring share the existing live-document/revision/disk guards. Versioned LSP edits are validated against the versions actually sent and mapped to native revisions. Java's coalesced edits retain a complete before/after preview. Initially unopened rename targets are opened and synchronized before recomputing the preview against their live versions. Applying a rename edits buffers; saving remains a separate action.

Completion materializes LSP list defaults and supports text edits, insert/replace ranges, multiline insertion/indentation and interactive snippet parameters. Selecting an issued item resolves lazy documentation/import edits when the server supports it. The symbol and additional imports form one revision/disk-checked native change plan. The editor checks its cursor/generation again before applying the plan, then records the complete result as one undo/redo transaction, preserving tabs and converting the final UTF-16 caret to glyph coordinates. Saving is separate. This acceptance path requires one cursor. Reader shares the widget and syntax; it does not start project language servers.

language_complete returns a sessionId plus items in original index order. language_completion_resolve and language_completion_prepare accept that issued session/index and expectedRevision; clients cannot submit arbitrary edits through these operations. Prepare is read-only and returns a normal change plan and caret. Existing changes_preview/apply/undo operations inspect or apply it; apply/undo require workspace.write. Sessions are limited to eight, five minutes and 8 MiB combined; each list contains at most 2000 items / 4 MiB, each item at most 256 KiB. Additional edits are limited to 256 / 1 MiB and must not overlap each other or the primary edit. Stale document/workspace revisions, server reconfiguration, disk conflicts and SDK writes are refused. Protected insertion/ranking fields cannot change during resolve; indentation mode is explicitly advertised as resolvable.

Snippets support numbered tab stops, repeated linked fields, forward references, nested defaults, explicit $0 final carets and choice lists. Tab/Shift+Tab moves through numeric field order; Escape finishes. Typing edits all mirrors in one widget transaction. A parameter badge shows the navigation keys; choice fields offer a dropdown. Replacing an outer field removes its nested fields. Undo, external document synchronization, read-only changes, reload and cursor moves outside the linked selections terminate the session. Redo restores text without resurrecting the temporary linked cursors. Automatic indentation is suspended inside fields so it cannot delete snippet delimiters; the prior setting returns on exit. Ordinary editor indentation and raw-tab undo/redo policies are preserved. Automatic completion is suppressed while editing linked fields. Explicit Ctrl+Space finishes that session and requests a fresh completion; nested interactive sessions are not stacked.

The SDL-free snippet library is shared by core completion and the editor. Prepare returns optional snippet metadata in explicit UTF-8 byte offsets within the resulting document: fields/ranges/parents/choices and a final caret. Offsets include import and multiline indentation changes; the ordinary cursor remains UTF-16. The UI resolves every byte boundary in one document pass, then tracks only affected glyph coordinates from actual widget transactions while typing. Inputs are limited to 8 KiB, expanded text to 64 KiB, nesting to 16, fields to 128, occurrences to 256 (128 per field), indexes to 65535 and choices to 64. Variables, transforms, recursive fields and coincident empty mirrors are refused. Reader includes the shared editor correction preserving the absence/presence of the final newline; it does not have a snippet insertion catalogue or LSP host.

Variables/transforms, commit-character acceptance, a user snippet catalogue and full code actions remain pending. Passive editor hints and Java selection/ranking notifications are ignored; no completion commands are executed. Other commands are refused. clangd retains --header-insertion=never: C++/Unreal automatic includes are not enabled by this change. Backend-specific unsupported methods fail explicitly.

Quick fixes and context actions#

The Code actions panel requests actual fixes/refactorings for the live cursor or selection: Rider Alt+Enter, Visual Studio Ctrl+. or Alt+Enter, VS Code Ctrl+. It filters quick fixes, refactorings and organize imports. Available actions can be applied to unsaved buffers or opened in the shared before/after preview, with the existing refactoring undo. Saving remains separate. The UI source compiles; complete desktop acceptance remains pending the protection-related GUI block.

The read-only MCP operations language_code_actions and language_code_action_prepare return issued summaries and a native change plan. Clients pass a live UTF-16 range/expectedRevision, then the sessionId/item index; they cannot submit arbitrary action edits. Lazy resolution uses only advertised codeAction/resolve. Sessions expire after five minutes and are bounded to eight / 8 MiB total, 256 actions / 2 MiB per list and 512 KiB per item. Revision, workspace generation, backend epoch, target paths, overlaps and disk baselines are checked. Literal-edit targets are opened/synchronized before recomputing the list; newly discovered lazy targets require a fresh query. Multi-file apply validates every affected buffer before changing any. changes_apply/undo require workspace.write.

Versioned context diagnostics must match the current LSP overlay. Unversioned publications are advisory; the cache is invalidated on document edits, but the protocol cannot establish their revision. Equivalent percent-encoded Windows file URIs are matched by their decoded path. Servers compute edits from the live range and all resulting plans still carry native revision/disk guards.

Actions requiring server commands, file create/delete/rename, change annotations or snippet text edits are unavailable with a reason. No server command executes. The pinned TypeScript server attaches a passive acknowledgement to ordinary import fixes; only its empty-command variant is omitted after the edit. Complete server-specific action coverage, interactive command arguments and Unreal asset / Blueprint refactorings remain pending. Actual native checks cover clangd typo fixes, TypeScript imports, Java import organization and Rust visibility rewrites; other actions depend on the connected backend's advertised methods.

Symbol documentation and parameter information#

Navigate > Quick documentation and Parameter information query the real server at the current cursor. The Code information panel displays documentation, overloads, parameter names and the active parameter when the provider reports it. Rider uses Ctrl+Q and Ctrl+P (Ctrl+Shift+Space is also available); Visual Studio and VS Code use Ctrl+K, Ctrl+I and Ctrl+Shift+Space. These actions share the command catalogue, user overrides and capability checks. Reader remains an editor without LSP services.

An open information panel follows the active document/cursor with a short debounce and at most one request in flight. Native revision/generation checks reject stale responses; the UI also rejects results for a previous cursor or document. Requests do not edit buffers, save files, enable a disabled server or execute documentation. Markdown/HTML returned despite the preferred plaintext format is displayed literally; rich documentation rendering and mouse-hover popups remain pending.

The read-only MCP operations language_hover and language_signature use path, expectedRevision and a zero-based UTF-16 position. Hover returns typed display sections and an optional validated document range. Signature help returns up to 32 overloads, 128 parameters each and 64 KiB of text. Parameter startByte/endByte are UTF-8 offsets in the returned label; -1 means an unmapped label. A missing/null provider activeParameter is preserved as -1 rather than inventing a selection. In particular, csharp-ls 0.28.0 omits the active index after a call's final comma; the signature still appears but that parameter is not highlighted. HTML may advertise signature help for embedded languages and return no signature on a tag. Unsupported methods fail explicitly; empty results remain normal at positions without information.

Installation and configuration#

The ordinary build installs locked language tools in runtime/tools. To install them separately, run python app/scripts/setup_languages.py, or select --rust, --java, --web. Archive SHA-256 values are pinned in app/language-tools.lock.json; web package versions/integrities are pinned in app/web-languages/package-lock.json. npm lifecycle scripts are disabled. Nothing is installed globally.

  • Web services require installed Node.js 20+ and npm. Syntax does not require Node.
  • The pinned JDT LS 1.50.0 requires installed Java 21+; JDK 24 was tested locally.
  • Rust uses an installed toolchain when Cargo is available, otherwise the private pinned rustc/Cargo/rust-src/rustfmt toolchain. Build scripts, procedural macros and check-on-save are disabled in the default analysis profile. Dependencies and project-specific Rust toolchains remain the project's responsibility.
  • Automatic TypeScript typing acquisition is disabled. JS/TS use project tsconfig.json/jsconfig.json and installed project dependencies; React types and framework plugins are not fabricated or bundled.
  • Automatic Maven/Gradle import and Java autobuild are disabled by default. Standalone Java files were tested; broader Java project import/build workflows remain future work.

language_configure accepts language (cpp, csharp, rust, java, typescript, html, css), enabled, optional arguments (complete executable argv) and settings. $initializationOptions separates initialization data from workspace configuration. Custom argv/settings replace the default launch profile. The legacy executable option remains supported; omitting language retains its previous C# behavior. Configuration applies to the current IDE session.

Installed programs can also be selected with CYCODE_NODE, CYCODE_JAVA, CYCODE_RUST_ANALYZER, CYCODE_CLANGD and the existing C# overrides. Cargo, npm and standalone Java build/run tasks now share the native project service and the existing shortcuts; Cargo targets also feed the native debugger. See Project tasks and Cargo workspaces for the workspace/features/profile/target additions and pending expanded acceptance. The explicit Cargo-to-Rust analysis action copies supported manifest/feature/ resolution options to initialization and server configuration, with optional local preference persistence. It does not adopt later task edits automatically or reproduce custom compilation profiles; see Rust analysis. An installed named Rustup toolchain can now be selected for Cargo and explicitly copied into the analysis snapshot. It uses the existing native process owners without requesting installation; see Rust toolchains for analyzer component/custom argv behavior and pending runtime acceptance. Java/web debug adapters, broader Maven/Gradle integration, framework previews, remaining server-specific code actions, advanced refactoring and external standard-library source navigation remain separate work. Linux/macOS builds and runtime behavior remain unverified.

Verification#

CTest exercises the six additional language entry points using actual servers, live completion, formatting, symbol structure and shutdown. TypeScript has cross-file definition/references, rename/apply/undo and type diagnostic checks. Rust/Java have actual definition/references, guarded rename/apply/undo and semantic token checks. CSS checks selector rename. A delayed-server lifecycle test rejects obsolete LSP edit versions. Missing optional runtimes are explicit CTest skips. Native tests also cover actual documentation/signatures, live C++ changes, C# overloads and provider selection limits, UTF-16 parameter ranges, bounded text, unsupported methods and delayed stale documentation/signature replies. The MCP suite verifies these operations with a read-only identity, including an emoji before the call, surrogate-boundary rejection and stale revisions. Native completion tests check actual TypeScript/Java/Rust imports, insertion across the installed language servers, atomic preview/apply/undo, session eviction and server restart, forged tickets, delayed obsolete resolves and disk conflicts. A headless real ImGui editor test exercises Ctrl+Space/Enter, interception before insertion, one-step undo/redo, raw tabs and a UTF-16 emoji caret without creating an OS window. These are distinct from full desktop acceptance, which remains pending the protection-related GUI block. The official MCP test checks read-only import preview and denied application, followed by writer apply/undo without saving. Snippet tests additionally verify real widget typing, mirrored Unicode fields, Tab/Shift+Tab, choices, nested removal, multiline editing, Escape, undo/redo and reload/read-only/external-edit termination. Exact final-newline tests cover load, replace, undo and redo. Native fixtures combine imports with linked field offsets; actual clangd and the official read-only MCP return two editable function arguments. verify_information.py prepares hidden GUI shortcut/capture acceptance for all three keymaps; its current execution remains pending the protection-related GUI block recorded in Validation. Code-action tests additionally exercise actual preview/apply/undo across four servers, lazy resolution, multi-file atomicity, forged/evicted tickets, stale diagnostics/replies, newly discovered targets, URI aliases and disk conflicts. The official MCP import-fix test verifies read-only preview, denied application, writer apply/undo and unchanged disk sources.

python app/scripts/verify_languages.py tests actual Ctrl+Space/Enter insertion and syntax in hidden IDE windows, then the shared Reader parsers in two themes. app/tests/test_mcp.py exercises actual TypeScript completion, an unsaved type change and permission rejection through the official MCP SDK and CyTools runtime.

pages.title: Live native build output
pages.html:
Live native build output#

Recognized source rows can now open existing workspace files through the shared native build.location parser. Live project logs supply their recorded task working directory; other/final logs use the workspace root. This is a guarded navigation hint, not a current diagnostic revision. See Compiler locations for formats and limits.

The Build panel has a Live build output section using CyUI Diagnostics and the shared log severity rules. It polls at most four times per second while the panel is visible, supports filtering/follow/copy, and shows the latest operation's ID, method and running/finished state. Final GUI task output and diagnostics keep their existing path; MCP returns the final result to its caller. Live messages do not imply success or completion.

Shared service and scope#

build.output / SDK build_output / ABI2 read the same Engine-owned memory tail without acquiring adapter, document or plugin execution locks. The operation requires process.execute, because output may contain private project data. It is read-only and has no workspace mutation group. Authorized SDK clients can inspect output while another job builds; read-only plugin callbacks can read it with this manifest permission. Trusted native plugin code is not OS-sandboxed.

Explicit CMake configure/build/test/package/workflow execution, MSBuild build/ rebuild/clean/restore and Unreal generation/database/build/prepare/UAT execution opt in at their main process calls. Sequential phases share one tail in actual pipe-read order. Stdout/stderr are merged by the existing pipe; their separate identity and original interleaving cannot be reconstructed.

Tool discovery and structured MSBuild evaluation never opt in. Background Unreal analysis has a separate cancellation owner and does not publish here. Cargo/npm/ Java/shader tasks now share the same journal implementation through the separate project.output service and a Build panel source selector; see Project output. Debugger terminals and arbitrary plugin processes retain their services. Process ownership, deadlines and cancellation remain unchanged.

The observer is scoped to the synchronous build thread and exact cancellation owner. Other threads/owners receive no observer. Callbacks check their captured stream ID and active reservation, so late callbacks cannot enter the next build. Journal failures do not cancel the build or release its reservation. Output from internally buffered tools, real-time scheduling and progress percentages are not promised. Failed starts may have no pipe output; inspect the final build response.

Reading the tail#

Start with {}. Responses contain streamId, revision, changed, operationId, method, running, cancelling, byteCount, droppedBytes, incomplete, encoding and output. Each build gets a distinct stream ID even when a caller reuses an operation ID. The latest tail survives completion/failure until the next explicit build or workspace destruction. An empty stream ID means no such build. Observation IDs do not confer authorization.

Send both observed streamId and revision to avoid repeating an unchanged tail. Equal observations return changed:false with empty output. Otherwise changed:true supplies a replacement of the whole display tail, including when a new build replaces the old one. It is not a chunk to append. Lifecycle and cancellation also advance the revision. Poll at about 250 ms or slower and check returned IDs rather than inferring identity from a reused operation ID.

The journal retains at most 256 KiB of raw bytes in bounded 8 KiB chunks. byteCount counts observed original bytes; droppedBytes counts bytes removed from the front. Tail overflow does not truncate or stop the build. incomplete records a journal allocation failure, independently of the process outcome. Original per-process output retains its existing 8 MiB cap.

Display text replaces invalid UTF-8 and NUL/control bytes, preserving CR/LF/tab; encoding is utf8-repaired. Polling/retention can split a character at an edge; a later replacement refreshes that display. Byte counters are not Unicode character counts or offsets in returned text. ANSI escapes are not interpreted; OEM/UTF-16/locale encodings are not detected. Original process output keeps its existing representation. No archive, temporary SDK artifact, MCP push, argument dump, automatic export or clipboard write is added.

Validation boundary#

Windows production compilation, MSVC /Zs and actual installed SDK/schema checks are separate from runtime acceptance. Existing opt-in build fixtures specify retention, revisions, scope isolation, late callbacks, text repair, failure/ cancellation and CMake pipe integration. They are syntax-checked only, neither built nor executed during the Kaspersky suspension. Real compiler/Unreal timing, concurrent SDK/plugin readers, GUI filtering/follow/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS execution remain unverified. See Validation.

Explicit CMake configure/build/test/package/workflow execution, MSBuild build/ rebuild/clean/restore and Unreal generation/database/build/prepare/UAT execution opt in at their main process calls. Sequential phases share one tail in actual pipe-read order. Stdout/stderr are merged by the existing pipe; their separate identity and original interleaving cannot be reconstructed. Tool discovery and structured MSBuild evaluation never opt in. Background Unreal analysis has a separate cancellation owner and does not publish here. Cargo/npm/ Java/shader tasks now share the same journal implementation through the separate project.output service and a Build panel source selector; see Project output . Debugger terminals and arbitrary plugin processes retain their services. Process ownership, deadlines and cancellation remain unchanged. The observer is scoped to the synchronous build thread and exact cancellation owner. Other threads/owners receive no observer. Callbacks check their captured stream ID and active reservation, so late callbacks cannot enter the next build. Journal failures do not cancel the build or release its reservation. Output from internally buffered tools, real-time scheduling and progress percentages are not promised. Failed starts may have no pipe output; inspect the final build response. Reading the tail # Start with {} . Responses contain streamId , revision , changed , operationId , method , running , cancelling , byteCount , droppedBytes , incomplete , encoding and output . Each build gets a distinct stream ID even when a caller reuses an operation ID. The latest tail survives completion/failure until the next explicit build or workspace destruction. An empty stream ID means no such build. Observation IDs do not confer authorization. Send both observed streamId and revision to avoid repeating an unchanged tail. Equal observations return changed:false with empty output. Otherwise changed:true supplies a replacement of the whole display tail , including when a new build replaces the old one. It is not a chunk to append. Lifecycle and cancellation also advance the revision. Poll at about 250 ms or slower and check returned IDs rather than inferring identity from a reused operation ID. The journal retains at most 256 KiB of raw bytes in bounded 8 KiB chunks. byteCount counts observed original bytes; droppedBytes counts bytes removed from the front. Tail overflow does not truncate or stop the build. incomplete records a journal allocation failure, independently of the process outcome. Original per-process output retains its existing 8 MiB cap. Display text replaces invalid UTF-8 and NUL/control bytes, preserving CR/LF/tab; encoding is utf8-repaired . Polling/retention can split a character at an edge; a later replacement refreshes that display. Byte counters are not Unicode character counts or offsets in returned text. ANSI escapes are not interpreted; OEM/UTF-16/locale encodings are not detected. Original process output keeps its existing representation. No archive, temporary SDK artifact, MCP push, argument dump, automatic export or clipboard write is added. Validation boundary # Windows production compilation, MSVC /Zs and actual installed SDK/schema checks are separate from runtime acceptance. Existing opt-in build fixtures specify retention, revisions, scope isolation, late callbacks, text repair, failure/ cancellation and CMake pipe integration. They are syntax-checked only, neither built nor executed during the Kaspersky suspension. Real compiler/Unreal timing, concurrent SDK/plugin readers, GUI filtering/follow/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS execution remain unverified. See Validation .

pages.title: Integrated MCP
pages.html:
Integrated MCP#

language_document_highlights / language.documentHighlights adds the shared permission-free in-document read (227 operations). Current document identity, revision and backend epoch are checked before and after the provider reply. Output contains actual Text/Read/Write kinds, sorted UTF-16 ranges, query position and invalid/truncated counts. Bounds are 4096 rows, 8192 records and 4 MiB. Disabled or unsupported providers are rejected; text-only highlights do not imply exhaustive semantic references. No cursor/source edits are exposed by this read. See Document occurrences for inputs, defaults and limits.

language_declaration, language_type_definition and language_implementation join language_definition/references in the shared native location pipeline. All five accept optional expectedDocumentId/expectedEpoch and return source identity, backend/epoch, method/position, validated fullRange/optional originRange and invalid/outside/truncated counts. Schemas bind each operation's returned method. Source lifetime is precise; other-file targets remain index observations. The surface has 226 operations; the three additions are permission-free reads without execution/mutation groups. See Source navigation.

language_symbols preserves complete symbol rows and now returns issued session/ resolveIndex references for scoped URI-only entries. language_symbol_resolve uses the original native server payload, two-minute/four-session bounded cache and workspace/lifecycle/monitor/epoch guards before and after resolving. Complete positions remain index observations. document_symbols retains precise document identity/range checks. language_status exposes symbolResolve capabilities. The added read operation has no permissions or mutation groups; 223 operations share the native owner and ABI2, with no independent Python model. See Symbol navigation.

build_location resolves one supplied compiler display line to an existing workspace source file. It uses the shared native parser without execution, source-content reads, permissions or mutation groups. The bridge does not inject a build operation ID or cancellation target. language_status diagnosticRevisions now pairs required native id/revision with the publication URI; raw diagnostics remain advisory until consumers verify that pair. The current manifest has 222 operations. See Compiler locations and Diagnostics.

project_status/project_output read the existing project task owner without waiting for execution/plugin/document locks or saved buffers. Status is permission-free; output requires process.execute and has no mutation group. Context, conditional replacement snapshots and Cargo rendered-message byte accounting are explicit. Read-job cancellation never targets the compiler. The manifest has 222 operations; see Project live output.

build_output reads the latest explicit CMake/MSBuild/Unreal live tail while a build owns the mutation group. It requires process.execute but is read-only and has no exclusive group. Conditional streamId/revision reads return replacement snapshots, never append-only chunks; byte counts and bounded display repair are explicit. The manifest has 222 operations. This uses normal SDK polling, not MCP push notifications; see Live build output.

unreal_artifacts / native unreal.artifacts add a read-only assessment of ordinary desktop Editor receipts, module IDs and recorded project binaries. The operation has no permissions/mutation group and uses a 64 MiB SDK memory reservation. The manifest now contains 222 operations. Native Unreal build results optionally add artifacts and inspectionError while retaining actual process outcome. Bound run/launch and desktop prebuild continuation require scoped ready outputs; profile configuration and SDK launch's explicit-build behavior remain unchanged. See Unreal outputs for bounds and incomplete/unsupported results.

Prepared Unreal launch settings now include a required non-null unrealLaunch profile/request binding. Common debug profile/configure/run/launch schemas accept it, null detachment or absence for legacy profiles. The native owner revalidates bound program/cwd/argv/runtime before write or actual launch; native Unreal build requires saved/reconciled workspace buffers. The desktop prebuild uses the bound context and guarded captured parameters, independent of toolbar changes. SDK launch still does not compile automatically. The current manifest has 222 operations and permissions/ABI stay unchanged; see Unreal launch.

unreal_launch_profile prepares typed UE4/UE5 editor/game/uncooked-server settings through the native Unreal inspector without compiling, saving or executing tools. It requires process.execute like debug_profile because expectedProfile can contain the saved environment. Send settings + expectedProfile to debug_configure for a guarded save, then use existing debug_run/debug_launch; SDK launch does not build automatically. The manifest now has 222 operations. See Unreal launch profiles for flags, bounds and pending acceptance.

unreal_automation_plan/run add reviewed UE5 cooking/packaging with explicit maps/container/deadline controls and issued input/tool/output guards. Run requires process.execute and workspace.write, uses the existing mutation group and actual build.status/cancel owner, and retains persistent workspace intent/logs/results. The bridge matches cancellation by operation ID and waits for the reviewed deadline plus postflight allowance. The manifest has 222 operations; Runtime/ actual UE acceptance remains pending. See Unreal automation.

vcs_replay_state/plan/apply add reviewed single-commit cherry-pick/revert, resolved continuation and quit tracking with retained work/index. Full source IDs and repository/state/plan guards exclude ranges, arbitrary options and external VCS providers. Apply persists an intent, retains actual process/inspection outcomes, requires VCS/workspace/process permissions and shares the existing mutation group. Native ownership is noncancellable; the bridge waits up to 1,200 seconds for repeated inspection/mutation/postflight. Actual Runtime acceptance remains pending. See Git replay.

vcs_merge_state/plan/commit/quit add actual merge blockers/staged review, guarded unsigned completion and quit tracking with retained working/index state. Typed requests bind repository/state/plan revisions and message/hooks policy; intent receipts are persistent workspace files. Actual process status and postflight inspectionError remain explicit. Mutations require VCS/workspace/process permissions, share the existing group and keep noncancellable native ownership. SDK Runtime acceptance remains pending. See Merge workflow.

vcs_checkout_plan/apply/undo expose reviewed single-file synchronization after staging, with persistent original/displaced backups and separate guarded Undo. Paths are repository-relative; binary bytes remain native. Apply rechecks the issued plan and complete index; Undo protects newer file content. Both retain workspace/VCS/process permissions and report partial/inspection outcomes. All three use noncancellable native ownership. Actual SDK Runtime acceptance remains pending. See Git working files.

vcs_conflict_list/inspect/plan/apply add typed Git structural conflict services. The new paths are repository-relative; documentPath remains workspace-relative. Preview/apply require observed repository/catalogue guards, explicit per-path choices and an additional preview revision on apply. Nullable text never carries binary bytes. Apply changes the index only, requires VCS/workspace/process permissions and retains noncancellable native ownership. Actual exit status plus catalogue or catalogError remains explicit. Four typed conflict operations are included; SDK Runtime acceptance remains pending. See Git conflicts.

vcs_worktree_plan previews move or repair with required observed repository/ catalogue guards and path/destination. Apply through vcs_worktree_move or vcs_worktree_repair with the same inputs and issued expectedPlanRevision. Plans expose checked paths and explicit file/index/transport effects; apply returns real process status plus catalogue or an unconfirmed catalogError. Preview is read-only; apply requires VCS/workspace/process permissions. Both retain noncancellable native ownership and existing 600-second bridge waits. Repair audits the full linked set because Git can update other linking files. Session selection is desktop-owned; SDK callers continue to select repositories explicitly. Runtime acceptance remains pending; see Git worktrees.

vcs_submodule_settings_plan previews one URL/tracking-branch metadata edit, including previous value redaction, existing overrides, exact argv and effects. vcs_submodule_settings requires its preview revision plus the same observed repository/catalogue/input guards. Both share native handling of staged/unstaged metadata, document/directory guards and actual postflight/index/checkout checks. Preview is read-only; application requires VCS/workspace/process permissions. Neither requests transport/staging/checkout; URL sync follows Git config rules. Literal, empty remote-default and dot parent-name tracking branches are supported. Actual Runtime/Git/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Git submodules.

vcs_submodule_deinit_plan inspects a clean, absorbed, parent-owned module and returns removal/preservation effects plus a separate preview revision. The guarded vcs_submodule_deinit removes only that checkout/local registration, preserving the gitlink, .gitmodules and Git metadata. It refuses ignored/untracked files, hidden flags, nested gitlinks and open native documents. Read preview has no mutation permission; the action requires VCS/workspace/process permissions and retains noncancellable native ownership. Actual removal/retention is checked after Git, including partial outcomes with exit zero. Runtime acceptance remains pending.

vcs_submodule_add_plan previews a new submodule locally. The separate vcs_submodule_add clones/stages only after the observed catalogue, repository and preview revisions match. Both share native guards/process ownership and typed actual/unknown metadata; read inspection has no mutation permission, while addition requires VCS/workspace/process permissions. See Git submodules for remaining runtime acceptance.

vcs_submodules reads configured top-level modules for an explicit Git repository. The guarded vcs_submodule_init/sync/update operations share native process ownership, typed actual state and the desktop's reviewed actions. Mutations require VCS, workspace and process permissions; no SDK task artifact staging or independent Python Git model is involved. Real Git/Runtime acceptance remains pending; see Git submodules.

debug_instruction_breakpoints replaces the full session-only list with explicit session/stop/revision guards. Disabled entries remain local, enabled entries carry actual adapter verification, and ambiguous failures leave synchronization false. It requires process.execute and is noncancellable after submission, sharing the desktop/plugin DAP owner. No process addresses are persisted into launch.json. See Instruction breakpoints.

debug_step_back, debug_reverse_continue and debug_restart_frame require explicit observed session/stop plus selected thread/frame references. Existing forward step/Continue operations retain optional queued context and gain typed, capability-gated granularity/singleThread options. All seven handlers are noncancellable after submission and expose actual lastExecution acknowledgement/ uncertainty, rather than inventing a completed target step. They require only process.execute and share the native GUI/plugin owner. See Execution controls.

debug_set_variable, debug_set_expression and debug_write_memory require process.execute and explicit observed session/stop generations. Expression edits also capture the selected frame; memory edits require expected bytes checked by a fresh read, with bounded explicit replacement bytes and subsequent read-back. The common native owner reports typed lastMutation outcomes, including partial or unconfirmed effects. These three handlers are noncancellable after submission and do not edit source or participate in document Undo. See Value and memory editing.

debug_data_breakpoint_info inspects a paused target; debug_data_breakpoints replaces the entire session list. Both require process.execute and observed session/stop generations. Replacement also needs dataBreakpointRevision and current-pause issued handles, with explicit verification/uncertain state. Its noncancellable SDK handler retains the native mutation outcome. See Data breakpoints.

debug_hot_reload uses the current debug_status.sessionGeneration and an optional unique operationId to build the imported JDT workspace and apply Java changes on the same native session. Both this operation and debug_cancel_reload require process.execute. Cancellation matches a pending call; the bridge retains the SDK reservation until its native result, and never rolls back an already sent redefine request. javaReload status reports actual returned class names, unchanged or failure. The cancellation operation has no workspace exclusive group so it can signal the running job. See Java debugging for requirements, VM limits and pending runtime acceptance.

Prepared text edits expose passive annotations and issued per-plan confirmation IDs. Inspect their labels/descriptions/files, then pass required IDs through changes_apply.confirmedAnnotations. The native Engine rejects missing, duplicate, unknown or foreign-plan IDs before mutation. Plain-plan calls remain compatible; permissions, scheduling and operation IDs are unchanged. See annotated changes.

Visual Studio solution/project build, clean/rebuild/restore, artifact evaluation and C++ index preparation use the native msbuild_* operations. Inspecting configurations is read-only; evaluation and builds require process.execute. See MSBuild.

Git branches, remotes, sync, stashes and conflict operations are documented in Version control, with separate vcs/workspace/process permissions.

Interactive terminal/run/debug operations are documented in Execution. They all require process.execute, including status/screen/profile reads. Persisting debug profiles and breakpoints also requires workspace.write. These native sessions survive individual Core jobs/tasks; explicit terminal_close/debug_stop or IDE/workspace shutdown ends them. Temporary task cleanup never deletes their original project files. The same debug_* contracts support native and .NET targets. runtime accepts automatic/native/dotnet, dotnet selects an explicit host or automatic discovery, and adapterArgs supplies optional bounded argv elements. For attach without a managed program path, select runtime=dotnet explicitly. Managed DAP output is in debug_status.output; debug_run provides a real terminal for interactive stdin.

The desktop starts its private CyToolsCore 0.10.1 companion if runtime/python exists. Open the MCP panel and copy/save its connection configuration. It references this running IDE instance. Configuration contains no token: tool.py reads the private Core descriptor and uses the existing SDK HTTP/MCP adapters.

Read access is the default configuration. The panel's editing switch selects the identity granted workspace.write, vcs.write, process.execute and plugins.execute. Repository build scripts and native plugin commands execute code; these are deliberate operation capabilities. Git honors repository hooks and signing configuration.

The default desktop configuration uses one read identity and one edit identity per GUI instance. Reusing the same configuration shares that identity's job visibility; different roles remain isolated. Dedicated authenticated clients can be provisioned through the SDK rather than assuming one credential means several independent users.

Operations are described in CyTool.json, generated by contracts.py. The official MCP adapter exposes op_<operationId>, plus cy_get_job, cy_events, cy_cancel_job and the SDK's session controls. A submitted job is not a completed result. Poll until Completed, Failed or Cancelled. A native failure becomes a failed job; transport success is not business success. Progress currently uses polling rather than MCP notifications.

Native exceptions produce failed jobs. A completed process operation can still contain a nonzero exitCode, including compilation errors and merge conflicts; inspect exitCode/timedOut/truncated before treating that result as successful.

Document writes require expectedRevision from a fresh read. Replacements change the live buffer; documents_save explicitly persists it. Save rejects external disk changes. The native service treats project documents as persistent workspace references. SDK temporary task cleanup removes job artifacts, never original source documents.

toolchains_detect and build_inspect are read operations; they describe installed tools and the saved CMake profile/targets without configuring the project. Tool discovery queries installed tool versions. build_configure and build_run require process.execute. They accept source, buildDirectory, configuration, toolchain (a detected ID or automatic), generator (a CMake name or automatic), and target (empty for default targets). Omitted fields use the active local profile. Configure prepares shared clangd settings and saves the profile only on success. Build validates target names and rejects configuration mismatches for single-config trees. The process result includes exitCode/output/timedOut/truncated and project metadata on success; a nonzero process exit has project=null. Always inspect exitCode even when the Core job completed. See Build services for paths and limitations.

Unreal operations are unreal_inspect, unreal_generate, unreal_database and unreal_build (prefixed op_ over MCP). Inspect is read-only; the other operations require process.execute. They accept project, engineRoot, target, platform and configuration, returning native Unreal project metadata. Inspect exitCode on every process result. The 180-second deadline and build cancellation limits also apply to these jobs. See Unreal services.

C/C++ and C# semantic operations use the same native servers and live overlays as the UI. C# activation through language_configure requires process.execute because loading projects evaluates MSBuild imports. Read-only document/status calls do not activate it. language_status returns per-server connection state and merged published diagnostics; language_definition and language_references accept path, expectedRevision and position {line, character}. Both coordinates are zero-based; character counts UTF-16 code units. Read the live document first, and convert positions from that text. References also accepts includeDeclaration (default true); both operations accept limit (default 1000, maximum 5000). Results include source revision, positionEncoding, workspace-relative locations with LSP ranges, truncated and outsideWorkspace. Outside-workspace locations are counted but omitted by default. Set includeExternal to true for registered read-only SDK locations; these carry an opaque sdk:// path, external=true and displayPath. sources_read accepts the issued source reference and returns a readOnly document with revision/text/displayPath. Arbitrary external paths and SDK writes remain refused. A changed live revision during a query fails the job; read again and retry. Semantic operations are available to the read identity and never save documents. language_complete accepts path, expectedRevision and a UTF-16 position and returns standard LSP items. Applying snippets, additional imports and completion resolve is pending. See C# language services.

language_highlight accepts path and expectedRevision and returns supported, generation, truncated and tokens. Tokens contain line/character/length in UTF-16, glyphStart/glyphEnd in Unicode codepoints, the negotiated type name and modifier names. A response is bounded to 50,000 tokens or a 4 MiB token payload. The native adapter validates ranges, overlaps and surrogate boundaries; obsolete revisions fail the job. Generation changes on live-document updates, restarts or server refreshes. supported=false requests lexical fallback. C# analysis must first be enabled; this read operation cannot activate it. Opened SDK references retain their read-only scope. Delta/range requests and modifier styling are not exposed yet.

language_symbols accepts query (up to 256 bytes), language (cpp by default or csharp), typesOnly, includeExternal and limit (up to 1000). language_document_symbols accepts path and expectedRevision, including previously opened SDK references. Results contain names, LSP kinds, container/detail, locations, truncation and UTF-16 encoding metadata; document results also carry the source path/revision.

language_rename accepts path, expectedRevision, position and newName; language_format accepts path, expectedRevision, optional range, tabSize and insertSpaces. Both prepare plans without editing. The result includes id/title/state/files/editCount; each file records its expectedRevision and edit count. changes_preview accepts id/path and returns before/after text and validated edits. changes_apply and changes_undo accept id and require workspace.write. They prevalidate all documents before changing any live buffer; they never save files. Fetch fresh document revisions after applying. Concurrent edits/disk changes reject the transaction. See Semantic editing for bounds, undo rules and C++/Unreal limitations.

Example parameters for op_language_definition:

json
{"parameters":{"path":"main.cpp","expectedRevision":7,"position":{"line":12,"character":8}}}

Semantic requests have a 15-second deadline including server initialization, and expired requests send LSP cancellation. clangd's available index may still be building; reference results are not a completeness guarantee. Accurate project compilation flags or compile_commands.json remain necessary. See the LSP position specification.

Cancellation is cooperative: a Core handler drains the native reply before releasing its reservation. It does not promise immediate native build cancellation. Native search has a 15-second deadline and build processes a three-minute deadline. The SDK's local HTTP request body is capped at 1 MiB, which also constrains large document replacement through the shared MCP route. The GUI file limit is 4 MiB.

For automated bridge tests, cycode_cli WORKSPACE --serve DESCRIPTOR exposes the same native Engine without an SDL window. tool.py can also run standalone SDK CLI/MCP commands with CYCODE_BRIDGE pointing at that descriptor. Standalone MCP connections have independent runtimes; the desktop shared service is the multi-connection path.
