Expression edits also capture the selected frame; memory edits require expected bytes checked by a fresh read, with bounded explicit replacement bytes and subsequent read-back. The common native owner reports typed lastMutation outcomes, including partial or unconfirmed effects. These three handlers are noncancellable after submission and do not edit source or participate in document Undo. See Value and memory editing . debug_data_breakpoint_info inspects a paused target; debug_data_breakpoints replaces the entire session list. Both require process.execute and observed session/stop generations. Replacement also needs dataBreakpointRevision and current-pause issued handles, with explicit verification/uncertain state. Its noncancellable SDK handler retains the native mutation outcome. See Data breakpoints . debug_hot_reload uses the current debug_status.sessionGeneration and an optional unique operationId to build the imported JDT workspace and apply Java changes on the same native session. Both this operation and debug_cancel_reload require process.execute. Cancellation matches a pending call; the bridge retains the SDK reservation until its native result, and never rolls back an already sent redefine request. javaReload status reports actual returned class names, unchanged or failure. The cancellation operation has no workspace exclusive group so it can signal the running job. See Java debugging for requirements, VM limits and pending runtime acceptance. Prepared text edits expose passive annotations and issued per-plan confirmation IDs. Inspect their labels/descriptions/files, then pass required IDs through changes_apply.confirmedAnnotations. The native Engine rejects missing, duplicate, unknown or foreign-plan IDs before mutation. Plain-plan calls remain compatible; permissions, scheduling and operation IDs are unchanged. See annotated changes . Visual Studio solution/project build, clean/rebuild/restore, artifact evaluation and C++ index preparation use the native msbuild_* operations. Inspecting configurations is read-only; evaluation and builds require process.execute. See MSBuild . Git branches, remotes, sync, stashes and conflict operations are documented in Version control , with separate vcs/workspace/process permissions. Interactive terminal/run/debug operations are documented in Execution . They all require process.execute, including status/screen/profile reads. Persisting debug profiles and breakpoints also requires workspace.write. These native sessions survive individual Core jobs/tasks; explicit terminal_close/debug_stop or IDE/workspace shutdown ends them. Temporary task cleanup never deletes their original project files. The same debug_* contracts support native and .NET targets. runtime accepts automatic/native/dotnet, dotnet selects an explicit host or automatic discovery, and adapterArgs supplies optional bounded argv elements. For attach without a managed program path, select runtime=dotnet explicitly. Managed DAP output is in debug_status.output; debug_run provides a real terminal for interactive stdin. The desktop starts its private CyToolsCore 0.10.1 companion if runtime/python exists. Open the MCP panel and copy/save its connection configuration. It references this running IDE instance. Configuration contains no token: tool.py reads the private Core descriptor and uses the existing SDK HTTP/MCP adapters. Read access is the default configuration. The panel's editing switch selects the identity granted workspace.write, vcs.write, process.execute and plugins.execute. Repository build scripts and native plugin commands execute code; these are deliberate operation capabilities. Git honors repository hooks and signing configuration. The default desktop configuration uses one read identity and one edit identity per GUI instance. Reusing the same configuration shares that identity's job visibility; different roles remain isolated. Dedicated authenticated clients can be provisioned through the SDK rather than assuming one credential means several independent users. Operations are described in CyTool.json, generated by contracts.py. The official MCP adapter exposes op_<operationId>, plus cy_get_job, cy_events, cy_cancel_job and the SDK's session controls. A submitted job is not a completed result. Poll until Completed, Failed or Cancelled. A native failure becomes a failed job; transport success is not business success. Progress currently uses polling rather than MCP notifications. Native exceptions produce failed jobs. A completed process operation can still contain a nonzero exitCode, including compilation errors and merge conflicts; inspect exitCode/timedOut/truncated before treating that result as successful. Document writes require expectedRevision from a fresh read. Replacements change the live buffer; documents_save explicitly persists it. Save rejects external disk changes. The native service treats project documents as persistent workspace references. SDK temporary task cleanup removes job artifacts, never original source documents. toolchains_detect and build_inspect are read operations; they describe installed tools and the saved CMake profile/targets without configuring the project. Tool discovery queries installed tool versions. build_configure and build_run require process.execute. They accept source, buildDirectory, configuration, toolchain (a detected ID or automatic), generator (a CMake name or automatic), and target (empty for default targets). Omitted fields use the active local profile. Configure prepares shared clangd settings and saves the profile only on success. Build validates target names and rejects configuration mismatches for single-config trees. The process result includes exitCode/output/timedOut/truncated and project metadata on success; a nonzero process exit has project=null. Always inspect exitCode even when the Core job completed. See Build services for paths and limitations. Unreal operations are unreal_inspect, unreal_generate, unreal_database and unreal_build (prefixed op_ over MCP). Inspect is read-only; the other operations require process.execute. They accept project, engineRoot, target, platform and configuration, returning native Unreal project metadata. Inspect exitCode on every process result. The 180-second deadline and build cancellation limits also apply to these jobs. See Unreal services . C/C++ and C# semantic operations use the same native servers and live overlays as the UI. C# activation through language_configure requires process.execute because loading projects evaluates MSBuild imports. Read-only document/status calls do not activate it. language_status returns per-server connection state and merged published diagnostics; language_definition and language_references accept path, expectedRevision and position {line, character}. Both coordinates are zero-based; character counts UTF-16 code units. Read the live document first, and convert positions from that text. References also accepts includeDeclaration (default true); both operations accept limit (default 1000, maximum 5000). Results include source revision, positionEncoding, workspace-relative locations with LSP ranges, truncated and outsideWorkspace. Outside-workspace locations are counted but omitted by default. Set includeExternal to true for registered read-only SDK locations; these carry an opaque sdk:// path, external=true and displayPath. sources_read accepts the issued source reference and returns a readOnly document with revision/text/displayPath. Arbitrary external paths and SDK writes remain refused. A changed live revision during a query fails the job; read again and retry. Semantic operations are available to the read identity and never save documents. language_complete accepts path, expectedRevision and a UTF-16 position and returns standard LSP items. Applying snippets, additional imports and completion resolve is pending. See C# language services . language_highlight accepts path and expectedRevision and returns supported, generation, truncated and tokens. Tokens contain line/character/length in UTF-16, glyphStart/glyphEnd in Unicode codepoints, the negotiated type name and modifier names. A response is bounded to 50,000 tokens or a 4 MiB token payload. The native adapter validates ranges, overlaps and surrogate boundaries; obsolete revisions fail the job. Generation changes on live-document updates, restarts or server refreshes. supported=false requests lexical fallback. C# analysis must first be enabled; this read operation cannot activate it. Opened SDK references retain their read-only scope. Delta/range requests and modifier styling are not exposed yet. language_symbols accepts query (up to 256 bytes), language (cpp by default or csharp), typesOnly, includeExternal and limit (up to 1000). language_document_symbols accepts path and expectedRevision, including previously opened SDK references. Results contain names, LSP kinds, container/detail, locations, truncation and UTF-16 encoding metadata; document results also carry the source path/revision. language_rename accepts path, expectedRevision, position and newName; language_format accepts path, expectedRevision, optional range, tabSize and insertSpaces. Both prepare plans without editing. The result includes id/title/state/files/editCount; each file records its expectedRevision and edit count. changes_preview accepts id/path and returns before/after text and validated edits. changes_apply and changes_undo accept id and require workspace.write. They prevalidate all documents before changing any live buffer; they never save files. Fetch fresh document revisions after applying. Concurrent edits/disk changes reject the transaction. See Semantic editing for bounds, undo rules and C++/Unreal limitations. Example parameters for op_language_definition: json Copy { "parameters" : { "path" : "main.cpp" , "expectedRevision" : 7 , "position" : { "line" : 12 , "character" : 8 } } } Semantic requests have a 15-second deadline including server initialization, and expired requests send LSP cancellation. clangd's available index may still be building; reference results are not a completeness guarantee. Accurate project compilation flags or compile_commands.json remain necessary. See the LSP position specification . Cancellation is cooperative: a Core handler drains the native reply before releasing its reservation. It does not promise immediate native build cancellation. Native search has a 15-second deadline and build processes a three-minute deadline. The SDK's local HTTP request body is capped at 1 MiB, which also constrains large document replacement through the shared MCP route. The GUI file limit is 4 MiB. For automated bridge tests, cycode_cli WORKSPACE --serve DESCRIPTOR exposes the same native Engine without an SDL window. tool.py can also run standalone SDK CLI/MCP commands with CYCODE_BRIDGE pointing at that descriptor. Standalone MCP connections have independent runtimes; the desktop shared service is the multi-connection path. {"parameters":{"path":"main.cpp","expectedRevision":7,"position":{"line":12,"character":8}}}

pages.title: Mercurial provider
pages.html:
Mercurial provider#

The bundled ABI2 extension cycode.mercurial contributes cycode.mercurial.provider. Git remains built in and selected by default. Enable Mercurial in Extensions, then choose Mercurial (Hg) in Version control and map the exact repository directory inside the workspace. The .hg directory must be local. Mapping a repository does not initialize, clone, pull or modify it.

Install Mercurial separately. Tool discovery uses an absolute CYCODE_HG override, managed tool locations or PATH. No client, credentials or Mercurial code is redistributed. The implementation targets the documented JSON/template and filepath: CLI interfaces; compatibility with an installed client still requires runtime acceptance. It has not been tested against any real hg version yet.

Operations and shared views#

Status reports modified, added, removed, missing and unknown files, the named branch and first parent changeset. Empty repositories have no fabricated parent. Two parents produce a merge warning. Diff uses the common CyUI Diff view; history and file annotations use read-only Review tabs. History is limited to 1–200 changesets (50 by default) with author, changeset, timestamp and description.

The twelve declared menu actions are:

  • Working-copy diff and repository history.
  • Annotations for one selected file.
  • Add one existing regular file, or stop tracking one file while preserving it.
  • Revert one file after entering REVERT; no .orig backup is created.
  • Commit tracked changes with an explicit nonempty message, without automatic add.
  • Update a clean tracked working copy to one verified changeset.
  • Create a bookmark or set a named branch for subsequent commits.
  • Pull from a configured remote alias without updating working files.
  • Push to a configured remote alias without forcing or allowing new branches.

Both remote forms default to the explicit alias default. Enter another configured alias, such as default-push, when required. Arbitrary remote URLs and local directory fallbacks are rejected. Branch/bookmark creation and remote aliases use bounded simple ASCII names; status can still display existing Unicode branch names. Update accepts a changeset ID or a simple named reference, including .; arbitrary revset expressions are rejected. Lookup must resolve to exactly one changeset, whose full node is passed to update --check. No clean/merge/force option is used.

Common provider menus/forms, project mappings, document guards and error reporting are shared with Git/SVN/Perforce. The host refuses write operations while the mapped scope has unsaved buffers or disk conflicts; clean buffers are reconciled after disk changes without overwriting edits made during an operation. Provider disable does not silently route its mapping to Git. Generic SDK/MCP access uses vcs_provider_action with plugin/process/workspace/VCS permissions; typed Git SDK operations explicitly remain Git-only. See Plugins and Version control.

Process, path and repository guards#

Every invocation uses an argv vector and the existing bounded native process owner, never a shell string. HGPLAIN, empty HGPLAINEXCEPT, UTF-8 strict output, noninteractive mode, no pager and disabled color stabilize parsing. Repository identity is checked using hg root --template "{hgpath|json}" and filesystem equivalence against the mapped .hg. Status/history/parents require complete structured responses. Invalid, excessively nested, oversized, timed-out, cancelled or truncated metadata cannot become a clean status or authorize an update.

File actions use an exact filepath:<repository-relative-file> selector after --; repository diff uses literal path:.. Parent traversal, administrative paths, nested repositories and symbolic-link traversal are rejected. Metadata paths outside the mapping are rejected too. This deliberately excludes operations on tracked symbolic links until a specific contract is implemented.

Mutations reject shared repositories, subrepositories, two-parent merges and unfinished rebase/histedit/graft/shelve states. Finish or abort those operations in the external client. Updates first reject any tracked working change; configured unknown/ignored-file overwrite policies are forced to abort. Reads remain available for inspection when possible, but this is not a conflict-resolution UI.

Metadata commands have a 15-second deadline; local final operations have 30 seconds; pull/push have 180 seconds. Each response is bounded to 512 KiB. Generic SDK requests allow 600 seconds for sequential preflight and execution. Known no-change exit 1 from commit/push is returned as success with noChanges:true and nativeExitCode:1; other failures are preserved. Each operation is serial within the native provider host. There is no interactive VCS cancellation UI yet.

The installed Mercurial configuration, extensions, hooks, authentication helpers and transports are trusted user tooling. Plain/noninteractive mode is not process isolation and does not disable hooks. No automatic credential configuration, authentication dialog or network operation occurs on repository selection.

The implementation follows the primary Mercurial documentation for root templates, exact file patterns, scripting, environment, update, paths, commit and push.

Verification and remaining scope#

Windows production compilation and MSVC /Zs checks of the client, ABI adapter and regression source passed. The opt-in runner regression specifies literal metacharacter/Unicode paths, empty parents, merge/shared/subrepository guards, exact file operations, pinned updates, remote aliases, no-change results, deadlines, malformed/partial metadata and missing clients. It also specifies actual production DLL registration, mapped-provider routing, dirty-buffer refusal and disable behavior. The existing MCP assertions include provider inventory and typed-Git isolation.

These regression sources have not been executed during the Kaspersky interruption. No hg subprocess, application window or native/MCP/GUI test was launched. See Validation for the checks actually performed. Real Mercurial local/network operations, authentication, hooks/extensions, large repositories, graphical interactions and clean installation remain unverified; Linux/macOS have not been built or run locally.

Remaining work includes clone/init, remove/move/copy, tag/bookmark management, merge/conflict resolution, rebase/histedit/graft, shelve, amend, shared/subrepository support, rich branch/remote views, credentials and cancellable VCS jobs. Repeated CLI startups are bounded but have not been benchmarked; a command-server adapter may be appropriate for frequent operations. This addition does not establish full Mercurial-client or Rider parity.

pages.title: Visual Studio and MSBuild projects
pages.html:
Visual Studio and MSBuild projects#

The native XML solution reader shares the existing model, build/evaluation/index services and guarded source access. See Project formats for configuration rules, tool prerequisites and pending execution validation.

Open a .sln, .slnx, .vcxproj, .csproj, .fsproj or .vbproj directly. Non-Unreal solutions use the native MSBuild service; Unreal continues to use UnrealBuildTool. A directory with CMakeLists.txt keeps its CMake workflow, while opening its generated .sln explicitly selects MSBuild. .slnx is not supported yet.

The MSBuild panel selects the solution configuration/platform, whole solution or one local project, and Visual Studio MSBuild or dotnet msbuild. It exposes build, rebuild, clean, package restore, explicit project evaluation and C++ code analysis. The existing Build project shortcut routes to this adapter. Rider Ctrl+F9 and the Visual Studio/VS Code build bindings execute the selected solution profile. All operations use the same native service from the GUI, CLI and CyToolsCore MCP. GUI build/rebuild saves modified document buffers first using normal revision/disk guards, and refuses to compile when a buffer cannot be saved. Native/MCP builds use the disk project; clients explicitly save their document edits before building.

Solution inspection parses ActiveCfg, Build.0 and Deploy.0, including nested folders, without loading MSBuild imports. Selecting a project builds its actual solution target, preserving MSBuild's dependency and configuration mapping behavior. Build uses the project target name without a :Build suffix; clean/rebuild use their named targets. Dotted project names use MSBuild's target-name escaping. Explicit package restore on a selected project uses its mapped configuration and project file.

MSBuild/dotnet tools are discovered independently of the launching shell. C++ builds require Visual Studio MSBuild on Windows. The .NET SDK backend builds managed projects using installed SDKs and their normal package/import configuration. These are trusted-project operations: targets, imports, property functions, packages and build events can execute code and write outside the source root according to their own project rules. Inspection does not evaluate those imports. Evaluation is an explicit process.execute operation, including evaluation with no build targets.

The last successful profile is saved atomically in .cycode/msbuild.json. Opening another explicit solution/project in the same directory preserves that entry's identity. Failed builds do not save a different selection. Artifact paths are read from actual evaluated TargetPath properties and can populate the native debugger profile for C++ executables. Managed compilation does not provide C# language services or a managed debugger.

Prepare code analysis uses MSBuild 17.8+ structured property/item evaluation. For enabled local .vcxproj files it derives compile_commands.json from actual ClCompile items, include paths, preprocessor definitions, forced includes, language standard and compile-as mode. It skips ExcludedFromBuild items. Analysis is capped at eight projects, 20,000 translation units and 32 MiB per operation. Select a project to prepare a separate index. AdditionalOptions produce review warnings rather than being silently treated as complete compiler flags. Advanced PCH/modules/custom toolchain cases require further work. Generated headers must already exist; this evaluation step does not compile them.

The shared clangd service reloads the prepared database. Cache inputs include the solution, local project files and existing local imports reported by MSBuildAllProjects; changed/deleted inputs invalidate cached artifacts/index metadata. New imports and SDK/tool updates may still require explicit preparation. Metadata and databases stay under .cycode/msbuild-cache rather than overwriting user compile_commands.json.

MSVC/C# file diagnostics with source coordinates are parsed, deduplicated and shown in Problems, with navigation restricted to workspace files. Directory identity checks handle MSVC expanding Windows short temp paths. General MSBuild/global errors remain available in Build output. Builds default to 150 seconds in the native API and accept timeoutSeconds overrides; the desktop remembers its own configurable build limit. Evaluation remains bounded to 15 seconds per project. Shared native cancellation is implemented; streaming remains pending. Process results expose exitCode/timedOut/truncated; callers must inspect them, since a completed MCP job can contain compiler errors.

The Windows native test creates a real two-project CMake-generated solution with a nested dotted project, builds/executes C++, exercises clean/rebuild and a changed Debug-to-Release mapping, prepares clangd navigation and checks actual compile errors. It also builds/executes an SDK C# fixture using installed .NET 8 packs and no NuGet network sources. A separate official MCP test verifies managed build/restore/evaluation and process permissions. Run app/scripts/verify_msbuild.py for the graphical workflow. Linux/macOS execution and F#/VB project builds remain unverified.

Primary references: MSBuild property/item evaluation, solution project targets, command-line reference.

pages.title: Document occurrences
pages.html:
Document occurrences#

Three connected changes share the existing native language owner: normalized document-highlight requests, independent occurrence geometry in CodeEditor, and a dockable inspector with kind filtering, navigation and explicit multi-selection. The new service is language.documentHighlights, also available as SDK/MCP language_document_highlights and a permission-free ABI2 JSON export. The SDK surface contains 227 operations. The C ABI and process/edit/Undo owners are unchanged.

Provider and source contract#

The request is LSP textDocument/documentHighlight; initialization advertises textDocument.documentHighlight.dynamicRegistration=false. Built-in C++/managed, other language servers and contributed backends all require an actual advertised documentHighlightProvider. Status exposes methods.documentHighlights. Disabled backends are not enabled by this read. Explicit requests can initialize an already configured/enabled server through the existing language service.

Input requires path, expectedRevision and a zero-based UTF-16 position. Optional expectedDocumentId and expectedEpoch guard the caller's source snapshot. includeExternal permits an already registered SDK source through the existing access policy; arbitrary external paths are not granted access. The response contains path, revision, documentId, backend, epoch, position, positionEncoding: utf-16, occurrences, invalid and truncated. Each occurrence has range and integer kind:

Kind Meaning from provider UI palette role
1 Text (including omitted kind) accent
2 Read info
3 Write error

Text highlights can be fuzzier than symbol references. The application does not infer semantic identity or classify reads/writes by matching names. Results may depend on the backend's current index. No claim of exhaustive semantic references is made for a text-only provider. Protocol reference: LSP document highlights.

Native checks retain the same open document identity/revision and backend epoch before and after the reply; unrelated document edits do not invalidate this read. Every endpoint must fit the live LF/UTF-8 buffer in UTF-16 coordinates without splitting a surrogate pair. Malformed rows are counted and omitted. Exact duplicate ranges collapse, preferring Write over Read over Text when the provider reports different kinds for the same span. Ranges are sorted by start/end. Null means no highlights; a non-array, non-null top-level response is rejected. The default row limit is 1000; callers may request 1–4096. Normalization visits at most 8192 records and retains at most 4 MiB of normalized rows; truncation is explicit.

Editor and inspector#

Navigate / Find Action exposes Highlight occurrences at caret. The Rider profile uses Ctrl+Shift+F7, following the documented Rider highlight command. View > Occurrences opens an ordinary dockable panel. Next/previous reported occurrence, Select reported occurrences and Clear occurrence highlights are also commands, available for custom bindings. Existing F3 document search and lexical occurrence selection shortcuts remain unchanged in every profile.

Automatic highlighting defaults on for an already ready, enabled, capable server. It waits 350 ms after the caret/source context changes. Only one request is in flight, and an unchanged successful, empty or failed context is not repeatedly requested. The panel can disable automatic requests; explicit refresh remains. Untitled/image/debugger-source tabs, smoke fixtures and Unreal's preparing-analysis phase do not start occurrence queries. Opened registered SDK text remains inspectable. The automatic/kind settings are session-local.

Replies are tied to path, document identity/revision, backend epoch and main-caret position. Late replies cannot move cursors. A changed context clears the old geometry/report, and Clear also suppresses a pending reply for that context. Moving to a different context clears suppression; an explicit highlight also retries. Internal next/previous/list navigation retains the report's original query anchor while adopting the new caret context; outside movement starts a new query. This is a single-anchor view, not Rider's multiple simultaneously pinned highlight sets or import-use analysis.

The panel shows Text/Read/Write counts, invalid/truncated state and display counts. Kind filters govern geometry, cyclic navigation and explicit selection. The common CyUI text filter governs only the virtualized location list; its labels/indices are cached until the report, filter, kind mask or locale changes. Locations display one-based UTF-16 line/column. Clicking a row or using next/previous navigates the current document only after checking its context again.

Independent display and selection#

The configured CodeEditor backend stores only one native glyph annotation. Adding occurrences as squiggles would overwrite overlapping diagnostics or plugin/search annotations. The host therefore builds its own bounded geometry model and draws unfilled palette-coloured outlines after the existing CodeEditor draw. Syntax foregrounds, native glyph annotations and Undo are not changed. The adapter uses the backend's public document/visual/screen coordinates and CodePoint width API for tabs, wide glyphs and wrapped/folded/scrolled rows, clipped to the editor child. It shares no new backend copy and does not modify CyUI or the downloaded editor. This requires an ImGui child-window lookup in the app adapter. Native multi-layer glyph annotations/backgrounds remain a library limitation; runtime visual acceptance of this independent outline approach is still pending.

Geometry retains at most 512 selected-kind occurrences, 64 lines per occurrence, 2048 line segments, 4096 glyphs per segment and 65536 glyphs total. The panel reports display truncation independently of native query truncation. Only visible visual rows are drawn. Theme palette roles and dp dimensions are read at draw time; changed tab width or kind mask rebuilds geometry. EditorTextMap shares the host's UTF-16-to-glyph boundary conversion with diagnostics, removing the duplicate decoder.

Select reported occurrences deliberately replaces the current cursor set with sorted forward ranges from the selected kinds; it does not preserve an old main cursor or backward selection direction. The entire report must be current and complete (invalid=0, no query truncation). Every selected span must be nonempty and disjoint, with at most 128 selections. All native ranges and editor glyph positions are preflighted before a single SetSelections call. There is no queued selection waiting for an asynchronous report, no partial selection and no source edit or Undo entry. Display truncation alone does not discard valid query rows.

Validation scope#

Existing semantic, command, module and language-lifecycle regression sources cover normalization/kinds/deduplication, malformed and Unicode ranges, budgets, navigation wrap/masks, selection limits/overlap/atomicity, source/Undo/annotation preservation, tab/wrap geometry, source/backend lifetime, unrelated edits, unsupported providers, clear-during-request and current-caret checks. They are source-checked with MSVC /Zs, not linked or executed under the current Kaspersky suspension.

Windows x64 production compilation and actual SDK manifest/schema plus pure bridge/data checks are recorded in Validation. No GUI, language server, SDK Runtime/native client, plugin or test executable is launched for this milestone. Actual timing, rendering, keyboard/focus, wrapping/folding/scrolling, Unicode, Undo interactions, multiple themes/densities/DPI/windows and Linux/macOS acceptance remain unverified. No dependency, CyUI module or executable target was added.

pages.title: Perforce provider
pages.html:
Perforce provider#

cycode.perforce is a bundled native ABI2 plugin; its provider is cycode.perforce.provider. Git remains built in and selected by default. Enable the plugin in Extensions and select Perforce (P4) in Version control with the project folder in the mapping field. The mapping uses the normal revision-checked .cycode/vcs.json service and deepest-root selection. Opening a project never creates a client, logs in, changes its view or runs a sync automatically.

Install the P4 CLI separately and configure the workspace using the normal P4 environment/configuration, client, ticket and trust files. Tool discovery checks absolute CYCODE_P4, packaged tools and absolute PATH entries. Neither P4 binaries nor credentials are packaged. The implementation uses current tagged JSON, fstat/reconcile and file-only submit options; real client/server version acceptance is still pending. It does not implement a P4API SDK or a second VCS engine.

Available actions#

Action Scope
status / inspect Selected client's opened files under the project, using filtered fstat -Ro. Shows action, changelist, type and unresolved status. This is not an automatic scan for unopened/offline edits or untracked files.
diff Project or explicit file; unified P4 working-copy differences against the opened depot revision, shared CyUI Diff review, headers reconstructed from tagged file records. Unopened files are not forced into the diff.
log / history Submitted changes affecting the mapped folder/file, default 50 and maximum 200, Unicode descriptions and first-line subjects. Dates are server Unix timestamps.
blame Selected file's #have revision; read-only revision/line annotations.
checkout edit for one existing regular file, default or explicit positive numbered changelist.
add One existing regular file, explicit literal filename handling, default or numbered changelist; respects P4IGNORE and the server typemap.
reopen Move one opened file into a default/numbered changelist. Does not create or edit changelist specifications.
revert One opened edit/add/delete only, requires confirmation:"REVERT". Discards local changes; P4 owns its file restoration/removal semantics. No editor Undo transaction can restore discarded disk content. Move/integration actions are rejected.
commit Submit one resolved edit/add/delete file in the default changelist with an explicit nonempty description. Excludes the open stream specification (-Sx); no whole changelist/default-client submission. Numbered-changelist and move/integration submissions need the external client.
sync Mapped project only; refuses opened project files, then runs read-only reconcile -n -a -e -d and refuses reported offline/untracked changes before syncing. No force, cleanup, silent reconcile, have-list-only update or branch switch.
lock / unlock Explicit selected file, current client/user, no force or administrator override.

The eleven custom actions are rendered by the common provider menus, palette and forms, using stable contribution/field IDs and the existing EN/FR catalogue. Review and Diff use the same editor/CyUI views as other providers. Git-specific UI stays specific to Git. P4 transport errors and partial responses remain visible.

For sync, configure P4IGNORE for normal generated/editor files as appropriate for your workspace, including unversioned .cycode metadata. The provider does not silently add ignore rules. A conservative preflight can refuse a sync that the external P4 client would allow; it does not overwrite ignored/untracked files on the application's own authority.

Common native/MCP route#

vcs_provider_action accepts, for example:

json
{"action":"checkout","contextPath":"Game/Source/main.cpp", "input":{"path":"Game/Source/main.cpp","changelist":"123"}}

The context determines the mapping; an explicit registered provider can override its ID for that request. Host-owned workspace/root fields cannot be replaced by plugin action input. Reads and writes through this generic SDK operation retain its existing conservative plugins.execute, vcs.write, workspace.write and process.execute permissions. Native GUI/CLI routes still select the mapped provider. Typed SDK Git operations explicitly select Git in the requested workspace repository; they reject external provider IDs and never execute a plugin under Git read-only permissions or try to validate provider output with Git-specific schemas.

The native SDK client waits up to 600 seconds for a generic provider action, covering sequential mapping/status/preflight/network budgets of these bundled providers. Cancellation retains the existing SDK reservation until the native operation returns; it does not introduce an early VCS process-cancel API.

Process and path contracts#

The plugin links only the shared native cycode_process/file utilities and JSON, without Engine, CyUI, ImGui, an extra process implementation or a new dependency. It uses argv, fixed cwd, owned children, bounded output and deadlines. Initial info identifies a configured client/user; subsequent commands explicitly pin those two identities. The mapped folder can be a subfolder of the P4 client root, but must stay inside the CyCode workspace. Each root/selected-file where query must return one positive matching mapping. Ambiguous overlay/exclusion query results, alternate/null client roots, UNC roots and symlink traversal are not supported. Settings/view/other-process changes during a multi-command operation are not an atomic transaction.

Paths are explicit local files or an application-generated project ... selector. Parent traversal, URL/drive/alternate-stream input and literal ... components are rejected. Normal file selectors escape %, @, #, * once; adding uses P4's literal-filename mode. Returned paths must be local and inside the selected root; matching accommodates Windows drive/path casing and P4's encoded mapping output. Opened move/integration pairs cannot escape a one-file revert/submit through their partner because those actions are rejected before mutation.

-ztag -Mj output is parsed as bounded JSON records, including code/severity/error categories. Only severity-2 EV_EMPTY (17) becomes a valid empty result for commands that allow one. Authentication, permission, malformed, unknown and truncated responses never establish a clean working copy. Output is limited to 512 KiB per process, 20,000 records and JSON depth 16; callback JSON stays under the common 4 MiB ABI limit. Info/mapping calls use 15 seconds, opened-file reads 30 seconds, and action/reconciliation calls 180 seconds per process. A timeout or overflow retains common native process ownership through termination.

The installed P4 client's configuration remains in effect, including charset, transport/SSO and configured diff helpers. The application never invokes an editor form, password prompt, login or trust acceptance; stdin is closed and calls remain bounded. Native extensions and configured client helpers are trusted code. Live dirty/disk-conflict checks and post-operation document reconciliation are supplied by the existing common VCS host. External filesystem/client/server races remain the client's responsibility; concurrently edited buffers are retained by CyCode.

Reference contracts: P4 JSON flags, fstat, mapping queries, submission and reconcile preview.

Verification and remaining work#

The production Windows plugin and source-only regression checks compile. The runner-injection regression source covers mapping, metacharacters, Unicode, changelists, one-file submission/revert, sync preflight, deadlines, empty results, authentication/permission failures, partial/malformed responses, outside paths, real production-DLL registration and dirty-buffer/disable routing. The MCP test source also exercises typed-Git isolation under a Perforce project mapping. Those native/MCP regressions are not executed during the Kaspersky interruption; no P4 server, P4 subprocess or application window is launched. See Validation for the exact checks actually performed.

Real authentication/SSO, exclusive file types, server triggers, binary/unicode files, large projects and GUI interactions remain unverified. Windows clean installation and Linux/macOS remain untested. Further work includes client/view configuration, numbered changelist creation/full submission, shelves/unshelve, move/delete/integrate, advanced resolve/stream/overlay workflows, offline scanning UI and cancellable VCS jobs. Mercurial has a separate bundled plugin with its own scope and pending acceptance. This plugin does not establish complete Rider/P4V parity.

pages.title: Plugin-owned adapter definitions, host-owned DAP sessions
pages.html:
Plugin-owned adapter definitions, host-owned DAP sessions#

The independent builtin.java provider now uses JDT LS and a bounded host-owned loopback DAP connection. It does not change the ABI2 stdio contribution contract; plugins cannot register either reserved built-in ID. The adapter catalogue now contains two built-ins plus up to 32 active contributions. Java launch setup, runtime prerequisites and pending acceptance are in Java debugging.

builtin.java now advertises launch and attach. Its host-owned javaAttach profile field stores the JDWP endpoint independently of vendor options; other adapters retain PID attach and do not receive this Java field in DAP payloads. Saving keeps the existing workspace.write/process.execute checks; attaching keeps process.execute. The C ABI and descriptor transports are unchanged. The Java adapter can connect to explicit remote targets while its CyCode DAP socket stays local; no plugin callback or Python service owns the target JVM.

ABI2 plugins can register stdio Debug Adapter Protocol adapters. The actual Debugger service launches and owns their processes, handles DAP framing and configuration, and supplies the existing breakpoints, stepping, stack, variables, watches, source views and program terminals. GUI, native/plugin host requests and MCP use this same service. An installed descriptor alone does not supply a missing debugger executable or implement a language's debug engine.

Registration#

Check the optional ABI2 tail size and CYCODE_HOST_FEATURE_DEBUG_ADAPTERS_V2 before contributing during init:

cpp
if (host->struct_size >= sizeof(CyCodeHostV2) &&    (host->features & CYCODE_HOST_FEATURE_DEBUG_ADAPTERS_V2)) {    host->contribute(host->context, "debugAdapter", R"({        "id":"example.tools.debugger",        "title":"Example debugger",        "type":"example-dap",        "arguments":["${pluginDir}/adapter", "--stdio"],        "requests":["launch","attach"],        "pidField":"processId",        "environment":{"ADAPTER_MODE":"stdio"},        "launch":{"console":"integratedTerminal"}    })", nullptr);}

The contribution is unconditional data: no callback, when or GUI context. Its ID must use the plugin namespace. The manifest needs process.execute. Missing permissions, unknown descriptor fields, duplicate IDs and malformed declarations are rejected during registration. A failed init removes its partial contributions. The original ABI2 prefix/layout and ABI1 remain compatible; the new feature is an additional bit in the existing optional tail.

Field Contract
id/title/type Required text. type is the adapter's DAP ID, also used during initialize; up to 128 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/dot/hyphen
arguments Required argv array, 1–128 entries, each at most 8 KiB. First entry is an executable path/tool name; it is resolved when explicitly launching, without a shell
requests Nonempty unique subset of launch/attach; defaults to launch only
pidField Numeric attach PID key: processId (default) or pid
environment Optional adapter-process environment overrides/removals (null); at most 64 entries / 16 KiB
launch/attach Optional adapter-specific request defaults, only for declared requests; objects of at most 16 KiB

The host adds the actual plugin owner to its internal snapshot. There are at most 32 contributed adapters and 64 KiB per descriptor. Options/defaults are bounded to 16 levels, 128 entries per collection, 8 KiB strings and 128-byte keys. Native validation occurs before serialization of nested options.

Only argv and environment string values expand ${pluginDir} and ${workspace}. Expansion is a single pass over the original text: inserted directory names are literal, including spaces and any variable-like characters. Unknown variables in those fields are errors. Launch/attach JSON strings remain literal. No project configuration is evaluated and no adapter starts during registration/enumeration. Adapters remain platform-specific tools; the manifest's existing OS/architecture and host compatibility checks still apply.

Selection, profiles and payloads#

The Debugger's Launch configuration tab selects an Adapter provider and edits its Adapter options (JSON). IDs persist in the existing .cycode/launch.json profile as adapterId; old profiles default to builtin, preserving the native and .NET adapter selection. There is one saved profile per workspace, not a new per-adapter catalogue. Profile edits affect the next launch; a running session stays bound to its original adapter definition.

debug.adapters / MCP debug_adapters returns the registry revision and summaries with id/title/type/plugin/requests. It includes builtin. It is read-only, starts no process and reveals no adapter argv, environment or option defaults. It lists active contributions, not proof that each executable is installed. plugins.list also contains contributed summaries and advertises the debugAdapters feature.

debug.configure, debug.launch and debug.attach accept adapterId and adapterOptions. Defaults from the selected launch/attach declaration are shallow merged with saved/per-call options. The host supplies common fields last: request/type/cwd, program/args/env on launch, stopOnEntry and the explicit attach PID. noDebug is false. Options cannot override those fields or internal adapter selection/transport fields. Nested option objects replace the corresponding defaults rather than recursively merging them.

The common program/script field, when nonempty, is resolved relative to the workspace and must name a real file; explicitly selected absolute programs remain allowed. The working directory must remain inside the workspace. A contributed adapter may use an empty program with its own options, such as a module name. User argv boundaries, Unicode and environment removals are preserved. The DAP request is capped at 64 KiB. The adapter's optional default exception filters are configured before configurationDone; richer exception filter UI remains pending. Native profile validation rejects unknown fields and validates nested options and scalar collections before serialization; vendor-specific parameters belong in adapterOptions.

The native worker uses initialize → launch/attach → initialized/configuration → configurationDone through the existing DAP transport. Unsupported launch/attach requests are rejected before process creation; unavailable providers disable the corresponding GUI commands and show a warning. An absent executable produces an installation/selection error. The host does not silently switch to a different provider. Native/.NET runtime and custom executable controls apply to builtin; contributed argv/environment belong to the registered definition.

Run without debugging still uses the existing native/.NET or project-task Run services. Selecting a DAP provider does not replace those runners. Language-server configuration and debugger selection remain independent.

Permissions and lifetime#

The Engine publishes one atomic active-plugin service snapshot for LSP and DAP. The DAP owner stores immutable active definitions and its own registry epoch. Identical registry refreshes do not invalidate queued launches. A queued contributed launch is rejected if the registry changed before execution, including a rapid disable/re-enable. Changing unrelated adapters does not revoke an already active session whose own definition remains identical.

Removing/disabling/changing the active adapter marks it revoked and wakes its owner, including when its channel is already idle/exited. Revocation interrupts request/configuration waits. The worker disconnects and stops the adapter, closes owned program terminals, invalidates frame/variable inspection and reports failure. Launched debuggees are terminated; explicitly attached processes are detached and remain alive. adapterRevoked exposes teardown in progress. Completion/failure of launch requests is reported after owned cleanup; the service retains ownership through termination. Unexpected adapter exit also cleans up launched targets. Workspace shutdown stops DAP work before waiting for plugin event callbacks.

The selected profile ID is retained after disable, so re-enabling restores an explicit choice rather than rewriting settings. Existing plugin libraries remain pinned until their normal reverse-order shutdown. DAP transport/child ownership belongs to the host, not the plugin's activation or shutdown callback.

Exported ABI2 host services now include:

  • debug.adapters: read-only summaries, no extra manifest permission.
  • debug.profile/status: require process.execute; allowed during read-only callbacks since they inspect cached data, which can include sensitive values.
  • debug.configure/breakpoints: require both process.execute and workspace.write; denied during read-only callbacks/snapshot handshakes.
  • debug.launch/attach/stop/pause/continue/next/stepIn/stepOut/evaluate/variables/ frame/thread/source: require process.execute and a normal mutating callback.

MCP retains the actual SDK permission checks for these operations. Native plugins and selected debug engines are trusted code with OS access; descriptor validation is not process sandboxing. Expression evaluation and adapter-specific options may execute target/debugger code. No arbitrary external filesystem writes are granted by a catalogue read. Reverse runInTerminal requests use bounded existing terminal services and a workspace-checked working directory, and are denied during teardown.

Bundled example, boundaries and validation#

The Unreal extension contributes cycode.unreal.lldb using the installed CodeLLDB tool and the same native DAP worker, with numeric pid attachment and C++ source language metadata. This replaces no UBT service and does not add Blueprint visualizers, Live Coding or verified UnrealEditor debugging. Existing installed CodeLLDB selection remains available through builtin too.

This addition supports stdio, one session per workspace and the implemented native DAP request set. TCP-only engines need a real stdio bridge supplied by their integration. Nested/child sessions, arbitrary reverse requests, custom DAP methods, remote attach setup, exception-filter controls, advanced memory/data breakpoints and adapter-specific UI are still separate work. Java/JS/browser/Python engines are not automatically installed or validated by registering this API.

Windows x64/MSVC production application/core/CLI and bundled plugins compile with tests disabled. Source assertions cover descriptor/option limits, variable expansion, metadata privacy, PID mapping, GUI parameter validation, native registry activation and official MCP permissions. Extended actual-LLDB acceptance covers contributed launch/attach and revoke/terminate/detach behavior when run; it has not been executed after the Kaspersky interruption. No new test executable or app window was launched. Linux/macOS and real third-party-adapter acceptance remain pending; see Validation and Testing.

pages.title: Signed local plugin packages
pages.html:
Signed local plugin packages#

Extensions > Plugin packages installs, updates and removes local native-extension packages. This installation-wide selection is separate from the existing per-project enable/disable settings. Six bundled/legacy extensions keep their existing discovery and app-update mechanism; managed packages cannot replace their IDs. The manager does not download packages or operate a marketplace.

Desktop workflow#

Choose a package folder or enter its path, then Inspect package. Inspection verifies the signature and all payload hashes without loading native code. It shows the publisher fingerprint, requested host-service permissions, version, target platform and compatibility. Publisher labels are local names, not verified organization names. Verify the fingerprint independently before explicitly enrolling a new publisher. The trust checkbox and Trust publisher button only enroll the key; installation requires a separate Install / update package action after the refreshed inspection.

Only signed packages from already trusted publishers can be installed. Updates must increase the numeric version and keep the same publisher key. A publisher change requires explicit removal followed by a fresh installation. The selected version and four previous versions are retained. Select previous version verifies the retained payload, publisher, host and dependency constraints before rollback. Removing a package checks required dependents before changing the selection.

Selection changes take effect for new application processes. Existing hosts keep their pinned versions, including when switching workspaces in the same process; there is no DLL hot replacement. The UI compares its actual discovered versions against the current selection and reports the difference. Revoking a publisher blocks future process discovery but cannot remove already loaded native code from an existing process. Per-project activation stays separate.

Unused versions can be deleted after they leave the selection/rollback history. The manager takes an exclusive native file lease; a version pinned by another host remains untouched with action:inUse. Deletion uses verified exact file paths, never recursive directory deletion. Unverifiable packages are reported for manual inspection. Cleanup is best effort when the OS denies access; unknown files are not swept. Package directories have a shortened content address for path length, while the complete signed identity is checked against the index before use.

Persistence and transactions#

The writable portable installation owns extensions-managed/, excluded from Git and release archives. It contains index.json, publishers.json, immutable package directories, staging and native lease markers. Do not store it in an SDK task workspace: installation is explicit persistent application state.

Global shared/exclusive OS leases coordinate index/trust reads and writes across processes. Byte-baseline atomic writes and SHA-512 revision tokens reject stale edits. Copying occurs outside the index lock; commit checks both revisions again. Files are copied exclusively into an owned staging directory and checked while streaming. A failed unpublished copy attempts exact-file cleanup, with directory identity checks. A successfully published version whose selection commit fails is an unused package, available for guarded cleanup. No existing version is overwritten. An ancillary catalogue error is reported separately from a successful selection commit. The existing UI-free manifest validator is reused by the loader and manager.

The loader freezes a verified selection on its first installation discovery in each process, with shared leases even for dormant packages. It verifies signatures, platform and trust before discovery, and rechecks the complete payload and signed identity before each first library initialization in a host. Switching workspaces cannot adopt an update prepared after process startup. Managed version leases outlive library use and initialization failures, and the process snapshot retains them until process exit. An installation with no managed store requires no store creation during ordinary plugin startup. On POSIX, new owned store directories use owner-only access; actual Linux/macOS behavior remains untested. Native plugins remain trusted code with the account's OS privileges. Signatures authenticate publisher/content; they are not process isolation or a filesystem sandbox. OS-level isolation of untrusted extensions remains separate work.

Package format#

A package is a directory containing package.json, signature.json and the explicitly listed payload. No archive extraction or install script runs. package.json contains:

json
{  "schemaVersion": 1,  "platform": "windows-x64",  "plugin": {    "id": "example.tools",    "name": "Example tools",    "version": "1.0.0",    "abi": 2,    "library": "example_tools",    "permissions": ["workspace.write"]  },  "files": [    {"path": "example_tools.dll", "size": 1234, "sha512": "<128 lowercase hexadecimal characters>", "executable": false}  ]}

The manifest uses the native extension SDK, including optional host version bounds, supported platforms and dependencies. Managed IDs are portable lowercase identifiers up to 100 bytes. The platform names the actual process OS/architecture. Its declared .dll, .so or .dylib library must be listed. The package supports up to 32 permissions and 32 dependencies, with known dependency fields only. Names are bounded; metadata never supplies runtime host state.

signature.json contains algorithm Ed25519, a 32-byte publicKey and a 64-byte signature, both lowercase hexadecimal. The signed message is the exact concatenation of UTF-8 CyCode plugin package v1 followed by LF and the raw package.json bytes. This is ordinary Ed25519, not Ed25519ph. The full package identity is SHA-512 of CyCode package identity v1, LF, the hexadecimal public key, LF and those raw bytes. File checksums use SHA-512 of file bytes. Whitespace changes require a new signature. Duplicate JSON keys, excessive nesting, symlinks/Windows reparse points, path traversal, alternate data streams, portable-name collisions and unexpected installed files/directories are refused. The host-generated manifest must match the signed declaration exactly.

Limits: 256 KiB package metadata, 2 KiB signature envelope, 256 files, 64 MiB per file and 256 MiB total; paths up to 1024 UTF-8 bytes, 32 components and 160 bytes per component. Actual OS/path limits still apply. Up to 64 selected packages and 128 publisher records are accepted. Dependency traversal is limited to 128 edges per path. The catalogue scans at most 4096 stored entries, returns 128 unused versions at a time and bounds storage-integrity diagnostics. Native initialization and external runtime dependencies still need real validation; matching metadata does not prove that a library exports the required ABI correctly.

Authoring#

app/scripts/package_plugin.py creates a package from an existing native build, an SDK manifest and explicit --file selections. Its optional authoring dependency is Python cryptography; the application itself uses pinned Monocypher 4.0.3. Supply an existing Ed25519 PKCS8 PEM private key outside the payload/output folders. No key is generated, downloaded or included. --ask-password reads an encrypted key's password interactively. Keep signing keys outside repositories and payloads.

sh
python app/scripts/package_plugin.py --manifest plugin.json --payload build/Release --file example_tools.dll --file LICENSE --platform windows-x64 --private-key ../publisher-keys/publisher.pem --output dist/example-tools-1.0.0

Use repeated --file arguments for assets/notices and --executable path for cross-platform helper permissions. The output must be a new directory outside the payload. The script does not load code. The native host remains the authoritative manifest/platform/ABI/dependency validator. Authoring failures may leave an incomplete output directory for inspection; it cannot be installed without valid metadata, signature and payload. Include the extension's own necessary license notices.

MCP and verification#

packages_list/inspect/install/remove/rollback/clean share the native service. Inspection/installation sources remain workspace directories; the desktop picker provides explicit access to folders elsewhere. Publisher enrollment/revocation is only exposed by the desktop, with no MCP trust-mutation operation. Read operations require plugins.execute; mutations also require process.execute and workspace.write. Install needs expectedRevision, expectedTrustRevision and expectedPackage from inspection. Rollback needs both state revisions; remove/clean need the selection revision. Results describe persistent installed state, not temporary task files.

The SDK declares these size-bounded filesystem transactions noncancellable and uses a separate plugin-packages exclusivity group for mutations. Read-only catalogue and inspection jobs do not take the workspace-mutations group. The bridge waits for the native result; after a transport/OS failure refresh the catalogue before retrying. No process runner, scheduler, identity or MCP implementation is duplicated.

Monocypher's official release archive was checked against its published SHA-512, then SHA-256 pinned in dependencies.lock.json. Its full notice is in licenses/Monocypher.txt. Source-only authoring path/duplicate-key checks and real SDK/schema checks passed. Native signature/install/update/rollback/concurrency and GUI acceptance remain unexecuted during the antivirus interruption. No signing key, plugin package, test DLL/executable or app window was created/launched for these checks. Windows production compilation is recorded in Validation; Linux/macOS and clean-machine installation remain untested.

Primary contracts: Monocypher Ed25519, SHA-512, official releases/checksums.
