pages.title: Native extension SDK — ABI 1 and ABI 2
pages.html:
Native extension SDK: ABI 1 and ABI 2#

ABI2 exposes language.documentHighlights through the same permission-free native read as the GUI and MCP. Contributed servers must advertise documentHighlightProvider; status includes documentHighlights. Output retains source identity/revision, backend epoch, query position and normalized Text/Read/Write ranges. C ABI layout/version and edit/process permissions remain unchanged; no STL/ImGui object crosses the boundary. The host's independent occurrence outlines preserve plugin glyph annotations. See Document occurrences.

ABI2 exports language.declaration, language.typeDefinition and language.implementation through the same native owner as definition/references. All five expose source identity/backend/method/position provenance and bounded validated Location/LocationLink rows. The JSON C ABI and read permission model remain; no STL/ImGui object crosses the boundary. Contributed backends use their actual advertised capabilities. See Source navigation.

ABI2 language.symbols/documentSymbols/status and the new language.symbolResolve export share the native hierarchical catalogue, document identity/revision and backend epochs. The JSON C ABI and read-only permission model remain. Resolve accepts only issued session/ index pairs, retains original server data natively and uses bounded expiry/cache and workspace/monitor/backend guards; it does not execute plugin/server commands. Contributed enabled language servers appear in the palette selector; the chosen server's actual advertised methods determine availability. Flat responses are preserved as roots; no host-invented parser/tree is registered. See Symbol navigation.

ABI2 exports read-only build.location with supplied text/directory and no additional permission. Existing source guards, parser and response are shared with the GUI/SDK through the unchanged JSON C ABI. Reading the output itself still requires process.execute. language.status diagnosticRevisions now carries document id/revision/URI, available to plugin consumers checking freshness. See Compiler locations and Diagnostics.

ABI2 exports project.status and project.output through the existing JSON host service. Output requires process.execute but is readable from read-only callbacks; status is permission-free metadata. Actual task/context/journal ownership remains native, with no STL observer or new C ABI crossing the plugin boundary. Trusted plugin processes are not automatically captured; see Project output.

ABI2 exports build.output as a read-only host service requiring process.execute because compiler output can contain private data. Read-only provider callbacks may call it with that permission. The existing JSON C ABI is unchanged, with no STL or native output callback exposed to plugins. Output from arbitrary native plugin processes is not captured; see Live build output.

ABI2 exports read-only unreal.artifacts without additional permissions; provider 1.5.0 advertises artifacts. Native debug run/launch checks current scoped Editor outputs, and Unreal build results include an assessment or postflight uncertainty. Configuration remains possible before compilation. No new C ABI or process owner; actual extension/Unreal acceptance is pending. See Unreal outputs.

Project provider callbacks for inspect, artifacts, launchProfile and automationPlan retain host read access and reject host mutation services, even if the plugin has workspace.write. These restrictions cover host callbacks, not arbitrary in-process native plugin code. Custom revision-control actions keep their existing dispatch.

Prepared launch profiles now carry a persistent unrealLaunch binding in the same JSON host services. debug.configure/run/launch use the native Unreal validator; null explicitly detaches for manual editing and legacy unbound profiles remain supported. No STL/context crosses the C ABI and no extra host operation is added. Bundled Unreal provider 1.5.0 uses the updated host behavior. Actual extension/ Unreal runtime acceptance remains pending; see Unreal launch.

ABI2 exports unreal.launchProfile through the same native inspector/profile generator as desktop/SDK. It requires process.execute, matching debug.profile, because its observed profile can contain a private environment; read-only provider callbacks may prepare but cannot save/launch. debug.configure accepts optional expectedProfile for conflict-safe saving and still requires workspace.write. Bundled Unreal provider 1.5.0 advertises launchProfile. No ABI/dependency change; actual plugin acceptance remains pending. See Unreal launch.

ABI2 exports unreal.automationPlan/automationRun for reviewed cooking/packaging. Plan is read-only; run requires process.execute and workspace.write, rejects read-only callback mutation and uses the common cancellable build owner/events. Issued previews/guards, persistent outputs and actual/uncertain outcomes match desktop/SDK. Bundled Unreal provider 1.5.0 advertises both actions with these permissions. No ABI change; actual plugin acceptance remains pending. See Unreal automation.

ABI2 exports vcs.replay.state/plan/apply through the shared reviewed cherry-pick/ revert owner. State/plan are read-only; apply requires process/workspace/VCS permissions and rejects mutation from read-only callbacks. Typed Git selection, guards, persistent intents and actual/uncertain outcomes match the desktop/SDK. No ABI/CyUI module change; actual plugin acceptance remains pending. See Git replay.

ABI2 exports vcs.merge.state/plan/commit/quit through the reviewed native owner. State/preview are read-only; commit/quit require all process/workspace/VCS permissions and retain noncancellable ownership. Message/hooks policy, metadata/ index/document guards, persistent intent and actual/uncertain outcomes match the desktop/SDK. No ABI/CyUI module change; actual plugin acceptance remains pending. See Merge workflow.

ABI2 adds vcs.checkout.plan/apply/undo for the shared working-file owner. Preview is read-only; apply/Undo require process/workspace/VCS permissions and retain noncancellable ownership. Binary payloads stay private to Resources; generic resource IDs cannot bypass Git preview guards. No ABI or CyUI module change; actual plugin acceptance remains pending. See Git working files.

ABI2 exports vcs.conflict.list/inspect/plan/apply through the common native Git owner. Only apply mutates, requiring process/workspace/VCS permissions; provider read-only callbacks cannot use it to mutate. Explicit repository/index/preview guards, index-only effects and actual/uncertain outcomes match desktop/SDK. No C ABI or CyUI module changes; native plugin acceptance is pending. See Git conflicts.

ABI2 now exports eight shared worktree methods: catalogue/plan are read-only, add/remove/move/repair require VCS/workspace/process permissions, and lock/unlock retain their existing VCS permission contract. Read-only provider callbacks cannot mutate through these exports. Move/repair use the native observed preview and postflight owner, including complete linked-set repair audit and uncertainty. C ABI and CyUI dependencies remain unchanged; real plugin acceptance is pending. See Git worktrees.

ABI2 vcs.submodule.settingsPlan and vcs.submodule.settings share the same reviewed URL/tracking-branch service as the desktop/SDK. Preview has no mutation permission; application requires all VCS/workspace/process permissions and retains noncancellable ownership. Old unsafe values stay private, other metadata/index/ checkout state is checked, and partial outcomes remain explicit. C ABI and module dependencies are unchanged; native/plugin runtime acceptance remains pending.

ABI2 also exports vcs.submodule.deinitPlan (inspection) and vcs.submodule.deinit (all VCS/workspace/process mutation permissions). They share the native reviewed cleanup guards and retained Git metadata, typed actual outcome and noncancellable process ownership. There is no ABI, dependency or module change. Real plugin/runtime acceptance is pending; see Git submodules.

The public contract is app/include/cycode/PluginAPI.h. Core/CLI remain free of SDL, ImGui and CyUI; the desktop renders the contributed models with its selected CyUI modules. Native extensions are trusted platform-specific code. The host loads installed manifests from runtime/plugins and extensions beside the installation, plus verified managed packages from the installation store. It never discovers code from a newly opened project's arbitrary plugin directory.

Six bundled extensions are built with CyCode: the ABI1 Text statistics reference, the ABI2 Unreal project tools, Subversion, Perforce, Mercurial and Diversion providers. Windows development archives include their manifests/libraries under extensions/. Native binaries must be rebuilt per OS and architecture. Signed local packages now have a separate installation/update/ removal/rollback workflow in Extensions; see Plugin packages. Marketplace/network distribution, untrusted-code isolation and hot replacement remain separate work. Bundled extensions retain the app's own update mechanism.

Manifest, activation and lifetime#

A manifest is UTF-8 JSON; library is a local basename without its extension:

text
{  "id": "example.tools",  "name": "Example tools",  "version": "1.2.0",  "abi": 2,  "library": "example_tools",  "hostVersion": {"minimum":"0.2.0","maximumExclusive":"1.0.0"},  "platforms": ["windows-x64","linux-x64","macos-arm64"],  "permissions": ["workspace.write"],  "dependencies": [    {"id":"example.base","minimum":"1.0.0","maximumExclusive":"2.0.0"}  ]}

Versions are numeric major.minor.patch (components 0–999999), not a complete SemVer range language. Dependencies are topologically ordered; missing/incompatible dependencies, duplicates, cycles, malformed manifests and registration failures are reported in the inventory. Optional dependencies use optional:true. An init failure removes that plugin's contributions and calls its available cleanup export.

hostVersion and platforms are optional. Older manifests remain accepted. Host version bounds use the same numeric major.minor.patch syntax; minimum is inclusive and maximumExclusive exclusive. Empty/reversed ranges, unknown range keys, invalid platform IDs and duplicate platforms are rejected. Platform IDs are windows-x64, windows-arm64, windows-x86, linux-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x86, macos-x64 and macos-arm64. The architecture describes the CyCode process, which is the architecture its native libraries must match.

Compatibility is checked before opening the DLL/shared library, including for disabled plugins. An incompatible plugin stays unloaded and appears with state:incompatible, compatibility.compatible:false and a precise error. Its required dependents cannot load. plugins.list.host supplies version, OS, architecture, platform and host feature names; the Extensions panel displays this host alongside compatibility errors. Declared platform support is metadata, not evidence of a tested Linux/macOS build. No package download or alternative binary is selected automatically.

The Extensions panel enables/disables an installed plugin for the current project. .cycode/plugins.json stores schemaVersion:1 and an enabled object. Configuration writes check both expectedRevision and the previous disk bytes before atomic replacement. Disabling a required dependency of an active plugin is rejected; enable dependencies before their dependent plugin.

A plugin disabled at startup is discovered without loading its native library. Enabled plugins whose required dependencies are disabled remain dormant too. Enabling a dormant plugin initializes it. Enabling its missing dependency also initializes dependents that are already enabled in project preferences, in dependency order; explicitly disabled plugins stay disabled. Disabling an already loaded plugin hides its commands, menus, panels, syntax and providers; its library and state remain pinned until host shutdown. ABI2 activation notifications let plugins stop their background work on disable; legacy extensions without this hook remain responsible for their own lifecycle until shutdown.

Start the GUI with --disable-plugins for a session with no installed native extension loading. CLI syntax is cycode_cli --disable-plugins WORKSPACE METHOD JSON. The flag does not rewrite project activation preferences.

ABI 2 entry points and ownership#

Export:

text
int cycode_plugin_init_v2(const CyCodeHostV2 *host, void **instance);void cycode_plugin_shutdown_v2(void *instance);

Shutdown is optional, but a plugin allocating an instance must release it. Verify abi_version == CYCODE_PLUGIN_ABI_V2 and struct_size before reading callbacks. Return zero on successful init. Store a host copy in each instance, rather than a DLL-global host pointer: several workspaces can share the same loaded library.

Activation notifications#

The original ABI2 host prefix remains unchanged. A trailing uint64_t features advertises optional capabilities. Read that tail only when struct_size is at least sizeof(CyCodeHostV2) for this header; existing binaries using the original prefix and its size check continue to work. A plugin requiring lifecycle support checks features & CYCODE_HOST_FEATURE_ACTIVATION_V2 after checking the size. No STL object or allocator crosses the boundary.

Export the optional hook:

cpp
extern "C" CYCODE_PLUGIN_EXPORT voidcycode_plugin_active_v2(void *instance, uint32_t active) noexcept;

With that feature, initialization registers dormant plugin state. Start background work only after active=1. Startup notification follows successful initialization with active dependencies; explicit activation follows the configuration's guarded disk commit. A failed configuration write does not notify activation. Duplicate enabled-state requests do not repeat notifications. active=0 follows successful disable, and must stop/join plugin-owned work before returning. At shutdown the host sends active=0 to active instances in reverse dependency order before calling their shutdown export; already inactive instances receive no extra stop. The host selects cleanup for the manifest's ABI only: a library exporting both shutdown families receives the matching one, preventing a second cleanup pass.

Notifications execute serially with normal plugin callbacks. They cannot veto a configuration change, call host services (including reads), or throw across the ABI. An escaped exception is recorded in lifecycle.error; native crashes cannot be contained. plugins.list includes lifecycle.supported (null before loading) and the last notified lifecycle.active state. The bundled Unreal extension uses this hook and retains its per-instance profile across disable/reactivate.

Document/workspace/build subscriptions use the separate events contribution and optional feature bits; see Workspace events. The lifecycle hook alone does not provide subscriptions or a process sandbox. Plugins without it keep their prior ABI1/ABI2 behavior.

host.contribute(context, kind, descriptor_json, callback) registers contributions during initialization. It returns zero on success. Host invocations are serial; callbacks receive their instance and UTF-8 JSON and must return plugin-owned JSON valid until the next invocation. Input/output are bounded to 4 MiB. No exceptions, STL objects, allocators or ImGui contexts cross the C boundary. An ABI2 result with a nonempty string error is a failed operation, propagated to the UI/MCP job as failure; catch exceptions inside the plugin and return that JSON.

host.request(context, method, parameters_json) is available from that plugin's callback thread. It returns host-owned JSON with ok and result, or ok:false and error; copy it before the next request. Requests from plugin worker threads or initialization are rejected. Exported services currently are workspace.describe, workspace.files, templates.list/preview/create, resources.preview/children/trash/events/apply/undo, documents.list/read/create/replace/save and unreal.inspect/ generate/build/database/prepare. Document/resource mutations and project creation require workspace.write in the manifest; Unreal process operations require process.execute. Document revisions, path containment and disk-save guards remain enforced by Engine.

Additional exports are tests.discover/run/cancel and language.configure (requiring process.execute), and read-only language.status/complete/hover/ signature/definition/references/symbols/documentSymbols/highlight.

The JSON host now also exports read-only language.codeActions/codeActionPrepare, language.rename/format and changes.preview. changes.apply/undo require workspace.write and are refused from provider read callbacks. Annotated plans retain passive labels and effective file groups; applying requires the issued per-plan confirmedAnnotations IDs for every required label. The same native guards and Undo serve the desktop and SDK; no C ABI layout changed. See annotated changes.

VCS/project read callbacks (detect/inspect/status/diff/log/history/show/blame) cannot call mutating host services. These are host-service checks, not an OS sandbox: a trusted native DLL still has the process user's OS privileges. MCP generic plugin callbacks/configuration require plugins.execute, workspace.write and process.execute; generic VCS actions also need vcs.write.

Contributions#

ABI2 host services also export vcs.submodules and guarded vcs.submodule.init/sync/update for the built-in Git provider. Mutations require vcs.write, workspace.write and process.execute, with observed repository and catalogue guards; read-only callbacks cannot mutate. They share the native process owner and return actual status rather than emulated VCS state. See Git submodules for pending runtime acceptance.

vcs.submodule.addPlan performs local inspection without mutation permission. The separate vcs.submodule.add requires all three permissions and the observed preview revision before cloning/staging. It refuses destination/metadata reuse, pins relevant index/parent context and returns actual process/refresh results. Neither changes the C ABI or introduces a plugin-owned Git process.

Debugger host services also export debug.memory/disassemble/exceptionInfo and paged debug.variables, with process.execute and stopped-generation guards. debug.functionBreakpoints/exceptionBreakpoints additionally need workspace.write to persist their checked configurations. All use the existing host-owned adapter, rather than entering plugin code for inspection. See Advanced debugging for capabilities, bounds and limits.

Build host services include build.inspect/presets/status/configure/run/cancel and msbuild.inspect/build/rebuild/clean/restore/evaluate/prepare. Read operations need no additional manifest permission; build execution and cancellation require process.execute. See Build cancellation for native reservation lifetime and the boundary of generic plugin-job cancellation.

project.inspect exports the common Cargo/npm/Java/Maven/Gradle/shader task model without executing tools. project.configure/build/test/install/script/launch/debug/cancel require process.execute, and read-only provider callbacks cannot invoke them. Those routes retain the same native workspace guards, deadline, process owner and cancellation as desktop/MCP requests; plugins do not supply a second task runner. Host callbacks are synchronous and serialized. A long plugin-issued task can be cancelled through the separate desktop/MCP project.cancel route; cancelling a generic plugin job does not automatically identify and cancel its nested task.

All ABI2 contribution IDs begin with the plugin ID plus a dot; duplicate IDs and built-in command replacement are rejected. Git's provider ID is reserved.

Kind Descriptor and callback
command id, title, optional category, context global/document/editor, shortcuts array and when. Callback receives context, active text/revision from GUI or explicit MCP input.
menu id, title, command belonging to the same plugin, location; no callback. Locations: file/edit/view/navigate/build/run/vcs/extensions/editor/project.
panel id, title, optional when; callback returns the model below. Host owns docking, native detached windows, DPI, keyboard and rendering.
project id, title, capabilities; callback receives action and parameters. Current generic invocation is plugins.project.
vcs id, title, capabilities and optional actions; callback receives action and parameters with workspace/root.
syntax id, name, extensions/filenames, optional base/wordLists/rules; no callback. Registration uses the common CyUI Code registry.
template id/title/language/buildSystem/requirements, entry/openFile, bounded files and optional typed fields; no callback. The host previews and creates files through the shared project service. See Project templates.
languageServer id/title/arguments/settings/languages; no callback or when. Requires process.execute; host-owned LSP process and shared semantic services. See Development workflows.
debugAdapter id/title/type/arguments/requests, optional launch/attach/environment/pidField; no callback or when. Requires process.execute; shared host-owned DAP worker, explicit profile selection and revocation. See Plugin debuggers.
events id, optional types filters and maxBatch 1–32; automatic serial callback for active plugins, initial read-only snapshot handshake, bounded journal and error suspension. See Workspace events.

when is an equality/membership object. The current GUI context contains document, readOnly, path, provider and project (unreal/msbuild/cargo/npm/java/folder as detected). Array values mean membership. This is intentionally not an arbitrary expression language. Commands, palette items and menu items share availability checks. Shortcuts use existing profile syntax, including chords; default plugin shortcuts yield to occupied host bindings. User overrides remain stored if a plugin is absent.

Panels and editing#

A panel is an asynchronous, dockable native application panel. Opening/refreshing calls its callback with event:read and context. The model accepts revision, text, properties, rows and actions:

text
{  "revision": 1,  "text": "Example model",  "properties": [    {"id":"enabled","title":"Enabled","value":true,"readOnly":false}  ],  "rows": [{"name":"Source","value":"workspace"}],  "actions": [{"command":"example.tools.inspect","title":"Inspect"}]}

Property types are boolean, signed integer, floating point and text. IDs must be stable. CyUI Inspector retains drafts; cancel does not call the plugin. A committed edit sends event:commit, property, value, expectedRevision and context. The plugin validates it, commits one application-owned transaction and returns the next model. The host does not invent history for arbitrary plugin data. A plugin requiring Undo/Redo must own that history and expose corresponding commands. Document edits still enter the normal editor synchronization/Undo path.

Models are validated before drawing, limited to 128 properties, 2,000 rows and 64 actions. Returned error text is displayed. A panel action can invoke only its owner's commands. The current model API is not an arbitrary ImGui/GPU callback or a specialized shader/web editor API.

Syntax packs#

A syntax descriptor can inherit any built-in catalogue ID through base and replace selected Lexilla wordLists, or define rules:

text
{  "id":"example.tools.config",  "name":"Example configuration",  "extensions":["examplecfg"],  "rules":{    "keywords":["option","section"],    "types":["vector","number"],    "lineComment":"#",    "blockCommentStart":"/*",    "blockCommentEnd":"*/",    "caseSensitive":true  }}

Rules also accept functions, quotes and a one-byte escape character. Names and lists are bounded before registration; CyUI performs its own definition checks. The host retains registration ownership across application contexts and restores built-in associations when the last owner releases a definition. Syntax changes never modify document text or Undo history. The CyUI registry is process-wide: simultaneous in-process application contexts share associations. Independent CyCode processes have independent registries.

This reuses CyUI's 101 built-in modes, including HLSL/GLSL/logs. It does not add completion, diagnostics, LSP or debugging for a newly colored language. Custom native lexer callbacks and debugger registration are not exported through ABI2. The separate languageServer contribution now supplies analysis for additional file types; a syntax descriptor alone still does not start a server.

CMake preset actions#

CMake plugins can also use build.presetPlan and build.presetRun through the existing JSON host request (process.execute for running). They share native review guards and cancellation ownership with the desktop/SDK; no C ABI layout change is required. See Preset actions.

Call and type hierarchies#

The existing JSON host request also exports language.hierarchyPrepare, language.hierarchyExpand and language.hierarchyStatus as read-only language services. Plugins use issued session/node IDs, not a raw URI/server item. No ABI layout change or separate language-process owner is introduced. See Hierarchies for bounds, backend and validation limits.

Revision control by project/root#

Git remains the built-in default. .cycode/vcs.json stores schemaVersion:1 and mappings:[{root,provider}]. The deepest matching root selects a provider for contextPath; the same mapping drives GUI actions, menus and native/MCP operations. vcs.context describes the current provider/capabilities/actions/mapping revision. vcs.configure atomically updates a mapping with expectedRevision. An explicit provider parameter overrides selection for an individual request.

Unavailable configured providers remain unavailable, with an explicit error. They never silently route writes to Git. Nested non-Git mappings remain supported. Git additionally follows the active file's nearest workspace repository or an explicit session-backed selector, with repository/identity parameters on typed SDK operations. Linked-worktree controls now share eight ABI2 host exports with the native Engine and SDK. See Git worktrees.

Provider status returns provider, repository, branch, files:[{status,path}] and message. Paths are checked against the workspace. Ordinary process actions return exitCode/output/timedOut/truncated. Additional provider actions are described by:

text
{  "id":"checkout","title":"Check out file","scope":"file",  "fields":[{"id":"description","title":"Description","required":true}]}

Actions must be advertised capabilities. scope is file or repository; fields are bounded text inputs with optional default/required. Host menus and the VCS panel adapt to these actions; Git-specific branch/stash/commit UI is hidden for other providers. vcs.providerAction accepts action, contextPath and input for generic MCP invocation. Unsupported capabilities fail explicitly. Mutations refuse dirty buffers and reconcile clean buffers after the operation.

The bundled cycode.svn.provider implements local SVN status/diffs, history/blame, file add/revert and mapped-copy commit/update with a separately installed client. It uses these same descriptors, root mappings and shared review views. See Subversion for exact scope, guards and unexecuted acceptance. The native test fixture separately exercises permissions and root persistence; it is not evidence of real-server validation. The bundled cycode.perforce.provider adds checked-client status/diff/history/annotations, file checkout/add/reopen/revert/submit/locks and clean-project sync. See Perforce for precise mapping/changelist/stream limits and pending real-server acceptance. The bundled cycode.mercurial.provider supplies JSON status/history, Diff/annotations, exact-file add/forget/revert, commit, verified clean update, bookmarks/named branches and configured-alias pull/push. It uses the same mapping/UI/guard contracts; see Mercurial for restrictions and pending real-client/GUI acceptance. The bundled cycode.diversion.provider adds status/review, commit/reset, branch creation, clean checkout/update and file locks using its automatic tracking/sync model. See Diversion for text-format limits and unexecuted runtime acceptance. Custom providers describes how a future independent revision-control backend contributes its own actions without Git emulation.

Typed SDK Git operations now explicitly select the built-in workspace-root Git service and accept only provider:"git". Native GUI/CLI mappings remain provider aware. External SDK provider calls use vcs_provider_action with its existing plugin/process/workspace/VCS permissions and generic result schema; they do not run under Git read-only permissions or Git-specific result validation.

Unreal extension and ABI1#

app/plugins/unreal is a working ABI2 example. It contributes conditional Build commands, a dockable project overview with revision-checked profile properties, and a project provider for detect/inspect/generate/prepare/database/build. It reuses Engine's existing Unreal services, canonical paths and process guards. Inspection is read-only; build/generation actions execute real trusted UBT rules. This adds an extension seam without removing existing Unreal functionality. The original backend/panel, Blueprint tools, Live Coding and Unreal Editor integration have not all been extracted or implemented.

ABI1 remains supported with its original CyCodeHostV1, add_command, add_vcs_provider and cycode_plugin_init entry point. CYCODE_PLUGIN_ABI stays 1; new code explicitly selects CYCODE_PLUGIN_ABI_V2. ABI1 shutdown is cycode_plugin_shutdown(void). Existing plugin IDs/callbacks keep working.

Verification and remaining scope#

CTest extensions loads real shared libraries and checks instance isolation, dependency ordering, activation persistence, callback permissions, document/model revisions, VCS routing and conflicting configuration writers. extension_ui renders the actual application views in EN/FR, six themes and three DPI scales with no native windows, and checks command/panel/syntax activation. unreal_extension uses a real temporary .uproject and target/module files without building user sources.

Compatibility boundary, activation notification, dormant-dependency and matching shutdown-family assertions have been added to the existing extension suite. During the current antivirus interruption they passed MSVC syntax checks only; they have not been executed. The app/core/CLI and bundled plugin compile on Windows with native tests disabled. See Validation.

ABI2 languageServer contributions now register additional file selectors and separate host-owned LSP processes through the shared completion, diagnostics, navigation and guarded edit paths. Registration requires process.execute, has no callback and does not start the server. Disabling removes routes, stops the owner and invalidates pending completion epochs. Language preferences and guarded save/forget are shared native host services; inspection does not activate saved servers and absent-plugin profiles are retained. See Language preferences. The host also exports test discovery, run/cancellation and language inspection/query/configuration services. See Development workflows for descriptors and limits.

Broader event subscriptions, extension installation/update/removal, crash isolation, arbitrary editor/GPU views, native custom debugger protocol APIs and additional third-party VCS adapters remain work items. These APIs do not establish complete Rider/Visual Studio feature parity.

Binary payloads stay private to Resources; generic resource IDs cannot bypass Git preview guards. No ABI or CyUI module change; actual plugin acceptance remains pending. See Git working files . ABI2 exports vcs.conflict.list/inspect/plan/apply through the common native Git owner. Only apply mutates, requiring process/workspace/VCS permissions; provider read-only callbacks cannot use it to mutate. Explicit repository/index/preview guards, index-only effects and actual/uncertain outcomes match desktop/SDK. No C ABI or CyUI module changes; native plugin acceptance is pending. See Git conflicts . ABI2 now exports eight shared worktree methods: catalogue/plan are read-only, add/remove/move/repair require VCS/workspace/process permissions, and lock/unlock retain their existing VCS permission contract. Read-only provider callbacks cannot mutate through these exports. Move/repair use the native observed preview and postflight owner, including complete linked-set repair audit and uncertainty. C ABI and CyUI dependencies remain unchanged; real plugin acceptance is pending. See Git worktrees . ABI2 vcs.submodule.settingsPlan and vcs.submodule.settings share the same reviewed URL/tracking-branch service as the desktop/SDK. Preview has no mutation permission; application requires all VCS/workspace/process permissions and retains noncancellable ownership. Old unsafe values stay private, other metadata/index/ checkout state is checked, and partial outcomes remain explicit. C ABI and module dependencies are unchanged; native/plugin runtime acceptance remains pending. ABI2 also exports vcs.submodule.deinitPlan (inspection) and vcs.submodule.deinit (all VCS/workspace/process mutation permissions). They share the native reviewed cleanup guards and retained Git metadata, typed actual outcome and noncancellable process ownership. There is no ABI, dependency or module change. Real plugin/runtime acceptance is pending; see Git submodules . The public contract is app/include/cycode/PluginAPI.h. Core/CLI remain free of SDL, ImGui and CyUI; the desktop renders the contributed models with its selected CyUI modules. Native extensions are trusted platform-specific code. The host loads installed manifests from runtime/plugins and extensions beside the installation, plus verified managed packages from the installation store. It never discovers code from a newly opened project's arbitrary plugin directory. Six bundled extensions are built with CyCode: the ABI1 Text statistics reference, the ABI2 Unreal project tools, Subversion, Perforce, Mercurial and Diversion providers. Windows development archives include their manifests/libraries under extensions/. Native binaries must be rebuilt per OS and architecture. Signed local packages now have a separate installation/update/ removal/rollback workflow in Extensions; see Plugin packages . Marketplace/network distribution, untrusted-code isolation and hot replacement remain separate work. Bundled extensions retain the app's own update mechanism. Manifest, activation and lifetime # A manifest is UTF-8 JSON; library is a local basename without its extension: text Copy { "id": "example.tools", "name": "Example tools", "version": "1.2.0", "abi": 2, "library": "example_tools", "hostVersion": {"minimum":"0.2.0","maximumExclusive":"1.0.0"}, "platforms": ["windows-x64","linux-x64","macos-arm64"], "permissions": ["workspace.write"], "dependencies": [ {"id":"example.base","minimum":"1.0.0","maximumExclusive":"2.0.0"} ] } Versions are numeric major.minor.patch (components 0–999999), not a complete SemVer range language. Dependencies are topologically ordered; missing/incompatible dependencies, duplicates, cycles, malformed manifests and registration failures are reported in the inventory. Optional dependencies use optional:true. An init failure removes that plugin's contributions and calls its available cleanup export. hostVersion and platforms are optional. Older manifests remain accepted. Host version bounds use the same numeric major.minor.patch syntax; minimum is inclusive and maximumExclusive exclusive. Empty/reversed ranges, unknown range keys, invalid platform IDs and duplicate platforms are rejected. Platform IDs are windows-x64 , windows-arm64 , windows-x86 , linux-x64 , linux-arm64 , linux-x86 , macos-x64 and macos-arm64 . The architecture describes the CyCode process, which is the architecture its native libraries must match. Compatibility is checked before opening the DLL/shared library, including for disabled plugins. An incompatible plugin stays unloaded and appears with state:incompatible , compatibility.compatible:false and a precise error. Its required dependents cannot load. plugins.list.host supplies version, OS, architecture, platform and host feature names; the Extensions panel displays this host alongside compatibility errors. Declared platform support is metadata, not evidence of a tested Linux/macOS build. No package download or alternative binary is selected automatically. The Extensions panel enables/disables an installed plugin for the current project. .cycode/plugins.json stores schemaVersion:1 and an enabled object. Configuration writes check both expectedRevision and the previous disk bytes before atomic replacement. Disabling a required dependency of an active plugin is rejected; enable dependencies before their dependent plugin. A plugin disabled at startup is discovered without loading its native library. Enabled plugins whose required dependencies are disabled remain dormant too. Enabling a dormant plugin initializes it. Enabling its missing dependency also initializes dependents that are already enabled in project preferences, in dependency order; explicitly disabled plugins stay disabled. Disabling an already loaded plugin hides its commands, menus, panels, syntax and providers; its library and state remain pinned until host shutdown. ABI2 activation notifications let plugins stop their background work on disable; legacy extensions without this hook remain responsible for their own lifecycle until shutdown. Start the GUI with --disable-plugins for a session with no installed native extension loading. CLI syntax is cycode_cli --disable-plugins WORKSPACE METHOD JSON. The flag does not rewrite project activation preferences. ABI 2 entry points and ownership # Export: text Copy int cycode_plugin_init_v2(const CyCodeHostV2 *host, void **instance); void cycode_plugin_shutdown_v2(void *instance); Shutdown is optional, but a plugin allocating an instance must release it. Verify abi_version == CYCODE_PLUGIN_ABI_V2 and struct_size before reading callbacks. Return zero on successful init. Store a host copy in each instance, rather than a DLL-global host pointer: several workspaces can share the same loaded library. Activation notifications # The original ABI2 host prefix remains unchanged. A trailing uint64_t features advertises optional capabilities. Read that tail only when struct_size is at least sizeof(CyCodeHostV2) for this header; existing binaries using the original prefix and its size check continue to work. A plugin requiring lifecycle support checks features & CYCODE_HOST_FEATURE_ACTIVATION_V2 after checking the size. No STL object or allocator crosses the boundary. Export the optional hook: cpp Copy extern "C" CYCODE_PLUGIN_EXPORT void cycode_plugin_active_v2 ( void * instance , uint32_t active ) noexcept ; With that feature, initialization registers dormant plugin state. Start background work only after active=1 . Startup notification follows successful initialization with active dependencies; explicit activation follows the configuration's guarded disk commit. A failed configuration write does not notify activation. Duplicate enabled-state requests do not repeat notifications. active=0 follows successful disable, and must stop/join plugin-owned work before returning. At shutdown the host sends active=0 to active instances in reverse dependency order before calling their shutdown export; already inactive instances receive no extra stop. The host selects cleanup for the manifest's ABI only: a library exporting both shutdown families receives the matching one, preventing a second cleanup pass. Notifications execute serially with normal plugin callbacks. They cannot veto a configuration change, call host services (including reads), or throw across the ABI. An escaped exception is recorded in lifecycle.error ; native crashes cannot be contained. plugins.list includes lifecycle.supported (null before loading) and the last notified lifecycle.active state. The bundled Unreal extension uses this hook and retains its per-instance profile across disable/reactivate. Document/workspace/build subscriptions use the separate events contribution and optional feature bits; see Workspace events . The lifecycle hook alone does not provide subscriptions or a process sandbox. Plugins without it keep their prior ABI1/ABI2 behavior. host.contribute(context, kind, descriptor_json, callback) registers contributions during initialization. It returns zero on success. Host invocations are serial; callbacks receive their instance and UTF-8 JSON and must return plugin-owned JSON valid until the next invocation. Input/output are bounded to 4 MiB. No exceptions, STL objects, allocators or ImGui contexts cross the C boundary. An ABI2 result with a nonempty string error is a failed operation, propagated to the UI/MCP job as failure; catch exceptions inside the plugin and return that JSON. host.request(context, method, parameters_json) is available from that plugin's callback thread. It returns host-owned JSON with ok and result, or ok:false and error; copy it before the next request. Requests from plugin worker threads or initialization are rejected. Exported services currently are workspace.describe, workspace.files, templates.list/preview/create, resources.preview/children/trash/events/apply/undo, documents.list/read/create/replace/save and unreal.inspect/ generate/build/database/prepare. Document/resource mutations and project creation require workspace.write in the manifest; Unreal process operations require process.execute. Document revisions, path containment and disk-save guards remain enforced by Engine. Additional exports are tests.discover/run/cancel and language.configure (requiring process.execute ), and read-only language.status/complete/hover/ signature/definition/references/symbols/documentSymbols/highlight . The JSON host now also exports read-only language.codeActions/codeActionPrepare, language.rename/format and changes.preview. changes.apply/undo require workspace.write and are refused from provider read callbacks. Annotated plans retain passive labels and effective file groups; applying requires the issued per-plan confirmedAnnotations IDs for every required label. The same native guards and Undo serve the desktop and SDK; no C ABI layout changed. See annotated changes . VCS/project read callbacks (detect/inspect/status/diff/log/history/show/blame) cannot call mutating host services. These are host-service checks, not an OS sandbox: a trusted native DLL still has the process user's OS privileges. MCP generic plugin callbacks/configuration require plugins.execute, workspace.write and process.execute; generic VCS actions also need vcs.write. Contributions # ABI2 host services also export vcs.submodules and guarded vcs.submodule.init/sync/update for the built-in Git provider. Mutations require vcs.write , workspace.write and process.execute , with observed repository and catalogue guards; read-only callbacks cannot mutate. They share the native process owner and return actual status rather than emulated VCS state. See Git submodules for pending runtime acceptance. vcs.submodule.addPlan performs local inspection without mutation permission. The separate vcs.submodule.add requires all three permissions and the observed preview revision before cloning/staging. It refuses destination/metadata reuse, pins relevant index/parent context and returns actual process/refresh results. Neither changes the C ABI or introduces a plugin-owned Git process. Debugger host services also export debug.memory/disassemble/exceptionInfo and paged debug.variables , with process.execute and stopped-generation guards. debug.functionBreakpoints/exceptionBreakpoints additionally need workspace.write to persist their checked configurations. All use the existing host-owned adapter, rather than entering plugin code for inspection. See Advanced debugging for capabilities, bounds and limits. Build host services include build.inspect/presets/status/configure/run/cancel and msbuild.inspect/build/rebuild/clean/restore/evaluate/prepare . Read operations need no additional manifest permission; build execution and cancellation require process.execute . See Build cancellation for native reservation lifetime and the boundary of generic plugin-job cancellation. project.inspect exports the common Cargo/npm/Java/Maven/Gradle/shader task model without executing tools. project.configure/build/test/install/script/launch/debug/cancel require process.execute , and read-only provider callbacks cannot invoke them. Those routes retain the same native workspace guards, deadline, process owner and cancellation as desktop/MCP requests; plugins do not supply a second task runner. Host callbacks are synchronous and serialized. A long plugin-issued task can be cancelled through the separate desktop/MCP project.cancel route; cancelling a generic plugin job does not automatically identify and cancel its nested task. All ABI2 contribution IDs begin with the plugin ID plus a dot; duplicate IDs and built-in command replacement are rejected. Git's provider ID is reserved. Kind Descriptor and callback command id, title, optional category, context global/document/editor, shortcuts array and when. Callback receives context, active text/revision from GUI or explicit MCP input. menu id, title, command belonging to the same plugin, location; no callback. Locations: file/edit/view/navigate/build/run/vcs/extensions/editor/project. panel id, title, optional when; callback returns the model below. Host owns docking, native detached windows, DPI, keyboard and rendering. project id, title, capabilities; callback receives action and parameters. Current generic invocation is plugins.project. vcs id, title, capabilities and optional actions; callback receives action and parameters with workspace/root. syntax id, name, extensions/filenames, optional base/wordLists/rules; no callback. Registration uses the common CyUI Code registry. template id/title/language/buildSystem/requirements, entry/openFile, bounded files and optional typed fields; no callback. The host previews and creates files through the shared project service. See Project templates . languageServer id/title/arguments/settings/languages; no callback or when. Requires process.execute; host-owned LSP process and shared semantic services. See Development workflows . debugAdapter id/title/type/arguments/requests, optional launch/attach/environment/pidField; no callback or when. Requires process.execute; shared host-owned DAP worker, explicit profile selection and revocation. See Plugin debuggers . events id, optional types filters and maxBatch 1–32; automatic serial callback for active plugins, initial read-only snapshot handshake, bounded journal and error suspension. See Workspace events . when is an equality/membership object. The current GUI context contains document, readOnly, path, provider and project (unreal/msbuild/cargo/npm/java/folder as detected). Array values mean membership. This is intentionally not an arbitrary expression language. Commands, palette items and menu items share availability checks. Shortcuts use existing profile syntax, including chords; default plugin shortcuts yield to occupied host bindings. User overrides remain stored if a plugin is absent. Panels and editing # A panel is an asynchronous, dockable native application panel. Opening/refreshing calls its callback with event:read and context. The model accepts revision, text, properties, rows and actions: text Copy { "revision": 1, "text": "Example model", "properties": [ {"id":"enabled","title":"Enabled","value":true,"readOnly":false} ], "rows": [{"name":"Source","value":"workspace"}], "actions": [{"command":"example.tools.inspect","title":"Inspect"}] } Property types are boolean, signed integer, floating point and text. IDs must be stable. CyUI Inspector retains drafts; cancel does not call the plugin. A committed edit sends event:commit, property, value, expectedRevision and context. The plugin validates it, commits one application-owned transaction and returns the next model. The host does not invent history for arbitrary plugin data. A plugin requiring Undo/Redo must own that history and expose corresponding commands. Document edits still enter the normal editor synchronization/Undo path. Models are validated before drawing, limited to 128 properties, 2,000 rows and 64 actions. Returned error text is displayed. A panel action can invoke only its owner's commands. The current model API is not an arbitrary ImGui/GPU callback or a specialized shader/web editor API. Syntax packs # A syntax descriptor can inherit any built-in catalogue ID through base and replace selected Lexilla wordLists, or define rules: text Copy { "id":"example.tools.config", "name":"Example configuration", "extensions":["examplecfg"], "rules":{ "keywords":["option","section"], "types":["vector","number"], "lineComment":"#", "blockCommentStart":"/*", "blockCommentEnd":"*/", "caseSensitive":true } } Rules also accept functions, quotes and a one-byte escape character. Names and lists are bounded before registration; CyUI performs its own definition checks. The host retains registration ownership across application contexts and restores built-in associations when the last owner releases a definition. Syntax changes never modify document text or Undo history. The CyUI registry is process-wide: simultaneous in-process application contexts share associations. Independent CyCode processes have independent registries. This reuses CyUI's 101 built-in modes, including HLSL/GLSL/logs. It does not add completion, diagnostics, LSP or debugging for a newly colored language. Custom native lexer callbacks and debugger registration are not exported through ABI2. The separate languageServer contribution now supplies analysis for additional file types; a syntax descriptor alone still does not start a server. CMake preset actions # CMake plugins can also use build.presetPlan and build.presetRun through the existing JSON host request (process.execute for running). They share native review guards and cancellation ownership with the desktop/SDK; no C ABI layout change is required. See Preset actions . Call and type hierarchies # The existing JSON host request also exports language.hierarchyPrepare, language.hierarchyExpand and language.hierarchyStatus as read-only language services. Plugins use issued session/node IDs, not a raw URI/server item. No ABI layout change or separate language-process owner is introduced. See Hierarchies for bounds, backend and validation limits. Revision control by project/root # Git remains the built-in default. .cycode/vcs.json stores schemaVersion:1 and mappings:[{root,provider}]. The deepest matching root selects a provider for contextPath; the same mapping drives GUI actions, menus and native/MCP operations. vcs.context describes the current provider/capabilities/actions/mapping revision. vcs.configure atomically updates a mapping with expectedRevision. An explicit provider parameter overrides selection for an individual request. Unavailable configured providers remain unavailable, with an explicit error. They never silently route writes to Git. Nested non-Git mappings remain supported. Git additionally follows the active file's nearest workspace repository or an explicit session-backed selector, with repository/identity parameters on typed SDK operations. Linked-worktree controls now share eight ABI2 host exports with the native Engine and SDK. See Git worktrees . Provider status returns provider, repository, branch, files:[{status,path}] and message. Paths are checked against the workspace. Ordinary process actions return exitCode/output/timedOut/truncated. Additional provider actions are described by: text Copy { "id":"checkout","title":"Check out file","scope":"file", "fields":[{"id":"description","title":"Description","required":true}] } Actions must be advertised capabilities. scope is file or repository; fields are bounded text inputs with optional default/required. Host menus and the VCS panel adapt to these actions; Git-specific branch/stash/commit UI is hidden for other providers. vcs.providerAction accepts action, contextPath and input for generic MCP invocation. Unsupported capabilities fail explicitly. Mutations refuse dirty buffers and reconcile clean buffers after the operation. The bundled cycode.svn.provider implements local SVN status/diffs, history/blame, file add/revert and mapped-copy commit/update with a separately installed client. It uses these same descriptors, root mappings and shared review views. See Subversion for exact scope, guards and unexecuted acceptance. The native test fixture separately exercises permissions and root persistence; it is not evidence of real-server validation. The bundled cycode.perforce.provider adds checked-client status/diff/history/annotations, file checkout/add/reopen/revert/submit/locks and clean-project sync. See Perforce for precise mapping/changelist/stream limits and pending real-server acceptance. The bundled cycode.mercurial.provider supplies JSON status/history, Diff/annotations, exact-file add/forget/revert, commit, verified clean update, bookmarks/named branches and configured-alias pull/push. It uses the same mapping/UI/guard contracts; see Mercurial for restrictions and pending real-client/GUI acceptance. The bundled cycode.diversion.provider adds status/review, commit/reset, branch creation, clean checkout/update and file locks using its automatic tracking/sync model. See Diversion for text-format limits and unexecuted runtime acceptance. Custom providers describes how a future independent revision-control backend contributes its own actions without Git emulation. Typed SDK Git operations now explicitly select the built-in workspace-root Git service and accept only provider:"git" . Native GUI/CLI mappings remain provider aware. External SDK provider calls use vcs_provider_action with its existing plugin/process/workspace/VCS permissions and generic result schema; they do not run under Git read-only permissions or Git-specific result validation. Unreal extension and ABI1 # app/plugins/unreal is a working ABI2 example. It contributes conditional Build commands, a dockable project overview with revision-checked profile properties, and a project provider for detect/inspect/generate/prepare/database/build. It reuses Engine's existing Unreal services, canonical paths and process guards. Inspection is read-only; build/generation actions execute real trusted UBT rules. This adds an extension seam without removing existing Unreal functionality. The original backend/panel, Blueprint tools, Live Coding and Unreal Editor integration have not all been extracted or implemented. ABI1 remains supported with its original CyCodeHostV1, add_command, add_vcs_provider and cycode_plugin_init entry point. CYCODE_PLUGIN_ABI stays 1; new code explicitly selects CYCODE_PLUGIN_ABI_V2. ABI1 shutdown is cycode_plugin_shutdown(void). Existing plugin IDs/callbacks keep working. Verification and remaining scope # CTest extensions loads real shared libraries and checks instance isolation, dependency ordering, activation persistence, callback permissions, document/model revisions, VCS routing and conflicting configuration writers. extension_ui renders the actual application views in EN/FR, six themes and three DPI scales with no native windows, and checks command/panel/syntax activation. unreal_extension uses a real temporary .uproject and target/module files without building user sources. Compatibility boundary, activation notification, dormant-dependency and matching shutdown-family assertions have been added to the existing extension suite. During the current antivirus interruption they passed MSVC syntax checks only; they have not been executed. The app/core/CLI and bundled plugin compile on Windows with native tests disabled. See Validation . ABI2 languageServer contributions now register additional file selectors and separate host-owned LSP processes through the shared completion, diagnostics, navigation and guarded edit paths. Registration requires process.execute , has no callback and does not start the server. Disabling removes routes, stops the owner and invalidates pending completion epochs. Language preferences and guarded save/forget are shared native host services; inspection does not activate saved servers and absent-plugin profiles are retained. See Language preferences . The host also exports test discovery, run/cancellation and language inspection/query/configuration services. See Development workflows for descriptors and limits. Broader event subscriptions, extension installation/update/removal, crash isolation, arbitrary editor/GPU views, native custom debugger protocol APIs and additional third-party VCS adapters remain work items. These APIs do not establish complete Rider/Visual Studio feature parity. { "id": "example.tools", "name": "Example tools", "version": "1.2.0", "abi": 2, "library": "example_tools", "hostVersion": {"minimum":"0.2.0","maximumExclusive":"1.0.0"}, "platforms": ["windows-x64","linux-x64","macos-arm64"], "permissions": ["workspace.write"], "dependencies": [ {"id":"example.base","minimum":"1.0.0","maximumExclusive":"2.0.0"} ] } int cycode_plugin_init_v2(const CyCodeHostV2 *host, void **instance); void cycode_plugin_shutdown_v2(void *instance); extern "C" CYCODE_PLUGIN_EXPORT void cycode_plugin_active_v2(void *instance, uint32_t active) noexcept; { "revision": 1, "text": "Example model", "properties": [ {"id":"enabled","title":"Enabled","value":true,"readOnly":false} ], "rows": [{"name":"Source","value":"workspace"}], "actions": [{"command":"example.tools.inspect","title":"Inspect"}] } { "id":"example.tools.config", "name":"Example configuration", "extensions":["examplecfg"], "rules":{ "keywords":["option","section"], "types":["vector","number"], "lineComment":"#", "blockCommentStart":"/*", "blockCommentEnd":"*/", "caseSensitive":true } } { "id":"checkout","title":"Check out file","scope":"file", "fields":[{"id":"description","title":"Description","required":true}] }

pages.title: XML solutions and CMake Presets
pages.html:
XML solutions and CMake Presets#

Visual Studio .slnx#

The chooser, workspace/tree, separate-window opening, MSBuild adapter and C# solution selection accept .slnx alongside .sln. Unreal discovery prefers .sln, then checks .slnx when absent. Several solutions require explicit selection. The UI-free reader uses pinned TinyXML2; opening does not evaluate imports, execute generators, require .NET or rewrite the solution.

It reads UTF-8/BOM and the existing UTF-16 decoding, logical /Folder/ paths with implicit parents, files/projects, display names, explicit GUIDs, stable host IDs, dependency references and missing/external paths. Configuration/platform products default to Debug/Release and Any CPU. Managed/native platform defaults, ordered BuildType/Platform/Build/Deploy rules, custom types/BasedOn and solution defaults feed the existing MSBuild model. The actual build engine receives the original solution; this reader does not replace its evaluator. Indexing retains its mapped configurations and permission/bounds checks. C# acceptance also depends on the installed language server's workspace support.

Bounds: 16 MiB input, 100,000 XML nodes, 32 XML/64 logical-folder levels, 10,000 items, 256 solution configurations, 200,000 project mappings and 64 custom types. DTD/unknown declarations, non-whitespace text, duplicate IDs/paths/configurations, applied inheritance cycles and malformed XML are rejected. Properties remain owned by the actual build engine. Niche project types/aliases need further real-project validation. Microsoft documents MSBuild 17.12+ for .slnx. References: MSBuild command reference, official solution schema/model.

CMake Presets#

The CMake panel selects Configure preset and an optional linked Build preset; Manual settings retains the existing adapter. Presets own binary directory, generator/toolchain and any fixed configuration. A target selection overrides the preset target set. Default build uses the configured tree; choose a build preset when its environment/jobs/targets are needed during compilation.

The bounded native reader handles CMakePresets.json/CMakeUserPresets.json versions 1–10, workspace-local include DAGs, implicit project inclusion by user presets, inheritance with earlier-parent precedence, environment/cache maps and null values, standard path/env macros and the defining file origin for ${fileDir}. Hidden presets serve as bases and are excluded from selectors. Entry errors remain explicit; malformed preset files do not disable manual project inspection.

Execution uses cmake --preset=NAME -S SOURCE -B BINARY or cmake --build --preset=NAME, with SOURCE as cwd. CMake applies cache variables, conditions, toolchains, environment, targets, jobs and execution options. CyCode adds compilation database/File API requests and a guarded binary directory. The installed CMake must support the chosen schema. Conditional availability is validated during execution; the metadata selector does not filter every condition.

Includes/binary paths must stay in the workspace after canonical resolution. A selectable configure preset needs binaryDir; vendor macros cannot determine host-owned build paths. In-source builds are refused. Snapshots are checked before and after successful execution; changes prevent profile/analysis publication. Native cancellation, deadlines and output bounds apply. Project scripts/toolchains remain trusted executable code. MSVC/Ninja presets with external environment setup still need a suitable developer environment.

Read-only build.presets / MCP build_presets returns entries, files and errors without executing CMake. build.inspect includes the catalogue. build.configure/build.run accept configurePreset/buildPreset, persisted in the successful local profile. Older manual profiles still load. Plugins export the same services; Python does not maintain a second model.

Bounds: 64 files, 2 MiB each/8 MiB total, 64 JSON/inheritance levels, 512 entries per family, 256 KiB per resolved preset/16 MiB total and 32 KiB path expansion. Test/package/workflow presets now have a shared preview and native execution path in View > CMake preset actions, with revision guards, cancellation and the existing build reservation. New runtime/GUI acceptance remains pending. Configured CTest retains its separate structured workflow; see Preset actions. Public catalogue metadata is bounded to 16 MiB and snapshots include root-file presence. CMake specification.

Validation#

New C++ assertions cover XML hierarchies/mappings/defaults, MSBuild inspection and invalid input; preset assertions cover includes/inheritance, user definitions, path/env expansion, hidden entries, changed snapshots, cycles and escaped paths. MSVC /Zs checks sources without generating test executables. Native execution and graphical acceptance remain suspended following the Kaspersky removals. Windows application compilation is recorded in Validation; Linux/macOS runtime behavior remains unverified.

Public catalogue metadata is bounded to 16 MiB and snapshots include root-file presence. CMake specification . Validation # New C++ assertions cover XML hierarchies/mappings/defaults, MSBuild inspection and invalid input; preset assertions cover includes/inheritance, user definitions, path/env expansion, hidden entries, changed snapshots, cycles and escaped paths. MSVC /Zs checks sources without generating test executables. Native execution and graphical acceptance remain suspended following the Kaspersky removals. Windows application compilation is recorded in Validation ; Linux/macOS runtime behavior remains unverified.

pages.title: Project task status and live output
pages.html:
Project task status and live output#

Recognized source rows can now open existing workspace files through the shared native build.location parser. Live project logs supply their recorded task working directory; other/final logs use the workspace root. This is a guarded navigation hint, not a current diagnostic revision. See Compiler locations for formats and limits.

The Build panel selects Native build output or Project task output. The latter follows Cargo, npm, standalone javac, Maven, Gradle and shader compilation through their existing ProjectTasks owner. It defaults to the project source for detected Cargo/npm/JVM projects. Explicit shader tasks in another primary project can use the selector. Each source keeps its own latest tail and identity.

The shared TaskOutput implementation replaces the previous build-specific journal. It stores at most 256 KiB in 8 KiB chunks, with distinct stream IDs, revisioned conditional reads, repaired display text and late-callback guards. Native builds and project tasks retain their separate existing reservations, process trees and cancellation tokens. No extra process owner or queue is added.

Native, SDK and ABI2#

project.status / project_status returns current running/cancelling state, operation ID and method, without waiting for execution, plugin or document locks. Its read is permission-free metadata, like build.status. It remains running until the owner returns, including process cleanup. A cancellation acknowledgement is not completed termination. Application terminals have a separate lifecycle.

project.output / project_output uses the same report as build.output, with an optional context containing system and workspace-relative directory. Context is absent before the first task, empty while its profile is not yet validated, then identifies the actual selected project. Context changes advance the revision. The result retains the last task's context after completion or failure.

Read initially with {}, then send both observed streamId and revision. An unchanged read has changed:false and empty output. Every changed read replaces the entire previous display tail; it is not appended as a delta. Stream IDs distinguish tasks even if a caller reuses an operation ID. Overflow drops the oldest display bytes without stopping a compiler. The journal survives until the next task or workspace destruction and is not a persisted history archive.

The output query requires process.execute because logs can contain private project data; it has no SDK mutation group and cannot cancel or start a task. ABI2 exports both reads, including output from read-only callbacks with that permission. The facade classifies these queries separately from executable project methods, so it does not inject an operation ID or propagate read-job cancellation to an executing build. Existing SDK identities, jobs and scheduling remain authoritative. No C ABI change is needed.

GUI task starts now receive distinct operation IDs. Cancel task captures that ID and retries while its own asynchronous request is entering the reservation; remote tasks use their observed ID. A stale ID does not target a different ID. Caller-supplied reused IDs still need caller coordination and are not credentials. Working state and workspace switching also observe SDK/plugin-owned project work. No force-stop or antivirus-setting change is introduced.

Cargo display framing#

Cargo format-version 1 metadata is excluded from the live display. Compilation protocol lines are framed across arbitrary pipe chunks: compiler-message uses rendered text (or its plain message fallback), compiler-artifact/build-script/ completion records are hidden, and ordinary stderr or unknown lines remain visible. No executable path is inferred from this display. Existing raw process collection and the final Cargo diagnostics/artifact parser remain unchanged.

Each live protocol line is capped at 64 KiB. An oversized line is explicitly omitted until the next newline, then framing resumes. Unexpected framing failures also produce an explicit message when observation is available. An unterminated last line is flushed once. These limits do not change the existing 4 MiB project process/result bound. A tool that buffers its own output may still appear silent.

Project byteCount/droppedBytes count bytes published to the display journal: rendered messages for Cargo, pipe text for ordinary commands. They are not Cargo JSON byte offsets, Unicode counts or a progress measure. UTF-8/control repair and partial edge-character limitations match native live output. No ANSI interpretation or legacy-code-page detection is provided.

Persistent Run terminals, arbitrary plugin processes, background Unreal analysis and standalone per-test result trees remain separate. Live Cargo text does not publish incremental Problems entries; structured diagnostics retain their final task-result path. Diagnostic navigation adds keyboard navigation over the already reported Problems/LSP locations.

Validation#

Windows production compilation, MSVC /Zs and actual SDK/schema checks are distinct from runtime acceptance. Opt-in existing build/project/module fixtures specify context revisions, ID reuse/late callbacks, fragmented/oversized Cargo records, plain text repair, status/dirty-buffer reads, cancellation and keyboard filtering. They are source-checked only during the Kaspersky suspension. Actual tool pipes, SDK/plugin concurrency, cancellation races, GUI/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS remain unverified. No fixture, task compiler or application is launched for acceptance.

pages.title: Cargo, npm and Java projects
pages.html:
Cargo, npm and Java projects#

The Build panel now follows these tasks through project_status/project_output, with task context, bounded live display and captured-ID cancellation. Cargo protocol records render readable compiler messages without exposing metadata inventories. Native/UI/SDK/ABI2 reuse the existing owner; actual runtime acceptance is pending. See Project live output and Diagnostic navigation.

Java/Maven/Gradle Debug now returns a debugProfile with the selected actual main class, Java executable and runtime classpaths; the GUI then uses the common DAP debugger. Cargo retains its program result. project.debug itself starts no debugger; see Java debugging for JDT LS/add-on setup and limits.

CyCode detects Cargo.toml, package.json and standalone Java sources when opening a folder or its project file. Maven pom.xml and Gradle build/settings descriptors also select their native adapter. View > Project tasks selects the project directory, configuration, target and arguments. Existing Build/Run shortcuts use the detected adapter: Rider Ctrl+F9 builds and Shift+F10 runs; Visual Studio/VS Code bindings are also routed through the shared command catalogue. Build errors appear in Problems. Unsaved IDE documents are saved before GUI tasks; native/MCP execution refuses any remaining dirty workspace document.

Project Implemented tasks Run/debug
Rust/Cargo Real workspace metadata; package/entire-workspace selection; bin/example/lib/test/bench targets; features; Debug/Release/custom profiles; offline/locked builds and Cargo tests Actual package/kind-identified binary or executable example in the integrated terminal; build-before-debug through native DAP; expanded runtime acceptance pending
npm web/Node Existing build/test scripts, selected named script, explicit dependency install Selected script, default start/dev, in a persistent integrated terminal
Java Standalone source-directory compilation with javac; Debug/Release symbols; compiler diagnostics Main classes discovered from compiled class-file methods and run through java in the terminal
Maven Real package/test/custom goal; effective-POM outputs and resolved runtime dependencies Compiled main classes and actual classpath, run through Java in the integrated terminal
Gradle Real build/test/custom task with optional module selection; Java source-set runtime model Compiled main classes and actual classpath, run through Java in the integrated terminal
HLSL/GLSL One selected shader source with typed stage/target/macros/includes; real DXC/glslang and Problems diagnostics Bounded DXIL/SPIR-V output; no GPU preview/run/debug

The Rust adapter uses installed Cargo, or CyCode's private pinned toolchain when Cargo is absent. cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps supplies actual workspace targets. Builds parse compiler JSON for diagnostics and executable paths; custom build-script/test executables are excluded from runnable artifacts. Outputs go under .cycode/cargo-target. Dependencies, build scripts and procedural macros execute when explicitly building/testing trusted projects, according to Cargo rules. The language-server default still disables automatic execution of those rules. See Cargo workspaces for typed cargo* options, required features, cache invalidation, workspace boundaries and pending runtime acceptance.

npm uses installed Node.js and its npm CLI with an argv vector. The selected script must exist in package.json. Install dependencies explicitly uses npm ci with a package-lock, otherwise npm install; lifecycle scripts follow the trusted project's npm configuration. Inspection and configuration never install dependencies or run scripts. Build/test commands use their corresponding scripts; the selected script controls Run/Run npm script. Framework toolchains and their packages belong to the project. Long-lived dev servers should use Run, then their terminal's stop control. CyCode does not open a browser or provide JavaScript/browser debugging yet.

The standalone Java adapter uses installed javac/java and UTF-8 source/argument files. Annotation processing is disabled (-proc:none). Compiler output is UTF-8; interactive output uses the attached terminal's encoding. Each compilation receives a fresh .cycode/java-build/<id>/classes directory. Runnable entry points come from actual public static main(String[]) methods in compiled classes. If several exist, select the qualified main class. Maven/Gradle use their own real build and resource processing, with bounded native model extraction, existing Java wrapper jars or explicit installed tool homes. Inspection does not run build scripts or download tools. See JVM builds for launcher requirements, module selection, checksums, dependency resolution and remaining framework limits. The built-in Java adapter now prepares the shared JDT LS launch debugger; actual runtime acceptance and a structured per-test result tree remain pending.

Native services and MCP#

ProjectTasks belongs to the SDL-free native Engine and is shared by GUI, MCP and permission-checked ABI2 plugin host services (project.*). Profiles live in .cycode/project-tasks.json; .cycode/project-build.json caches inspected inputs/targets/artifacts. Paths are workspace guarded, including symlinks. Failed builds clear runnable artifact metadata. Builds always invoke the real tool; cached metadata never substitutes for a compilation.

project_inspect reads manifests and cached targets without executing project code. The following operations require the SDK's process.execute permission:

  • project_configure, project_build, project_test, project_install, project_script.
  • project_launch returns a terminal id for the existing terminal read/write/close operations.
  • project_debug_target builds a Cargo binary or executable example and returns its executable for the existing debug_configure/debug_launch operations; it does not launch a debugger.
  • project_cancel stops the current compiler/test/script process tree. Persistent run terminals have their own terminal_close lifecycle.

The execution profile accepts system (automatic/cargo/npm/java/maven/gradle/shader), directory, configuration, package, target, script, mainClass, sourceDirectory, offline, timeoutSeconds and args. One native project task runs per instance, with a default 180-second total process deadline, configurable up to 24 hours, and 4 MiB output bound. GUI Cancel and CyToolsCore job cancellation terminate the actual owned process tree. Internal request correlation prevents cancelling a different running task. The SDK owns jobs, identities, permissions and reservations; the native bridge only dispatches authenticated IPC.

Windows x64 is the local validation target. Linux/macOS implementations remain unverified. This milestone does not establish full Rider project/debugger parity.

system:shader adds separately installed DXC/glslang compilation through the same build/cancel/deadline service. Its typed shader* fields, secondary panel and artifact/dependency limits are documented in Shader compilation.

References: Cargo metadata, Cargo JSON messages, npm run-script, javac.
