pages.title: Project creation
pages.html:
Project creation#

File → New project (also file.newProject in the command palette) opens the native CyUI wizard. Choose a template, project name and an existing parent directory. Preview shows the exact UTF-8 files, syntax highlighting and tool requirements. Create and open publishes a new directory and opens its project entry and first source file. The optional new-window checkbox launches a separate instance only on that explicit action.

Template ID Generated entry Native build adapter
cpp.console CMake directory, C++20 source and CTest smoke test CMake configure/build
c.console CMake directory, C17 source and CTest smoke test CMake configure/build
rust.console Cargo manifest, Rust 2021 source and unit test Cargo configure/build/test/run
csharp.console Visual Studio .sln, SDK .csproj, C# source MSBuild restore/build/run
java.console src/main/java/Main.java Standalone javac/java build/run
web.javascript HTML/CSS, ES modules, npm scripts and local server npm build/test/run
cycode.unreal.cppGame (bundled plugin) .uproject, runtime module, Game/Editor target rules Existing Unreal generation/build/index services

Active ABI2 plugins can contribute additional models and typed options to this same wizard. The bundled Unreal extension provides the C++ game model. Select the installed engine association (default 5.3), then generate/build using the Unreal view. Its name must start with a letter and use letters, digits or underscores. Unreal Engine itself remains an external installation.

.NET targets are explicitly selectable: net8.0 (default), net9.0, net10.0. Install a compatible SDK and matching targeting/runtime packs. The wizard does not run a tool installer, restore packages, execute project code, initialize Git or choose a project license. Each project contains build/run instructions in its README. No extra CyCode or CyUI dependency enters generated projects.

The web template uses only Node built-ins (Node 18+ for node --test). Build checks JavaScript syntax; it is not a bundler. Run serves an explicit list of assets on 127.0.0.1:3000; pass another port to the start script if needed. It does not launch a browser. No npm install or external package is necessary. Java and .NET include a --self-test executable path, not a test framework; their broader IDE test integrations remain pending. CMake tests run through CTest in the generated build directory, as explained in its README.

Native API, MCP and plugin access#

ProjectTemplates belongs to the UI-free native core. Engine exports:

  • templates.list / MCP templates_list: catalogue and target frameworks.
  • templates.preview / MCP templates_preview: {template, name, destination?, framework?, options?} returns exact files/content, an issued plan ID, requirements, instructions, project entry and initial source file. No writes.
  • templates.create / MCP templates_create: {id} applies that issued plan. Requires workspace.write in the actual CyToolsCore runtime and plugin host.

MCP/plugin destinations are workspace-relative and cannot expand that workspace boundary. An omitted destination uses the project name. The destination parent must already exist and the final directory must not exist. Desktop uses the same native class with the parent explicitly selected in its wizard; it does not extend the current Engine/MCP workspace or its document permissions.

Names start with an ASCII letter and contain up to 64 letters, digits, _ or -. Windows device names are rejected on every platform. Traversing/protected paths, links and redirected directories are refused. Plans are immutable, expire after ten minutes, and retain the newest 32 per instance. Unknown, expired, evicted or already-created plans cannot be applied.

Catalogue entries include the supplying plugin, fields, nameStyle and a registry revision. Preview returns resolved options, plugin ownership and its catalogueRevision. Disabling/enabling a plugin or changing the registry invalidates pending plugin plans; preview again. Creation holds the host's activation guard through the filesystem commit. Preview does not invoke plugin callbacks. The GUI refreshes the choices and removes a stale preview when plugin activation changes.

Creation checks the original root/parent directory identity, exclusively allocates a sibling staging folder, writes files without replacement and verifies every file against the preview. A same-volume exclusive rename publishes the folder: Windows MoveFileExW without replacement, Linux renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) or macOS renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL). Unsupported filesystems fail without an overwrite fallback. Failure cleanup removes only matching generated files and empty staging directories; unexpected changed content is retained. These checks are protection against stale previews and accidental overwrites, not an OS sandbox for hostile code racing filesystem operations.

The workspace switch uses existing document safeguards. If modified documents prevent opening, creation still succeeds and the wizard retains the created project and an Open created project button. Save/close the old documents, then retry. Opening the source preserves normal editor Undo/Redo. Creation does not offer a destructive project-wide Undo.

Limits#

Six models are built in; the Unreal C++ game model belongs to its bundled plugin. Additional models use installed native ABI2 plugins, not arbitrary project-local JSON files. Standalone data-pack installation, binary template assets, scripting, conditional file sets, automatic SDK acquisition, CMake Presets and broader framework/test models remain work. Creating a model does not implement a new build-system adapter; use an existing adapter or an explicit project provider.

Windows x64 is the local validation platform. Linux/macOS implementations are present but have not been built or executed locally. See Validation.

Writing an ABI2 project template#

Register host.contribute(context, "template", descriptor_json, nullptr) during initialization, using an ID under the plugin's namespace. No ABI structure/layout changes or STL values cross the C boundary. The descriptor is copied, checked and owned by the host. See the Unreal example and native SDK.

json
{  "id": "example.tools.console",  "title": "Example console",  "language": "cpp",  "buildSystem": "cmake",  "nameStyle": "identifier",  "requirements": ["CMake and C++ compiler"],  "fields": [    {"id":"standard", "title":"C++ standard", "type":"choice",     "choices":["17","20"], "default":"20"}  ],  "entry": ".",  "openFile": "src/main.cpp",  "instructions": "Configure and build ${project.name} with CMake.",  "files": [    {"path":"CMakeLists.txt", "text":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(${project.identifier} LANGUAGES CXX)\nadd_executable(${project.identifier} src/main.cpp)\nset_property(TARGET ${project.identifier} PROPERTY CXX_STANDARD ${option.standard})\n"},    {"path":"src/main.cpp", "text":"int main() { return 0; }\n"}  ]}

Metadata requires id/title/language/buildSystem/requirements; files require path/text. entry is a declared file/directory (. is the new project root), and openFile must be a declared file, with exact spelling. nameStyle defaults to portable; identifier additionally excludes hyphens. Optional order controls the plugin catalogue order; templates do not use contextual when expressions.

Fields have stable id/title/type/default, optional help, and choices for choice fields. Types: boolean, choice, identifier (ASCII letter followed by letters/digits/underscores), or value (1–128 ASCII letters/digits/underscores, dots, hyphens or braces; suitable for version/GUID values). Values are checked both at registration and preview; unknown options and non-advertised choices fail.

Substitutions in file paths, text, entry and instructions are ${project.name}, ${project.identifier} (hyphens become underscores), ${project.slug} (lowercase), ${project.upper} (uppercase identifier), and ${option.ID}. Booleans produce true/false. Unknown tokens in these two namespaces fail; other ${...} strings remain literal, preserving CMake/JavaScript source. There is no script/expression execution, callback, automatic license or repository initialization.

Bounds: 32 plugin templates / 1 MiB of registered descriptors; 256 KiB per descriptor; 16 option fields / 32 choices per field; 1–64 UTF-8 text files, 64 KiB per source text, 256 KiB after expansion in total, 128 filesystem entries, 16 path levels. Paths reject absolute/root-relative/traversing/protected names, Windows device names, file/directory collisions and ASCII case aliases. Platform filesystem checks still protect exclusive creation for other name collisions.

Run serves an explicit list of assets on 127.0.0.1:3000 ; pass another port to the start script if needed. It does not launch a browser. No npm install or external package is necessary. Java and .NET include a --self-test executable path, not a test framework; their broader IDE test integrations remain pending. CMake tests run through CTest in the generated build directory, as explained in its README. Native API, MCP and plugin access # ProjectTemplates belongs to the UI-free native core. Engine exports: templates.list / MCP templates_list : catalogue and target frameworks. templates.preview / MCP templates_preview : {template, name, destination?, framework?, options?} returns exact files/content, an issued plan ID, requirements, instructions, project entry and initial source file. No writes. templates.create / MCP templates_create : {id} applies that issued plan. Requires workspace.write in the actual CyToolsCore runtime and plugin host. MCP/plugin destinations are workspace-relative and cannot expand that workspace boundary. An omitted destination uses the project name. The destination parent must already exist and the final directory must not exist. Desktop uses the same native class with the parent explicitly selected in its wizard; it does not extend the current Engine/MCP workspace or its document permissions. Names start with an ASCII letter and contain up to 64 letters, digits, _ or - . Windows device names are rejected on every platform. Traversing/protected paths, links and redirected directories are refused. Plans are immutable, expire after ten minutes, and retain the newest 32 per instance. Unknown, expired, evicted or already-created plans cannot be applied. Catalogue entries include the supplying plugin , fields , nameStyle and a registry revision. Preview returns resolved options , plugin ownership and its catalogueRevision . Disabling/enabling a plugin or changing the registry invalidates pending plugin plans; preview again. Creation holds the host's activation guard through the filesystem commit. Preview does not invoke plugin callbacks. The GUI refreshes the choices and removes a stale preview when plugin activation changes. Creation checks the original root/parent directory identity, exclusively allocates a sibling staging folder, writes files without replacement and verifies every file against the preview. A same-volume exclusive rename publishes the folder: Windows MoveFileExW without replacement, Linux renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE) or macOS renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL) . Unsupported filesystems fail without an overwrite fallback. Failure cleanup removes only matching generated files and empty staging directories; unexpected changed content is retained. These checks are protection against stale previews and accidental overwrites, not an OS sandbox for hostile code racing filesystem operations. The workspace switch uses existing document safeguards. If modified documents prevent opening, creation still succeeds and the wizard retains the created project and an Open created project button. Save/close the old documents, then retry. Opening the source preserves normal editor Undo/Redo. Creation does not offer a destructive project-wide Undo. Limits # Six models are built in; the Unreal C++ game model belongs to its bundled plugin. Additional models use installed native ABI2 plugins, not arbitrary project-local JSON files. Standalone data-pack installation, binary template assets, scripting, conditional file sets, automatic SDK acquisition, CMake Presets and broader framework/test models remain work. Creating a model does not implement a new build-system adapter; use an existing adapter or an explicit project provider. Windows x64 is the local validation platform. Linux/macOS implementations are present but have not been built or executed locally. See Validation . Writing an ABI2 project template # Register host.contribute(context, "template", descriptor_json, nullptr) during initialization, using an ID under the plugin's namespace. No ABI structure/layout changes or STL values cross the C boundary. The descriptor is copied, checked and owned by the host. See the Unreal example and native SDK . json Copy { "id" : "example.tools.console" , "title" : "Example console" , "language" : "cpp" , "buildSystem" : "cmake" , "nameStyle" : "identifier" , "requirements" : [ "CMake and C++ compiler" ] , "fields" : [ { "id" : "standard" , "title" : "C++ standard" , "type" : "choice" , "choices" : [ "17" , "20" ] , "default" : "20" } ] , "entry" : "." , "openFile" : "src/main.cpp" , "instructions" : "Configure and build ${project.name} with CMake." , "files" : [ { "path" : "CMakeLists.txt" , "text" : "cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(${project.identifier} LANGUAGES CXX)
add_executable(${project.identifier} src/main.cpp)
set_property(TARGET ${project.identifier} PROPERTY CXX_STANDARD ${option.standard})
" } , { "path" : "src/main.cpp" , "text" : "int main() { return 0; }
" } ] } Metadata requires id/title/language/buildSystem/requirements ; files require path/text . entry is a declared file/directory ( . is the new project root), and openFile must be a declared file, with exact spelling. nameStyle defaults to portable ; identifier additionally excludes hyphens. Optional order controls the plugin catalogue order; templates do not use contextual when expressions. Fields have stable id/title/type/default , optional help , and choices for choice fields. Types: boolean , choice , identifier (ASCII letter followed by letters/digits/underscores), or value (1–128 ASCII letters/digits/underscores, dots, hyphens or braces; suitable for version/GUID values). Values are checked both at registration and preview; unknown options and non-advertised choices fail. Substitutions in file paths, text, entry and instructions are ${project.name} , ${project.identifier} (hyphens become underscores), ${project.slug} (lowercase), ${project.upper} (uppercase identifier), and ${option.ID} . Booleans produce true/false . Unknown tokens in these two namespaces fail; other ${...} strings remain literal, preserving CMake/JavaScript source. There is no script/expression execution, callback, automatic license or repository initialization. Bounds: 32 plugin templates / 1 MiB of registered descriptors; 256 KiB per descriptor; 16 option fields / 32 choices per field; 1–64 UTF-8 text files, 64 KiB per source text, 256 KiB after expansion in total, 128 filesystem entries, 16 path levels. Paths reject absolute/root-relative/traversing/protected names, Windows device names, file/directory collisions and ASCII case aliases. Platform filesystem checks still protect exclusive creation for other name collisions. { "id": "example.tools.console", "title": "Example console", "language": "cpp", "buildSystem": "cmake", "nameStyle": "identifier", "requirements": ["CMake and C++ compiler"], "fields": [ {"id":"standard", "title":"C++ standard", "type":"choice", "choices":["17","20"], "default":"20"} ], "entry": ".", "openFile": "src/main.cpp", "instructions": "Configure and build ${project.name} with CMake.", "files": [ {"path":"CMakeLists.txt", "text":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)
project(${project.identifier} LANGUAGES CXX)
add_executable(${project.identifier} src/main.cpp)
set_property(TARGET ${project.identifier} PROPERTY CXX_STANDARD ${option.standard})
"}, {"path":"src/main.cpp", "text":"int main() { return 0; }
"} ] }

pages.title: Unsaved-document recovery
pages.html:
Unsaved-document recovery#

Issued untitled drafts, including empty drafts, now use these same checkpoints. They restore into memory and require Save as to become source files. Session coordinates/window keys are applied after explicit recovery; see Untitled documents. Text never silently restores at startup.

The native Engine checkpoints modified text buffers once per second on its own worker. There is no autosave to project files. The first dirty buffer creates a session under .cycode/recovery/; opening an unchanged workspace creates no recovery directory. File indexing, search and the watcher exclude this directory.

On startup, inactive sessions are offered in View > Recovery and Find Action. Select a checkpoint for a read-only, syntax-colored CyUI preview. Restore buffer opens the complete text in memory. Restoration is one editor Undo transaction; Undo returns to the previously loaded text, and Redo restores it again. Save is a separate explicit action. Previous editor Undo history is not serialized.

A changed file retains a save conflict instead of overwriting external changes. If the original was deleted, restoration creates only a buffer; explicit Save recreates its path without overwriting a file that appeared in the meantime. Preview is bounded to 64 KiB by default (256 KiB maximum through MCP); truncating the preview does not truncate restoration. Refresh the preview if its target revision or disk state changed. A dirty target must first be saved or closed.

Right-click an inactive entry to discard its checkpoint, including a corrupt payload that cannot be previewed. The confirmation removes that backup only. Successful Save, explicit document discard/reload and Quit > Discard retire the current instance's matching checkpoints. A shutdown that retains dirty buffers keeps their last checkpoint and attempts a final flush.

Storage and guards#

Each session holds an operating-system file lock: Windows file sharing or POSIX flock. A live instance's entries are visible as In use and cannot be previewed, restored or discarded by another instance. No process-ID timeout guesses that an instance has crashed. The lock is released by process exit, including abrupt exit.

Checkpoints use normalized UTF-8 payloads and separate original disk bytes. BOM, CRLF and CR-only metadata preserve the source encoding/newline convention on Save. An atomic index references immutable payloads only after their writes are flushed. Lengths and FNV-1a fingerprints detect corrupt or mismatched payloads; fingerprints are corruption checks, not signatures or authentication. Redirected recovery directories and paths outside the canonical workspace are rejected. The directory contains plaintext working code and should remain excluded from version control.

Restoration checks the selected checkpoint, the target revision and a fingerprint of the current disk content. Before removing the abandoned source entry, the restored buffer must have its own durable checkpoint. If that transfer fails, the source is retained and the UI reports the failure. Original project files are never removed by recovery cleanup.

Limits are 128 dirty documents / 128 MiB of combined text and baselines per session, and the existing 4 MiB UTF-8 limit per document. Exceeding a quota or a write failure is reported; earlier checkpoints remain. The list examines at most 512 directory entries and returns the newest 256 records by default (up to 1,024 requested). Older inactive sessions have no automatic expiration. Interrupted writes may leave unreferenced payloads; these are never treated as recoverable documents and are not recursively swept. A corrupt index is reported for manual inspection.

The interval is best effort: an abrupt exit can lose edits made since the last completed checkpoint. There is no power-failure guarantee, historical Undo journal, untitled-document model or large-file recovery. Separate bounded tab/cursor/panel/ layout metadata now restores workspace sessions; see Workspace sessions.

Shared services and verification#

GUI and CyToolsCore/MCP use the same Engine and document revisions:

  • recovery_status, recovery_list and recovery_preview are read-only.
  • recovery_flush, recovery_restore and recovery_discard require workspace.write. Restore requires expectedRevision and expectedDiskState from preview, plus the session/id/checkpoint reference.
  • workspace_poll includes checkpoint health. Write failures surface in the desktop without requiring the user to open Recovery first.

CTest recovery uses a real child process that exits without destructors after an automatic checkpoint. It covers Unicode/BOM/CRLF, active-instance isolation, revision/disk conflicts, missing files, corruption, path rejection, quota retention, failed transfers and 4 MiB payloads. recovery_ui exercises the real editor and CyUI view without native windows, including Restore/Undo/Redo/edit/Save and EN/FR, six themes and three DPI values. Python integration uses the real native bridge, CyToolsCore permissions and a killed/restarted process. See Validation for executed results and platform limits.

pages.title: CyCode 0.2.1
pages.html:
CyCode 0.2.1#

The Help menu, contextual buttons and keyboard shortcuts now open an illustrated English/French CyDoc manual. The complete reader, search, diagrams, images and API reference are bundled for offline use and published online.

  • Documentation
  • Documentation française
  • The README displays the application logo and opens the visual reader.
  • GitHub Actions regenerates the same reader on main-branch changes.
  • Includes the native development milestones recorded in the changelog.

Windows x64 production binaries were built with native tests disabled. No native application, MCP runtime or updater was launched for this release. Clean-machine, native interaction and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending. This remains a development IDE with the feature limitations recorded in the manual.

Extract the complete Windows archive to a writable directory. Visual C++ 2022 x64 runtime and OpenGL 3.3 are required. External compilers, language servers, Git and debuggers must be installed separately. The optional MCP needs CyToolsCore. The -update.zip archive is intended for the application's explicit update flow. The original application is GPL-3.0-only; bundled dependencies retain their licences.

pages.title: Workspace file operations
pages.html:
Workspace file operations#

Git working-file synchronization reuses this service for reviewed binary installation/removal, retaining original/displaced content in the same persistent trash. Host-owned payload plans have separate apply/Undo entrypoints; generic JSON resource calls cannot consume them. Closed-root checks protect source/trash documents under the Engine lock; common events refresh image previews. No public resource schema change or new target is needed. Actual new filesystem/Undo acceptance remains pending; see Git working files.

View > Files uses the common CyUI::Assets browser. It shows one physical directory at a time, including empty directories and ignored/hidden project files. The existing Project tree and fast file search keep their ripgrep ignore rules; they offer the same file-action dialogs through context menus. Empty directories are visible in Files even when absent from the source-file index.

The Files toolbar creates files/folders and undoes the last GUI file operation. Rename/Move and Delete are also available through the Project command catalogue. F2 and Delete act on the selected physical resource only while Project or Files has keyboard focus. Editor keymaps and symbol rename remain separate. Ctrl/Cmd+F focuses the current Files browser or trash filter; Escape cancels a dialog.

The action dialog prepares a preview before enabling Apply. Paths are relative to the workspace, and destination parent folders must already exist. A move never overwrites its destination. Dirty, conflicted or changed affected documents block the operation; save/reconcile them and prepare another preview. The active entry selected by directly opening a solution/project cannot be moved/deleted.

Moves preserve open document identities, text Undo history, active tab and native window identity, including detached windows. The GUI consumes the same operation events when a move originates in MCP or a trusted plugin. Issued language edits are invalidated by fresh document revisions; language overlays close/reopen at the new path. Text is copied on revision changes, not unconditionally every frame.

Deleting moves the complete file/directory into .cycode/trash/item-…/payload. Original relative path, timestamp and a content guard are recorded before the move. The Project trash tab lists dated entries and prepares guarded restoration, including after application restart. There is no permanent-delete or empty-trash action. No automatic expiry is applied. Restoring refuses occupied destinations and modified/corrupt payloads. An alternative destination may be supplied.

Open text buffers survive deletion with a missing-file marker. Restoring their unchanged original data reattaches them; a changed buffer blocks restoration until saved or closed. Typing remains possible, and an explicit Save can recreate the deleted path. A clean missing buffer is also recreated by explicit Save. Changes made after deletion use the ordinary crash-recovery worker. The retained trash copy is independent, so it cannot overwrite a newly recreated file.

Transactions and limits#

resources_preview hashes a bounded snapshot without changing project files. Its issued plan captures the open-document identities/revisions and disk state. resources_apply checks those guards before committing an exclusive filesystem move/create. resources_undo prepares the inverse action and checks that content still matches its last applied state. Undoing a creation moves it to project trash; it does not recursively delete user data. Text Undo and file-operation Undo have separate command IDs. File-operation plans live only in the current native process, with the newest 32 retained and previews expiring after ten minutes. Deleted payloads remain restorable through the persistent trash even after plans are gone.

The snapshot limit is 4,096 entries, 64 directory levels, 256 MiB total content and 128 affected open documents. Large/unsupported actions fail before moving their source. The physical browser returns up to 2,048 children after examining at most 8,192 directory entries. Trash listing examines at most 2,048 entries and returns the newest 256 by default. Truncation is explicit. The GUI loads directories in background requests; it does not recursively scan the workspace every frame.

Operation events are bounded to 128 records / 4 MiB and use a monotonic cursor. A gap clears stale navigation history and open text tabs reconcile by stable native document identities. Those identities belong to one Engine lifetime. Watcher/index counters are invalidated immediately after a committed operation. .cycode, .git, installation runtime/data, redirected paths and symbolic links are protected. Regular/binary files use the same reversible filesystem operation; text editing's 4 MiB UTF-8 limit is independent of this service.

Windows uses MoveFileEx without replacement. Linux uses renameat2 with RENAME_NOREPLACE, and macOS uses renamex_np with RENAME_EXCL. No overwrite-capable rename fallback or cross-volume copy/delete fallback is used. Hash guards detect ordinary concurrent changes/corruption and are not authentication. They do not promise an atomic compare-and-rename against arbitrary external writers. Exclusive destination handling prevents a destination that appeared concurrently from being replaced. The implementation does not promise recovery from every power-loss state.

Shared SDK/MCP/plugin surface#

  • resources_preview, resources_children, resources_trash and resources_events are read-only operations.
  • resources_apply and resources_undo require workspace.write.
  • Trusted native plugins may call the same exported host services. Their manifest needs workspace.write for mutations, and read-only provider callbacks cannot mutate the host. This does not isolate native DLLs at the OS level.
  • The SDK's jobs/sessions/permissions/MCP remain supplied by the real CyToolsCore runtime. Workspace sources and trash are persistent project data, never temporary task artifacts.

These are physical path changes. Includes, solution/project manifests, Unreal reflection names/assets and debugger breakpoints are not rewritten. Semantic file rename via LSP resource edits, cross-volume moves, case-only renames on a case-insensitive filesystem, rich multi-selection/copy/paste, persisted file-operation Undo/Redo and drag/drop folder-target integration remain future work. The common Assets module supplies drag payloads but no folder-drop event in the pinned API. Browser favorites are session-local. A physical directory containing protected metadata cannot be moved as a whole.

See Validation for executed native, headless UI and MCP checks. Windows is the locally tested platform; the POSIX implementations remain unverified.

pages.title: Roadmap
pages.html:
Roadmap#

Current milestone#

Detailed update history now combines explicit metadata-only inspection, cached CyUI text/category filters with twelve-row pages, and selected recovery details/copying. Native reports exclude raw metadata; new receipts have informational timestamps. Scan/row/byte limits and omitted-record notices remain explicit. Actual native/GUI/ clipboard/cancellation/theme/DPI acceptance, pagination beyond the bounded snapshot, exhaustive/append-only auditing and Linux/macOS updates remain. See Update history.

The staged recovery helper now has visible EN/FR phase/count progress, cooperative Stop/Escape/close requests and a joined worker that keeps the dialog alive until work actually finishes. Result dialogs distinguish cancellation before/after this attempt's installed-file moves, offer an explicitly copied report and retain an exclusive best-effort plan-bound receipt. These are source/build/data checked; real Windows UI/clipboard/close/blocked-I/O/partial-commit interruption and receipt failure acceptance remain, alongside unattended/legacy and Linux/macOS updating. See Recovery controls.

Recovery retries now reuse verified prepared originals from this active transaction, with bounded exact ownership/source maps, mixed-directory references and fresh capacity accounting. Missing/changed/foreign/legacy hints remain on disk and fall back to verified original backups. Mutable phases do not authorize completion. Actual resume/low-space/lock/copy/interruption/native-helper/GUI acceptance, space reservation, power-loss durability and Linux/macOS updating remain. See Recovery resumption.

Recovery now checks its own allocation-aware copy/retention headroom, stages and verifies all originals before moving targets, and rechecks the complete file baseline and metadata space before commit. Preview guidance and plan-bound receipts distinguish insufficient/unknown capacity and preparation/commit failure. Real low-space/quota/lock/copy/cancellation/native-helper/GUI acceptance, space reservation, power-loss durability and Linux/macOS updates remain. See Recovery preparation.

Installation now adds allocation-aware extraction/pre-replacement budgets, retained space receipts, compatible typed failure history and complete-baseline rollback verification. Pending-marker removal is guarded for install/rollback/recovery. Source/build/data checks are separate from actual low-space/quota/filesystem/helper and GUI acceptance. Space reservation, power-loss durability and Linux/macOS automatic updates remain. See Installation checks.

Download/staging now checks additional space before transfer, full fallback and preparation, with caller quotas and conservative helper/catalogue/journal/spare allowances. Release-bound phase/counter observations and a sampled network-only rate/ETA distinguish received bytes from verified readiness. Thirty actual policy assertions are compiler-evaluated. Real low-space/quota/HTTP/GUI acceptance and Linux/macOS updating remain. See Download observations.

Update retry now adds an explicit fresh-download action that preserves old data, category-based EN/FR guidance and one quiet local refresh after failed/cancelled attempts. Resume/fresh share native integrity/ownership guards, and a refresh does not restore a proposal or network consent. Windows source/build/data verification is distinct from pending real HTTP/locking/GUI/platform acceptance. See Download retry.

Interrupted downloads now retain exact asset checkpoints, resume through validated byte ranges and safely fall back to a fresh folder when Range is ignored. Full SHA-256 remains mandatory; partial summaries are explicitly unverified. Nineteen compiler-evaluated response assertions pass without native test execution. Actual private/network/filesystem/GUI acceptance, power-loss guarantees and automatic Linux/macOS transport remain; see Download resumption.

Update storage now adds explicit bounded inspection, acknowledged reversible retirement of obsolete owned downloads, and guarded receipt-based restoration. History/backups remain; this does not free disk space. Actual native/GUI acceptance, permanent pruning, legacy/incomplete caches and pagination remain. See Update storage.

Guided format-2 update recovery now adds immutable preimages, bounded full review, explicit EN/FR helper confirmation and resumable baseline restoration that retains original backups. Native crash/filesystem/GUI acceptance, unattended restoration, legacy journals and power-loss durability remain; see Update recovery.

Verified download rediscovery, bounded attempt history/reporting and cancellation/ retry states now extend the application updater. Guided recovery and explicit partial-transfer resume extend these services; real helper/cache/GUI acceptance remains pending.

Application updating now covers startup stable-GitHub discovery, explicit proposal, verified download and post-close Windows x64 portable replacement/restart, plus matching release archive authoring. Installation-scoped leases/manifest checks and ordinary-failure rollback preserve local ownership. Real HTTP/private/helper/ filesystem/GUI acceptance, unattended/legacy recovery, signing, installers and automatic Linux/macOS transport/packages remain. See Application updates.

Actual document highlights now share bounded native Text/Read/Write normalization, source/backend provenance and SDK/ABI2 access. CodeEditor draws independent palette outlines; a dockable inspector adds kind filtering, navigation and atomic reported-range selection. GUI/server/SDK/plugin/POSIX acceptance and multi-anchor highlight/import-use parity remain pending. No exhaustive semantic-reference claim or new backend annotation layering is made. See Document occurrences.

Source navigation now adds actual declaration/type-definition/implementation requests, bounded validated Location/Link normalization and precise source/backend ownership for all five definition/reference variants. The result dock adds cached filtering, cyclic keyboard selection/reveal, copy, stale inspection and explicit refresh at the active caret. SDK/ABI2 share the native owner (226 SDK operations). Native/server/index/SDK/plugin/GUI/POSIX acceptance is pending; no independent analysis, merged index or guaranteed current other-file target positions are claimed. See Source navigation.

Symbol navigation now includes on-demand resolution of URI-only workspace symbols, issued bounded sessions/cached replies and pre/post workspace/lifecycle/monitor/ backend guards. The palette waits for actual locations, isolates query/selection replies and explicitly refreshes the same search. SDK/ABI2 share the native resolve operation (226 SDK operations). Structure and built-in/plugin server choice remain. Actual server/SDK/plugin/GUI/POSIX acceptance is pending; no merged cross-language index or guaranteed fresh workspace-index positions is claimed. See Symbol navigation.

Three diagnostics milestones now pair publication/document identities and revisions across close/reopen/reload, add severity filters and full selected message details, and navigate supported compiler output through shared build.location / build_location (226 operations). No language/analysis engine is added. Native/GUI/SDK/plugin/POSIX acceptance stays pending; current CyUI still has no forced diagnostic-row scroll/selection API. See Diagnostics and Compiler locations.

Three connected milestones now cover project task status/live output, Cargo protocol display framing and filtered diagnostic keyboard navigation. Native and project builds share TaskOutput's implementation but keep their existing owners. GUI captured-ID cancellation and workspace guards include remote tasks; SDK/ABI2 expose project_status/project_output (226 total operations). Problems commands reuse existing build/LSP data and guarded document opening, without a new analysis engine. Runtime pipe/keyboard/SDK/plugin/GUI/POSIX acceptance remains pending; see Project output and Diagnostics.

Explicit native builds now expose a bounded, revisioned live output tail through the Build panel, SDK and ABI2, reusing existing process/cancellation ownership. Adapters opt in to main user-facing execution, excluding structured discovery. The manifest has 226 operations. Runtime pipe/SDK/plugin/GUI/POSIX acceptance remains pending; see Live build output.

Ordinary Unreal Editor output inspection now checks target receipt context/type, module BuildIds and receipt/manifest-listed project files through native UI/SDK/ ABI2/provider 1.5.0. Bound actual run/launch and prebuild continuation require fresh scoped readiness, while configuration remains available before compiling. Native build results retain process/postflight uncertainty; file lists are virtualized. The SDK has 226 operations. Full engine/plugin dependency, ABI/architecture, closed-source freshness and nonstandard layout validation remain outside this assessment; real Unreal/GUI/POSIX acceptance is pending. See Unreal outputs.

Unreal launch profiles now preserve their build context and normalized options. Desktop prebuild uses the bound target/configuration, with captured parameters and saved-profile/draft/build-ID/open-document guards before automatic debug launch. Native configure/run/launch validate linked fields; explicit detachment supports manual editing and legacy profiles remain usable. The current SDK has 226 operations; provider 1.5.0 and ABI2 use the same core. Actual persistence/build/debug/GUI/POSIX acceptance remains pending. See Unreal launch.

UE4/UE5 launch profile preparation now connects editor, standalone game and uncooked server modes to the shared Debugger/Terminals. Typed map/listen/port/ resolution/log/entry/build options, DebugGame and observed-profile save guards are exposed in CyUI/SDK/ABI2 and provider 1.5.0. Actual launch/debug/GUI/POSIX acceptance remains pending; PIE/Blueprint/Live Coding/editor RPC and cooked binary/session orchestration remain separate work. See Unreal launch.

Reviewed UE5 cooking/packaging now shares native/UI/SDK/ABI2 ownership, game target/ map/container controls, one-attempt input/tool/output guards, per-run staging/ archive/logs and actual cancellable build outcomes. The Unreal provider exposes both new methods. Windows compilation and schema checks are distinct from pending actual UAT/UBT/artifact/cache/cancellation/plugin/GUI/POSIX acceptance. Editor/Live Coding integration, Blueprint/asset tools, advanced packaging profiles/ platforms/signing/deployment and complete package validation remain separate work; see Unreal automation.

History actions and the Replay view now provide single-commit cherry-pick/revert, source patch preview, resolved continuation and quit tracking that retains local work/index. Native UI, three SDK methods and ABI2 exports share the common merge inspector, guards, persistent intents and actual postflight. Windows compilation/ schema checks are distinct from pending real Git/SDK/plugin/GUI/POSIX acceptance. Multi-commit/ranges/mainline, interactive rebase and abort/skip/reset recovery remain separate work; see Git replay.

The Git Merge view now inspects real blockers/parents/conflicts, opens staged Diff review and previews either an unsigned merge commit or quit-tracking while retaining local files/index. Native UI, four typed SDK operations and ABI2 host exports share index/metadata/document guards, persistent intent receipts and actual raw parent/tree/index postflight. Hooks are an explicit reviewed choice. Windows compilation and schema checks pass; real Git/hook/receipt/concurrency, SDK/plugin/GUI/POSIX acceptance remains pending. Signed/autostash/octopus completion, abort/reset recovery and interactive rebase are still separate work; see Merge workflow.

CyCodeReader is now an independent repository owning the shared editor source module. It adds its own native/data extensions, language definitions, encoding conversion and real CyToolsCore/MCP over open documents. Its project services, folder search, macros and unsaved-document recovery remain separate work; see https://github.com/MrMybal/CyCodeReader. CyCode builds only the IDE and consumes the shared module at the revision in app/editor-source.lock.json.

Native desktop, CyUI themes/docking, UTF-8 editing, revision-safe saves, file lookup, background cancellable text search, Git's local workflow, toolchain detection, saved CMake profiles/targets and compilation database integration, C++ LSP completion/diagnostics, definitions/references shared with MCP, native command/VCS extension ABI and live MCP integration. Native multi-window documents/panels, independent instances, solution inspection and UnrealBuildTool generation/build/index are implemented, with UE 5.3 executed on Windows. Executable commands share Rider, Visual Studio and VS Code keyboard profiles with editable bindings/chords. This catalogue covers the current services, not all actions provided by those IDEs. Actual server code actions now share issued sessions, lazy resolution and guarded preview/apply/undo through the native core, GUI and MCP. Native acceptance covers C++ typo fixes, TypeScript imports, Java import organization and Rust rewrites; full desktop acceptance remains pending. See Languages. C++ symbol/type/member search, registered read-only SDK/engine source browsing, multi-file rename previews/apply/undo and .clang-format formatting are implemented through shared native services. Blueprint/asset-aware rename is not provided.

C# completion/diagnostics, definitions/references, types/members, semantic rename and Roslyn formatting share these document/revision services through an independent server. Actual .NET project references and unsaved buffers are exercised on Windows. See C#; managed DAP debugging is implemented for the tested .NET 8 console workflow. Broader framework and language workflows remain pending.

Interactive PTYs and real DAP run/debug/attach services are implemented, with source breakpoints, stack/locals/watches, stepping and program-terminal I/O exercised on Windows. See Execution for the tested boundaries. Git branches, remotes, fetch/fast-forward pull/push, stashes, history/blame and text conflict inspection/resolution are implemented. See Version control.

Next: daily C/C++ use#

Project creation now provides six built-in models: C/C++ CMake, Rust Cargo, C# .sln/.NET, standalone Java and web, with exact previews and guarded exclusive creation. Installed ABI2 plugins can add bounded declarative templates and typed options. The bundled Unreal extension now adds a C++ game with module and Game/Editor targets. See Project templates. Standalone data-pack installation, binary/conditional templates, automatic SDK selection and broader framework/test models remain pending.

General MSBuild solution/project build, clean/rebuild/restore, configuration mapping, evaluated artifacts and C++ indexing are implemented. Windows C++ and SDK C# builds are executed. See MSBuild for the supported scope.

  • Richer command contexts, macOS keymaps and broader semantic search/index coverage; continue implementing the remaining Rider workflows as real services/actions. Actual LSP call/type hierarchy, lazy branch/site navigation and shared SDK/native-plugin sessions are implemented; runtime/GUI/backend acceptance remains pending. See Hierarchies.

  • .slnx inspection and shared MSBuild/C# opening are implemented; new runtime acceptance remains pending. Broader project-system/toolset/custom-target coverage, multiple solution roots and advanced MSBuild compiler/analysis flags.

  • Broader engine/SDK versions and roots, Blueprint/asset tools, Unreal-aware refactoring, Live Coding and editor/debugger integration. Normalize compiler-specific analysis flags further (UE 5.3/clangd 18 still reports an engine intrinsic compatibility diagnostic despite successful member completion/navigation).

  • CMake configure/build presets now use native metadata and actual CMake execution; test/package/workflow previews and native execution now share that build/cancel service, with native/GUI acceptance pending; see Preset actions. Broader custom/cross toolchains, compiler wrappers, configuration variants and broader validation of GCC, modules/PCH/unity/framework workflows.

  • Command-based/resource-edit refactorings and broader code-action coverage remain. Annotated text-edit previews and per-plan confirmations now share the native service, SDK and plugin host; native/GUI acceptance is pending. See Annotated changes. Pull-diagnostic/unversioned provider coverage and framework-specific tests/coverage beyond the implemented configured CTest discovery/selection/cancellation; broader external-header navigation beyond registered SDK roots.

  • Versioned diagnostics now have CodeEditor squiggles/tooltips with native revision guards and theme roles. New runtime/graphical acceptance remains pending; see Editor diagnostics.

  • Semantic full/delta transport, bounded server bases and one full fallback are implemented in the shared language worker; native/backend/GUI acceptance and performance measurements remain pending. See semantic updates. Range/viewport requests, advanced modifier styles and broader raw-string/ preprocessor fallback coverage remain.

  • Windows recursive filesystem notifications, conflict-aware external-change reload and an in-memory paged path index are implemented. Native Linux/macOS watchers, persistent path/symbol indexes, full selection/horizontal-scroll/hidden-fold restoration, historical Undo recovery, large-file editing and broader Unicode benchmarks remain. Unsaved UTF-8 buffers now have per-instance crash checkpoints and guarded preview/restore with editor Undo/Redo; see Recovery. Workspace-relative tabs/cursors, document scroll anchors, wrap/visible folds, image camera/filter settings, recent files, panel visibility and docking layout now restore from bounded per-instance metadata with live-instance leases, source fingerprints and image-dimension guards; runtime/graphical acceptance remains pending. See Workspace sessions. Engine-owned untitled drafts, first-save/Save as to new files, same-editor Undo, empty-draft recovery and explicit session-coordinate restoration are now implemented and Windows compiled. Native/GUI acceptance, overwrite review/external destinations, automatic draft-text restoration and full persisted Undo remain pending; see Untitled documents.

  • Physical file/folder create/move/delete, guarded previews, inverse actions and persistent project trash are implemented through Engine/GUI/MCP/plugin services. Semantic file/resource refactoring, project/include/breakpoint rewriting, richer multi-selection/drag/drop/copy workflows, cross-volume moves and persisted file Undo/Redo remain. See Resources.

  • CMake/MSBuild/explicit Unreal work now shares native cancellation, operation IDs and a reservation retained until work stops, with GUI/MCP/plugin controls. New runtime regressions remain suspended after the antivirus interruption; see Build cancellation. Semantic-request cancellation, and background-analysis streaming remain pending. Explicit native builds and project tasks now have separate bounded live tails with one shared implementation; see Live build output and Project output. Main build/generation deadlines are now configurable through desktop preferences and shared native/MCP/plugin requests.

  • Broader terminal compatibility/IME/fonts, shell integration and split sessions; remote/core-dump workflows and further backend coverage. Capability-gated function/exception breakpoints, paged scopes, register scopes, read-only memory and disassembly are implemented and Windows compiled; their new runtime acceptance remains pending. See Advanced debugging. Data breakpoint inspection/full-list replacement now uses actual capabilities, pause/session handles, revisions and verification through the shared UI/SDK/plugin owner. Native/hardware/GUI acceptance, range controls and persistent targets remain pending; see Data breakpoints. Paused variable/expression setters and memory writes now share the same native owner, with observed session/stop/frame guards, expected-byte preflight, read-back and explicit partial/unconfirmed outcomes. Native target, adapter, concurrent-client and graphical acceptance remain pending; see Value and memory editing. Granularity/single-thread options, reverse stepping/Continue and selected-frame restart now use capability/context-guarded native requests with actual event handling and noncancellable SDK outcomes. Real backend recording/restart, side effects, concurrent thread states and GUI acceptance remain pending; see Execution controls. Session-only instruction breakpoint replacement, conditions/disabled entries, actual verification/events and guarded disassembly drafts now share the native/SDK/plugin owner; real adapter/GUI acceptance and mode/symbol re-resolution remain pending. See Instruction breakpoints. Actual step-in target queries, issued pause/frame-bound choices and explicit targeted execution now share the native/SDK/plugin owner; real adapter/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Targeted step-in. Set next statement now shares that target implementation and the native/SDK/plugin owner, with actual source guards and pending relocated-stop handling; runtime acceptance is pending. See Set next statement. This skips code. Run to cursor now uses a verified temporary source-breakpoint lease, guarded Continue and original list restoration through the native/SDK/plugin owner. Document/disk/context and pending-reply guards are implemented; real adapter/cleanup/concurrency/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Run to cursor. Full non-stop per-thread inspection, virtual-source run-to-cursor and force-run behavior remain.

Complete version control and plugins#

  • Multiple/nested Git roots, selected-repository hunks and linked-worktree catalogue/create/lock/unlock/clean removal are now implemented in the shared Engine/GUI/SDK. Windows compilation is checked; native/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Git worktrees. Session-backed repository selection, reviewed linked-worktree move and intact-pointer repair after manual relocation are now implemented in native/UI/SDK/ABI2, with runtime acceptance pending. Cross-instance document coordination, arbitrary main/bare/custom-layout repair and worktree pruning remain. Configured top-level submodule inspection and guarded init/sync/recorded-commit update now share the native/SDK/plugin owner and a reviewed GUI, with actual Git/runtime/GUI acceptance pending. Separate local addition preview and reviewed clone/stage are implemented, with catalogue/HEAD/index/destination/metadata guards and pending runtime/GUI acceptance. Separate reviewed deinitialization now protects ignored/untracked files, normal index flags, native documents and retained parent-owned metadata; actual removal/runtime/GUI acceptance is pending. Existing-repository adoption, permanent removal and recursive bulk workflows remain. URL/tracking-branch editing now has reviewed native/SDK/plugin/UI operations, preserving metadata edits/index/checkout and reporting effective overrides; real Git/GUI acceptance remains pending. Local override editing and custom Git-directory layouts remain; see Git submodules.
  • Credential UI, interactive rebase, multi-commit/mainline replay, automatic rename topology, Git attribute/filter/EOL checkout semantics and arbitrary staging-line selection remain. Separate per-file raw stage-zero installation/absent-index removal now uses native/UI/SDK/ABI2 ownership, persistent trash and guarded Undo; actual filesystem/Git/GUI/POSIX acceptance is pending. See Git working files. Structural conflict catalogue/inspection and reviewed index-only binary/missing-side/grouped rename-path choices now share native/UI/SDK/ABI2 ownership. Local files and buffers are retained; rename topology is explicit, symlink/gitlink conflicts remain external, and real Git/GUI acceptance is pending. See Git conflicts. Issued text hunks now support guarded staging/unstaging with the common Diff view.
  • Project/root-specific VCS selection, provider-aware menus/custom actions, extension activation/dependencies, native ABI2 instances, panels, commands and declarative CyUI syntax extensions are implemented. The bundled Unreal adapter exercises project contributions against existing services.
  • The bundled SVN provider now implements status/diff/history/blame and guarded add/revert/commit/update, with shared alternative-provider Review tabs. Real SVN acceptance remains pending; see Subversion.
  • A bundled Perforce provider now covers opened-file status, Diff/history/annotations, checkout/add/reopen/revert/one-file submit/locks and guarded sync. Windows compiled; real P4 client/server validation, advanced changelist/shelf/stream/resolve work and GUI acceptance remain pending; see Perforce.
  • A bundled Mercurial provider now covers status/review, exact-file add/forget/revert, commit, clean update, bookmarks/named branches and configured-alias pull/push. Windows compiled; real Hg, native/MCP/GUI acceptance, advanced merge/rewrite/ shared/subrepository workflows and performance benchmarks remain pending; see Mercurial.
  • A bundled Diversion provider now covers status/review, commits/file reset, branch creation, clean checkout/update and locks with automatic tracking/sync. Windows compiled; real client/agent/text-format/native/MCP/GUI acceptance, shelves/tags/reviews/merge/conflict/submodule management and performance work remain pending; see Diversion. Future independent systems use the existing generic provider contract; no backend protocol or implementation is invented for the owner's planned system.
  • Richer provider-specific diff/conflict/status contracts.
  • Manifest OS/architecture/host-version checks and ABI2 activation/deactivation notifications are implemented. Enabled dormant dependents resume when their dependency is activated. Native regression execution for this change remains suspended after the antivirus interruption; see Plugins.
  • Signed local install/update/remove/rollback and guarded unused-version cleanup now use the native package service, explicit publisher trust and immutable versions with host leases. Native/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Plugin packages. Network discovery/marketplace, automatic updates and process isolation for untrusted extensions remain.
  • Plugin language-server registration now routes actual services through independent host-owned processes. Python/Pyright and GLSL Analyzer are integrated; HLSL has a configurable backend awaiting runtime validation. See Development workflows.
  • Native workspace/document/resource/build events and automatic ABI2 subscriptions are implemented, with bounded replay, snapshot handshakes, manifest permissions and failure suspension. Windows compiles; new runtime acceptance is pending. See Workspace events.
  • ABI2 stdio-DAP registration now uses the common native debugger, explicit profile selection, permission-checked host/MCP requests and revocation. The Unreal plugin contributes CodeLLDB. Windows compilation/source checks passed; native runtime acceptance remains pending. See Plugin debuggers.
  • Built-in Java launch and JDWP attach now use JDT LS's Microsoft java-debug add-on, a bounded loopback DAP connection, actual task-generated launch profiles and separate persistent local/remote JVM endpoints. Runtime/network/GUI acceptance is pending. Manual HCR now performs a guarded incremental JDT build/redefine, with explicit result/cancellation handling; automatic synchronization of external build outputs and further Java-specific workflows remain. See Java debugging.
  • Additional real language/debug engines, generic TCP/child-session integrations and specialized GPU editor APIs; extraction of remaining built-in project UI into extensions.
  • Generic panel properties have commit/revision contracts; arbitrary extension-owned data still needs its own Undo/history implementation. There is no automatic global Undo for every plugin operation.

More languages and editor views#

  • Per-workspace language-server launch/settings and activation preferences are implemented in the native core, GUI, MCP and plugin host. Defaults remain unresolved until launch; instances use revision and file locks. New runtime validation remains suspended; see Language preferences.

  • C# broader managed debugging (frameworks, exceptions, async and web workflows), broader Roslyn code actions beyond the shared edit-only transport, snippet variables/transforms and a user catalogue, metadata/generated source views, Razor, rich documentation rendering/mouse hover and broader SDK/framework coverage beyond the implemented Roslyn language services and MSBuild builds. See C#.

  • Cargo workspace/member/features/custom-profile and bin/example/lib/test/bench controls now share native build/test planning, metadata/cache and package/kind executable guards. Windows compiled; expanded Cargo/GUI acceptance remains pending. Named installed Rustup selection now shares Cargo and analysis launch planning; Windows compiled, actual runtime/GUI acceptance pending. Installed toolchain listing/management, arbitrary paths/cross-target runners, advanced Rust debugging and framework test discovery remain; see Cargo workspaces. Explicit Cargo manifest/features/offline/locked analysis snapshots now use local preferences and the shared Rust server owner; Windows compiled, actual backend/GUI acceptance pending. Exact package/target/custom-profile analysis parity and automatic adoption of task changes remain outside this mapping; see Rust analysis and Rust toolchains. Maven/Gradle build/test/run now use real tools and runtime dependency models; Windows compiled, actual JVM runtime acceptance pending. Maven reactor/import parity, Gradle Tooling API, structured framework tests, advanced Java debugging and JPMS/Android remain. The JDT LS launch/attach path is implemented with runtime/network acceptance pending; see Java debugging and JVM builds. Analysis defaults disable Rust build scripts/procedural macros/check-on-save and automatic Java Maven/Gradle imports.

  • Web framework/code-action coverage, advanced snippets and browser/debugger integration beyond the connected JS/TS/HTML/CSS servers and npm task/dev-server terminal execution.

  • HLSL/GLSL compilation now uses typed DXC/glslang requests, guarded output and real-tool diagnostics through shared ProjectTasks; Windows compiled, tool/native/ GUI acceptance pending. GPU preview, reflection/resources/materials, renderer permutations and Unreal shader environments remain. See Shader compilation.

  • Mixed-project workspaces and broader per-project activation beyond the implemented language-server preferences.

Public distribution#

  • Project license selected: GPL-3.0-only. Provide recipients access to the exact corresponding source, including pinned CyUI/shared-editor dependencies and build scripts, alongside binary distributions. Dependency licenses remain applicable.
  • Run actual Windows/Linux/macOS build and runtime matrices, including Unicode/IME, filesystem differences, DPI and portable icon/font coverage.
  • Windows portable release-based updates and ordinary-failure rollback are implemented; actual acceptance remains pending. Installers, unattended/legacy recovery, automatic Linux/macOS updates, clean-machine validation, signing and contribution docs remain.
  • Reproducible end-user packages with complete third-party notices.

pages.title: Run to cursor
pages.html:
Run to cursor#

CyCode arms a verified source breakpoint at the editor cursor, then sends one ordinary DAP Continue. Existing breakpoints and exceptions can stop the program before that destination. On the next actual stop, the native owner replaces that file's breakpoint list with its original list. The temporary point is never saved in the project configuration. This executes program code and has no source Undo.

Desktop#

Pause a debug session, select a saved workspace source document and place its cursor on the destination line. Choose Run > Run to cursor, the Find Action command, or Debugger > Run to cursor. Rider uses Alt+F9; the Visual Studio profile uses Ctrl+F10. The VS Code profile has no new default binding. Custom bindings retain priority. These are Windows/Linux profiles; dedicated macOS schemes and actual keyboard acceptance remain pending.

The document must already be open, unchanged since the captured native revision, clean and byte-equal to its on-disk baseline. Validation runs before arming and again immediately before Continue. Other unsaved tabs do not block this command. The line must exist in that document and the adapter must verify that exact line. A missing/unverified/relocated destination, different verified source path or unmatched virtual source reference prevents continuation. This does not prove that the loaded binary was built from the current file, or lock future disk edits. Adapter-owned virtual sources and files outside the workspace remain unsupported for this workflow; Set next statement has a separate source model.

An existing enabled, unconditional destination breakpoint is reused. An enabled conditional breakpoint, hit condition or logpoint at that line rejects the action instead of changing its behavior. Disabled entries and all original conditions, hit conditions and log messages remain in the original list.

The panel displays verification/progress, cleanup uncertainty and the actual stop reason. A destination hit is reported only when the adapter's stopped event names its actual breakpoint ID. Missing hit IDs remain unknown; another reported ID does not become a fabricated destination hit. The interface uses CyUI Core roles, existing style dimensions and English/French labels. No new CyUI module is needed.

Native owner and recovery#

RunToCursor owns one bounded, revisioned temporary-breakpoint lease. Debugger owns its transport and runs the whole operation on the existing DAP worker; Engine validates native document identity/revision and saved bytes. The worker captures the complete original source list and maps enabled entries to DAP's replacement response order. One temporary unconditional point is appended only when an existing destination cannot be reused. The persisted breakpoint map is unchanged; stale verification metadata is removed during the temporary overlay.

Before Continue, the owner checks session/stop/thread, source identity, current saved bytes, original breakpoint equality and intervening stopped/continued events. It sends one Continue, with optional capability-gated singleThread, and preserves the actual allThreadsContinued response. Stepping granularity and goto target IDs are not accepted. Existing target catalogues expire on execution submission.

An early stopped event is retained even when it arrives before Continue's reply. Cleanup restores the original requested list and publishes the adapter's actual verification for it. Original points can still be unverified or relocated by the adapter; acknowledging replacement does not prove physical address identity. After cleanup, normal stack inspection refreshes the current pause.

An arming failure with a settled reply and confirmed pause attempts one original list restoration. An unanswered request retains its identity and replyPending; late replies are consumed without automatically repeating or continuing an action. An uncertain Continue requires an actual stopped event before restoration. Other debugger mutations are blocked while the lease is active; status remains readable, and Pause or Stop remain available. Restoration itself needs a confirmed pause, settled requests and the current lease revision. The panel's Restore source breakpoints action supplies these guards. A restoration error keeps the lease unconfirmed and requires an explicit recovery action. Stopping the session releases the lease; there is no automatic retry, target restart or process kill.

SDK/MCP and plugins#

debug_run_to_cursor maps to debug.runToCursor. Capture the actual document ID, revision, current breakpoint list and debug context rather than inventing them:

json
{"path":"src/main.cpp","line":40,"sessionGeneration":3, "stopGeneration":7,"threadId":11,"expectedDocumentId":2, "expectedRevision":9,"expectedBreakpoints":[],"singleThread":false}

The path refers to an already-open persistent workspace document, not a CyTools task artifact. No file is staged or copied by this operation. All inputs except singleThread are required. The response is the common debugger state, including runToCursor: status, monotonic revision, active/restorePending/replyPending, captured session/path/line, temporary, stopConfirmed, actual verification, nullable targetHit, stopReason, message and actual continueResult. lastExecution records the actual debug.continue acknowledgement separately from restoration uncertainty.

debug_restore_run_to_cursor / debug.restoreRunToCursor uses the currently observed session, pause and lease revision, for example:

json
{"sessionGeneration":3,"stopGeneration":8,"expectedRevision":12}

Both operations use the real CyToolsCore manifest/handler, process.execute, the existing workspace mutation group and noncancellable metadata. ABI2 plugins use the same methods through host->request; no new C ABI or Python editor/debug owner is introduced. Acknowledgement is not evidence that the destination was hit.

Bounds: 1 MiB serialized native request and original list, 1000 source entries including disabled points, destination lines 1..10000000, path 8192 UTF-8 bytes, condition/hit/log text 4096 bytes, replacement reply 512 KiB with exact enabled entry count. Actual optional breakpoint IDs are signed int32; missing IDs remain missing. Coordinates retain DAP integer bounds. Pre-ack breakpoint events are bounded to 256 entries / 1 MiB total / 64 KiB each. Malformed or relocated target verification refuses continuation; excess events mark the lease unconfirmed.

Verification and remaining acceptance#

Source-only MSVC /Zs checks cover the native owner/worker, Engine, UI, command profiles, plugin exports and regression sources. Assertions specify preservation and enabled-to-wire mapping, collision/capacity rejection, observed guards, verification bounds/signed IDs, deferred events, stop ordering, actual hit reports, revisioned restoration and uncertainty. Constructor compatibility is also checked. The actual CyToolsCore loader and Draft 2020-12 schema data checks accept all 187 operations, typed outcomes, mandatory fields, permissions, cancellation metadata, defaults/custom bindings and translated controls.

These are compilation and data checks, not executed native assertions. Real adapter arming/cleanup, source/binary mismatch, late transport replies, concurrent events/threads, SDK/plugin Runtime, GUI/keyboard/scrolling/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending during the Kaspersky native-test suspension. See Validation and Testing for completed checks.

Primary contracts: DAP specification, Rider stepping, Visual Studio debugger navigation.

pages.title: Cargo options for Rust analysis
pages.html:
Cargo options for Rust analysis#

View > Project tasks > Apply Cargo options and restart Rust copies the current Cargo manifest, features, default-feature and offline/locked options to the Rust language server. It is an explicit restart/enable action. Editing build controls, inspecting a project or reading saved preferences does not start a server.

Remember for this project stores that snapshot in local application-owned language preferences. Uncheck it for this session only. Later Cargo task edits do not silently change the saved snapshot; apply again to adopt them. The existing revision/file-lock guard rejects competing preference writers before replacing the server configuration. A host without a preferences directory applies only session settings. Raw executable arguments and server settings remain separate.

Mapping#

Cargo task option rust-analyzer setting
directory The guarded Cargo.toml becomes the single linkedProjects manifest.
cargoFeatures cargo.features list, including package/feature names.
cargoAllFeatures cargo.features: "all".
cargoNoDefaultFeatures cargo.noDefaultFeatures.
offline / cargoLocked --offline / --locked in cargo.extraArgs, for metadata and other Cargo invocations.
cargoToolchain Optional named Rustup context for the server/Cargo/rustc; empty keeps the base launch. See Rust toolchains.

The override replaces those fields in both initialization options and the rust-analyzer configuration namespace sent through the existing LSP client. Legacy flat Rust settings remain consistent too. Explicit check.features and check.noDefaultFeatures are reset to null so normal checks inherit the Cargo feature selection. Existing --offline, --locked and --frozen extra arguments are replaced by the typed choices without accumulating duplicates. Other trusted settings, argv, environment resolution, sysroot and extra arguments are preserved. Custom override commands or feature flags in other raw arguments can still affect the server and remain the user's configuration responsibility.

Minimal custom settings gain the same disabled defaults for automatic build scripts, procedural macros and check-on-save as the installed Rust configuration. Explicit user settings enabling them are retained. No project-supplied executable, shell command or initialization JSON is imported by this typed action. Rust-analyzer can evaluate Cargo metadata/toolchains and resolve dependencies on explicit startup; offline/locked have their normal Cargo meanings.

Package, target-kind/name, Debug/Release and custom compilation profiles remain build controls. Rust-analyzer loads the linked Cargo workspace and does not reproduce those exact build selections or arbitrary profile-specific cfg/env in this integration. Build-script-generated cfg/types still depend on the user's separate build-script/proc-macro settings. This addition does not establish full equivalence between compiler and analysis behavior.

Native, SDK and plugins#

project.inspect / MCP project_inspect includes an optional rustAnalysis object for Cargo projects. It is derived from the normalized task profile without Cargo execution. Forward it as cargoProject to the existing process-authorized language.configure / MCP language_configure with language: "rust":

json
{  "language": "rust",  "cargoProject": {    "manifest": "member/Cargo.toml",    "features": ["member/gpu"],    "allFeatures": false,    "noDefaultFeatures": true,    "offline": true,    "locked": true  }}

enabled defaults to true. save: true requires the current expectedPreferencesRevision; the saved launch retains relative manifest and typed options, not resolved tool paths or derived initialization data. Core/MCP reading never activates that preference. Desktop first-document activation uses the existing saved-server policy. The ABI2 JSON host shares these same operations without a C ABI layout change or another process owner.

Omitted cargoProject retains the existing override, including when editing raw argv/settings. cargoProject: null removes it and returns to the base settings. Problems > Configure language server also shows the manifest and a removal action that commits only on Apply. Use installed defaults clears the draft override; Reload restores the saved one; Cancel leaves the running configuration intact. Forget saved settings keeps the existing current-server behavior.

The profile accepts only manifest/features/allFeatures/noDefaultFeatures/offline/ locked and optional toolchain. Feature names retain Cargo task limits (128 unique items, 256 UTF-8 bytes each); manifest paths use portable forward slashes, at most 8192 bytes, and must name Cargo.toml within the opened workspace. Parent traversal, absolute/drive/ADS paths and escaping symlinks are rejected. Enabled configuration validates the file and derived 64 KiB settings limit before preference writes or server changes. Disable remains possible after the manifest disappears; later Enable validates the path again. No automatic file watcher adopts task-profile changes.

Validation#

Windows production compilation, source-only MSVC checks and actual SDK schema examples are recorded in Validation. Native mapping, dual LSP settings, immutable base/clear, disabled/read-only policy, path/size guards, preference conflict and reopen assertions extend the existing lifecycle test target. They have not run under the current antivirus-related suspension. Actual rust-analyzer import/resolution, restarts/epoch invalidation, multi-instance behavior, GUI keyboard/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending.

References: rust-analyzer configuration, Cargo build options.

pages.title: Named Rustup toolchains
pages.html:
Named Rustup toolchains#

Project tasks > Rustup toolchain (empty is automatic) selects an installed Rustup toolchain for Cargo configuration/build/test and build-before-run/debug. Leave it empty to retain the previous installed Cargo/private fallback behavior. The adapter does not change Rustup defaults, directory overrides or project files.

cargoToolchain accepts up to 128 ASCII letters/digits, dots, hyphens and underscores, beginning with a letter or digit. Examples of syntax include stable, nightly-2026-10-01, a version/host-qualified name or an existing custom linked toolchain name. These examples do not assert local installation. Paths, leading +/options, whitespace and shell separators are rejected.

Cargo execution#

Explicit names use an argv vector equivalent to:

text
rustup run <name> -- cargo metadata/build/test <Cargo arguments>

The command separator keeps a literal command/argument from becoming a Rustup option. CyCode never adds --install, queries installed versions, installs Rustup or edits its configuration. Missing toolchains/components are reported by Rustup in task output or server logs. Cargo dependencies and trusted build scripts retain their normal behavior; offline/locked flags still belong to the Cargo invocation.

Rustup is found through the existing managed/system tool resolver, including PATH and CYCODE_RUSTUP. Inspection lists its path without invoking it. Explicit selection requires a standard working Rustup installation/proxy setup; it does not use CyCode's private standalone Cargo as a substitute. Rustup owns custom toolchain/component fallback rules.

The selected name sets the child process's RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN; CARGO/RUSTC use cargo/rustc through Rustup's configured proxy PATH. CyCode's derived private Cargo home/compiler environment is not injected for a named toolchain. Output directory, deadline, cancellation and process-tree ownership stay in ProjectTasks. No shell or discovery subprocess is added.

The cache includes the name. Changing it clears cached targets/artifacts; builds always invoke the real tools. Version/date names can express an intended pin, but this implementation does not attest installed bits. Updating an installed toolchain under the same name is not a watched cache input; the next actual build is still owned/evaluated by Cargo.

Rust analysis#

Apply Cargo options and restart Rust also copies the selected name into the local/session cargoProject analysis snapshot as optional toolchain. Empty/omitted names preserve the legacy profile shape. Later task changes still need explicit application; changing a build name does not restart analysis.

For a named snapshot, installed defaults request:

text
rustup run <name> -- rust-analyzer

This requests the analyzer component in Rustup's selected context. Missing components require separate installation; custom-toolchain fallback belongs to Rustup. An explicit user analyzer argv is retained as the command inside that same wrapper, allowing an already installed compatible server. Availability of Rustup alone does not prove that the toolchain or analyzer component is installed.

Both initial and subsequent configuration use cargo.sysroot: "discover" instead of retaining CyCode's private fallback sysroot. cargo.extraEnv receives the three selection variables; conflicting copies in check.extraEnv are removed so normal checks inherit them. Other trusted options/extra arguments remain; arbitrary custom commands can still choose their own compiler behavior. Existing automatic build-script/proc-macro/check-on-save policy is retained.

The existing LanguageService owns the Rustup/analyzer process tree and restart epoch. Enabled preference application validates the manifest/settings and Rustup presence before writing preferences or replacing the current configuration; it does not probe installation by launching Rustup. Disabled settings can still be stored/stopped without Rustup. Removing the snapshot or applying an empty name restores the base launch/environment/sysroot. Saved profiles retain a symbolic name, not resolved Rustup/compiler paths.

MCP/plugins use the same cargoToolchain task field and language_configure.cargoProject.toolchain; operation IDs, permissions and the native C ABI layout are unchanged. Project/pref inspection does not launch tools.

Validation and limits#

See Validation for Windows production compilation, MSVC syntax checks and the actual SDK manifest/schema examples. Wrapper literals, separator/ no-install policy, names/bounds, environment projection, cache invalidation, analyzer component/custom argv, sysroot and disabled preference assertions extend existing opt-in test targets and have not been executed under the current antivirus-related suspension. No Rustup, Cargo, compiler, analyzer or GUI run validated this addition. Missing-component behavior, native cancellation, actual feature/toolchain coherence, Unicode paths and Linux/macOS remain unverified.

Installed-toolchain listing/management, arbitrary toolchain paths, cross-target runners and broader Rust debugger/framework coverage remain separate work.

References: Rustup toolchains, overrides, installation/proxies, Rustup run implementation.
