pages.title: C++ and C# semantic editing
pages.html:
C++ and C# semantic editing#

Document highlights now use actual server Text/Read/Write results through the shared native owner, with precise source lifetime/backend checks and bounded UTF-16 normalization. The GUI adds a debounced single-anchor outline layer, filtered occurrence inspection, navigation and preflighted multi-selection. Text-kind reports may be fuzzier than symbol references; no local name classifier or exhaustive-usage claim is added. See Document occurrences for the native contract, one-glyph-annotation limitation and pending acceptance.

Declaration, type definition and implementation now join definition/references through actual configured language servers, including contributed backends. Precise source identity/revision and backend epoch guards permit unrelated edits; shared bounded Location/LocationLink validation protects all five result forms. The References dock adds filtered keyboard selection, copy and explicit refresh at the active caret. Other-file positions remain index observations. See Source navigation for capabilities and pending acceptance.

The shared native symbol services now preserve bounded hierarchy, complete extents, selection ranges and deprecation, with precise document/backend ownership guards. Workspace queries can retain URI-only entries and resolve their position on selection through the original server using issued bounded sessions. SDK/ABI2 and the palette share expiry/cache and workspace/lifecycle/monitor/backend guards. They power the Structure view and explicit per-server palette search across configured languages. This adds presentation/navigation rather than a new parser or index. See Symbol navigation for limits and pending real-server/GUI/SDK/plugin acceptance.

C# uses the same native document/revision/edit transactions through a separate Roslyn server. Completion, definitions/references, type/member lookup, semantic rename and Roslyn formatting use actual project references. See C# for prerequisites, activation, synchronization and limits. The clangd-specific details below apply to C++.

The GUI and CyTools/MCP call the same native Engine and clangd connection. Correct compilation flags and an available index are necessary. Unreal analysis preparation provides UHT headers and the managed compilation database automatically.

Semantic coloration#

The ordinary editor augments its immediate lexical colors with semantic tokens from clangd or Roslyn. This classifies project aliases, methods and function references, locals/parameters/fields and enum constants using project analysis. Unreal naming conventions remain a fallback; actual variable classifications can override a guessed F/U/A-prefixed type. Unreal's generated headers and compilation database remain necessary for complete engine results. clangd also identifies inactive preprocessor branches, shown with a muted foreground. Both dark and light themes use the same roles with contrast adjustment.

The UI waits 300 ms after a change, prioritizes visible documents and allows two color queries at once. Stale revisions/generations are discarded, and an edit or undo immediately reverts affected displays to lexical coloring. Source text, undo history, identifier selection and completion are independent from the display overlay. Malformed or unsupported responses leave lexical coloring available. Unknown token kinds retain lexical colors; modifier styling, range updates and full backend/ framework/Unreal-version coverage are not claimed.

Full/delta transport is now negotiated through the same native worker, with bounded immutable bases and a single full-request fallback. It still reconstructs the complete document overlay; actual delta/GUI acceptance remains pending. See incremental token updates for bounds, refresh/ restart invalidation and remaining verification.

MCP language_highlight returns the same normalized tokens with source revision, backend generation, supported and truncated flags. Its positions and lengths are zero-based UTF-16; glyphStart/glyphEnd are distinct Unicode codepoint indexes used by the native widget. The operation accepts an opened issued SDK reference without granting filesystem writes. C# must first be enabled through language_configure.

Protocol references: LSP semantic tokens, clangd classifications.

Search and navigation#

Call/type hierarchy now complements symbol lookup with actual LSP callers/callees and base/derived types. Navigate commands, lazy tree expansion and individual call-site navigation share issued revision-guarded sessions with the SDK and native plugin host. Backend capabilities and registered SDK roots still apply. New runtime/GUI acceptance is pending; see Hierarchies.

The search palette has Types, Symbols and Members tabs. Workspace symbols use workspace/symbol; file structure uses hierarchical textDocument/documentSymbol and retains container names. Queries are debounced, stale results discarded and locations opened with UTF-16 coordinate conversion. Results are bounded to 1,000 symbols and may be incomplete while clangd indexes. Rider defaults are Ctrl+N, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N and Ctrl+F12. Prefixes # and @ select symbols and members.

Definitions/references can opt into external SDK locations. Only discovered Unreal Engine/Source and Engine/Plugins roots, compiler headers and registered OS SDK roots are eligible. The Engine issues sdk:// references after validating canonical paths; sources.read accepts only issued references, rechecks their root and opens a read-only document. The UI shows its absolute path and read-only badge. Workspace-relative document operations still reject arbitrary external paths and SDK writes. SDK source files are UTF-8, at most 4 MiB, and do not expand editable workspace permissions. The installed UE 5.3 Actor.h path was exercised on Windows; other platforms remain unverified. Nonstandard SDK installation roots may need additional discovery.

Rename, preview and undo#

Shift+F6 prepares a C++ rename using prepareRename and rename. It is a semantic operation, not a workspace string replacement. An explicit before/after preview lists affected files and edit counts. Code wraps within each column; whitespace decoration is hidden. Changed lines use subtle semantic red/green backgrounds and margin markers; syntax contrast is adjusted against plain and changed backgrounds. Theme/language changes refresh the preview styling and marker labels.

Apply changes validates every affected live revision/text and disk baseline before changing any buffer. It opens affected files in the background and preserves the originating editor. No source file is saved implicitly. Save all persists changes through the ordinary conflict-checked document service. Undo refactoring reverses the whole transaction only when every affected document still matches the applied revision/text and its current disk baseline. It also works after an explicit save, creating unsaved reverse edits. Later editing, closing a document or an external disk change rejects the whole transaction rather than partially reverting it.

There are at most eight retained plans, each with up to 100 files and 16 MiB of before/after text. Old plans are pruned after 20 minutes when new plans are created. Edits are validated for UTF-16 bounds, surrogate boundaries, overlap and expected old symbol text. File create/delete/rename operations and SDK modifications are refused. Versioned documentChanges require the shared LSP owner's current overlay mapping. Index completeness limits cross-file rename coverage. Blueprint assets, serialized Unreal names, arbitrary macro transformations and other languages are not handled by this C++ rename implementation.

Annotated text edits now retain labels/descriptions, effective file groups and per-plan confirmation IDs through the shared preview/apply/undo path. The desktop shows annotated corrections before applying; required labels need individual confirmation. SDK/plugins use the same native guard. Actual annotated-backend/ GUI acceptance remains pending; see annotated changes.

Formatting#

Format document (Rider Ctrl+Alt+L) and Format selection (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+L) request clangd formatting, including the project's .clang-format rules, tab size and spaces. The normal UI command applies the validated result to live buffers and supports editor undo. MCP prepares a plan; changes_apply explicitly performs the edit.

The public MCP operations are described in MCP integration. Native tests exercise real clangd, cross-file rename, shadowed identifiers, Unicode, formatting, revision/disk conflicts and SDK access checks. Desktop acceptance uses real keyboard input and captures the preview in all six themes plus French.

SDK source files are UTF-8, at most 4 MiB, and do not expand editable workspace permissions. The installed UE 5.3 Actor.h path was exercised on Windows; other platforms remain unverified. Nonstandard SDK installation roots may need additional discovery. Rename, preview and undo # Shift+F6 prepares a C++ rename using prepareRename and rename. It is a semantic operation, not a workspace string replacement. An explicit before/after preview lists affected files and edit counts. Code wraps within each column; whitespace decoration is hidden. Changed lines use subtle semantic red/green backgrounds and margin markers; syntax contrast is adjusted against plain and changed backgrounds. Theme/language changes refresh the preview styling and marker labels. Apply changes validates every affected live revision/text and disk baseline before changing any buffer. It opens affected files in the background and preserves the originating editor. No source file is saved implicitly. Save all persists changes through the ordinary conflict-checked document service. Undo refactoring reverses the whole transaction only when every affected document still matches the applied revision/text and its current disk baseline. It also works after an explicit save, creating unsaved reverse edits. Later editing, closing a document or an external disk change rejects the whole transaction rather than partially reverting it. There are at most eight retained plans, each with up to 100 files and 16 MiB of before/after text. Old plans are pruned after 20 minutes when new plans are created. Edits are validated for UTF-16 bounds, surrogate boundaries, overlap and expected old symbol text. File create/delete/rename operations and SDK modifications are refused. Versioned documentChanges require the shared LSP owner's current overlay mapping. Index completeness limits cross-file rename coverage. Blueprint assets, serialized Unreal names, arbitrary macro transformations and other languages are not handled by this C++ rename implementation. Annotated text edits now retain labels/descriptions, effective file groups and per-plan confirmation IDs through the shared preview/apply/undo path. The desktop shows annotated corrections before applying; required labels need individual confirmation. SDK/plugins use the same native guard. Actual annotated-backend/ GUI acceptance remains pending; see annotated changes . Formatting # Format document (Rider Ctrl+Alt+L) and Format selection (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+L) request clangd formatting, including the project's .clang-format rules, tab size and spaces. The normal UI command applies the validated result to live buffers and supports editor undo. MCP prepares a plan; changes_apply explicitly performs the edit. The public MCP operations are described in MCP integration . Native tests exercise real clangd, cross-file rename, shadowed identifiers, Unicode, formatting, revision/disk conflicts and SDK access checks. Desktop acceptance uses real keyboard input and captures the preview in all six themes plus French.

pages.title: Incremental semantic token updates
pages.html:
Incremental semantic token updates#

The existing native language worker now negotiates LSP full/delta semantic tokens. This applies to clangd, Roslyn and built-in or plugin language servers that advertise full-document tokens with delta support. The desktop and the existing language_highlight SDK/native-plugin service share this transport; no public operation, permission, CyUI dependency or editor model is added.

The first request is full. When the server provides a resultId, subsequent queries may send textDocument/semanticTokens/full/delta with that opaque ID. Edits reconstruct the previous integer array before the existing UTF-16/Unicode, legend, overlap and display-budget checks. Offsets refer to the same old array, not token numbers; edits need not arrive sorted or on token boundaries. Equal-position insertions preserve their response order. Full replacements, empty edit lists and null results are supported. Omitted resultId forces the next request to be full; the empty string remains a valid opaque ID.

Reference: the official LSP 3.17 semantic token specification.

Cache ownership and invalidation#

Each independent native language worker owns an in-memory LRU cache. Its limits are 16 documents and 4,000,000 uint32 values (16,000,000 bytes of integer data, plus IDs/container overhead). Each result holds at most 1,000,000 values and its opaque ID at most 4 KiB. A delta contains at most 4,096 edits and 1,000,000 inserted values; the final array also respects the result limit. Negative, fractional, oversized, out-of-bounds, overlapping or incomplete results are refused.

Requests retain immutable snapshots, so eviction or a concurrent response cannot change a delta's base. In-flight snapshots remain alive until the existing bounded request finishes; the cache budget does not include these retained snapshots or transient JSON/decoding buffers. No snapshot or result ID is persisted or exposed as a document reference. Decoded SDK results keep their existing shape.

Ordinary edits retain the previous server base, as required for delta updates. Opening/closing a document, stopping/restarting a backend, and a server workspace/semanticTokens/refresh request discard affected bases. A separate refresh generation distinguishes those resets from ordinary document edits. Responses whose document/semantic generation changed are rejected. Engine revision guards and the editor's immediate return to lexical colors remain active.

Failure and fallback#

An RPC failure or structurally malformed delta discards its base and retries one full request within the original query deadline. The worker retains the same request/promise and outstanding-query accounting; a retry does not extend the timeout or start another process. If that full request fails, the existing caller receives an error and lexical coloring remains available. Stale generations are rejected without retrying in the obsolete context.

Raw array validation occurs before caching; source positions, token types, modifiers and Unicode boundaries retain the existing decoder's checks. An invalid source-position/full response produces an error rather than display data. This change reduces the protocol payload when a backend supplies a smaller delta; it still reconstructs and decodes a full document for the existing overlay. No latency, memory or throughput improvement has been measured locally.

Scope and verification#

Range/viewport requests, advanced modifier styling, semantic-request cancellation, dynamic capability registration and broader backend benchmarks remain separate work. Servers without delta support continue to use full requests. Reader's shared lexical coloring implementation is unchanged.

semantic_token_tests.cpp extends the existing opt-in cycode_tests target; no new runner is introduced. Assertions cover unsorted and integer-granularity edits, empty/deletion/full/null responses, immutable bases, Unicode decoding, integer/ edit/result bounds and LRU eviction. These are currently checked with MSVC /Zs only, with no object, test executable or test execution. Actual server delta negotiation, fallback/deadline/refresh concurrency, GUI behavior, themes/DPI and Linux/macOS remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky interruption. See Validation for the production build and source/schema checks.

pages.title: HLSL and GLSL compilation
pages.html:
HLSL and GLSL compilation#

Project tasks can select system:shader alongside the existing language build adapters. A standalone folder containing shader sources is detected automatically when it has no primary Cargo/npm/JVM/CMake model. For an existing C++/Unreal workspace, open View > Project tasks and choose Use shader tasks in this project. That explicit secondary panel does not replace the primary CMake/MSBuild/Unreal build shortcuts. Select a workspace-relative source, or choose a detected source. A single candidate is selected automatically. Include-only .hlsli files are not offered as standalone compilation targets.

The app uses separately installed tools discovered through PATH or explicit CYCODE_DXC / CYCODE_GLSLANGVALIDATOR executable overrides. No shader compiler is downloaded or executed by opening/inspecting a project. Configure saves the profile and checks the selected source/options without invoking the compiler; without a selected source it only saves the incomplete profile for later choice. Build executes the actual compiler through the existing native ProjectTasks process owner, cancellation token, output limit and configurable total deadline. GUI Build saves dirty buffers first; native/MCP execution refuses remaining dirty documents using the same workspace guard as the other project adapters.

Input Compiler Targets
HLSL Microsoft DXC DXIL or Vulkan SPIR-V, Vulkan 1.0–1.3
GLSL Khronos glslangValidator SPIR-V for Vulkan 1.0–1.3 target environments or OpenGL

Stage options are vertex, fragment, geometry, tessellation control/evaluation, compute, mesh and task. GLSL additionally accepts its ray-tracing stages. Automatic stage selection uses .vert, .frag, .comp, etc., including compound suffixes such as .frag.hlsl / .comp.glsl. A plain .hlsl / .glsl requires explicit stage choice. HLSL uses the selected entry point and shader model (default 6_0), mapped to the actual DXC target profile. The compiler decides whether that model supports the selected stage/features. GLSL source entry remains main. HLSL ray-tracing library/export workflows are explicitly refused rather than inferred.

Typed fields in the saved project profile and existing project_* MCP/plugin requests are shaderSource, shaderLanguage, shaderStage, shaderTarget, shaderEntry, shaderModel, shaderDefines and shaderIncludes. Definitions contain unique NAME or NAME=value entries; include directories are checked workspace paths. Each option remains one argv argument, including spaces/Unicode. Application arguments and arbitrary compiler flag injection are not supported by this adapter. Existing process.execute permissions apply to execution.

Build writes a fresh .cycode/shader-build/<id>/shader.dxil or shader.spv and only publishes an artifact after successful, noncancelled, nontruncated completion and bounded size/container-magic checks. Those checks identify the container; the actual compiler owns semantic validation. Failed partial outputs are not published. Recognized DXC Clang-format and glslang diagnostics map guarded workspace paths to Problems; unknown formats/external source locations remain in the build log. Ambiguous nonzero GLSL numeric source IDs are not mapped to an invented file.

Artifacts describe the current compile result, not a reusable dependency cache. Inspection does not claim a fresh build from an old output; rebuild explicitly after include changes. Source discovery is capped at 4096 candidates / 200,000 visited entries / depth 64. Process output is capped at 4 MiB, published diagnostics at 5000 and the generated artifact at 64 MiB. No shader binary is run as a program.

This implements compilation, not a GPU renderer or live preview. Reflection, resource binding/material editors, renderer-specific shader permutations, cross-stage pipeline validation, WGSL, legacy FXC models and Unreal's shader compilation environment are separate work. Shader Task does not reproduce Unreal engine-generated macros, virtual includes or ShaderCompileWorker.

Windows production compilation and syntax-only checks cover the planner, ProjectTasks integration, panel and added contract sources. No DXC/glslang process, shader test executable, GPU preview or app window was launched during the current antivirus interruption. Actual tool versions/outputs/diagnostics and graphical acceptance remain pending; Linux/macOS remain untested.

Primary contracts: DXC options, DXC SPIR-V code generation, glslang standalone options.

pages.title: Source navigation and result locations
pages.html:
Source navigation and result locations#

Definition, declaration, type definition, implementation and references share one native read-only pipeline. They use the configured language server for the source, including contributed backends; there is no independent parser or guessed fallback. The existing References dock hosts results for all five operations and preserves its layout/session identity.

Commands and language support#

Command Native / SDK Default bindings
Go to definition language.definition / language_definition Existing F12 and profile bindings
Go to declaration language.declaration / language_declaration Assignable; no default
Go to type definition language.typeDefinition / language_type_definition Rider Ctrl+Shift+B; assignable elsewhere
Go to implementation language.implementation / language_implementation Rider Ctrl+Alt+B; Visual Studio / VS Code Ctrl+F12
Find references language.references / language_references Existing profile bindings, including Shift+F12

All commands use the existing menu/action catalogue and keyboard preferences. Rider's build remains Ctrl+F9; the former extra Ctrl+Shift+B build alias is removed from that default profile so it can select the type. Other profiles retain their build bindings. Explicit user overrides remain editable through keyboard settings. Rider's C++ shortcut reference and type navigation reference are documented by JetBrains and Go to Type Declaration. The other implementation defaults follow Visual Studio and VS Code.

The three added operations require the corresponding declarationProvider, typeDefinitionProvider or implementationProvider on every backend. A ready server without the capability disables the UI command, and the native worker rejects unsupported calls explicitly. It never substitutes a definition result for an unsupported operation. Existing definition/reference routing remains compatible. The status methods expose declaration, typeDefinition and implementation. No server is installed or enabled by inspection; an already enabled lazy server can initialize on a request through the existing service owner.

The initialize capabilities advertise static linkSupport for definition and the three new requests. These follow the official LSP contracts for declaration, type definition and implementation. Language/project/index completeness and the meaning of returned implementations remain properties of the actual backend. This does not implement Rider-specific inheritance analysis, decompilation or a merged cross-language index.

Shared native location catalogue#

The input keeps path, expectedRevision and a zero-based UTF-16 position. Optional expectedDocumentId and expectedEpoch check the caller snapshot. includeExternal retains the existing registered SDK/engine root policy, and references retains includeDeclaration. The native owner checks the same source identity/revision and backend epoch after the server reply. Editing another document no longer rejects a source navigation read. Editing, closing/replacing the source or changing its backend rejects the reply. Other semantic mutations/completion retain their existing workspace-generation rules; document identity is also checked there.

NavigationLocations accepts null, one Location, an array of Locations or LocationLinks. The existing path/range navigation fields remain. Every normalized row includes fullRange; a link may also include originRange. Target selection must lie within its extent. All ranges have ordered nonnegative integer LSP coordinates. Origins must fit the exact live UTF-16 source without splitting a surrogate pair. A target referring to that same source is checked against its live buffer as well. URI strings are nonempty, NUL-free and at most 8 KiB.

The owner resolves only workspace or explicitly permitted registered SDK sources. External references remain issued read-only handles. Source scope is checked; target existence/content is read through the existing guarded opener when chosen. Other-file positions remain server-index observations, even when another buffer is open. They are not an atomic disk snapshot or verified current target revision.

Duplicate path/selection destinations collapse to their first valid row, retaining that row's extent/origin. Results sort by path, then selection start/end. Limits are 5,000 returned rows (or the smaller requested limit), 16,384 considered records and 4 MiB for the normalized location array. Stopping at a budget reports truncated. Malformed ranges/rows, invalid URIs and resolution exceptions count as invalid; the existing outsideWorkspace counter counts scope-filtered/unavailable source references. The core is UI-free and reuses Hierarchy range validation and SymbolTextBounds, without a new parsing/indexing dependency.

Reports also include source path/revision/documentId, backend/epoch, method, the requested UTF-16 position and positionEncoding. SDK output schemas bind method to the called operation. GUI/MCP and ABI2 plugins call the same native owner. The three added SDK operations bring the manifest to 226 operations; the ABI2 JSON exports add those three native methods without a C ABI or permission change. They are read operations without permissions or mutation/execution groups.

Result view and activation#

The header identifies the operation and source position. A shared CyUI filter narrows cached path/line/column labels. Previous/Next and Up/Down select matching rows cyclically; Enter or a row click opens the selected destination through the existing document/history service. Keyboard selection can reveal a clipped row inside the result child view. Copy locations copies the filtered labels without reading target source contents. Invalid/unavailable/truncated counts remain visible.

Single-result non-reference queries jump automatically only while the source tab, identity/revision/backend and original active caret still match. Multiple results and references remain in the dock. UI query tickets discard obsolete replies. At reply consumption the owner refreshes language status before checking readiness and epoch, so lazy-server initialization is not judged against an old status copy.

Results retain their observations when the source closes/changes or its backend changes; a stale warning blocks opening those rows. Inspection/copy remains available. Refresh at caret explicitly reruns the selected operation in the currently active supported source and clears the result/filter selection. It does not pretend to refresh an old source position. Filter/selection are transient view state; the existing panel visibility/docking persistence remains.

Capability checks borrow the current server/method objects instead of copying all server diagnostics every frame; the command capability map is immutable and created once. This removes repeated snapshot copies without claiming a measured benchmark. Ordinary editor edits, close, reload and accepted completions retain the observations for the stale-context guard. Workspace/resource changes can still clear the result set. Activation does not access a borrowed result after source-opening side effects.

Existing CyUI Core filtering, palette roles and ImGui controls supply the view; no module, adapter, dependency, process or Undo owner is added. Native data and editing/history ownership remain in CyCode.

Verification limits#

Regression sources extend the existing semantic, command, module and language lifecycle targets. They specify Location/Link normalization, duplicates/order, malformed/Unicode origin ranges, budgets, filter/cache/keyboard wrap, bindings, capability negotiation, caller identity/epoch, unrelated edits, edit/close/ replacement/disable, unsupported providers and late UI tickets. They are compiled with MSVC /Zs only; no fixture executable is linked or run.

The actual SDK loader and schemas validate all 226 operation contracts, exact native facade forwarding, invalid forms/bounds, permissions and EN/FR labels. Windows production builds keep BUILD_TESTING=OFF. Actual language-server/index/ SDK/plugin behavior, keyboard/focus/scroll, Unicode destinations, themes/DPI/ multi-window and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending under the Kaspersky native test suspension. See Validation.

pages.title: Targeted step-in
pages.html:
Targeted step-in#

When several calls share a source line, CyCode can query the debug adapter for the functions it can enter and submit one explicit choice. GUI, SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugins share the existing native DAP worker. Availability requires the actual supportsStepInTargetsRequest capability, a paused selected thread and a frame present in the inspected stack. No targets are inferred from source syntax.

Desktop#

Use Run > Choose step-in target, the same command in Find Action, or Debugger > Execution controls > Choose step-in target. The Step-in targets tab also provides Read step-in targets. Read the list, select a function, then choose Step into selected target. Reading never resumes the program; selecting a row never executes it. No first target is selected automatically. Existing keymaps remain intact; the new command can receive a custom shortcut.

Rows have stable host-issued identities independent of their labels. The table shows the actual function label and optional reported starting line/column. A multiline label is shown in full in its tooltip. The full optional end range is also retained in the SDK result. A genuine empty result is displayed as such. Stepping granularity and the selected-thread option from Execution controls apply only when separately advertised by the adapter. All controls use CyUI Core, translated English/French labels, theme/style roles and DPI-scaled dimensions.

Common service#

StepInTargets is now a compatibility alias for the UI-free DebugTargets implementation, defaulting to the step-in family. Goto uses a separate instance of that same implementation; see Set next statement. Each instance owns a single catalogue and keeps signed int32 DAP target IDs private. Its monotonic catalogue counter is not reset when a session ends. Refreshing replaces the previous catalogue, including within the same pause. debug_status.stepInTargetCatalog is the current issued catalogue ID, or "" when none is available. It does not contain target descriptions or raw adapter IDs.

References expire on execution submission, continued/stopped/invalidation/memory events, disconnect, selected frame/thread changes and adapter capability changes. Both query and execution require explicit observed sessionGeneration, stopGeneration, threadId and frameId. They must still match at native dispatch; a query response is checked against the live context again before it is issued. Late responses cannot populate a different stop's catalogue. The GUI additionally checks the catalogue ID when displaying an asynchronous result, so a refresh by another client clears its previous choices.

The query sends DAP stepInTargets with only the selected frameId. Targeted execution resolves a host handle, validates optional stepping settings and sends exactly one DAP stepIn with the private targetId. The entire catalogue is consumed before submission, including when acknowledgement later fails. Legacy debug.stepIn continues to reject both raw targetId and issued target fields. An explicit refresh is required to obtain another choice after an attempt.

lastExecution.method is debug.stepIntoTarget. Its public arguments contain the issued target, frameId, threadId and optional stepping settings, never the raw adapter target ID. The existing applying/accepted/unconfirmed outcomes, actual stopped-event refresh and rapid-stop preservation apply. Acceptance only acknowledges the request. There is no automatic retry, source Undo, rollback or cancellation after execution submission.

SDK/MCP and plugins#

debug_step_in_targets maps to debug.stepInTargets; debug_step_into_target maps to debug.stepIntoTarget. Both require process.execute. The execution operation is noncancellable in the real CyToolsCore manifest and handler. ABI2 host->request uses exactly these native methods and guards. No C ABI version change, extra executable, external dependency or new CyUI module is required.

For an observed session 3, stop 7, selected thread 11 and frame 9:

json
{"sessionGeneration":3,"stopGeneration":7,"threadId":11,"frameId":9}

A query result contains the same context plus catalogId and targets. Each target has an issued string id, the actual label, and optional line, column, endLine, endColumn. Pass the selected returned ID as target with that same captured context; do not reconstruct or persist handles. For example, if the actual result issued step-1-0:

json
{"sessionGeneration":3,"stopGeneration":7,"threadId":11,"frameId":9, "target":"step-1-0","granularity":"line","singleThread":false}

Limits: one catalogue, 128 targets, 4 KiB query/execution request, 512 KiB adapter reply and 4096 UTF-8 bytes per nonempty label. Unknown public request fields, invalid/duplicate signed adapter IDs, NUL text, malformed coordinates, oversized responses and reversed explicit ranges are rejected before publishing a catalogue. Extra adapter response fields are ignored. Optional positions retain DAP's 0..9007199254740991 integer bounds: initialize requests one-based lines and UTF-16 columns; zero is retained as unknown and omitted from the table. Missing optional positions remain absent. Duplicate labels with different IDs remain distinct.

Verification and remaining acceptance#

MSVC /Zs checks cover the native/UI implementations and regression assertions for context/capability changes, refresh/expiry, signed IDs, duplicates, actual empty results, bounds, raw-ID isolation, stepping options and captured GUI parameters. These assertions have not been linked or executed. Actual CyToolsCore manifest loading and schema examples check the 183-operation catalogue, typed input/output, legacy field isolation, permissions, execution cancellation metadata and labels. See Validation for the completed production/source checks.

Real CodeLLDB/NetCoreDbg/java-debug/plugin adapters, nested/inlined calls, late events/timeouts, SDK/plugin runtime, keyboard/scrolling/themes/DPI and graphical acceptance remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky native-test suspension. Linux/macOS builds remain pending. Run-to-position and full non-stop thread UI are separate work; this does not provide them.

pages.title: Subversion provider
pages.html:
Subversion provider#

CyCode builds cycode.svn as a bundled native ABI2 plugin. Its provider ID is cycode.svn.provider; Git remains the default. Enable Subversion in Extensions, open Version control and choose Subversion (SVN) with the working-copy folder in the mapping field. Mapping is explicit, persisted in .cycode/vcs.json and shared by menus, the panel and native/MCP requests. No checkout or repository creation runs when selecting a provider or opening a project.

Install the Subversion command-line client separately. Tool discovery checks CYCODE_SVN (an absolute executable), packaged tools and absolute PATH entries. No client is downloaded or bundled. The implementation targets the modern SVN 1.10+ command-line interface; real client/version/server acceptance is pending. Project paths cannot select the executable or inject command options.

Operations#

Action Scope and behavior
status / inspect Local info --xml and status --xml --ignore-externals; mapped workspace paths, named changelist entries, text/property/tree conflicts, relative repository URL and working revision. No update check or network poll.
diff Working copy or explicit local file; SVN internal unified diff, displayed through the shared CyUI Diff review. No staging area.
log / history XML history, default 50 and maximum 200 revisions; author/date/first-line subject plus full messages in the read-only Review view. A local target defaults to its BASE history.
blame Selected file at BASE, read-only annotations; may contact the server.
add Selected file only, depth empty, no automatic properties or parent addition.
revert Selected file only, depth empty; requires confirmation:"REVERT". Discards text/property changes and unschedules additions/deletions. SVN does not provide Undo for this action.
commit All tracked changes in the mapped copy, explicit nonempty UTF-8 message, no external inclusion. Conflicts must be resolved first.
update Mapped copy, ignores externals, postpones conflict decisions, requires a clean tracked copy. Untracked obstructions remain protected by SVN's own refusal rules.

The plugin advertises seven custom actions; host menus and command palette use those descriptors. Git branch/remotes/staging/stash views stay specific to Git. Alternative-provider diffs, history and annotations now have their own Changes / Review tabs; this fixes the previous early return that hid their preview. Action titles/fields use the existing EN/FR catalogue and shared theme/DPI styles.

Native/MCP example after configuring a mapping:

json
{"action":"log","contextPath":"Source/main.cpp","input":{"limit":25}}

Pass this to vcs_provider_action. Mutations use the same operation with, for example, action:"commit", input:{"message":"Describe the change"} or action:"revert", input:{"path":"Source/main.cpp","confirmation":"REVERT"}. The generic SDK operation conservatively retains its existing plugin/process/ workspace/VCS permission requirements, including for provider reads. It does not weaken the separate typed read-only Git operations.

Ownership and guards#

The mapped folder must be the exact SVN working-copy root inside the opened workspace. Subdirectories of an outside working copy are rejected. Nested directory checkouts/externals require their own mapping; targeted file externals are rejected after a separate local XML status check. Operated paths must be local, workspace-relative, inside the selected root and outside .svn; parent traversal, URLs and symbolic-link traversal are rejected. The host also checks provider paths. Status can display symlink entries; this provider does not operate on them. Paths receive an explicit local prefix and final peg escape, including names with literal @; no shell or project-generated command string is used.

Common process/tool discovery lives in cycode_process, shared by the native core and plugin without copying its source or linking UI/Engine services into the DLL. Calls are synchronous on the existing background VCS worker, serial with plugin callbacks. Local commands have 15 seconds; history/blame/commit/update have 180 seconds per process, with 512 KiB output bounds. Native process ownership kills owned children on timeout/output overflow. Complete XML is required before interpreting a status or allowing an update/commit. Partial failures return exitCode/output/timedOut/truncated/cancelled; large callback responses fail above the existing 4 MiB ABI bound. Invalid bytes in textual client output become Unicode replacement characters; XML file paths remain UTF-8.

Commands always use --non-interactive --no-auth-cache. Existing system SVN authentication/configuration is used; CyCode does not collect passwords, approve certificates or save credentials. SVN's configured transports may run installed helpers. See SVN authentication flags and the official quick start.

Host mutations refuse dirty buffers and open files whose disk bytes differ from their baseline. This check also strengthens other external VCS providers. After an operation, clean buffers are reconciled and concurrently modified/deleted/ unreadable buffers are retained. A provider operation and mapping changes share the native VCS lock. External filesystem/other-process races are not atomic with SVN; changes made during execution are preserved by the editor reconciliation. Disable waits for the serial callback; there is no new early-cancel VCS API or process isolation boundary for trusted native plugins.

Validation and remaining scope#

The new contract regression source injects a fake runner: no SVN subprocess is needed for XML/property/tree-conflict/changelist parsing, file-external rejection, root/peg/argv guards, deadlines, truncation and mutation checks. It also specifies real production-DLL loading, mapping, disk-conflict rejection and disable-without-fallback assertions. Existing extension GUI regressions now cover alternative-provider Diff Review in six themes, EN/FR and three DPI scales. These sources are syntax-checked only; no test executable is built or run during the current antivirus interruption. Actual build/check results are recorded in Validation.

Real SVN local/server operations, authentication, conflicts, GUI interactions, Windows clean installation and Linux/macOS remain unverified. Checkout/creation, delete/move/copy, branch/tag/switch/merge, changelists, locks, sparse/external editing, rich SVN conflict resolution, credentials UI and cancellation require further implementation. Perforce now has a separate bundled provider; Mercurial also has its own bundled plugin. Typed SDK Git operations are explicitly Git-only; external SVN calls use the generic permission-checked provider operation. This addition is not complete Rider or full SVN-client parity.

pages.title: Document structure and symbol navigation
pages.html:
Document structure and symbol navigation#

Three connected features reuse the existing native language services: a bounded hierarchical symbol catalogue, a dockable Structure panel, and an explicit language server choice in Go to type / Go to symbol / Search Everywhere. No independent parser, index, Python editor model, dependency or CyUI module is introduced.

Shared native results#

language.documentSymbols / SDK language_document_symbols and language.symbols / language_symbols retain the flat symbols compatibility list. Each row now also has:

Field Meaning
node, parent, depth Nonzero snapshot-local ID, represented parent ID (0 for a root), nesting depth
range Existing navigation/selection range, zero-based UTF-16
fullRange Complete symbol extent for caret containment
deprecated Server deprecation flag/tag

Names, details, kinds and containers come from the server. Hierarchical DocumentSymbol trees preserve their represented parents. Flat SymbolInformation responses remain roots; the application does not infer a tree from names. Duplicate rows are removed. A filtered, unavailable or malformed parent may leave valid descendants as roots, retaining their textual container context. Node IDs belong to one result snapshot and are not persistent semantic identities.

Results include backend, configuration epoch, invalid malformed-row count, outsideWorkspace, truncated and the existing encoding marker. Document results also include path, revision and documentId. Optional expectedEpoch and document expectedDocumentId inputs check the caller's snapshot. Language status exposes each server's epoch, including contributed server IDs; the existing ABI2 JSON host exports share these results without a C ABI change. Existing permission classifications remain. The added language_symbol_resolve operation brings the SDK surface to 226; ABI2 adds language.symbolResolve without a C ABI change.

Document replies require the same open identity/revision and backend epoch after the server responds. Closing, replacing, editing or reconfiguring invalidates the reply. Unrelated open-document edits no longer invalidate a document structure query. The owner verifies that selection and body ranges refer to that same file and fit its current UTF-16 buffer. A single pass indexes line lengths and surrogate splits; validating many symbols does not repeatedly scan the entire file. Registered SDK sources keep their issued read-only references and gain a new identity on loading a new source snapshot.

Workspace queries retain their workspace-edit/configuration guard; returned positions remain index observations rather than verified current document ranges. External sources still require registered SDK/engine roots and explicit includeExternal. No arbitrary external path access is added.

Bounds are 1,000 returned rows (or the smaller requested limit), 8,192 considered records, nesting depth 64 and a 4 MiB normalized symbol array. Names/details/URIs and tag arrays are bounded. Malformed ranges, kinds and envelopes are rejected or counted. Exceeding a collection budget reports truncation. A malformed present range is not treated as an unresolved symbol. URI-only workspace entries now use the deferred workflow below; document symbols still require real ranges.

Deferred workspace-symbol locations#

The client advertises workspace.symbol.resolveSupport for location.range, plus the existing supported kinds and deprecation tag. The worker checks the server's workspaceSymbolProvider.resolveProvider before sending workspaceSymbol/resolve; language.status.methods.symbolResolve exposes that capability for each configured built-in/contributed backend. This follows the official LSP 3.17 workspace-symbol contract.

Complete rows retain their previous shape. A valid URI-only workspace row carries unresolved: true, resolveIndex, normal display metadata and a scoped path; range and fullRange are absent. Its report carries a session reference. There is no fabricated line zero. Names, kinds and tag/text validation still apply; source-access filtering occurs before issuance. Exact duplicate deferred records share one row and do not consume a second opaque-data cache entry.

GUI, MCP language_symbol_resolve and ABI2 language.symbolResolve submit only session, index (the row's resolveIndex) and optional expectedEpoch. The native owner retains the original server object/data and backend; callers cannot inject arbitrary resolve payloads. A successful response contains one complete symbol, backend, epoch and positionEncoding: utf-16. The returned name/kind/URI must match the issued item, and only its location range is adopted. The same normalized UTF-16 range and workspace/registered SDK source guards apply again. Read-only SDK references remain read-only; no command, source edit, arbitrary external read or backend installation/activation occurs.

Sessions are process/workspace local: at most four, each expiring two minutes after creation. They hold at most 1,000 raw items, 64 KiB per raw object and 1 MiB of raw/resolved cache payload per session. The independent normalized list stays bounded to 4 MiB. Oversized raw rows increment invalid; unavailable/outside sources increment outsideWorkspace. Unknown, unissued, expired or evicted session/index pairs require a new search. Successful bounded resolutions are cached without extending expiry; a full cache may return a valid result without retaining it. No persistent semantic identity or index is added.

Workspace buffer/lifecycle generation, observed workspace-monitor revision and backend epoch are captured at search, checked before resolving (including cached hits) and checked after the server reply. A changed context requires Refresh. Background filesystem activity can invalidate this conservative session guard; Refresh retries against a newer observation. The monitor is not an atomic disk snapshot, and workspace symbol positions remain server-index observations rather than verified live-buffer ranges. Document structure retains its more precise document identity/range checks and permits unrelated edits.

Structure panel#

View > Structure opens an ordinary dockable/multi-window panel, hidden by default. Existing session visibility and docking restoration include it. It follows the active supported source and uses the same document-symbol service as the member palette and SDK. Images, untitled drafts and debugger source references do not issue structure requests. Opened SDK sources remain read-only.

The panel provides a shared CyUI filter with matching ancestor context, source or alphabetical order, a caret-following scope and explicit Locate/Refresh actions. Alphabetical sorting reuses CyUI's ASCII/Latin case/accent folding; this is not full Unicode collation. Both sort orders and filtered visibility are cached. Locate clears the current filter and reveals the enclosing scope. Caret-follow reveals a newly entered scope without discarding the filter. Source extents are half-open, with exact point ranges also supported.

Click a symbol label or press Enter on a focused tree node to navigate through the existing document/history service. Arrow/disclosure actions retain tree navigation. Clicking a destination disables caret-follow until re-enabled. Caret reveal opens ancestors and scrolls inside the tree's own child view. Kind, deprecation and server detail are shown without translating source names. Filters, sorting and follow state are view state for the current workspace; only the normal panel visibility/docking state is persisted.

Requests are debounced and limited to one in-flight structure request. Request tickets, document ownership and configuration epochs prevent obsolete replies from appearing. Hidden/reopened panels can repeat the same request. Empty results do not trigger a polling loop; Refresh, a document edit or a context change can request again. C++ structure stays inactive during desktop Unreal preparation. No server is installed or enabled automatically. An already enabled lazy server may initialize when the user requests structure, through its existing owner.

Symbol palette#

The server selector offers Automatic (active document, falling back to C++) and enabled available built-in/contributed servers. Known unsupported workspace-symbol methods are disabled. One chosen server is searched; this is not a merged search across all language indexes. The selection lasts for the current workspace. File structure/member lookup always belongs to the active document's backend. Kinds and server details help distinguish similarly named results.

Changing the query/server/context, closing the palette or switching modes prevents late results/errors from populating another query. Backend-picker Enter/arrow handling is separated from result activation. Existing Rider/Visual Studio/VS Code bindings and @ member / # symbol prefixes remain. The new persistent view has no default shortcut; custom bindings can target view.structure.

Deferred rows show “Location on selection” instead of a line number. Click/Enter keeps the palette open, shows resolution progress and opens the source only after a current successful reply. Errors stay visible with Refresh available. Changing the query, server, mode or selected action/file, or dismissing the popup prevents a late resolution from opening a document. An explicit Refresh creates a new UI request ticket even for the same text, so an older same-query reply cannot win. Resolution uses a separate single in-flight UI future; dismissing the view discards its reply rather than terminating the language server. Existing worker deadlines and queue limits remain. These view/timing interactions still need native/GUI acceptance under the current test suspension.

Validation limits#

Regression sources extend existing semantic, module and lifecycle fixtures: hierarchical/flat/duplicate/malformed/deferred responses, bounds, UTF-16/point scopes, cached order/filter changes, opaque-data preservation/capability negotiation, issued index/session checks, resolution caching/eviction, unrelated edits, close/reopen/replacement, server disable, malformed/changed destinations and stale palette/panel/selection replies. They are checked with MSVC /Zs only. The real installed SDK loader and schemas validate the new contracts and EN/FR data. Actual server timing/filesystem, keyboard/focus, docking/multi-window, Unicode destinations, SDK/plugin execution, themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending under the Kaspersky native-test suspension. See Validation.
