No independent parser, index, Python editor model, dependency or CyUI module is introduced. Shared native results # language.documentSymbols / SDK language_document_symbols and language.symbols / language_symbols retain the flat symbols compatibility list. Each row now also has: Field Meaning node , parent , depth Nonzero snapshot-local ID, represented parent ID (0 for a root), nesting depth range Existing navigation/selection range, zero-based UTF-16 fullRange Complete symbol extent for caret containment deprecated Server deprecation flag/tag Names, details, kinds and containers come from the server. Hierarchical DocumentSymbol trees preserve their represented parents. Flat SymbolInformation responses remain roots; the application does not infer a tree from names. Duplicate rows are removed. A filtered, unavailable or malformed parent may leave valid descendants as roots, retaining their textual container context. Node IDs belong to one result snapshot and are not persistent semantic identities. Results include backend , configuration epoch , invalid malformed-row count, outsideWorkspace , truncated and the existing encoding marker. Document results also include path , revision and documentId . Optional expectedEpoch and document expectedDocumentId inputs check the caller's snapshot. Language status exposes each server's epoch, including contributed server IDs; the existing ABI2 JSON host exports share these results without a C ABI change. Existing permission classifications remain. The added language_symbol_resolve operation brings the SDK surface to 226; ABI2 adds language.symbolResolve without a C ABI change. Document replies require the same open identity/revision and backend epoch after the server responds. Closing, replacing, editing or reconfiguring invalidates the reply. Unrelated open-document edits no longer invalidate a document structure query. The owner verifies that selection and body ranges refer to that same file and fit its current UTF-16 buffer. A single pass indexes line lengths and surrogate splits; validating many symbols does not repeatedly scan the entire file. Registered SDK sources keep their issued read-only references and gain a new identity on loading a new source snapshot. Workspace queries retain their workspace-edit/configuration guard; returned positions remain index observations rather than verified current document ranges. External sources still require registered SDK/engine roots and explicit includeExternal . No arbitrary external path access is added. Bounds are 1,000 returned rows (or the smaller requested limit), 8,192 considered records, nesting depth 64 and a 4 MiB normalized symbol array. Names/details/URIs and tag arrays are bounded. Malformed ranges, kinds and envelopes are rejected or counted. Exceeding a collection budget reports truncation. A malformed present range is not treated as an unresolved symbol. URI-only workspace entries now use the deferred workflow below; document symbols still require real ranges. Deferred workspace-symbol locations # The client advertises workspace.symbol.resolveSupport for location.range , plus the existing supported kinds and deprecation tag. The worker checks the server's workspaceSymbolProvider.resolveProvider before sending workspaceSymbol/resolve ; language.status.methods.symbolResolve exposes that capability for each configured built-in/contributed backend. This follows the official LSP 3.17 workspace-symbol contract . Complete rows retain their previous shape. A valid URI-only workspace row carries unresolved: true , resolveIndex , normal display metadata and a scoped path ; range and fullRange are absent. Its report carries a session reference. There is no fabricated line zero. Names, kinds and tag/text validation still apply; source-access filtering occurs before issuance. Exact duplicate deferred records share one row and do not consume a second opaque-data cache entry. GUI, MCP language_symbol_resolve and ABI2 language.symbolResolve submit only session , index (the row's resolveIndex ) and optional expectedEpoch . The native owner retains the original server object/data and backend; callers cannot inject arbitrary resolve payloads. A successful response contains one complete symbol , backend , epoch and positionEncoding: utf-16 . The returned name/kind/URI must match the issued item, and only its location range is adopted. The same normalized UTF-16 range and workspace/registered SDK source guards apply again. Read-only SDK references remain read-only; no command, source edit, arbitrary external read or backend installation/activation occurs. Sessions are process/workspace local: at most four, each expiring two minutes after creation. They hold at most 1,000 raw items, 64 KiB per raw object and 1 MiB of raw/resolved cache payload per session. The independent normalized list stays bounded to 4 MiB. Oversized raw rows increment invalid ; unavailable/outside sources increment outsideWorkspace . Unknown, unissued, expired or evicted session/index pairs require a new search. Successful bounded resolutions are cached without extending expiry; a full cache may return a valid result without retaining it. No persistent semantic identity or index is added. Workspace buffer/lifecycle generation, observed workspace-monitor revision and backend epoch are captured at search, checked before resolving (including cached hits) and checked after the server reply. A changed context requires Refresh. Background filesystem activity can invalidate this conservative session guard; Refresh retries against a newer observation. The monitor is not an atomic disk snapshot, and workspace symbol positions remain server-index observations rather than verified live-buffer ranges. Document structure retains its more precise document identity/range checks and permits unrelated edits. Structure panel # View > Structure opens an ordinary dockable/multi-window panel, hidden by default. Existing session visibility and docking restoration include it. It follows the active supported source and uses the same document-symbol service as the member palette and SDK. Images, untitled drafts and debugger source references do not issue structure requests. Opened SDK sources remain read-only. The panel provides a shared CyUI filter with matching ancestor context, source or alphabetical order, a caret-following scope and explicit Locate/Refresh actions. Alphabetical sorting reuses CyUI's ASCII/Latin case/accent folding; this is not full Unicode collation. Both sort orders and filtered visibility are cached. Locate clears the current filter and reveals the enclosing scope. Caret-follow reveals a newly entered scope without discarding the filter. Source extents are half-open, with exact point ranges also supported. Click a symbol label or press Enter on a focused tree node to navigate through the existing document/history service. Arrow/disclosure actions retain tree navigation. Clicking a destination disables caret-follow until re-enabled. Caret reveal opens ancestors and scrolls inside the tree's own child view. Kind, deprecation and server detail are shown without translating source names. Filters, sorting and follow state are view state for the current workspace; only the normal panel visibility/docking state is persisted. Requests are debounced and limited to one in-flight structure request. Request tickets, document ownership and configuration epochs prevent obsolete replies from appearing. Hidden/reopened panels can repeat the same request. Empty results do not trigger a polling loop; Refresh, a document edit or a context change can request again. C++ structure stays inactive during desktop Unreal preparation. No server is installed or enabled automatically. An already enabled lazy server may initialize when the user requests structure, through its existing owner. Symbol palette # The server selector offers Automatic (active document, falling back to C++) and enabled available built-in/contributed servers. Known unsupported workspace-symbol methods are disabled. One chosen server is searched; this is not a merged search across all language indexes. The selection lasts for the current workspace. File structure/member lookup always belongs to the active document's backend. Kinds and server details help distinguish similarly named results. Changing the query/server/context, closing the palette or switching modes prevents late results/errors from populating another query. Backend-picker Enter/arrow handling is separated from result activation. Existing Rider/Visual Studio/VS Code bindings and @ member / # symbol prefixes remain. The new persistent view has no default shortcut; custom bindings can target view.structure . Deferred rows show “Location on selection” instead of a line number. Click/Enter keeps the palette open, shows resolution progress and opens the source only after a current successful reply. Errors stay visible with Refresh available. Changing the query, server, mode or selected action/file, or dismissing the popup prevents a late resolution from opening a document. An explicit Refresh creates a new UI request ticket even for the same text, so an older same-query reply cannot win. Resolution uses a separate single in-flight UI future; dismissing the view discards its reply rather than terminating the language server. Existing worker deadlines and queue limits remain. These view/timing interactions still need native/GUI acceptance under the current test suspension. Validation limits # Regression sources extend existing semantic, module and lifecycle fixtures: hierarchical/flat/duplicate/malformed/deferred responses, bounds, UTF-16/point scopes, cached order/filter changes, opaque-data preservation/capability negotiation, issued index/session checks, resolution caching/eviction, unrelated edits, close/reopen/replacement, server disable, malformed/changed destinations and stale palette/panel/selection replies. They are checked with MSVC /Zs only. The real installed SDK loader and schemas validate the new contracts and EN/FR data. Actual server timing/filesystem, keyboard/focus, docking/multi-window, Unicode destinations, SDK/plugin execution, themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending under the Kaspersky native-test suspension. See Validation .

pages.title: Local verification and native tests
pages.html:
Local verification and native tests#

Detailed update history adds twenty actual attention/phase/count/outcome assertions, bringing updater policy checks to 115 compiler-evaluated assertions. Opt-in bodies specify discovery beyond twelve metadata rows, no created locks, sorting/unknown times, selected/full report exclusions, foreign/oversized/invalid records, cancellation and budgets. A GUI fixture specifies test-session exclusion. Bodies remain syntax-only under the antivirus suspension; no native history/helper/GUI fixture is generated or run. See History for pending acceptance.

Recovery controls add sixteen assertions on production phase-local progress and stable phase codes, bringing installation/recovery plus download policies to 95 compiler-evaluated assertions. Source-only fixtures specify typed pre-cancellation, progress reuse/foreign-plan rejection, exact fresh/reused copy bytes, result receipt states and report exclusions. The helper manifest/EN-FR catalogue/project references are checked as data; production PE resources are read without executing them. Stop/close timing, clipboard, blocked I/O, cancellation after file moves, receipt failures and graphical theme/DPI/restart acceptance are still unexecuted. No native fixture is built or run during the antivirus suspension. See Recovery controls.

Space/progress checks add nine constexpr headroom assertions and two multi-case meter contracts to the existing nineteen HTTP assertions. They evaluate actual production code in MSVC /Zs: resumed/full/complete offsets, invalid bounds, rate sampling/smoothing/stalls, reset counters/clocks and ETA bounds. A source-only native fixture describes caller-space observation and retained-file behavior. Real low-space/quota/write-failure and network/GUI acceptance remains pending; no disk-filling fixture, native test executable or app is run. See Download observations.

Update-retry source contracts add exact/most-advanced checkpoint selection, fresh noninspection and file retention, cancelled/invalid modes and typed response errors. Module source fixtures inject completed inspection futures to specify preserved feedback, quiet refreshed candidates, replaced digests and failed/cancelled local refreshes; they never invoke a real transfer. Smoke/test-session source guards cover fresh downloads and post-attempt scanning. These fixture bodies are syntax checked only, not linked or executed. Existing nineteen constexpr response assertions are still compiler-evaluated. See Download retry.

Download-resume verification evaluates nineteen static assertions on the actual production constexpr response policy through MSVC /Zs, without native execution. Additional opt-in source contracts cover checkpoint/asset identity, readonly inspection, foreign/rejected/unknown metadata, limits and interrupted staging. Actual transfer, WinHTTP headers, locking, cancellation and GUI acceptance remain pending; see Download resumption.

Cache-maintenance source fixtures cover owned/legacy/current protection, read-only review, active leases, stale/pending/cancelled actions, reversible moves, receipt and destination conflicts, partial restore, and retained metadata/backups/user data. Core/module source checks only; no native fixture or maintenance operation is run. See Update storage.

Guided recovery sources specify immutable plan preparation, read-only/conflicted review, exact confirmation guards, bounded/non-overwriting restoration, retained backups/user files, cancelled/stale actions, instance exclusion, partial restoration resume and legacy refusal. Existing opt-in core sources only; no native execution under the Kaspersky suspension. See Update recovery.

Update-cache follow-up sources specify restart discovery, bound outcome history, retryable archives, cancellation, corrupted helpers/archives, foreign metadata, pending markers, outside staging paths, retained downloads and changed release digests. These bodies are syntax-checked only under the existing native-run suspension; no SDK Runtime or executable fixture is imported or run.

Application-update regression sources join the existing core/module targets, without another test executable. MSVC /Zs checks the native release, transport, package, helper, UI and integration/regression sources. No fixture/helper/app is launched. Source cases specify version/asset/digest/path rejection, locked-file rollback, user-data retention, repeated-version refusal, installation lease exclusion, skip/manual proposal behavior, test-session network guards and cancelled close intent. Five Python authoring tests execute only in-memory ZIP/JSON/hash/PE-header data; no fake EXE file is written or run. The existing CI matrix includes this data-only suite, but has not run remotely. Production build and PE resource inspection do not establish real HTTP/helper/rollback/GUI/platform acceptance. See Application updates and Validation.

Occurrence regression sources extend existing semantic, command, module and language-lifecycle fixtures with no new executable target. MSVC /Zs checks affected production/regression sources only; fixture bodies are not linked or run. Cases specify actual capability negotiation, source/backend lifetime and unrelated-edit handling, normalization/kinds/Unicode/budgets, cyclic masked navigation, atomic selection/source/Undo preservation, independent annotation geometry, native tab/wrap metrics and clear-during-request. Actual SDK load_manifest and all 227 operation schemas pass pure bridge/data guards, strict result forms, permissions, status and EN/FR forwarding checks. No SDK Runtime/native client is imported. Production and source/schema checks do not establish GUI, server or platform acceptance. See Document occurrences and Validation.

Source-navigation regression sources extend the existing semantic, command, module and lifecycle fixtures without a new executable target. MSVC /Zs checks 16 distinct affected production/regression sources, including final focused range/signature/ownership refinements. Sources specify Location/Link/duplicate/ malformed/Unicode/budget cases, cached filtering/keyboard wrap, profile bindings, capability negotiation, caller identity/epoch, unrelated edits, source edit/close/ replacement/server disable, unsupported methods and late UI tickets. They are not linked or run. Actual SDK load_manifest and all 226 operation schemas pass strict per-method outputs/provenance, caller guards, bounds/invalid forms, permissions, exact facade forwarding and EN/FR data. Native/server/SDK/plugin/GUI/ POSIX acceptance remains pending. See Source navigation.

Deferred-symbol regression sources extend those same existing targets: URI-only versus malformed ranges, opaque data and capability negotiation, issued/unissued indices, oversized cache entries, stable/cached replies, four-session eviction, edit/close/server-disable during resolution, changed/missing destinations, and query/selection reply isolation. MSVC /Zs passes the eight affected production sources and final seven core/UI/regression sources; no fixture is linked/run. The actual installed SDK loader/all 223 operation schemas pass complete versus pending symbol shapes, session/index budgets, invalid forms, permissions, exact native facade forwarding and EN/FR data. Actual server timing, TTL/cache, keyboard/ GUI/SDK/plugin and POSIX acceptance remains pending. See Symbol navigation.

Symbol/structure regressions extend existing semantic, module and language lifecycle fixtures without a new executable target. MSVC /Zs passes 13 affected core/UI/model/fixture sources plus a final four-source cache/sort check. Sources specify hierarchy/flat/malformed/duplicate results, bounds, UTF-16, ancestor filtering/order, precise document lifetime, unrelated edits and late query/panel replies. The real SDK loader/all 222 schemas check expanded output/input forms, invalid cases, unchanged permissions, exact forwarding and EN/FR labels. Fixtures are neither linked nor run. Real server timing/SDK/plugin/GUI/docking/ keyboard/Unicode/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending under the Kaspersky suspension. See Symbol navigation.

Diagnostics/source-link regression sources extend existing build, module and language lifecycle fixtures. MSVC /Zs checks 17 affected sources, without linking or executing those fixtures. The actual SDK loader/all schemas validate 222 operations, build_location forms/control-byte rejection/read classification and identity-bearing language status. Production builds keep BUILD_TESTING=OFF. Actual parser/filesystem execution, worker timing, SDK/plugin/GUI keyboard/focus, Unicode/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS checks remain pending under the Kaspersky suspension. See Compiler locations and Diagnostics.

Three project-output/navigation milestones extend existing build/project/module fixtures without new executable targets. Sources specify shared journal context/ revision/ID reuse, fragmented/oversized Cargo protocol records, plain text repair, read-only status/output with dirty buffers, active cancellation ownership, filtered wrapping/file anchors and Rider/Visual Studio/VS Code bindings. They pass MSVC /Zs only and are neither linked nor run. Actual SDK loader/all schemas check 222 operations, contextual report shapes, permission/mutation-group isolation, pure bridge read classification and EN/FR labels. Real process, keyboard, SDK/plugin, GUI/themes/DPI/concurrency and POSIX acceptance remain pending under the Kaspersky suspension. See Project output and Diagnostics.

Live build output extends the existing opt-in build fixture without a new target. Sources specify ID/revision/reused-ID boundaries, thread/token/nested isolation, retention/byte counts, control/UTF-8 repair, cancellation/failure retention, late callback rejection and CMake pipe integration. Sources pass MSVC /Zs only; no fixture is built or executed during the Kaspersky suspension. Actual SDK loader/ all schemas validate 219 operations, including idle/live/conditional/overflow/error report forms, permissions/no mutation group, pure bridge data and EN/FR labels. Real process/SDK/plugin/GUI/POSIX acceptance remains pending; see Live build output.

Unreal artifact assertions extend the existing solution test target without a new executable. Sources specify missing/matching Editor receipts, actual target type/configuration/project/BuildId checks, manifest-listed file absence, mismatched plugin IDs, invalid filename/path variables/escapes, metadata limits, content-only scope and unsupported platforms. Continuation assertions reject missing/unready assessments. These are MSVC /Zs source checks only: do not generate their metadata binary placeholders or execute fixtures during the Kaspersky suspension. The actual SDK loader/all 218 schemas and pure bridge data validate report forms, bounds, outcome uncertainty, permissions/reservation, ABI2 and localized controls. Production remains BUILD_TESTING=OFF; actual build/load/GUI/POSIX acceptance is pending.

The existing extension fixture also specifies host read access and denied document/ refactoring writes for project inspect, artifacts, launchProfile and automationPlan callbacks. Its sources are MSVC /Zs checked only; no DLL fixture is built or loaded.

The same opt-in solution fixture now specifies bound-profile persistence/reload, explicit detachment, invalid program/runtime/request rejection, captured successful continuation and failures for changed draft/saved profile/build ID/context, cancelled/ timed-out/truncated/uncertain builds and document revisions/identity/conflicts. Additional clean opens are allowed. These assertions are MSVC /Zs checked only, not executed. The actual SDK loader/all schemas also check nested binding payloads, legacy/null profiles and required prepared bindings. Production remains tests OFF; actual build/debug/persistence/cancellation/GUI and POSIX acceptance is pending.

Unreal launch extends the existing solution test target with pure mode/argv/ listen/map/port/dimension/configuration assertions, metadata-only editor/map fixtures, content-only/missing-target checks and debug-profile stale-save guards. These source assertions are syntax-checked, not executed. Do not run them or create their empty binary placeholders during the current Kaspersky suspension. Use production BUILD_TESTING=OFF and the real SDK loader/schema checks without Runtime. Actual editor/game/server/debug/GUI/DPI/keyboard and POSIX acceptance remains pending; see Unreal launch.

Unreal automation extends the existing opt-in solution fixture, without another test target. Twelve distinct native model/service/UI/build/plugin/integration/ fixture sources pass MSVC /Zs, with final targeted host/DPI/outcome/ownership checks. Source assertions specify typed phases/maps/containers/deadlines, nonwriting preview, cancellation before dispatch, stale rules and occupied-output preservation; these assertions have not run. Real CyToolsCore loader/all Draft 2020-12 schemas pass for 218 operations, including two new automation contracts, guards, bounds, uncertain outcomes, permissions/groups, cancellable build owner/ bridge, ABI2 exports, bundled provider and EN/FR controls. Production builds keep BUILD_TESTING=OFF. Actual UAT/UBT/cook/package/commandlet, tool trees/caches/logs/ artifacts/cancellation/concurrency, SDK Runtime/plugin/GUI/themes/DPI and Linux/ macOS remain unverified during the Kaspersky suspension. See Unreal automation.

Single-commit cherry-pick/revert extends the existing VCS fixture target without another executable target. Ten distinct model/service/UI/integration/fixture sources pass MSVC /Zs, with a targeted final metadata guard check. Source assertions specify invalid IDs/options, stale/open-document guards, default hook suppression, real cherry-pick/revert outcomes, resolved continuation and dirty-buffer/index/ disk preservation on quit. These native assertions have not run. Actual SDK loader/all Draft 2020-12 schemas pass for 214 operations, including three new replay contracts, action/ID/guard rules, bounds/blockers, uncertain results, permissions/groups, noncancellable ownership, 1,200-second wait, typed adapter, three ABI2 exports and EN/FR controls. Actual Git/tools/receipt/filesystem/ concurrency/SDK Runtime/plugin/GUI/themes/DPI/POSIX acceptance remains pending during the Kaspersky suspension; see Git replay.

Merge completion/quit extends the existing opt-in VCS target, without another executable target. Ten distinct native model/service/UI/integration/fixture sources pass MSVC /Zs; targeted final checks cover raw commit parsing, exact-limit messages and intent-to-add blocking. Fixture assertions specify stale metadata/ index rejection, dirty-buffer/index/disk preservation on quit, metadata guards, hook failure/default suppression and actual commit parents/tree/index outcomes. They have not run. Actual CyToolsCore loader/all Draft 2020-12 schemas pass for 211 operations, including four merge contracts, guards, limits, action/message/ hooks rules, permissions/groups, noncancellable ownership, typed adapter, four ABI2 exports and EN/FR controls. Production Windows builds keep BUILD_TESTING=OFF. Real Git/hooks/receipt/filesystem/concurrency, SDK Runtime/plugin/GUI/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending during the existing Kaspersky suspension; see Merge workflow.

Working-file synchronization extends the existing VCS/resource fixtures, without another executable target. Fourteen distinct C++ sources pass MSVC /Zs: binary file primitives, Resources/Engine/VCS owner, UI/plugin integration and two fixture sources. Assertions specify exact binary installation, retained original/newer bytes, creation/deletion Undo, closed managed metadata, stale index/file guards, generic-API bypass refusal and exclusive-create refusal. These assertions have not run. Actual SDK loader/all Draft 2020-12 schemas pass for 207 operations, including three working-file contracts, bounded data/effects, permissions/groups, noncancellable ownership, typed adapter, three ABI2 exports and EN/FR controls. Runtime filesystem/Git/SDK/plugin/GUI/themes/DPI/POSIX acceptance remains pending during the Kaspersky suspension; see Git working files.

Structural Git conflict work extends the existing opt-in VCS target with a source fixture, without another executable target. Ten distinct C++ model/service/UI/ integration/fixture sources pass MSVC /Zs; no test objects/DLLs/EXEs are built or launched. Assertions specify complete/malformed NUL records, SHA-1/SHA-256/modes, path ambiguity, absent sides, stale previews, binary/modify-delete/rename-rename groups, unrelated staged data and dirty-buffer/file preservation. These native assertions have not run. Actual CyToolsCore load_manifest and all Draft 2020-12 schemas pass for 204 operations, including four conflict contracts, effects, permissions/groups, noncancellable ownership, typed adapter and EN/FR controls. Runtime Git/hooks/transport/index/filesystem/concurrency, SDK/plugin/GUI and POSIX acceptance remain pending; see Git conflicts.

Three Git milestones extend the existing workspace-session and VCS fixture sources, without another test target. MSVC /Zs checks fourteen distinct model/service/UI/ plugin/test sources. Assertions specify optional legacy-compatible Git session selection, automatic/root/identity/path guards, maintenance request boundaries, read-only preview, stale token/parent identities, occupied/open destinations, staged/untracked/ignored retention, manual relocation, orphan/external/sibling refusal and actual index/link outcomes. Final native bounds/service/UI checks pass separately. No native assertion, test object/DLL/EXE or Git fixture was run/built. Data-only examples use the actual SDK loader and all Draft 2020-12 schemas for 200 operations, including the three new typed contracts, observed guards/effects, bounds, permissions/groups, noncancellable ownership, pure adapter, eight ABI2 exports and EN/FR controls. Runtime/real Git/session/GUI/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain unexecuted during the Kaspersky suspension.

Submodule URL/tracking-branch settings extend the existing pure and Git fixture sources with shared address validation, branch/default/dot argv, ordered unrelated configuration/duplicate records, staged/unstaged retention, stale parent branch/ preview, normal flags, open metadata, local overrides, redacted unsupported values and real URL/branch/default postconditions. Ten sources pass MSVC /Zs, with final service/UI/fixture checks repeated after changes. These assertions were not run. Data-only checks through the actual SDK loader accept all 197 operations and validate request/output/guard/effect/bound schemas, ownership, permissions, pure parameter adaptation, ABI2 exports and English/French controls. No SDK Runtime, native fixture/config mutation or GUI was launched. Runtime/concurrency and themes/keyboard/DPI/Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending during the Kaspersky suspension; see Git submodules.

Submodule deinitialization extends the existing pure/VCS fixture sources rather than creating a test executable. MSVC /Zs checks ten model/service/UI/plugin/test sources. Assertions specify fixed quiet/no-force argv, complete normal index flags, conflicts/nested gitlinks, stale preview, ignored/untracked/hidden files, open native documents, unrecorded child commits and actual retention/removal. No fixture or native assertion was run. Data-only checks through the actual SDK loader validate all 195 operations, preview/apply schemas, effects/guards/bounds, permissions, ownership, real pure parameter adapter, plugin exports and EN/FR controls. Git removal and filesystem concurrency, SDK Runtime, GUI/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending during the Kaspersky suspension.

Submodule addition extends the existing pure and Git repository fixture sources. Assertions specify normalized fixed argv, address/name/branch bounds, read-only previews, stale preview/parent branch/directory rejection, tracked-but-absent and orphan metadata destinations, config-name reuse, hidden .gitmodules edits and open-document guards. They are MSVC /Zs compilation checks only; no fixture was run, no clone was attempted and no native test objects/DLL/executable were built. Actual SDK loader/schema data checks accept 193 operations, typed local previews with unresolved remote commit, required observed guards, real pure parameter adaptation, permissions/cancellation and translated controls. Git/network/index/ filesystem/concurrency, SDK/plugin Runtime, GUI and platform acceptance remain unexecuted; see Git submodules.

Submodule parser/argv assertions join the existing VCS test target through git_submodule_tests.cpp. They specify NUL/Unicode/newline records, SHA formats, conflict stages, duplicate/path/count limits and exact single-module init/sync/ checkout arguments without force/recursive/custom modes. MSVC /Zs covers native, UI/routing/plugin and regression sources without building or executing tests. The real SDK loader/schema data checks accept 191 operations, typed catalogue/ process states, required observed guards, permissions, cancellation metadata, translated controls and the actual pure Git parameter adapter. Real Git operations, filesystem/transport guards, external races, SDK/plugin Runtime, GUI and other OSes remain unexecuted; see Git submodules.

Run-to-cursor assertions join the existing debugger target through run_to_cursor_tests.cpp; command-profile and captured document/context assertions extend commands_tests/module_tests. MSVC /Zs passed sixteen distinct core/UI/test sources and the final Debugger/CommandUI adjustments without building test objects, DLLs or executables. Cases specify original breakpoint preservation, disabled wire mapping, destination collisions, bounds, guards, actual verification/hit IDs, deferred events, stop ordering and uncertain restoration. The actual SDK loader/ schema data checks accept 187 operations, mandatory source/context fields, typed lease/repair outcomes, permissions, noncancellable metadata and translated controls. Actual native assertions, transport races/late replies, disk/source/binary changes, adapter cleanup, SDK/plugin Runtime, GUI and platform acceptance remain unexecuted; see Run to cursor.

Set-next-statement assertions join the existing debugger target through goto_target_tests.cpp, with captured-option/context assertions in module_tests. MSVC /Zs covers seventeen native/UI/test sources and produces no test object, fixture DLL or test executable. Existing step-in and execution-epoch assertions also compile against the common DebugTargets implementation. Actual SDK loader/ schema data checks accept 185 operations and typed selected-source/goto/pending states, bounds, permissions, noncancellable execution and translated controls. VM moves, event/deadline behavior, SDK/plugin runtime and keyboard/graphical/ multiplatform acceptance remain unexecuted; see Set next statement.

Targeted step-in adds step_in_target_tests.cpp to the existing debugger target and captured-handle/frame/options assertions to module_tests.cpp. MSVC /Zs checks fifteen native/UI/test sources without linking or running tests; the final Debugger/UI/target assertions were checked again after the last adjustments. Actual SDK loader/schema examples validate 183 operations, typed catalogues and targeted acknowledgements, explicit guards, bounds, legacy field isolation, process-only permissions, noncancellable execution and translated controls. Context equality, target lifecycle and event behavior are native assertions, not an executed schema guarantee. Real adapters, SDK/plugin runtime and graphical/ multiplatform acceptance remain pending; see Targeted step-in.

Instruction breakpoint assertions join the existing debugger target through instruction_breakpoint_tests.cpp. Common verification/data contracts and module draft assertions are checked with /Zs only. No native assertions, fixtures, test objects/DLLs/executables, SDK Runtime or GUI are executed. Actual SDK loader/ schema data checks cover 181 operations and typed instruction states, guards, bounds, permissions, noncancellable metadata and English/French labels. Actual adapter/concurrency/graphical/platform acceptance remains pending; see Instruction breakpoints.

Advanced execution adds debug_execution_tests.cpp to the existing debugger target, and context/option capture assertions to module_tests.cpp. They are /Zs source checks only, with no generated test object/DLL/executable or fixture execution. Cases cover legacy wire defaults, capabilities, guard/frame mismatches, restart hints, options, bounds, actual thread reports and immediate-stop ordering. Actual SDK data/schema checks cover all 180 operations and the new contracts. Backend record/reverse/restart, thread scheduling, SDK/plugin runtime, GUI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending; see Execution controls.

Value/expression/memory mutation contracts add debug_mutation_tests.cpp to the existing debugger target. MSVC /Zs checks its assertions without objects or native execution: capability/context/frame bounds, readOnly preference, exact wire bytes, base64 padding, missing/partial counts, response and hex limits. Actual CyToolsCore loader/schema examples validate 177 operations, typed lastMutation states, permissions/noncancellable handlers and English/French labels. Target execution, adapter errors/late events, memory protection/concurrency and GUI acceptance remain suspended; see Value and memory editing.

JDWP endpoint/payload/PID routing/persistence assertions extend existing debugger sources, and typed Java attach draft assertions extend module_tests.cpp. The Unreal extension's native catalogue expectation includes both built-in adapters. These receive /Zs syntax checks only, without new test objects/DLLs/executables, network connections, DNS lookup, SDK Runtime, fixtures or GUI execution. Real SDK loader/schema examples cover bounds, legacy/default profiles and isolation of the PID-only schema branch. See Java debugging.

Java launch option/capability/wire-argument assertions extend the existing debug_inspection_tests.cpp and adapter catalogue/revocation assertions extend debug_tests.cpp. No additional test executable was introduced. Current checks are MSVC /Zs only: no assertions, JVM/JDT LS, debugger socket or GUI run. Real CyToolsCore loader/schema examples validate all 170 operations and Java profile/ project outputs without Runtime/worker execution. See Java debugging.

Ordinary builds compile CyCode, its CLI and bundled plugins with BUILD_TESTING=OFF. They do not compile native test executables or run CTest. A fresh direct CMake configuration also defaults to tests off. Existing CMake caches retain explicit user choices; pass -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF when reusing an old cache directly. The build script always sets this option explicitly.

For routine source verification:

sh
python app/scripts/verify_sources.pypython app/scripts/build.py --plan --no-install

The first command parses Python syntax and JSON source data without importing project modules, generating executables, launching native tools or downloading dependencies. It does not check C++ compilation or application behavior. The second prints the planned commands without running them or fetching dependencies.

To compile the application without copying over the root executable:

sh
python app/scripts/build.py --no-install

The usual source/dependency/tool setup still applies; this is a real C++ build. It does not open the application. --core-only limits it to the core/CLI/plugins.

Explicit native validation#

The following commands deliberately create native test executables and fixture libraries. Some suites compile and execute generated C/C++/.NET/Rust/Java projects, load plugin DLLs, start language servers, spawn child processes or debug programs. They must not run as a side effect of compiling or checking source files.

sh
# Compile native tests, without executing them or replacing the root app.python app/scripts/build.py --build-tests# Compile and execute the suite, serially; stop at the first failure.python app/scripts/build.py --run-tests# Core/CLI version, without CyUI.python app/scripts/build.py --core-only --run-tests# Filter execution; compilation still builds the native suite.python app/scripts/build.py --run-tests --test-filter "^(commands|completion_defaults)$"

Normal build caches use runtime/build[-vs] or runtime/core-build[-vs]. Test caches use runtime/tests-build[-vs] or runtime/tests-core-build[-vs]. Test builds never copy an executable to the project root. The runner sets TEMP, TMP and TMPDIR to runtime/test-workspaces/native or core, so suites that use the system temporary-directory API keep owned fixtures in an identifiable project directory. Suites with explicit data/validation fixtures retain them. There is no antivirus exclusion for these directories.

The PowerShell wrapper exposes -BuildTests, -RunTests, -TestFilter, -NoInstall and -Plan with the same behavior. CI opts into core native validation explicitly; the configured matrix has not been run on GitHub locally.

The MCP unittest suite and verify_*.py desktop/build/debugger scripts are separate integration checks. They can also launch native executables or compile fixtures. They are not part of the source-only check or ordinary build. Choose them explicitly when the relevant environment is ready. Desktop acceptance must use hidden windows and preserve any instance the user already has open.

Antivirus interruption#

Kaspersky has been reported deleting native test executables on this workstation. The detection name/report has not been inspected, so no false-positive diagnosis is established. Local native validation is currently suspended. Source checks remain available; do not treat them as a substitute for pending runtime validation.

On deletion or launch failure, stop the run and keep the build/test log. Do not loop on recompilation, restore quarantined executables, disable protection or add folder-wide exclusions. Inspect the antivirus report for the exact file and detection first. The build runner does not retry a failed test run. Its separate build and execution options permit reviewing generated files before any launch. An unsigned executable can still be detected when explicitly built or run; this workflow does not promise to change the antivirus verdict.

See Validation for results and pending failures.

Ordinary builds compile CyCode, its CLI and bundled plugins with BUILD_TESTING=OFF . They do not compile native test executables or run CTest. The build script always sets this option explicitly. It does not check C++ compilation or application behavior. The second prints the planned commands without running them or fetching dependencies. To compile the application without copying over the root executable: sh Copy python app/scripts/build.py --no-install The usual source/dependency/tool setup still applies; this is a real C++ build. It does not open the application. --core-only limits it to the core/CLI/plugins. Explicit native validation # The following commands deliberately create native test executables and fixture libraries. Some suites compile and execute generated C/C++/.NET/Rust/Java projects, load plugin DLLs, start language servers, spawn child processes or debug programs. CI opts into core native validation explicitly; the configured matrix has not been run on GitHub locally. Desktop acceptance must use hidden windows and preserve any instance the user already has open. pages.title: Solutions and Unreal Engine
pages.html:
Solutions and Unreal Engine#

The reviewed cook/package workflow now has typed maps/container controls, per-attempt staging/archive/logs and shared cancellable native/UI/SDK/ABI2 execution. Actual Unreal acceptance remains pending during the Kaspersky suspension; see Unreal automation.

Use File > Open solution (Ctrl+O) to select a .sln or .uproject. A path can also be passed as the first argument, with --workspace, or dropped onto the application. File > New window launches an independent process; Open solution in new window selects another project without switching the current workspace.

Opening a solution inspects project declarations, solution folders, solution items, configurations and nested hierarchy. UTF-8/BOM and UTF-16 solutions are accepted. Missing generated projects are marked; the workspace file tree provides the actual sources. Solution inspection does not evaluate MSBuild. For an Unreal project, normal desktop opening prepares its code analysis automatically as described below. External references have a context menu to open a separate instance; they do not widen the current workspace's document/MCP permissions. General Visual Studio solutions can be inspected, edited and built through the shared MSBuild adapter.

An Unreal .uproject opens directly, including when no .sln exists. A matching .uproject beside a selected .sln is detected. A directory containing one Unreal project can also be opened; ambiguous projects require selecting the intended .uproject. Target.cs, module Build.cs rules, local .uplugin descriptors and declared modules/plugins appear in the Unreal Engine panel.

The engine is found using CYCODE_UNREAL_ENGINE, registered EngineAssociation installations, or engine references in the solution. The panel also accepts an explicit engine directory. Detection reads Build.version without installing or downloading an engine. Select a matching engine with a built UnrealBuildTool, its .NET runtime and the target platform SDK/toolchain.

Native commands#

All operations share native services between the UI, CLI and CyToolsCore/MCP:

Operation Action
unreal.inspect / unreal_inspect Read project, engine, targets, modules, plugins and analysis status
unreal.generate / unreal_generate Generate project files with UBT -ProjectFiles -Game; refresh the solution tree
unreal.database / unreal_database Run UBT -Mode=GenerateClangDatabase -ExecCodeGenActions into a managed analysis directory
unreal.prepare / unreal_prepare Prepare UHT/analysis automatically, or reuse a matching validated cache
unreal.build / unreal_build Build the selected target/platform/configuration with UBT
unreal.automationPlan / unreal_automation_plan Preview one typed UE5 cook/package action and managed output context
unreal.automationRun / unreal_automation_run Execute its issued preview once through the shared cancellable build owner

Native names use dots; MCP names are prefixed with op_ and use underscore IDs. Inputs are project, engineRoot, target, platform and configuration. Inspect needs no process permission. Generation, preparation, indexing and compilation execute trusted Unreal C# rules and require process.execute in MCP.

UBT receives separate argv entries and runs from Engine/Source. The bundled .NET runtime is preferred. No shell command is assembled from project names. A discovered Editor target and host platform are selected by default. Configurations are Debug, DebugGame, Development, Shipping and Test; platform choices require the corresponding Unreal SDK. Output is bounded to 8 MiB and operations currently have a 180-second default deadline. The native build service supports explicit cancellation and 1..86400-second deadlines; see Build cancellation. Automation has a separately reviewed 3600-second default. Streaming remains future work.

Successful operations persist .cycode/unreal.json. Project generation writes the usual Unreal Intermediate/solution files. Analysis preparation runs UHT/code generators without a full C++ build and writes compile_commands.json under .cycode/unreal-analysis/TARGET/PLATFORM/CONFIGURATION. It preserves an existing root database and starts/reloads shared clangd with the selected database. A matching cache is reused after checking rule/header inputs, source paths, generated headers and response files. Cache misses force UHT header generation so individually missing headers are recreated despite otherwise current UBT timestamps. UBT also owns its normal engine/user caches and logs. Inspection and capture mode remain read-only; normal Unreal desktop opening performs preparation in the background.

Correct Unreal analysis requires engine include paths/macros and generated UHT headers. Preparation supplies these automatically; failures are reported in Build, with a retry in the Unreal panel. Unreal macros/types also have a small local completion catalogue while analysis is starting. Engine members and project symbols come from clangd. Assets are listed but are not text editors. Blueprint analysis, Unreal Editor automation, Live Coding, richer cooking/packaging, Unreal debugging and asset-aware refactoring are pending. C++ definition/reference navigation can open registered Engine/Source and Engine/Plugins sources in read-only tabs. Semantic C++ rename previews references across project files; it does not update serialized Unreal names or Blueprint assets. C# rules have syntax colouring, not a Roslyn project service.

Validation#

Windows x64 / installed Unreal 5.3 was executed: actual project-file generation, Editor-target compilation to a module DLL, UHT generation for a USTRUCT/UPROPERTY, UBT compile_commands.json and a clangd definition into the struct's header. The user's CyTrace_Plugin .sln/.uproject was inspected/rendered read-only; compilation used a separate CyCode-owned project. Other engine versions and Linux/macOS execution remain unverified.

Use the private Python runtime:

text
python app/scripts/verify_unreal.py --engine ABSOLUTE_ENGINE_ROOTpython app/scripts/verify_unreal_completion.py --engine ABSOLUTE_ENGINE_ROOTpython app/scripts/verify_unreal_navigation.pypython app/scripts/verify_windows.py

The first script writes its owned fixture under data/validation, apart from normal UBT caches/logs. It never builds the user's existing project. Reports are under data/reports. Native tests cover solution hierarchy/configurations, missing/external projects, UTF-16, cycles and workspace confinement. MCP tests verify discovery and rejection of process actions by a read-only client. After generating the owned completion fixture, verify_unreal_navigation.py checks that AActor opens Engine/Source/Runtime/Engine/Classes/GameFramework/Actor.h as a read-only SDK tab, leaving the fixture's source on disk unchanged.

References: Epic project file generation, Epic code/project management, Microsoft solution format.

pages.title: Unreal Editor output inspection
pages.html:
Unreal Editor output inspection#

The Unreal build outputs section of Unreal Engine inspects build metadata and file presence without executing UBT, starting an editor or loading a binary. Choose the bound launch profile or current Unreal settings, then inspect. The last result shows its actual target/platform/configuration; changing the controls does not turn that observation into a fresh check. File lists are virtualized and scroll horizontally. Copying the report is explicit.

unreal_artifacts / native unreal.artifacts expose the same read-only service to SDK/ABI2. Bundled Unreal provider 1.5.0 advertises artifacts; ABI remains 2. No permission or workspace-mutation group is required for this metadata query. Its 64 MiB SDK memory reservation does not cap the whole IDE or external tool memory.

Assessment scope#

The supported ordinary layout is a modular UE4/UE5 desktop Editor target using Development or DebugGame. Selected engine/project directories come from the existing native inspector. The artifact pass then checks:

  • A nonempty selected editor executable and shared engine .modules BuildId. DebugGame uses the engine's shared Development module manifest and the configuration-specific editor executable.
  • A project .target receipt for projects declaring modules or having Source-owned module rules. TargetType must be Editor, and target name, platform, configuration, project reference, BuildId and optional launch path must match. The target filename alone is not proof of target type.
  • The project's root module manifest, plus project-owned .modules files listed by the receipt. This includes receipt-listed project plugin manifests. Their BuildIds must match the selected engine; their module filenames must be plain filenames and refer to nonempty regular files.
  • Nonempty project-owned receipt products of type DynamicLibrary or Executable. Engine build-product inventories, symbols and other resources are excluded.

Content-only projects do not require a project code receipt or root module manifest. This assessment does not resolve project/plugin activation, target or module descriptor filters, external/unlisted plugin directories, transitive dependencies or the complete installed engine. In particular, an unlisted content-only project's code plugin is outside this assessment. Receipt-listed project plugin outputs are checked without guessing plugin enablement.

The service does not load or validate PE/ELF/Mach-O, architecture, ABI, PDB/symbol quality, package installation or source freshness. Matching IDs and file presence do not prove successful module loading or compilation against the latest closed source files. Engine/module IDs are never rewritten to make a mismatch disappear.

Custom monolithic editors, architecture-suffixed receipts/manifests and other nonstandard layouts need an adapter; missing/unknown evidence remains unverified. The existing explicit detachment/manual profile workflow remains available and leaves final module acceptance to Unreal. No new parallel engine implementation or copied Epic code is introduced.

Bounds and results#

The artifact pass reads at most 4 MiB per metadata file, 16 MiB in aggregate, 256 metadata files and 8192 receipt products, and records up to 4096 entries and 128 issues. Its cooperative five-second budget is checked between filesystem work; it cannot interrupt an OS filesystem call. Initial workspace/engine discovery continues to use the existing inspector and its separate bounds. Large metadata, unknown path variables, escaping canonical paths, malformed data, metadata changes during reading and exhausted budgets produce an incomplete assessment. Only $(EngineDir) (the installation's Engine directory) and $(ProjectDir) receipt roots are expanded; no shell or environment expansion is involved.

Responses contain supported, complete, ready, receiptRequired, profile, receipt/engine-manifest summaries, product/manifest/module lists, issues and an observation revision. Ready means supported + complete + no detected issue in this scope. Missing/incompatible files can be a complete negative assessment; parse/limit/race failures are incomplete. The revision fingerprints the report, not file contents, and is not an issued execution permit or frozen snapshot.

Build and launch behavior#

Native unreal.build retains its actual process exit/output/cancel/timeout data and adds an artifact assessment after inspection. A failed postflight/profile save is reported through inspectionError, retaining process data and marking the project unavailable when necessary. Preparation/index consumers handle that uncertainty instead of treating an unavailable project as a configured model. A zero process exit remains distinct from artifact readiness.

Desktop compilation-before-debug requires a complete, ready artifact assessment for the matching bound profile before continuing. Native bound debug.run and debug.launch recheck current artifact metadata/files before starting a terminal or DAP launch; SDK and plugin callers use the same owner. Configure remains possible before the first project compilation. Attach-by-PID is unchanged. Existing profile/draft/build/document guards, process ownership and cancellation remain in force. This does not make build/check/launch one atomic transaction: files can change after inspection, and Unreal remains the runtime authority.

Windows production compilation, MSVC /Zs and actual SDK schema validation are performed locally. Native fixture assertions, actual Unreal build/module loading, filesystem races, GUI/keyboard/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS execution remain unverified during the current Kaspersky suspension. No test/editor process is launched for this milestone.

Metadata semantics were read from installed UE 5.3 TargetReceipt, ModuleManifest and WriteMetadataMode sources and receipt examples, alongside Epic's primary BuildID documentation. Epic engine sources/binaries are not copied or distributed by this addition.

pages.title: Reviewed Unreal cooking and packaging
pages.html:
Reviewed Unreal cooking and packaging#

Unreal Engine > Cook and package Unreal content adds cook-only and build/cook/stage/package/archive actions. Desktop, CyTools/MCP and ABI2 plugins share the native Unreal owner and existing cancellable build service. The packaged game is not launched by the submitted command.

Configure and review#

Open the actual .uproject/solution and select the matching installed Unreal Engine 5. Automation requires its precompiled AutomationTool and editor commandlet binary, a discoverable .NET host and a project Target.cs entry for the requested game target. Names ending in Editor are rejected. Rule evaluation, actual target type, supported SDKs and engine/project compatibility are assessed by Unreal when the command runs; the planner does not execute C# to infer them. Blueprint-only projects without project target rules and mobile/server/console workflows remain outside this initial service.

Choose Cook content or Package and archive, a game target, platform and configuration. Platform/configuration reuse the Unreal controls above the new section. Desktop choices are Win64, Linux, LinuxArm64 and Mac; availability still requires an appropriate engine/toolchain. Select whether to build game code. Packaging exposes Pak, IoStore and compression; IoStore/compression require Pak. Unchecked IoStore/compression produce explicit skipiostore/ForceUncompressed arguments so project defaults do not silently enable those requests. Unreal's platform/package rules remain authoritative for the resulting container layout.

Enter one existing /Game/Folder/Map package per line without .umap. Empty uses the project's packaging defaults. There are at most 64 names, 512 UTF-8 bytes each, and an 8,000-byte combined map argument budget. Options, plus separators, URLs, relative traversal, object/file extensions and duplicate/case-ambiguous names are refused. Explicit plugin/Engine map mounts are not mapped by this initial selector.

Preview Unreal automation resolves canonical project/engine paths and shows the exact argv, cwd and managed output/archive locations. No tool is executed and no output directory is created. Native previews are per Engine instance, capped at 16 and valid for ten minutes. Cancel automation preview drops the desktop review; native unused entries expire. Reopening a core loses its issued previews.

The deadline is 1..86,400 seconds, default 3,600. Run must supply exactly the value reviewed with the plan. Changing controls invalidates the desktop preview. Late preview replies for changed controls are discarded.

Run, cancellation and retained files#

Run reviewed Unreal automation requires the issued planId/revision and saved, reconciled workspace documents. Native preflight rechecks descriptor/target rule content, explicit map file stamps, engine version, tool/editor stamps, workspace/engine directory identities and output vacancy. Binary/map stamps use path/size/modification metadata; they are not executable signatures or complete content hashes. This is an argument/context review, not a frozen snapshot of all sources, assets, configuration or caches. Builds use current project inputs.

The adapter starts the selected precompiled AutomationTool directly through its resolved .NET host/apphost with separate argv entries. It reuses the existing Unreal managed-tool discovery; legacy and newer host platform folder aliases are recognized. It does not copy the engine's batch scripts or build UAT itself. Missing precompiled tools must be built/installed through Unreal first. Runtime environment includes the selected .NET root/host and the managed UAT log folder.

The command requests BuildCookRun, unattended UTF-8 output and no Perforce/editor compilation. Package adds stage/package/archive, explicit staging/archive paths and reviewed container options. It does not request clean, deploy, run, upload or SDK installation. Project rules, custom scripts, native tools and packaging settings remain trusted executable code; signing/encryption or external effects configured by them are not sandboxed away. Ordinary Unreal Intermediate, Saved, cook/build/DDC and engine/user caches can change.

Each attempt reserves a new .cycode/unreal-automation/uat-... directory through exclusive creation. Existing managed output is never deleted or reused. Packaging staging/archive live below that directory; cook uses Unreal's normal project cooked-data paths. The same directory retains:

  • intent.json: the reviewed plan before dispatch, not proof of completion;
  • output.log: up to 8 MiB of raw captured process output;
  • logs/: UAT's own logs, whose sizes and additional engine/child log locations remain controlled by Unreal;
  • result.json: the adapter's actual process/postflight result when writable;
  • stage/ and archive/ for package actions, including partial results on failure.

The preview permits one execution attempt after preflight. Errors, cancellation, timeouts and truncated output do not delete artifacts or automatically retry. Build > Cancel build, the palette, build_status/cancel and SDK cancellation use the existing correlated operation ID and owned process tree. The reservation stays held until native work stops. Late owner/SDK cancellation can augment the returned job status after the adapter result was recorded; inspect the job as well as the retained files. Inspect/preview fail busy rather than waiting behind a long Unreal operation. No cross-instance/global project freeze is claimed.

Copy automation output path and Open automation log expose the retained results. They are persistent workspace data, not temporary SDK task artifacts; SDK session cleanup does not own or remove them. There is no automatic editor Undo/rollback, distribution, package launch or deletion workflow.

Actual outcomes and contracts#

The result retains exitCode/output/timedOut/truncated/cancelled. Invalid or cut UTF-8 in the returned text is replaced with outputRepaired=true; output.log keeps the original bytes. Postflight checks managed directory identity and looks for an ordinary archive file, bounded to 2,000 entries/five seconds. A zero exit without an observed archive carries inspectionError. Observing a file does not validate the full archive, platform binary, installation or game behavior. receiptError reports failure to persist result.json without hiding the actual process status. The UI shows a warning for unconfirmed results instead of a success toast.

SDK operation Native / ABI2 host method Effect
unreal_automation_plan unreal.automationPlan Typed cook/package controls; no process/output creation
unreal_automation_run unreal.automationRun Issued planId, expectedRevision, exact timeoutSeconds; one cancellable attempt

Run requires process.execute and workspace.write, shares the SDK workspace mutation group and the native build owner, and publishes common build events. The bridge generates an operation ID, correlates build.cancel and extends its wait to the chosen deadline plus native postflight allowance. Native host permission checks also reject writes from read-only plugin callbacks. The bundled Unreal provider 1.5.0 advertises both actions with the matching permissions. No C ABI, dependency, executable target or CyUI module is added. The 256 MiB SDK reservation is for bridge/metadata work; external Unreal tool memory/disk use is project-owned and has not been measured here.

Validation and remaining scope#

Windows production compilation and MSVC /Zs, real CyToolsCore manifest loading and Draft 2020-12 schema/data validation are distinct from actual Unreal acceptance. The existing opt-in solution fixture adds pure phase/map/container/deadline cases, nonwriting preview, cancelled-before-dispatch, stale-rule rejection and occupied output retention. These native assertions have not run during the existing Kaspersky suspension; no test/native fixture process, UAT, UBT, commandlet or packaged game was launched for this milestone.

Argument/runtime setup was checked against the installed UE 5.3 primary source files RunUAT, ProjectParams and CopyBuildToStagingDirectory. Actual UE versions, tool/child process trees, logging/caches/artifacts/cancellation, SDK/plugin/GUI, keyboard/themes/DPI and Linux/macOS remain unverified. Live Coding, Unreal Editor automation, asset/Blueprint refactoring, advanced target/platform/signing/profile management, device deployment and complete package validation remain separate work.

The phase model follows Epic's build operations documentation.

pages.title: Unreal editor, game and server launch profiles
pages.html:
Unreal editor, game and server launch profiles#

The Unreal Engine panel prepares the same persistent run/debug profile used by CyCode's Debugger and native terminals. Preparation reads project/engine metadata and file existence; it does not compile, save or start anything. It supports installed UE4 and UE5 editor executables for the current host platform. Windows production compilation and schema checks are performed locally; actual Unreal launch, debug, GUI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending during the current Kaspersky suspension of native execution.

Desktop workflow#

  1. Open the .uproject or matching .sln, select its installed engine and current host platform in Unreal Engine. Choose Development or DebugGame.
  2. Expand Unreal launch profile. Select editor, standalone game or uncooked server. Game/server use the installed editor executable and uncooked content, rather than a cooked distribution executable.
  3. Optionally enter an existing map such as /Game/Maps/Main, without .umap. The file must exist below this project's Content directory. Empty uses Unreal's project default. Plugin and /Engine maps, asset object references, URLs and arbitrary console commands are outside this typed preparation.
  4. Game mode offers windowed/fullscreen resolution, and Listen server for an explicit map. Listen/server modes use the chosen port. Unreal log window is opt-in. DebugGame selects the configuration-specific editor executable (for example, UnrealEditor-Win64-DebugGame.exe); a missing variant is reported rather than launching Development. It must already be installed/built.
  5. Building before debugging requires a discovered target whose name ends in Editor, selected above. Disable this option for content-only projects. This is a name/discovery check, not execution or evaluation of Target.cs rules.
  6. Preview and inspect the executable and each literal argument. Apply with Use this Unreal launch profile. This saves .cycode/launch.json through the common debugger and opens its panel. It does not start a process.
  7. Use existing Run without debugging to start the profile in an owned native terminal without compilation, or Debug / Continue for the shared DAP service and optional build-before-debug workflow. Compilation uses the project, engine, Editor target, platform and configuration stored in the launch profile, independently of later toolbar changes. Select/install a compatible native adapter in the debugger; preparation does not install one. The bundled Unreal plugin also exposes an explicit CodeLLDB adapter entry.

The common saved profile retains its environment, watches, terminal choice and other unrelated fields when the generated patch is applied. Generated fields select the builtin native adapter and clear previous adapter arguments/options, avoiding inheritance of a Java/.NET or unrelated plugin launch configuration. The saved executable/arguments and unrealLaunch binding survive restart. The binding contains the observed Unreal profile and normalized launch request. The preparation form restores its mode/map/network/window settings from that binding. Load bound Unreal build settings explicitly restores the build controls and refreshes native inspection; it does not run a build or editor. There is still one persistent launch profile store. Top-level stopOnEntry and buildBeforeLaunch remain authoritative when changed after preparation; validation uses those current values over the stored request.

Program, working directory, arguments and native runtime stay bound while the profile is linked. Regenerate through the Unreal panel to change them, or use Detach Unreal launch settings before manual editing. This explicitly saves unrealLaunch=null when the manual profile is next applied/launched. Environment, watches, compatible adapter selection, stop-on-entry and the build preference remain editable. The native owner also rejects mismatched bound fields through MCP/plugins, before a configuration write or process dispatch. Missing engine, map, configuration-specific editor or required Editor target is reported.

Legacy/manual profiles without the binding keep their previous workflow and load with a null binding. Standalone native Debugger integrations that provide no Unreal validation callback can continue using unbound profiles; a bound profile requires the common Engine's validator before it can be saved/launched.

Previews are discarded when their Unreal inputs or manual debugger draft change. Saving compares expectedProfile with the complete current native profile before updating it. A mismatch produces DebugProfileConflict; disk baseline/atomic-save guards remain in force. Updating a watch alone does not reload and overwrite unrelated unsaved profile fields in the desktop.

Compilation before debugging#

The desktop saves/reconciles documents, captures the complete launch parameters, manual draft, observed saved profile, open workspace document identities/revisions and build operation ID, then dispatches the existing cancellable unreal.build owner with the bound five-field build context. Unreal building also rejects dirty or conflicted native workspace buffers before starting a tool.

After compilation, automatic DAP launch requires a confirmed exit zero with no cancellation, timeout, truncated output or inspection/receipt uncertainty, plus an available result whose observed Unreal profile matches the bound context. The result must also contain a complete, ready assessment of that context's ordinary Editor outputs. Actual native run/launch rechecks those outputs before dispatch, while configuring a profile remains possible before compilation. See Unreal output inspection for receipt/module/file checks, limits, content-only behavior and excluded dependency/ABI coverage. The build ID, manual draft, saved profile and captured open document identities/ revisions must still match. Dirty/conflicted documents, saved source edits during the build, or closing/reopening a captured document stop automatic launch. Opening an additional clean document does not by itself stop it. No retry is automatic.

The captured parameters, rather than newly edited fields, are sent to the shared debugger. expectedProfile is rechecked during queued configuration saving and removed before the native launch request; it is not forwarded to a DAP adapter. Run without debugging still does not compile. Existing terminal/DAP ownership, cancellation and shortcuts remain in force, including in mixed project workspaces.

These guards cover the launch/profile context and captured live documents. They are not a snapshot of every closed source file, engine binary or build input, and do not make compile/save/launch one atomic filesystem or tool transaction.

The preview generates a profile; it does not freeze execution inputs. It does not reserve binaries, maps or content, check listening port availability, validate module compatibility, or promise successful editor startup. Tools/project code can change before an actual launch.

MCP and plugins#

unreal_launch_profile maps to unreal.launchProfile in the same native Engine. Optional parameters are existing Unreal project/engine/target/platform/configuration fields plus:

Field Values/default
mode editor (default), game, server
map Empty or existing /Game/... package; same lexical validation as cook/package
listen false; true requires game mode and an explicit map
log false; requests Unreal's separate log window when enabled
windowed true for game; ignored/normalized false for editor/server
width, height 1280 × 720; width 320–16384, height 200–16384
port 7777; 1–65535, emitted for server/listen only
stopOnEntry false; used by the DAP launch
buildBeforeLaunch true; desktop build-before-debug preference

Response fields are normalized request, a settings patch, observed unrealProfile, saved expectedProfile, and explicit startsProcess=false, savesProfile=false, usesUncookedContent=true. Preparation requires process.execute, matching debug_profile, because the saved profile can include private environment variables. The desktop does not dump that snapshot into build output. The SDK workspace-mutation exclusive group is not acquired for preparation.

Send settings plus expectedProfile to debug_configure; its existing process.execute and workspace.write permissions apply. Then use debug_run or debug_launch. These SDK/native launch operations do not perform the desktop's optional compilation step: explicitly build through unreal_build and inspect its actual result first when needed.

Prepared settings now require a non-null unrealLaunch binding in their result. The ordinary debug profile/configure/launch/run schemas accept that binding or null, and retain compatibility with an absent field in legacy profiles. Both native configure and actual run/launch revalidate bound executable/cwd/argv and runtime through the Unreal owner. SDK unreal_build uses explicit parameters; SDK debug_launch/debug_run still do not compile automatically. Clients can read the persisted binding via debug_profile to coordinate their own workflow. Persist detachment through debug_configure; a null override passed only to an SDK run/launch is a one-off override, consistent with other launch fields.

ABI2 exports preparation with the same process.execute permission; read-only provider callbacks may prepare a profile but cannot save or launch it. Bundled Unreal provider 1.5.0 retains launchProfile and the common binding checks; ABI version stays 2.

Existing attach-by-PID remains in the shared debugger, with its normal detach/ termination semantics. This addition does not implement Blueprint debugging, PIE control, Live Coding, editor RPC, multiplayer session orchestration, remote client connection profiles, or packaged game/server discovery. Those need their own engine integration and runtime acceptance.

Argument semantics follow Epic's primary command-line guide and argument reference. Configuration-specific executable naming was also inspected read-only in installed UE 5.3 UBT, LaunchEngineLoop, App and ModuleManifest sources and editor filenames. No Epic source or engine binaries are copied or distributed by this addition.

pages.title: Untitled documents and Save as
pages.html:
Untitled documents and Save as#

File > New text document opens a draft without creating a source file. The existing New file dialog also offers Open unsaved, using the entered basename (for example scratch.cpp) to select the shared CyUI lexical syntax. Draft names contain no folders. Plain text is the default for the direct command. CodeEditor retains normal editing, in-document search, folding, multi-cursor and live Undo/Redo.

The native Engine owns drafts, their text, revisions and IDs. An issued reference has the form untitled://<unique-id>/<name>. It is not a filesystem path. Read, replace, close, global text search and recovery share that same native model; there is no separate Python or GUI text store. Up to 64 drafts / 64 MiB of native UTF-8 text are accepted. Individual editor text limits and recovery's shared 128-document / 128-MiB quota still apply. Empty drafts remain dirty so they are checkpointed and must be explicitly saved or discarded.

Drafts created by MCP/native plugins appear in real tabs without stealing focus. Externally closed live documents retire their GUI views. If an editor still has uncommitted local text, it is rescued into a new native draft with the same editor Undo rather than dropped; quota failures leave the local view dirty and report an error. Save dialogs for externally closed documents are dismissed.

First save and copies#

Save on a draft opens Save as. Save as also works for editable file-backed text. Enter a new workspace file in an existing folder. The native service rejects an occupied disk path or open-buffer path, an invalid source revision and paths outside the workspace. It uses the existing exclusive/atomic text writer and retains UTF-8/BOM and line-ending settings. It does not create destination folders or overwrite existing files. An OS save picker, overwrite-with-review and arbitrary external save destinations are not implemented by this workflow.

After a successful write, the document switches to the new path with its live identity retained. The old disk file remains unchanged when saving a file-backed document under another name. The UI keeps the same CodeEditor and native window key, preserving the current text Undo/Redo, and applies the saved-file syntax and existing language activation policy. Host move/save events contain metadata only. Old recovery data is retired after commit. Language-service warnings are reported separately from an already successful save.

Save all writes file-backed buffers and queues drafts for individual destinations. Cancelling Save as stops the remaining draft queue and cancels an associated close/quit request; it leaves the buffers open. Close/discard checks the observed revision before retiring a live buffer and its recovery data.

The VS Code Windows profile uses Ctrl+N for a draft, Ctrl+Shift+S for Save as and Ctrl+K, S for Save all, following the official keybinding reference. Rider retains Ctrl+N for type lookup; the new draft and Save as commands are available from File/Find Action and editable bindings. The existing New file command remains available. Full macOS keymap validation remains separate work.

Recovery and session metadata#

The existing recovery worker checkpoints drafts, including empty drafts, once per second. A process closing or crashing can leave an inactive checkpoint. View > Recovery verifies and previews it; Restore buffer reopens the same issued draft reference in memory. This operation never invents a project file. Save as is still required to persist it as source. Live target/recovery revisions are checked, and the source checkpoint is consumed only after the restored draft has a new durable checkpoint. Explicit discard removes the selected recovery data.

Workspace sessions store draft tab/window keys, cursor and approximate scroll metadata alongside the existing file tabs. Draft text remains owned by Recovery. When the user explicitly restores a draft from Recovery, its matching session coordinates and detached-window key are applied. Text is not automatically restored at startup. Complete Undo history is not serialized. Recovery data is persistent project state under .cycode/recovery, excluded from source indexing and publication, rather than an SDK temporary artifact.

Untitled documents use shared lexical coloring; file-backed language-server, semantic refactoring, filesystem/VCS and breakpoint operations require Save as first. Drafts are excluded from filesystem polling/resource operations and from recent/closed-file lists; their own recovery route handles later reopening. Project execution checks continue to concern actual project files.

Shared SDK/native plugin access and validation#

CyToolsCore exposes documents_create_untitled, documents_save_as and documents_close with workspace.write permission. Existing documents_read/replace and recovery operations accept issued references. These three short mutations are noncancellable once dispatched so cancellation is not reported after a commit. Save as and close require expectedRevision. The native ABI2 host exports the same methods with the existing permission checks; no C ABI shape or SDK runtime is duplicated. SDK draft creation/replacement also has its existing input-text bound.

Native regression sources cover no-source-file creation, revisions, refusal of overwrites, same-identity Save as, retention of the original disk file, empty-draft recovery, session validation and keymaps. They belong to the existing opt-in core test target; no new test executable is added. During the Kaspersky interruption the existing opt-in resource GUI target also gains MCP draft/view/close, local-edit rescue and Undo/window identity assertions. No new GUI runner is introduced; they are syntax checked only. Actual native/GUI acceptance, cancellation/focus, Undo across Save as, multi-window restoration, themes/DPI and Linux/macOS remain unexecuted. See Validation.
