pages.title: Resuming interrupted application downloads
pages.html:
Resuming interrupted application downloads#

The Windows x64 portable updater now keeps interrupted transfer bytes. An explicit Download or resume update action searches a bounded set of local checkpoints for the exact release asset, resumes when the HTTP response permits it, and only then creates the existing verified installation candidate. It never resumes a network transfer or installation automatically at startup.

Space checks and transfer observations#

Before creating a download work folder or opening a transfer, CyCode checks caller- available space on the installation volume. It repeats the check before creating a fresh full-download fallback and again before staging helper/catalogue files. The additional-space estimate is:

remaining archive bytes + installed helper size + 4 MiB catalogue + 64 KiB journals + 32 MiB spare

A resumed prefix is already on disk, so it is subtracted from the remaining archive amount. A full-response fallback needs the entire archive in a new folder while the earlier partial stays. Completed cached bytes still require staging headroom. The helper allowance is conservative even when a staged helper already exists. Bounds reject invalid sizes/offsets before arithmetic; totals stay within the existing 256 MiB archive / 64 MiB helper limits. Nothing is preallocated or deleted.

Windows reads 64-bit bytes available to the caller through GetDiskFreeSpaceExW, including per-user quota limits. An unavailable query stops with a storage error, rather than pretending unknown space is zero or unlimited. Known insufficient space has its own EN/FR failure guidance and retained observed/required counters. These probes run in the existing worker, not on every rendered frame.

This is a download/staging preflight, not a reservation, filesystem allocation promise or full installation/extraction/recovery budget. Other processes can consume space afterward, allocation units can add overhead and a real write can still fail. Existing write checks, guarded preparation and retained files remain necessary. No pruning, antivirus change or automatic network retry is introduced.

Each attempt has a release-bound status object: immutable target version/size, atomic phase, initial retained prefix, network-byte count, last required/available space observation and full-fallback flag. The phases distinguish preparation, receiving, SHA-256 verification, staging, verified readiness, cancellation and failure. Reaching the byte total does not offer installation until the existing complete verifier succeeds. Supplying mismatched telemetry context is refused.

The Updates view shows MiB, bytes received during this attempt, a sampled transfer rate and approximate remaining transfer seconds. Retained prefix bytes never inflate that rate. Samples update at intervals of at least half a second, smooth successive rates and drop an estimate after more than three seconds without new data. Changed/rolled-back clocks, reset counters and non-receiving phases reset the meter. Invalid bounds or estimates longer than a day remain unspecified. Hashing/staging/install time is excluded. The meter is main-thread arithmetic; drawing multiple views does not resample it or query disk/network state.

Last observations stay explicitly labelled with their own target version, even when later release checks change the current offer. The clipboard report includes these bounded numeric counters, phase and fallback flag; it still excludes URLs, credentials and raw exception text. Observations are not an atomic installation snapshot or persistent transfer history.

Explicit retry controls and feedback#

The normal Download or resume update action selects the most advanced exact matching checkpoint within the existing scan budget. Start a fresh download passes an explicit native DownloadMode::fresh: selection returns without even inspecting old checkpoints, then creates a new uniquely owned work directory. No previous partial, prepared archive or metadata is deleted or truncated. This can consume additional disk space. Both actions retain the same installation, manifest, version, lease, response, size, SHA-256 and final preparation checks. Fresh mode does not persist in preferences or become a new startup policy.

Native DownloadError carries a fixed category independently of its technical message. Access, network, invalid response, storage, integrity, busy, installation and other failures select EN/FR titles and next-step guidance through the shared UpdateFeedback policy. System filesystem exceptions are treated as storage errors; unclassified exceptions remain other. Cancellation stays neutral. No message substring matching or automatic credential lookup beyond the existing environment contract is added. Technical details are collapsed in the Updates view; they are not copied into the update report.

After an interrupted/failed attempt, the desktop schedules exactly one bounded local inspection. It never starts another transfer/check, restores installation consent or reopens an update proposal. The original error/category/cancellation notice remains visible. A failed or cancelled inspection has separate feedback; a successful scan refreshes the partial summaries and can rediscover a fully verified archive. A candidate with the same version but a digest different from the current known release is discarded. Successful preparation already has its verified candidate and does not trigger this extra inspection. Closing, smoke and test-session guards exclude new post-attempt work. Manual Refresh remains available.

The explicit copy report records whether a transfer was attempted, its requested mode, current failure code and observed progress. It includes no technical exception text, asset URLs, token values or headers. These are current in-memory observations, not persistent transfer history; existing helper outcome history remains separate.

Ownership and checkpoint#

UpdateDownload shares binding, local metadata and response validation with the existing UpdateTransfer and UpdateCache owners. There is no SDK operation, plugin ABI change, extra runtime, executable target or CyUI module. The SDK stays at 227. Native automatic transport remains Windows x64 only.

The installation must be a current portable distribution, with no development checkout or pending installation. Its managed manifest is freshly validated and the candidate must be newer than both installed and running versions. A shared installation lease prevents replacement while downloading; the shared cache lease excludes cache retirement. A fail-fast exclusive data/updates/download.lock serializes all CyCode download writers for that copy, across desktop instances. No other instance is terminated or waited on indefinitely.

Each new download-* directory starts with an atomic resume.json (format 1), binding installation, version, exact platform/name, numeric repository asset API URL, expected size and GitHub SHA-256. Neither tokens, authorization headers, redirect URLs, signed query strings nor release notes enter this record.

Discovery reads at most 128 top-level entries and five entries per partial folder. Metadata is capped at 8 KiB; archives at 256 MiB, helpers at 64 MiB and optional message catalogues at 4 MiB. Relative/foreign paths, unknown files, symlinks, reparse points, special files, hard links, oversized payloads and ambiguous archive-plus-partial states are rejected without removal. Completed prepared folders and digest-rejected checkpoints are not transfer candidates. The most advanced matching partial is selected; exhausting the scan can mean starting a new download while older bytes remain elsewhere.

The actual ordinary file size supplies the offset, rather than a trusted saved counter. The Windows writer opens without truncation, verifies native file type, link count and exact length, and prevents other writers/deletion while open. Failures and cancellation close the handle and retain received bytes. Flushing on interruption is best effort; a checkpoint does not guarantee power-loss durability or imply a verified prefix. Only the final complete digest is trusted.

HTTP response policy#

Each attempt starts again at the repository's numeric API endpoint, obtaining a new redirect when needed. Tokens remain restricted to that repository's API, and HTTPS/host/redirect/deadline/size guards remain. GitHub documents both direct streaming and redirected downloads in its release asset API. Header retrieval follows the system WinHttpQueryHeaders contract. These documents do not establish live access or range behavior for this private repository; that still needs actual network acceptance.

For an offset greater than zero, the request sends Range: bytes=OFFSET- and Accept-Encoding: identity. Before consuming any body bytes, the final response must be 206 with one exact Content-Range: bytes OFFSET-(SIZE-1)/SIZE and, when present, matching Content-Length. Encoded bodies, duplicate/malformed headers, wrong offsets/end/total, wildcards, overflow and unexpected statuses are refused. A full zero-offset 200 response is also allowed, with exact recorded size checks. Every stream is bounded to remaining bytes; EOF must produce the complete size.

A valid full 200 response to a nonzero range means the server ignored Range. CyCode consumes none of that body into the old partial. It retains the old folder, creates a new owned folder, and makes one full-download fallback attempt. This can occupy additional disk space. It does not truncate or replace the original. A network error or cancellation does not automatically loop/retry.

When all bytes are present, including a previous interruption after transfer, CyCode recomputes SHA-256 over the whole archive before renaming/staging. A digest failure retains the file and atomically marks its checkpoint rejected, so the next explicit download starts elsewhere. A correct full archive can finish staging without another network request. Existing helper/catalogue files are not blindly overwritten; changed staged helper data stops staging and rejects that checkpoint so the next explicit retry can start elsewhere. The normal prepared verifier still rechecks archive and installed/staged helper before presenting installation. Only the unchanged owned resume marker is removed after successful preparation; cleanup failure leaves a protected record. Histories, transaction backups and user files retain their existing owners.

Desktop observations and verification#

Startup and Refresh downloaded updates discover bounded partial summaries without network requests, hashing their prefixes or creating leases. At most 12 summaries are retained, separately labelled incomplete, with observed/expected byte counts and their folder paths. The copy report includes these counts/paths, not asset URLs or secrets. Failed/cancelled attempts trigger one local refresh; observations can still become stale, and manual Refresh reads them again. A release check obtains the current exact asset binding before a restarted app can offer a transfer. Download cancellation describes retained bytes, progress starts at the resumed offset, and smoke/test sessions cannot start transfers. The existing explicit install/save/close workflow is unchanged.

Thirty compiler-evaluated assertions cover production policies: nine headroom bounds/offset calculations, two multi-case meter contracts and nineteen HTTP response assertions. The latter cover: full/partial acceptance, ignored-range fallback, malformed/overlapping/incomplete ranges, size/header errors, encodings, overflow and bounds. No test executable is required for those assertions. Additional opt-in native source fixtures describe checkpoint identity, readonly observations, caller-space observation/retention, replaced asset/size/digest, unknown files, size limits, interrupted staging, rejection markers and foreign metadata. Retry follow-ups add most-advanced/exact-identity selection, fresh-mode noninspection/retention, cancelled selection and typed response errors. Injected-future GUI sources cover quiet local refresh, preserved feedback, replaced digests and cancelled/failed inspections. They are source checked only, not linked or run under the Kaspersky suspension.

Production builds and data-only packaging/source checks do not establish real WinHTTP headers, private credentials, interruption/resumption, filesystem locking, GUI/progress/cancellation or clean-machine behavior. Those acceptance checks, Linux/macOS builds and power-loss durability remain unverified. See Validation, Application updates and Update storage.

The helper now applies a separate allocation-aware extraction/pre-replacement installation budget. Download observations still do not reserve space or guarantee installation/recovery writes.

pages.title: Update history and recovery receipts
pages.html:
Update history and recovery receipts#

Application updates > Update history offers Inspect detailed update history. This explicitly runs a cancellable native metadata inspection without opening/hashing an archive or backup payload, downloading, installing, restoring or running the helper. The short startup/cache summary remains until this inspection finishes. Native/ filesystem/GUI acceptance is pending; see Validation.

Viewing a snapshot#

Twelve entries appear per page. The shared CyUI text filter searches versions, English/translated results, UTC dates, category, state, failure code and directory. Categories show all entries, those needing attention, installations or recoveries. Waiting/failed/restart- failed installations and cancelled/failed recoveries need attention. Labels/matches are cached until the query, category, locale or inspected snapshot changes; there is no per-frame filesystem probe.

Selection shows the directory and recorded recovery stage, prepared/completed counts, fresh copied bytes, installed-file moves and pending-marker removal. These are historical statements about that attempt, not the current installation. Filters, locale, page changes and successful inspection clear selection. Failed/cancelled inspection retains the previous snapshot. Ordinary cancellation and joined shutdown own the future; smoke/GUI test sessions cannot invoke real inspection. No automatic refresh, retry, network request or proposal is triggered.

Observed rows sort by recorded time descending, then stable directory identity. New recovery receipts contain informational Unix seconds. Older format-1 receipts without time sort after dated entries and show Date unavailable; filesystem times are not substituted. Recorded times do not establish trustworthy chronology. Installation history is the latest result.json per staged download, not an append- only record of every state. Recovery has one immutable result per advertised work attempt; early failure/reporting failure/process termination can leave no receipt.

Bounded native inspection#

UpdateHistory belongs to cycode_updates and reuses shared staging/outcome parsers. It accepts a Windows portable installation and reads direct download-* metadata plus direct recovery-* receipts under direct transaction-* directories. Numeric work names use the existing validator. It does not recurse through restored, replaced or backup trees, or follow paths provided by receipts. Unsafe/reparse/ symlink ancestors, nonregular/hard-linked metadata, foreign identities, malformed fields and unsupported outcomes are refused. No lock, history or cache file is created; no payload is changed.

Each snapshot visits at most 512 direct cache entries and then 128 total direct transaction children, including unrelated names in both budgets. It retains at most 128 rows and reads at most 4 MiB of history metadata. Prepared/outcome/result records are capped at 8 KiB, work identities at 64 KiB, and captured pending text at 8 KiB. The portable-mode manifest check retains its separate 2 MiB bound. Cancellation runs between bounded reads/entries; blocked filesystem calls can delay it. Changing/unreadable records can be rejected. This is an observation across different moments, not a filesystem transaction.

Enumeration is a bounded prefix. Within it, download and transaction paths have stable processing order; installation rows can exhaust the row budget first. Time sorting orders only retained rows. Pages do not fetch omitted records or guarantee the newest records across the entire cache. Visible rejection/limit notices avoid claiming an exhaustive audit. Unknown, legacy and omitted data is never deleted.

Recovery work.json format 1 must agree on installation, actual transaction, version and plan SHA-256. Its captured format-2 pending identity must agree too. The format-1 result must bind that version/plan and have known phase/outcome codes, booleans, bounded counters and an optional valid time. Preparation is bounded to 4096, actionable union entries to 8192 and fresh copy bytes to 258 MiB. Counts must be ordered; completed entries require recorded installed-file moves. A restored receipt requires complete phase, completed counts and pendingCleared. Failed/ cancelled receipts cannot claim complete marker removal.

This checks metadata consistency only. It does not hash recovery.json, backups, prepared copies or installed files. A locally edited coherent receipt remains advisory. Real actions still require full native validation and explicit consent; see Recovery and Installation.

Copying results#

Copy selected history entry includes one cached row. Copy update report adds the entire retained history snapshot when inspected, alongside the existing report. Filters/pages affect selection/display only; full reports include all retained rows. Clipboard/formatting failure is caught and displayed.

Native history JSON is capped at 256 KiB, has format 1 and observationOnly=true, and contains the installation once, relative record/transaction paths, typed outcomes, optional times, counters and rejection/limit/budget observations. Raw metadata extras, captured pending bytes, technical errors, environment values and credentials are excluded. Copying is explicit; there is no automatic export/upload. Reports cannot authorize recovery, deletion or restart.

Integration and validation#

UpdateHistory/UpdateHistoryPolicy join the existing native updater library and UpdateHistoryUI the existing UI library. No executable target, external dependency, CyUI module, SDK operation or plugin ABI is added (227 operations / ABI2). The native owner stays free of SDL/ImGui/SDK links. EN/FR use the generated catalogue; stock controls inherit themes and dimensions use cyui::dp/style. The helper retains Comctl32 v6/asInvoker.

Twenty compiler-evaluated assertions cover attention/phase/outcome/count policies. Opt-in native bodies specify metadata-only discovery beyond twelve rows with absent payloads, no created locks, sorted/unknown times, selected/full report exclusions, foreign/oversized/invalid records, cancellation and budgets. An existing GUI fixture specifies test-session exclusion. Those bodies are syntax-checked only, never linked/run under the antivirus suspension. Actual filesystem/cancellation/races, keyboard/filter/page/selection/clipboard, themes/density/DPI, clean-machine and Linux/macOS acceptance remain unexecuted. The UI offers no restore/delete action.

pages.title: Installation space and failure outcomes
pages.html:
Installation space and failure outcomes#

The Windows portable updater checks installation headroom after validating the archive, manifests and current owned files. This is separate from the earlier download/staging budget. It does not change startup checking, installation consent, save/close handling or all-instance/cache leases.

Space observations#

The native helper resolves the installation volume and reads its allocation unit. It rounds each extracted file, including manifest.json, up to that unit. Geometry must be a power of two between 512 bytes and 16 MiB; unknown/unsupported geometry stops preparation. Caller-available space uses the existing 64-bit observation, including caller quotas. The 32-bit free-cluster count is never used for capacity. See Microsoft's volume-root API and allocation geometry API.

For archive entry count N, directory allowance D and allocation unit U, the initial additional-space estimate is:

rounded extracted payload + (N + D + 64) * U + 32 MiB metadata + 32 MiB spare

D conservatively counts every parent component twice for each new entry (extraction/destination), and once for each present original (backup destination). Shared directories may therefore be counted repeatedly. The native parser still bounds entry count to 4096, total uncompressed bytes to 256 MiB and each file to 64 MiB. Budget arithmetic rejects invalid inputs rather than overflowing. This estimate does not charge the already-present archive/originals again; ordinary installation backs up originals by same-volume rename rather than by copying.

The first observation precedes transaction-directory creation and extraction. After extraction, hash verification and immutable recovery inputs, a second observation repeats the metadata/directory/spare allowance without charging the already-extracted payload. It precedes the pending marker and first original move. Known insufficient space is a distinct installation failure, reporting required and available bytes; neither observation authorizes installation by itself.

A transaction retains space.json with version, allocation unit, payload sizes, entry/directory allowances, both budgets and the initial available bytes. A successful second check adds space-before-commit.json. Failure before transaction creation cannot have a transaction receipt; helper attempt reporting remains best effort. Receipts are observations, not reservations or durable consent.

Filesystem metadata, sparse/compressed files, quotas and concurrent activity can still cause a later write to fail. The allowance is conservative, not an exact filesystem allocation prediction. There is no preallocation, automatic deletion, disk-filling probe or full recovery-copy space guarantee. Recovery now has its own copy/retention budget and preparation, also without reservation. Network-share/unusual filesystem geometry and actual low-space/quota behavior remain unverified.

Truthful failure reporting#

The existing failed outcome remains compatible. result.json format 1 can now add an optional failure field; old records without it remain valid:

Code Meaning
preparation Validation/extraction/preparation failed before this attempt replaced installed files.
space A known insufficient-space observation blocked replacement.
rolled-back Replacement failed; the complete prior presence/size/SHA-256 baseline was verified and the owned pending marker removed.
recovery-required Replacement started, and restoration or safe completion could not be established. Preserve the marker and all backups.

Only failed records accept these four codes. Unknown codes or codes on other states reject that cache observation without deleting its payload. Non-installation helper failures can still have an unclassified failed outcome. A successful install followed by restart failure remains restart-failed. EN/FR helper dialogs and the Updates history use the same application catalogue; clipboard reports add only the stable failure code rather than raw exception text.

Before the pending marker is committed, an exception never starts rollback and never claims recovery is needed merely because a journal write also failed. The helper best-effort records preparation-failed. Once replacement starts, an ordinary failure reverses known replacements/moves and verifies every affected path against its original presence, size, independent regular-file status and SHA-256, including paths it never moved. Conflicts, missing originals or reporting failures retain the recovery guard and report recovery-required. This is still a multi-file operation; external races and power loss are not made atomic.

Pending marker ownership#

Creation is exclusive: a pending marker appearing during preparation is never adopted as an overwrite baseline. Successful install, verified rollback and guided recovery remove only a bounded, independent regular marker whose exact bytes still match their own baseline. The Windows handle disallows concurrent writers and renames while verifying and marking that same opened file for deletion. Changed, linked, missing or busy markers fail closed. This uses the documented handle information API and file disposition contract. Ancestor checks are observations, not protection against arbitrary hostile same-user directory races. Keep all transaction data if completion is uncertain. See guided recovery.

Build and verification#

UpdateBudget/UpdateInstall stay within the existing native updater, with no new runtime, target, CyUI module, workspace SDK operation or plugin ABI. The helper retains its minimal links and uses OS dialogs without SDL/ImGui. Ordinary builds keep BUILD_TESTING=OFF. The opt-in existing core target gains source contracts for allocation arithmetic, failure-code compatibility, changed/linked/busy marker retention, preparation failure and verified rollback. MSVC /Zs checks their source; constexpr assertions evaluate actual arithmetic and code mappings. No fixture body, updater, recovery helper or GUI is run during the antivirus interruption.

Windows compilation, data-only checks and source audit are recorded in Validation. Real low-space, permissions, cancellation, concurrent writers, power/process interruption, helper restart, EN/FR dialogs, DPI and Linux/macOS acceptance remain pending. Automatic updating still targets only Windows x64 portable distributions; this change does not supply a Linux/macOS transport or installer.

pages.title: Interrupted application-update recovery
pages.html:
Interrupted application-update recovery#

CyCode now implements explicit, guided restoration for new format-2 update transactions on Windows x64 portable installations. It adds no executable target, UI module, third-party dependency or workspace/SDK operation. Native runtime, filesystem/GUI and power-loss acceptance remain unexecuted; see Validation.

Starting recovery#

An interrupted replacement keeps data/updates/pending.json and blocks ordinary CyCode/CLI startup. Do not remove that marker to bypass the block. The application may itself be absent or a mixture of old/new managed files, so the full IDE does not start a recovery window or implicitly execute a discovered helper.

Open the affected transaction's RECOVERY.txt. It names the existing staged CyCodeUpdater.exe in data/updates/download-... . Double-click that helper to open recovery, or invoke that same staged copy with --recover followed by the exact installation directory. The installed root helper directs the user to this staged copy. Running a helper without a pending update only displays an information box; it does not start an installation.

The helper verifies its own location, prepared metadata and hash against either recorded package version. It reads the active transaction, presents old/new versions, restore/remove/already-restored counts and bounded conflict details. Conflicts block confirmation. A fresh space observation adds estimated required and caller-available bytes; insufficient/unknown capacity blocks confirmation with EN/FR guidance. Capacity is not part of the reviewed file baseline or durable consent: native recovery recomputes it under the exclusive lease. The restore question defaults to No. Declining changes no installation file. Close every GUI/service instance and other updater using this installation before accepting. Recovery takes an exclusive native installation lease and never kills processes or elevates itself.

After successful restoration, a second question defaults to No for restarting CyCode. A restart rechecks the current manifest-owned executable under a shared installation lease before direct CreateProcess. Restart failure is reported as a restart failure after completed restoration. It does not recreate a pending marker.

The native helper uses OS dialogs rather than linking ImGui/SDL/the IDE. A small adapter reads the application's existing EN/FR catalogue and language preference. Download staging captures updater-messages.json so messages remain available when package UI files have moved. Missing/corrupt catalogue data falls back to English. Backend diagnostic details remain technical text. No credential or environment read is needed for recovery. The Updates history records Previous installation restored; catalogue/history/report data uses the existing owners.

Durable inputs and bounded validation#

Before any original file moves, installation writes immutable before.json and after.json manifest bytes, recovery.json, and RECOVERY.txt into its unique transaction directory. The plan records original presence, hashes and sizes, and the exact replacement set. The original manifest, CyCode.exe and CyCodeUpdater.exe records are required; other previously missing managed files remain absent after restoring that baseline.

The pending marker has format 2 and binds the canonical installation's direct transaction-* directory, release version and SHA-256 of recovery.json. The plan has format 1; this is independent of package manifest updateFormat 1. JSON journal/ pending writes reuse the existing atomic text writer and disk baseline. Immutable plan inputs are completed before the pending marker; review never trusts a move counter or the mutable phase journal to decide what to overwrite.

Plan metadata is capped at 8 MiB, each manifest at 2 MiB and the pending marker at 8 KiB. Each manifest has at most 4095 payload files, 64 MiB per file and 256 MiB total. Both before/after manifests share the same native validator as installation; their union rejects case collisions and file/directory prefix changes. Every plan record must agree with those manifests. Original helper/executable/manifest records are mandatory. Development checkouts, foreign transactions, protected paths, traversal, special files, reparse/symlink ancestors, hard-linked payloads and unsupported/legacy formats are rejected.

Read-only review validates the complete managed union and backup states. Unexpected sizes are rejected without hashing arbitrary large files. Each hash has a streaming size limit and cancellation checks per 64 KiB chunk. Unrelated project/data/plugin files are not scanned or changed. Conflict details retain at most 32 rows while the total conflict count remains complete. This is a manifest-bounded filesystem inspection, not a per-frame task or performance benchmark.

Restoration and interruption#

After confirmation, the native service reacquires exclusive ownership and repeats the full review. The exact pending/plan/path/hash/presence snapshot must still match. A changed file, missing backup or changed pending marker blocks that reviewed action.

For each original, an already-restored target is left in place. Otherwise a verified original backup must exist, and the target must be absent or exactly match the known replacement. A previously absent target may only be absent or the known replacement. Unknown/local changes block restoration.

All needed originals are first copied into a unique recovery-*/restored tree through exclusive, bounded, flushed copies and individually reverified. No installed target moves during this phase. A copy/hash/write/cancellation failure retains prepared work and original backups, with installed paths unchanged by this attempt. The complete pending/plan/target/backup baseline is then scanned again; changed context blocks commit. A second headroom check excludes already-prepared copy payload.

Only after this preparation are verified replacements moved into that same recovery-*/replaced tree, preserving their bytes. Prepared originals are rechecked before the corresponding destination moves, then renamed into unoccupied targets without overwrite. An external edit racing a move is retained and stops recovery. Original backups are never consumed. Files that were absent before installation return to absence; the package manifest is restored last. Unknown files and extension/user data remain untouched. There is no copy after vacating a target.

A final full scan must show the prior baseline everywhere, with the same pending and plan binding. Only then is recovery-status.json marked complete and pending.json removed through the verified independent file handle. Changed/linked/busy markers remain; a successful postflight never authorizes deleting a replacement marker. See marker ownership. Status records identify the recovery work directory. A failure retains the pending guard, original backups and recovery copies. A subsequent new review can accept originals already restored by a previous attempt and finish remaining work. The helper now offers cooperative cancellation between operations/chunks and keeps the progress window open until the worker stops. Process interruption is handled by the same later review rather than replaying uncertain counters.

This remains a multi-file restoration, not a crash-atomic directory swap. Atomic metadata/flushes do not prove power-loss durability of every filesystem/volume. Neither process/power interruption nor concurrent external writers are accepted without fresh file validation. No unattended restoration, completed-update downgrade selector, cache pruning or automatic Linux/macOS installer is added.

Reversible cache management shares a cache lease with the staged helper and refuses pending installations. It does not move recovery transactions or original/replacement backups.

Recovery space and retained preparation#

Recovery has its own budget in the existing UpdateBudget owner. It charges only originals still required by the restore, rounded to the actual volume allocation unit, minus verified reusable allocation already on disk. Replacements retained by same-volume rename and already-existing backups, archives and old recovery work are not charged as new payload. Directory allowances count two parent paths per copy (staging/final) and one per retained replacement; shared parents may be counted repeatedly. The estimate is:

allocated copies - verified reusable allocation + (copy count + retained count + parent allowances + 64) * allocation unit + 32 MiB metadata + 32 MiB spare

Original/installed sets each retain their existing 4096-entry and size bounds; copy count and retained count are independently bounded to 4096. A zero-action recovery still charges metadata/spare for journal/marker completion. An unknown geometry/capacity stops; a known shortfall reports required and available bytes. The preview does not create recovery work or modify installed files. Its space fields are observations only: callers cannot authorize a restore by changing them.

Under the exclusive installation lease, the initial check precedes work creation. After staging every copy and revalidating the full file baseline, the second check charges the same metadata/directory/spare allowances without charging the now- existing copies again. Initial space.json and space-before-commit.json receipts bind the release/plan, counts, allocation unit, payload footprint, required and available bytes; copiesPrepared identifies the second estimate. Existing files and retained failed preparations already occupy their disk space.

recovery-status.json records preparing, recovering and complete. Ordinary failures record preparation-failed if this attempt moved no installed path, otherwise recovery-needed. Both retain pending.json, original backups and work files; these phases never replace the full baseline scan used for later review. A disk-space failure before work creation need not have a new receipt. Reporting is best effort when storage itself is unavailable. No old work is automatically deleted.

These checks are conservative estimates, not reservations or exact filesystem allocation predictions. Concurrent writers, quota/metadata changes, permissions and power loss can still interrupt commit. A later new review derives remaining copies from verified current targets, not prior counters. Real low-space, copy- failure, lock/cancellation, native dialogs/restart and Linux/macOS acceptance remain unverified. Live progress and cooperative stopping are implemented as described below; their actual native-window acceptance is still pending.

Reusing verified preparations#

A retry can reuse complete original copies prepared by an earlier interrupted attempt of this exact active transaction. It still starts from the current pending/plan/target/backup scan and asks for normal explicit restoration consent. Original backups remain mandatory and are retained; a prepared copy cannot replace a missing or corrupt authoritative backup. Files already restored are excluded. There is no automatic recovery, completed-update downgrade or partial-file append.

New recovery work records an immutable work.json identity (format 1), binding the canonical installation, active transaction directory, version, plan SHA-256 and exact pending bytes. Immutable prepared.json (format 1) maps original managed names to recovery-work directory basenames. A fresh attempt can therefore retain references to several earlier source directories without copying those payloads again. Names must belong to the original plan; directory values cannot contain paths, traversal or arbitrary identifiers. The map is a hint, not proof that the predicted files were ever written.

Both records are created exclusively before publishing the new mutable status pointer and before starting a copy. If this setup fails, the previous status hint is preserved. Each retry starts only from the active transaction's last status hint. It validates the work identity, map, source-directory identities and each candidate's independent regular-file status, exact size and SHA-256. A mutable phase such as complete never establishes file readiness or installation completion.

Lookup is bounded: 8 KiB status, 64 KiB per work identity, 4 MiB / 4096 entries in the preparation map, and 32 distinct work identities including its owner. Invalid identities count toward this directory limit. Each needed original has at most one candidate and bounded-size hashing; the original set retains its 256 MiB plus 2 MiB manifest bound. No recursive history/directory walk or arbitrary source path is followed. Oversized, foreign, special, changed or missing data is ignored and kept. Required originals are then copied anew into a unique directory under the ordinary headroom check. Partial earlier copies are never truncated or overwritten. Limits can reduce reuse; older unreferenced work remains protected.

The preview reports verified available copies, remaining copies from backups and ignored/limited preparation hints in EN/FR. RecoverySpace keeps logical copy count, bytes and allocation for the complete remaining restore, plus reusedFiles, reusedBytes and reusedAllocation. Initial additional headroom deducts only verified already-existing reused allocation; metadata/directory/spare allowances remain. The native preflight recomputes these observations under exclusive ownership, so supplied counts or a changed cache cannot authorize a smaller budget.

A new work map is published before copying, letting a later attempt find completed files even if the previous process stopped mid-preparation. Valid reused payloads stay in their earlier directories until guarded commit. Missing/new payloads are copied into the new directory. Before the first target moves, all selected source identities and copies are checked again, along with the full installation baseline and commit headroom. Each source identity/copy is checked again at its move. A selected file that changes during preparation stops rather than being overwritten or trusted. As before, an interruption after commit starts may require another full review; this is not a crash-atomic or hostile-writer-proof operation.

Initial/commit space receipts add actual reuse counts/allocation and hint-limit flags. Original backups, unused/modified preparations and receipts remain on disk; there is no cleanup or reclaimed-space claim. A retry may reference older copies, so work directories must not be deleted manually while recovery is pending. Legacy preparation directories without these new identity/map records are kept, but their copies are prepared again from verified originals. Actual resume, low- space/concurrency, lock/copy/interruption and native dialog acceptance remain unexecuted; the implementation is source/build/data checked only.

Visible progress, stopping and result reports#

After the existing default-No confirmation, a native Windows progress window starts the same recovery service on a joined worker. The worker publishes plan/transaction- bound atomic observations; the window reads them without filesystem/network probes. Inspection, preparation, prepared-file verification, restoration and final baseline checking have distinct EN/FR labels. Counts show verified prepared copies and completed restore/remove entries. Reused copies count as prepared without inflating bytes copied during this attempt. Copied bytes are actual reported writes, including a partial failed write; they are not proof of flushing or durable recovery.

Preparation/restoration percentages describe completed files in that phase only. Unknown/empty totals, inspection, hashing and final checking remain indeterminate; there is no fabricated overall percentage or ETA. All entries moved still requires full postflight and exact owned-marker removal before success. The public native RecoveryProgress is a single-attempt observation tied to the exact plan digest and transaction. A foreign or already-claimed instance cannot authorize recovery.

Stop recovery, Escape and closing the progress window request the same cooperative stop. The dialog vetoes closing while work remains, disables repeated stop requests and shows a stopping message. It never detaches or force-terminates the worker. Cancellation checkpoints occur between operations and 64 KiB copy/hash chunks; blocked filesystem calls can delay stopping. A late stop after actual completed postflight remains a success. Cancellation is a typed internal outcome, distinguished from ordinary failures. Its result distinguishes no installed path moved by this attempt from an attempt that has already moved installed paths. Earlier attempts may already have changed the installation. Both stopped cases retain the pending guard and backups and require a fresh review, without automatic retry or rollback.

The result window offers Copy recovery report on an explicit button only. Its bounded JSON (at most 32 KiB) contains version/context/plan identity, stable phase, counts, copied bytes and whether this attempt moved installed paths. Raw exceptions, environment variables and credentials are excluded; optional technical details are displayed separately. Clipboard failure is reported while retaining the result. Successful restoration offers an explicit restart with Close selected by default; restart still uses the existing verified executable/installation lease.

Once a work directory has been advertised, recovery attempts best-effort creation of work/recovery-result.json (format 1, at most 8 KiB). It checks that work's original plan-bound identity and creates the receipt exclusively, never overwriting an unknown receipt. Fields include version/plan, state (restored/cancelled/failed), observations and pendingCleared. On interruption it records the stage where work stopped; the copied result uses the final terminal phase. Early preflight failure or reporting/ storage failure may leave no receipt. Reporting failure cannot turn a known completed restoration into failure. Receipts/counters are observations, never authority for a later restore, deletion or restart.

New receipts also contain informational Unix seconds in time. Earlier format-1 receipts remain readable without this field. Once ordinary startup is available, the IDE's explicit detailed history inspection can show receipts alongside installation outcomes, with filters/pages and copying. It checks metadata agreement without rehashing plans, backups or current files; a recorded result is not proof of current installation completeness.

The thin helper uses the system TaskDialogIndirect component and Comctl32.lib, with an explicit embedded Common-Controls v6 manifest and asInvoker execution level. The approximately 200 ms native callback timer only reads progress and checks worker readiness. Button callbacks use the documented S_FALSE close veto. All window messages stay on the UI thread and the worker is joined before its review/progress/cancellation state is destroyed. No ImGui/SDL/SDK context, new target or CyUI module is introduced. System theme, keyboard, scaling, close/cancel timing and real clipboard/restart behavior remain to be accepted on Windows; automatic Linux/macOS recovery remains unavailable.

Older or damaged transactions#

Format-1/legacy pending journals cannot supply trustworthy baseline-presence and replacement records. They remain manual recovery cases. Missing/changed immutable inputs, helpers or required backups also block guided recovery. Keep all data and extract a complete distribution into a new directory, then transfer user data explicitly, or perform a careful manual restoration. Do not delete unknown or modified files to force a green check. Never clear the marker until installation completeness is established.

Verification#

These sources are MSVC /Zs checked only; no native fixture, helper or app is launched. Additional opt-in fixtures specify allocation/ownership estimates, ignored supplied space observations and all-copy preparation before a locked first destination, with unchanged targets/marker and retained plan-bound space receipts. Sixteen new constexpr assertions evaluate actual recovery budget bounds without executing fixture bodies. Twelve further assertions evaluate actual resume headroom, including full/partial reuse, over-deduction, invalid counts, zero-byte files and overflow. Opt-in fixtures now specify mixed-directory reuse across retries, advisory phase rejection, changed-copy fallback/preservation, foreign/missing work identity, traversal/hardlink refusal and mandatory original backups. Sixteen additional constexpr assertions evaluate phase-local progress, zero/invalid totals, upper bounds, rounding, postflight indeterminacy and all eight phase codes. Native source fixtures specify typed pre-cancellation, per-attempt progress ownership, failed/successful receipts, copied-report exclusions, actual copied-byte counts and zero fresh-copy bytes on a reused preparation. Those bodies are not run. Production build/resource inspection is recorded separately in Validation; actual recovery acceptance remains pending.
pages.text: Interrupted application-update recovery # CyCode now implements explicit, guided restoration for new format-2 update transactions on Windows x64 portable installations. It adds no executable target, UI module, third-party dependency or workspace/SDK operation. Native runtime, filesystem/GUI and power-loss acceptance remain unexecuted; see Validation . Starting recovery # An interrupted replacement keeps data/updates/pending.json and blocks ordinary CyCode/CLI startup. Do not remove that marker to bypass the block. The application may itself be absent or a mixture of old/new managed files, so the full IDE does not start a recovery window or implicitly execute a discovered helper. Open the affected transaction's RECOVERY.txt. It names the existing staged CyCodeUpdater.exe in data/updates/download-... . Double-click that helper to open recovery, or invoke that same staged copy with --recover followed by the exact installation directory. The installed root helper directs the user to this staged copy. Running a helper without a pending update only displays an information box; it does not start an installation. The helper verifies its own location, prepared metadata and hash against either recorded package version. It reads the active transaction, presents old/new versions, restore/remove/already-restored counts and bounded conflict details. Conflicts block confirmation. A fresh space observation adds estimated required and caller-available bytes; insufficient/unknown capacity blocks confirmation with EN/FR guidance. Capacity is not part of the reviewed file baseline or durable consent: native recovery recomputes it under the exclusive lease. The restore question defaults to No. Declining changes no installation file. Close every GUI/service instance and other updater using this installation before accepting. Recovery takes an exclusive native installation lease and never kills processes or elevates itself. After successful restoration, a second question defaults to No for restarting CyCode. A restart rechecks the current manifest-owned executable under a shared installation lease before direct CreateProcess. Restart failure is reported as a restart failure after completed restoration. It does not recreate a pending marker. The native helper uses OS dialogs rather than linking ImGui/SDL/the IDE. Download staging captures updater-messages.json so messages remain available when package UI files have moved. Missing/corrupt catalogue data falls back to English. Backend diagnostic details remain technical text. No credential or environment read is needed for recovery. The Updates history records Previous installation restored; catalogue/history/report data uses the existing owners. The plan records original presence , hashes and sizes, and the exact replacement set. The original manifest, CyCode.exe and CyCodeUpdater.exe records are required; other previously missing managed files remain absent after restoring that baseline. The pending marker has format 2 and binds the canonical installation's direct transaction-* directory, release version and SHA-256 of recovery.json. The plan has format 1; this is independent of package manifest updateFormat 1. JSON journal/ pending writes reuse the existing atomic text writer and disk baseline. Plan metadata is capped at 8 MiB, each manifest at 2 MiB and the pending marker at 8 KiB. Each manifest has at most 4095 payload files, 64 MiB per file and 256 MiB total. Each hash has a streaming size limit and cancellation checks per 64 KiB chunk. Unrelated project/data/plugin files are not scanned or changed. A changed file, missing backup or changed pending marker blocks that reviewed action. For each original, an already-restored target is left in place. Otherwise a verified original backup must exist, and the target must be absent or exactly match the known replacement. A previously absent target may only be absent or the known replacement. pages.title: Application updates from GitHub Releases
pages.html:
Application updates from GitHub Releases#

CyCode checks the stable Releases of MrMybal/CyCode in the background after a bounded local cache inspection, starting 1.5 seconds after desktop startup. It offers a newer version without downloading or installing it automatically. The preference defaults on; View > Application updates can disable it, check manually, open the release, postpone a proposal or skip a specific version. Manual checks can review a skipped version. Preferences remain in data/settings/ui-preferences.json, with no credentials.

The initial milestones cover release discovery/presentation, verified download, explicit portable replacement/restart and compatible release authoring. Follow-up milestones add verified restart discovery, persistent attempt history and clearer cancellation/retry states. Native update services are independent of the workspace engine, SDL, ImGui and CyToolsCore. No workspace MCP operation or plugin installation permission is added; the SDK still has 227 operations. CyUI's existing Core controls provide the UI; no new CyUI module or third-party runtime is selected.

Desktop flow#

  1. An asynchronous check reads the latest stable release. Exact numeric version comparison accepts vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH or MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, without leading zeroes or prerelease/build suffixes. Each component is at most 65535. Drafts, prereleases, equal versions and downgrades are never proposed as stable updates.
  2. The proposal shows the new version and bounded plain-text release notes. Later dismisses it for this run; Skip this version persists the suppression. A new version is proposed again. Startup connection errors remain in the Updates view rather than interrupting editing. No failed check is reported as up to date.
  3. Download or resume update starts one bounded background transfer, with progress and cancellation. A missing compatible asset or GitHub digest leaves the release available through its browser link. Cancellation is observed between bounded network operations; it is not instantaneous inside a blocking WinHTTP call.
  4. Install update and restart is a second explicit action after successful SHA-256 verification. It uses the existing save/discard/cancel close flow, including unsaved documents. Cancelling that close disarms installation immediately.
  5. Only after that flow accepts closing does the desktop launch the staged CyCodeUpdater.exe. A launch/validation failure keeps the current UI open. The helper waits up to 120 seconds for all GUI/service instances of this copy to release their shared installation lease. It never terminates another process. CyCode's ordinary teardown still owns language servers, builds and sessions.
  6. After installation and lease release, the helper starts the new CyCode normally. Existing saved preferences/workspace/session restoration retain ownership of reopening the project. A restart failure leaves backups and reports the failure.

Automatic native checking/download/installation currently supports Windows x64. Other builds compile the shared model/guards and offer GitHub Releases manually; automatic Linux/macOS transport/packages/installers are not implemented. GUI tests, smoke sessions and the CLI do not start update network requests. The CLI does hold an installation lease while serving native workspace operations.

Repository and transfer contract#

The endpoint is fixed to https://api.github.com/repos/MrMybal/CyCode/releases/latest. The default stable selection follows the documented GitHub Releases API. A compatible asset must be named exactly CyCode-VERSION-windows-x64-update.zip, be uploaded, have a positive size no greater than 256 MiB, and belong to this repository's numeric release-asset endpoint. At most 1024 assets and 4 MiB of release metadata are accepted. Notes are capped at 32 KiB on a UTF-8 boundary. Only one cache inspection, check or download runs in a desktop instance. There is no timer that continually polls unchanged metadata or automatically retries an error. Startup checks run once per process; GitHub rate limiting is reported.

GitHub's digest: sha256:... field is required for an installable asset; it is documented in the release asset API. The downloaded byte count and SHA-256 must match before staging. The helper hashes the archive again before extraction. SHA-256 verifies integrity relative to the authenticated GitHub metadata; it is not an independent publisher signature.

The UI caches advisory installation mode instead of parsing the manifest every frame; download/launch/apply retain fresh native guards. Network work does not remove the main loop's normal idle frame wait. No performance benchmark is claimed.

The Windows transport uses WinHTTP and normal certificate validation, HTTPS/443 only, with bounded connect/send/read timeouts and overall deadline checks. Redirects are handled explicitly, with at most six requests. Only api.github.com, github.com, release-assets.githubusercontent.com and objects.githubusercontent.com are accepted. Cookies and implicit authentication are disabled.

For a private repository, set one of the following in the environment before starting CyCode, in priority order: CYCODE_UPDATE_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN. An appropriate GitHub token needs access to this repository's Contents (read). Do not put it in a project, preference file, release asset or chat. It is sent only as an Authorization header to this repository's API endpoints, never forwarded to asset/CDN redirects, saved in preferences, placed in argv or printed in logs. Public releases need no token. Browser login alone does not configure WinHTTP. 404 means no accessible release/repository, not a successful up-to-date result.

Installation, ownership and recovery#

Use detailed update history for explicit metadata inspection, text/category filters, twelve-row pages and recorded recovery details. Selected entries or retained snapshots can be copied without reading archive/backup payloads. Scan limits and unknown dates remain visible; observations do not verify the current installation or authorize recovery.

In-place installation requires an update-enabled portable package with manifest.json updateFormat: 1, matching platform, and both CyCode.exe and CyCodeUpdater.exe. A development checkout containing .git is never replaced. Legacy distributions remain able to check/open a release, but require a first manual extraction of a current portable package. The installation folder must be writable, as with the existing portable settings layout.

The helper is copied from the installed package into a unique download directory in data/updates. Its hash must match the installed manifest before copying and before launch. No new updater is executed directly from an unverified download. The helper and the archive must share the bound staging directory; paths and version arguments are passed directly to CreateProcess, without a shell.

The update ZIP is a stored, single-volume ZIP with no comments/ZIP64/data descriptors, at most 4096 regular files, 64 MiB per file and 256 MiB total. Its single root must be CyCode-VERSION/. The parser validates central/local header agreement, CRCs, data extents, case-insensitive duplicate/conflicting paths and ordinary file types. Traversal, absolute/drive/ADS paths, Windows device names, symlinks/reparse points, hard-linked existing targets and protected data/runtime/ .git path components are rejected. Archive entries must exactly match the manifest plus the manifest itself. Every extracted file's size/SHA-256 is verified first.

Only the union of the previous and new manifests' owned files can change. Unknown files, separately installed extensions, projects, data, settings and recovery data remain outside that set. Changed package-owned files, including documentation or bundled providers, block replacement instead of being overwritten silently. Missing owned files may be repaired; an unknown existing file at a new target blocks it. Layout/case-only path conflicts may require a manual fresh extraction.

Allocation-aware installation space checks precede extraction and replacement, with retained observations and distinct failure codes. Extraction finishes before originals move. The helper writes a journal and owned pending marker, moves originals into a transaction backup on the same volume, installs the new managed files, and verifies the installed hashes including manifest.json. An ordinary exception triggers reverse restoration, retaining a modified/conflicting target for manual recovery rather than deleting external changes. Successful updates keep backups and a completed journal in data/updates/transaction-*. A rolled-back outcome requires full original presence/size/hash verification; pending-marker removal requires exact bytes and an independent opened file. Preparation failures do not claim an incomplete rollback when a journal write fails.

This is a multi-file transaction, not a crash-atomic directory swap; power-loss durability is not guaranteed. Interrupted replacement retains pending.json, transaction journals and backups, and blocks ordinary startup. New format-2 transactions now support guided recovery: the staged helper previews the exact baseline and required/available recovery space, asks for confirmation, then stages all guarded copies before moving installed targets. It revalidates context and commit headroom while retaining original backups. A retry can reuse complete verified preparations from this active transaction through bounded source maps, while retaining changed or incompatible earlier data. The helper now shows phase/count progress, supports cooperative stop requests and keeps the worker joined before closing. Result dialogs offer an explicit copied report; plan-bound result receipts are best effort. These observations never replace fresh validation. Real native/GUI acceptance remains pending. It does not launch the full IDE through the pending block. RECOVERY.txt identifies the staged helper.

Legacy/damaged transactions remain manual cases. Preserve pending.json and all transaction/recovery files; restore carefully or extract a complete distribution into a new directory before transferring user data. Clear the guard only after a complete installation is established. There is no unattended restoration or cache pruning. Interrupted transfers retain bound partial downloads for explicit retry; completed verified downloads can be rediscovered. See Download resumption for exact range/fallback and integrity rules.

Reversible storage management#

The Updates view now offers explicit Update storage inspection, reviewed retirement of new-format obsolete downloads and receipt-backed restoration. Payloads move outside the active cache while metadata/history remain. Shared cache leases protect downloads/helpers/recovery. Backups and current/legacy/unknown data remain protected. Retirement retains disk usage; permanent pruning is not added.

Download space and progress#

The existing download worker now checks conservative additional-space headroom before transfer, before a full-download fallback and before staging. The view reports last observed caller space, a distinct low-space failure and separate receiving/hash/staging/readiness phases. It also shows network-only rate and an approximate remaining transfer time, excluding the retained prefix and later verification/installation. No per-frame filesystem probe or space reservation is added. The clipboard report contains bound numeric observations and phase codes. This is not a full installation/extraction space guarantee; see Download observations for exact budgets and limitations.

Interrupted HTTP downloads#

Explicit download actions can resume only a checkpoint matching the current release version, exact asset API identity/name/platform, size and SHA-256. Partial summaries are observations, never installation candidates. A shared installation/cache lease and exclusive per-copy download lease protect staging; validated 206 ranges precede any append. If a full response ignores the range, the previous file remains and one full transfer starts in a fresh folder. Cancellation/error retain received bytes, and complete SHA-256 is mandatory before normal preparation. Startup never resumes network transfers automatically. The fresh-download action bypasses existing checkpoint selection without removing old files. Categorized EN/FR failure guidance and optional technical details explain retry choices. Failed/cancelled attempts trigger one quiet local refresh that keeps their result; it never retries the network or reopens a proposal. Copy reports contain requested mode/category/progress rather than raw exception text. See Download resumption for records, budgets and limitations.

Verified downloads across restarts#

Startup inspects local staging asynchronously, even when network checking is turned off. Turning off the startup preference also suppresses automatic cached proposals. The Updates view exposes Refresh downloaded updates independently of GitHub access. It neither creates work directories nor changes cached files. A network check retains a valid prepared download. A changed digest reported for the same release invalidates the old in-memory candidate and requires downloading again. If GitHub reports no newer stable release while a cached candidate remains, the UI describes that difference instead of claiming the running copy is latest.

Discovery accepts only the installation's own data/updates/download-* directories, with bounded numeric directory names, exact version/platform archive names and bound prepared.json metadata (8 KiB maximum). It checks that the version is newer than both the running application and installed manifest; it rejects development copies and pending installations. The archive and both staged/installed helpers must be ordinary, single-link files without reparse/symlink ancestors. Helper sizes/hashes must match the current installed manifest; the archive SHA-256 is recomputed. No new helper from inside an archive is executed. The same verification is used after downloading and again immediately before installer launch.

The scan visits at most 128 directory entries, orders candidates by numeric version, verifies at most four candidates with a combined archive budget of 512 MiB, and keeps at most twelve attempt summaries. Helper hashing is separately bounded to 64 MiB per file. Streaming limits also reject growth past the reserved budget, not only oversized inputs observed before hashing. Cancellation is observed between entries and each 64 KiB hash chunk. Rejected entries and exhausted budgets are visible; no completeness claim is made after reaching a budget. Invalid/foreign/corrupt entries remain untouched. Metadata/archives are not scanned or hashed on every rendered frame.

Restoring a download never restores installation consent or the quit request. Install update and restart still goes through ordinary document save/close and all-instance exclusion. A failure at desktop handoff keeps the UI open and clears the candidate; refresh or a new download can revalidate it. Cancelling network or local inspection produces a neutral cancelled state, without an up-to-date result. No request is started or proposal raised by a new startup operation during closing.

Persistent attempt history#

The existing helper writes a small result.json beside prepared.json, using the shared atomic text-file writer with a disk baseline. It records format 1, bound version/archive digest, state and Unix timestamp. States distinguish waiting for instances, installed, failed and installed-but-restart-failed. Outcome reporting is best effort and cannot turn a successful installation into failure. A power loss can leave a waiting record; the UI labels it as waiting or interrupted, without guessing whether a helper is currently alive.

The Updates history reads these records with the same path/size/binding guards. Failure records keep a valid archive available for an explicit retry. Successful old-version records remain visible after an upgrade while their packages stop being installation candidates. The existing update-error.txt contains bounded local helper error details. Copy update report places versions, states, timestamps, local staging paths and candidate SHA-256 on the clipboard only after a click; it does not read environment credentials, release URLs or error-file contents. Invalid records are counted; a refresh does not delete logs, archives or backups.

These outcomes are diagnostic summaries, separate from transaction journals. They do not recover a partially replaced installation or bypass pending.json. The guarded startup block remains; the separate guided-recovery service consumes new format-2 transactions. Legacy recovery remains manual.

Authoring a compatible release#

Use a clean source checkout with the selected release version consistently set in CMake and app/CyTool.json. Build Windows Release with BUILD_TESTING=OFF; the CyCode target includes the production CyCodeUpdater dependency. Then run:

powershell
python app/scripts/package_windows.py --build runtime/build-modules-clean --configuration Release

The packager checks AMD64 PE32+ executable headers and reads the three executables' PE version resources through system APIs; it never executes CyCode or cycode_cli for version detection. It refuses dirty source, missing/mismatched versions, private/unsafe entries and oversized payloads. The manifest records owned paths, sizes, SHA-256, source revision, license and pinned dependency identities. It produces a normal compressed human-download ZIP, a deterministic stored CyCode-VERSION-windows-x64-update.zip, and SHA256SUMS.txt. Both distributions contain the same update-enabled manifest and production helper.

Publish a stable GitHub Release tagged vVERSION (or VERSION) with both archives and SHA256SUMS.txt attached. GitHub supplies the asset digest used by the client; verify that it matches the locally generated checksum. A source-only release or one containing only the normal ZIP can be viewed but cannot be installed by this updater. Building/packaging does not publish or upload anything. This task has not created a commit, tag or release and has not pushed.

Validation and remaining acceptance#

Five pure Python tests exercise in-memory archive authoring, exact file hashes/sizes, stored compression, reproducible bytes, PE-header rejection, versions and protected/colliding paths without writing or launching EXE fixtures. Native regression sources extend existing opt-in core/module targets: release parsing/digest/URL/platform guards, rollback on a locked file, successful replacement preserving user data, repeated version rejection, lease exclusion, ignored/manual proposals, test-session I/O guards and cancelled install intent. Follow-up sources cover cached rediscovery, retryable history, cancellation, corrupted helper/archive, foreign metadata, pending markers, outside paths, retained downloads and replaced asset digests. These are MSVC /Zs checked, not linked/run. The existing CI matrix gains the Python data-only tests; it has not been run here.

Production compile, source/schema checks and PE-resource reads are recorded in Validation. Native HTTP/download/helper/restart, filesystem/rollback, multi-instance timing, actual GitHub private access, GUI and clean-machine acceptance remain pending under the existing Kaspersky suspension. No app, helper, server, SDK Runtime or native fixture is launched during this work. The connected GitHub service could not read the repository (404), so no claim of an authenticated live-release check is made.

pages.title: Reversible update-cache management
pages.html:
Reversible update-cache management#

The Application updates view now includes Update storage: explicit background inspection, reviewed retirement of obsolete download payloads and guarded cache restoration. This reorganizes the active cache; it does not free disk space. There is no permanent deletion or automatic retention policy. Installation recovery backups, user settings/projects, current/newer releases and unknown/legacy content remain protected. Native filesystem/lease/GUI acceptance is pending.

The separate detailed history inspector reads retained prepared/ outcome metadata even after owned payloads move away. It does not reverify payloads, change retirement eligibility or authorize restoration. Recovery receipts remain protected and advisory.

Desktop workflow#

  1. Open View > Application updates > Update storage, then Inspect update storage. Nothing runs automatically at startup or on every frame. Scanning/hashing uses a cancellable background future and the main loop retains its ordinary idle wait.
  2. The list shows eligible older downloads, retired caches, protection counts and budget limits. Review retirement selects one download. The detail shows its version, source directory, payload names and recorded sizes. Only after checking I reviewed this cache action can Retire reviewed download run.
  3. Payloads move into a unique data/updates/retired-* directory. Prepared metadata, installation outcomes/error logs and original directories remain in place, so ordinary update history stays available. No executable is started.
  4. Inspect again, then Review cache restoration to inspect a retained receipt and its source/destination/file list. The same acknowledgement controls Restore reviewed cache files. Existing destinations, changed files and conflicts block restoration. Already-restored payloads need no second move.
  5. Results show verified file/recorded-byte counts and the retained receipt path. Cancellation or a filesystem failure can leave a partial move; inspect its receipt again to restore through the same observed-state checks. No automatic retry, process termination, archive execution or workspace edit is added.

Controls use the existing CyUI/Core style and EN/FR application catalogue. The native owner is part of cycode_updates, with no new target, external dependency, CyUI module, SDK operation or plugin ABI. GUI, helper and core reuse native path, manifest, staging metadata, outcome and non-overwriting move implementations.

Ownership and compatibility#

New downloads write prepared.json format 2, retaining the original installation, version, archive name and release SHA-256 fields for compatibility with existing staging readers. Its files object additionally records size/SHA-256 for the archive, copied installed helper and optional staged translation catalogue. This is separate from package manifest updateFormat 1, recovery pending format 2 and history format 1. Archive/helper digests come from the release/installed manifest and ordinary final verification still checks actual files before download success. Legacy downloads remain readable/installable through existing guards, but are not eligible for retirement because they lack this explicit cache ownership snapshot.

A retirement candidate must be strictly older than both the running application and installed manifest. The installation must be Windows x64 portable, with a valid managed manifest and no pending update. Development checkouts are refused. Only the exact recorded payload names are eligible: the version/platform archive, CyCodeUpdater.exe and optional updater-messages.json. All must be ordinary, single-link files with the recorded sizes/hashes and safe ancestors. Unknown files/subdirectories, missing/altered payloads, foreign metadata, active/waiting outcomes and unsupported metadata formats protect the whole entry. Existing history/error files are retained rather than moved or read into a report.

Inspection visits at most 128 direct entries and retains at most eight candidates and eight retired summaries. Each inspection phase has a combined 512 MiB payload- hash budget; archive/helper/catalogue caps remain 256/64/4 MiB. Metadata is separately bounded (8 KiB prepared/outcome/status, 1 MiB retirement receipt, 2 MiB installed manifest). Hash/cancellation checks operate in 64 KiB chunks. Rejections and exhausted budgets are visible; no complete inventory or performance claim is made. Protected transaction/recovery directories are not traversed or sized.

Transactions and concurrent use#

A mutating action acquires a shared installation lease and an exclusive cache.lock lease, then repeats the selected review. The installed manifest digest, staged metadata identity and payload snapshot must still match. New downloads, updater handoff/helper execution and guided recovery hold a shared cache lease; maintenance fails immediately if the cache is in use. Acquisition is fail-fast rather than a blocking lock-order cycle. Independent metadata readers remain read-only; no installation/source operation or permissions are exported through SDK/MCP.

Before a payload moves, retirement writes retirement.json into its unique retired work directory. It binds the installation, original download directory/version, prepared metadata SHA-256 and exact owned file records. status.json is written atomically against its captured disk baseline; the immutable receipt never depends on a moved-file counter. Payloads move without replacing existing targets and are hashed again at destination. Source prepared/outcome/error records remain.

Restoration validates the receipt against the still-bound source metadata and inspects both locations for each payload. Exactly one location must contain its known bytes: already at source means unchanged; absent source plus verified retained file means restorable. Both present, both absent, modified data, unsafe paths or foreign/changed receipts block the reviewed action. Unknown retained directory content also blocks the entry. The actual observed state, including status bytes, forms the fresh-action guard. Final installed-root and full receipt postflight precede a completed status. The receipt remains as an audit record after restoration.

An external edit racing a move may be retained in the retired directory while the action stops; it is never silently overwritten or permanently deleted. A process interruption releases leases and leaves receipt/status/payloads for a fresh review. This remains a multi-file move, not a power-loss-atomic transaction. Permanent pruning, incomplete/legacy cache cleanup, pagination beyond the scan budget and automatic Linux/macOS maintenance are not implemented. Reversible retirement continues to use disk space; manual removal requires a separate, informed decision.

Verification#

Opt-in native core sources specify read-only inspection, old/current/legacy and unknown-content protection, active cache leases, changed payload/manifest/pending state, cancellation, receipt changes, destination conflicts, partial restoration, retained metadata/backups/user files and repeated-action rejection. Existing GUI fixture sources assert test-session guards. These are compiler syntax checks only, not executed native filesystem tests under the Kaspersky suspension. Source/data, production build, PE resources and whitespace checks appear in Validation. No application/helper/test process is launched.
