Each inspection phase has a combined 512 MiB payload- hash budget; archive/helper/catalogue caps remain 256/64/4 MiB. Metadata is separately bounded (8 KiB prepared/outcome/status, 1 MiB retirement receipt, 2 MiB installed manifest). Hash/cancellation checks operate in 64 KiB chunks. Rejections and exhausted budgets are visible; no complete inventory or performance claim is made. Protected transaction/recovery directories are not traversed or sized. Transactions and concurrent use # A mutating action acquires a shared installation lease and an exclusive cache.lock lease, then repeats the selected review. The installed manifest digest, staged metadata identity and payload snapshot must still match. New downloads, updater handoff/helper execution and guided recovery hold a shared cache lease; maintenance fails immediately if the cache is in use. Acquisition is fail-fast rather than a blocking lock-order cycle. Independent metadata readers remain read-only; no installation/source operation or permissions are exported through SDK/MCP. Before a payload moves, retirement writes retirement.json into its unique retired work directory. It binds the installation, original download directory/version, prepared metadata SHA-256 and exact owned file records. status.json is written atomically against its captured disk baseline; the immutable receipt never depends on a moved-file counter. Payloads move without replacing existing targets and are hashed again at destination. Source prepared/outcome/error records remain. Restoration validates the receipt against the still-bound source metadata and inspects both locations for each payload. Exactly one location must contain its known bytes: already at source means unchanged; absent source plus verified retained file means restorable. Both present, both absent, modified data, unsafe paths or foreign/changed receipts block the reviewed action. Unknown retained directory content also blocks the entry. The actual observed state, including status bytes, forms the fresh-action guard. Final installed-root and full receipt postflight precede a completed status. The receipt remains as an audit record after restoration. An external edit racing a move may be retained in the retired directory while the action stops; it is never silently overwritten or permanently deleted. A process interruption releases leases and leaves receipt/status/payloads for a fresh review. This remains a multi-file move, not a power-loss-atomic transaction. Permanent pruning, incomplete/legacy cache cleanup, pagination beyond the scan budget and automatic Linux/macOS maintenance are not implemented. Reversible retirement continues to use disk space; manual removal requires a separate, informed decision. Verification # Opt-in native core sources specify read-only inspection, old/current/legacy and unknown-content protection, active cache leases, changed payload/manifest/pending state, cancellation, receipt changes, destination conflicts, partial restoration, retained metadata/backups/user files and repeated-action rejection. Existing GUI fixture sources assert test-session guards. These are compiler syntax checks only, not executed native filesystem tests under the Kaspersky suspension. Source/data, production build, PE resources and whitespace checks appear in Validation . No application/helper/test process is launched.

Historical validation evidence. Read the dates and the remaining limitations before relying on a result.

Validation — 2026-11-05#

Earlier milestones were exercised locally on Windows x64. New work below distinguishes compilation/schema checks from runtime acceptance. Linux/macOS builds and clean-machine installation have not been executed. A core CI matrix is configured but has not run on GitHub. The project license is GPL-3.0-only; the full text and project copyright notice are in the root LICENSE and COPYRIGHT.

Executed checks#

Current detailed update-history snapshot — 2026-11-05#

Three connected milestones add explicit metadata-only installation/recovery history, cached CyUI text/category filters with twelve-row pages, and selected receipt details/copying. UpdateHistory stays in cycode_updates; UpdateHistoryUI stays in the existing UI owner. Shared staging/outcome parsers preserve existing cache behavior. No target, dependency, module, SDK operation or plugin ABI is added (227 / ABI2). Production testing/Demo/Audio/Gallery remain OFF with the same eight CyUI modules, minimal helper project references and GUI-free native updater dependency boundary.

The native read-only snapshot observes at most 512 direct cache entries and 128 direct transaction children, retaining at most 128 rows within 4 MiB of history metadata. Prepared/outcome/result files stay capped at 8 KiB, work identities at 64 KiB and captured pending text at 8 KiB; portable manifest detection has its separate 2 MiB cap. No lock/history/cache file is created, and no archive, backup payload or arbitrary receipt-supplied path is read. Invalid/foreign/linked/oversized records are omitted with rejection/limit observations; unrelated names also count toward directory bounds. Pages cover retained observations, not omitted records or an exhaustive newest-first inventory across the entire cache.

Recovery work/pending/result identities must agree on actual installation, transaction, version and plan digest. Known phases, booleans, ordered/bounded counts, fresh-write byte bounds and coherent outcome/marker fields are required. This does not hash plans, backups or current files; historical metadata never authorizes a restore or proves current installation completeness. New best-effort receipts add informational Unix seconds; earlier receipts without time show an unknown date and sort after dated observations. Installation history remains one latest outcome per download; early/reporting/process failures can leave no recovery receipt.

The GUI's joined/cancellable future is included in the existing updater busy state, cannot run in smoke/test sessions, and only replaces the cached snapshot on success. Cancellation/failure preserves the prior result. CyUI filtering searches English and translated labels, failure/state codes, category, UTC dates, versions and paths; matches/labels rebuild only when the filter/category/locale/snapshot changes. Filtering, pages, locale and successful refresh clear selection. Explicit clipboard actions use a native 256 KiB report excluding raw metadata extras, pending bytes, technical errors, environment and credentials. Full update reports include retained history independently of visible filters/pages; selected reports contain one row. Formatting/clipboard errors are caught in the view.

Twenty new static assertions evaluate actual production attention/phase/count/outcome policies; installation/ recovery/download policy assertions total 115. Opt-in bodies specify discovery beyond twelve rows with absent payloads, no created locks, sorting/unknown times, selected/full report exclusions, foreign/inconsistent/oversized/overflow/negative records, cancellation and scan bounds. A GUI fixture specifies test-session guards. These bodies are not linked or executed; source compilation is not runtime evidence.

Explicit limits#

  • This is not Rider feature parity. The native terminal and DAP C++/.NET debuggers are implemented; complete refactoring coverage, framework-specific test discovery, shader/web previews, broader debugger tooling and a marketplace are still pending. Advanced Git branches, sync, stashes, issued text-hunk staging and ordinary text-conflict resolution are implemented; interactive rebase and complex/binary/deletion conflict UI remain pending.
  • CMake, MSBuild and UnrealBuildTool are implemented build adapters. Blueprint/asset editing, Live Coding and actual UnrealEditor debugging remain pending. Unreal 5.3 was exercised on Windows; other versions/platforms remain unverified. Other VCS systems have an extension ABI, not bundled working providers.
  • Local toolchain validation covers MSVC x64/Visual Studio and Clang/Ninja on Windows. GCC discovery is implemented but GCC was not installed or executed here. MSVC/Ninja, CMake Presets, custom toolchain files, cross compilation, compiler wrappers and advanced module/PCH/unity/framework workflows remain unverified or pending. File API analysis commands are derived metadata, not a replacement build system.
  • UTF-8 editor files are limited to 4 MiB. Shared Core HTTP requests have the SDK's 1 MiB body limit. Mixed newlines are retained on no-op saves and normalized to the detected convention on edits. Legacy text encodings are rejected rather than converted.
  • Dirty buffers override disk results for literal and regex search. Unsaved regex snapshots are limited to 128 buffers / 64 MiB. Case folding in dirty literal buffers is currently ASCII-oriented. Search previews/row counts and process output are bounded.
  • The path snapshot is capped at 200,000 files/32 MiB of ripgrep output and cached in memory, with 20,000-item/8 MiB pages. Windows notifications invalidate structural changes; ignored/open files also reconcile periodically. Global Git ignore changes require manual refresh. Persistent path/symbol indexing remains pending; see Workspace monitoring.
  • clangd requires correct compilation flags/compile database for real project analysis. Reference results depend on its available index and may be incomplete while it builds. Definitions/references omit external locations by default; registered SDK sources can be requested and opened read-only through issued references. Other external sources remain refused. The current C++ rename does not update Blueprint assets, serialized Unreal names or every macro/refactoring case. Complete refactoring coverage remains pending. Semantic positions/ranges are zero-based UTF-16; text-search columns remain one-based UTF-8 byte offsets. Published diagnostics are asynchronous and can lag behind typing. Semantic requests are capped at 32 outstanding per backend, with a 15-second C++ deadline or 60 seconds for C# including project loading, and LSP cancellation on expiry. There is no immediate user cancellation/streaming control yet.
  • Core cancellation retains reservations until native operations stop. Cargo/npm/ standalone-Java task cancellation was exercised previously. CMake/MSBuild/explicit Unreal controls are now implemented and Windows-compiled; their new runtime scenarios remain suspended. Streaming output and semantic-request cancellation are pending. See Build cancellation.
  • Native CMake/Unreal subprocesses default to 180 seconds (MSBuild 150), with timeoutSeconds overrides and a separate persisted desktop preference. Long-build runtime acceptance is pending. Output remains capped at 8 MiB.
  • Native multi-window behaviour was exercised on Windows. Linux/macOS GUI execution remains unverified. ImGui platform viewports have window-manager limitations on Linux, particularly Wayland window positioning; no Wayland parity is claimed.
  • The default shared MCP configurations represent one read identity and one editing identity per GUI instance. Reusing a role shares its job visibility.
  • Native plugins are trusted platform-specific binaries. ABI2 provides commands, menus, model panels, syntax, project/VCS providers and host-owned LSP/DAP contributions, with shared build/project-task exports. Process isolation, hot reload, installation/update/rollback, signatures and marketplace remain pending. Bundled SVN/P4/Hg/Diversion adapters compile, but their real client/server/GUI acceptance is unexecuted. Full builtin project extraction remains pending.
  • Dependencies/tools are development prerequisites. There is no tested public installer, updater, signing workflow or clean-machine runtime package.

Reproduce#

Start with python app/scripts/verify_sources.py. An ordinary app/scripts/build.py build does not build or execute tests. Explicit native validation uses python app/scripts/build.py --run-tests in a separate cache; it is currently suspended locally. See Testing before running the integration commands below, which launch native programs and sometimes compile generated projects. Set CYCODE_TEST_CLI to the absolute built CLI and run private Python -m unittest discover -s app/tests -p test_mcp.py -v. Run private Python app/scripts/verify_desktop.py, Python app/scripts/verify_gui.py, Python app/scripts/verify_navigation.py and app/scripts/verify_build.py --cli ABSOLUTE_CLI. Run benchmark.py with the same --cli argument to regenerate measurements. Tests use owned temporary workspaces; they do not edit the user's existing projects. Run app/scripts/verify_cmake.py --cli ABSOLUTE_CLI for toolchain/profile GUI acceptance. Run private Python app/scripts/verify_windows.py for two-instance/window lifecycle acceptance, and app/scripts/verify_unreal.py --engine ABSOLUTE_ENGINE_ROOT for actual UBT/UHT/clangd acceptance. See Unreal integration. Run app/scripts/verify_semantic.py for semantic editing and six-theme preview renders. After the owned Unreal completion fixture exists, verify_unreal_navigation.py checks actual engine-header navigation. Navigation/window acceptance fixtures stay under data/validation so they also run within the managed workspace permissions. Run verify_terminal.py and verify_debugger.py for actual execution/debugging GUI acceptance. See Execution for bounds, lifecycle and remaining scope. Run verify_managed_debugger.py for the .NET 8 console DAP and PTY acceptance. Run app/scripts/verify_semantic_highlights.py for C++ and cross-project C# semantic color acceptance in hidden desktop windows. It checks the actual OS hidden flag, live source text (including tabs), unchanged disk sources and backend token results; captures are written to data/reports/semantic-highlights. --managed-only limits this check to C#. CYCODE_TEST_GUI can select a built executable. This suite does not open visible IDE windows.

Run verify_vcs.py for Git panel/shortcut/history/stash/conflict GUI checks. Run verify_msbuild.py on Windows for solution/project build, C++ index, diagnostic and .NET GUI acceptance. See MSBuild for bounds and remaining coverage.

Latest C# milestone regression checks: C++ desktop rename/apply and format/undo, actual Unreal AActor read-only navigation and native detached/two-instance lifecycle passed after the completion transaction fix. The current root executable also opened CyTrace_Plugin.sln read-only: 57 projects, 20 configurations and four existing missing project references; no build or project-source modification was performed.

Explicit native validation uses python app/scripts/build.py --run-tests in a separate cache; it is currently suspended locally. See Testing before running the integration commands below, which launch native programs and sometimes compile generated projects. Set CYCODE_TEST_CLI to the absolute built CLI and run private Python -m unittest discover -s app/tests -p test_mcp.py -v. Run private Python app/scripts/verify_desktop.py, Python app/scripts/verify_gui.py, Python app/scripts/verify_navigation.py and app/scripts/verify_build.py --cli ABSOLUTE_CLI. Run benchmark.py with the same --cli argument to regenerate measurements. Tests use owned temporary workspaces; they do not edit the user's existing projects. Run app/scripts/verify_cmake.py --cli ABSOLUTE_CLI for toolchain/profile GUI acceptance. Run private Python app/scripts/verify_windows.py for two-instance/window lifecycle acceptance, and app/scripts/verify_unreal.py --engine ABSOLUTE_ENGINE_ROOT for actual UBT/UHT/clangd acceptance. See Unreal integration . Run app/scripts/verify_semantic.py for semantic editing and six-theme preview renders. Latest C# milestone regression checks: C++ desktop rename/apply and format/undo, actual Unreal AActor read-only navigation and native detached/two-instance lifecycle passed after the completion transaction fix. The current root executable also opened CyTrace_Plugin.sln read-only: 57 projects, 20 configurations and four existing missing project references; no build or project-source modification was performed.

pages.title: Git and revision control
pages.html:
Git and revision control#

History context actions now connect to a Replay view for one cherry-pick/revert, with source patch review, guarded continuation after conflict resolution and quit tracking with retained local work/index. Source IDs, complete index/state, documents and persistent intent receipts share native/UI/SDK/ABI2 ownership. Actual Git/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Git replay.

The Merge view now connects actual conflict/staged review with previewed unsigned commit completion and quit tracking while retaining local files/index. It shares native SDK/ABI2 ownership, explicit hooks policy, persistent intent receipts and actual ordered-parent/tree/index checks. Quit is distinct from abort/reset; autostash/other operations remain external. Runtime acceptance is pending; see Merge workflow.

Separate working-file preview/apply/Undo now follows index conflict resolution: raw staged-byte installation or absent-index removal reuses persistent trash and common resource guards, with closed affected text/metadata and explicit partial outcomes. Automatic rename topology and Git filter/EOL checkout semantics remain outside this action. Actual filesystem/Git/GUI acceptance is pending; see Git working files.

Git conflicts now expose actual mode/OID stages, absent sides and binary-safe inspection without forcing every path into a text document. Preview/apply supports explicit index choices across a group of rename-related paths while preserving local files and open buffers. This does not perform physical checkout/rename/ deletion or infer rename topology. Native/UI/SDK/ABI2 share guards and actual postflight; real Git/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Git conflicts.

Repository selection now restores through the existing desktop session with an identity check. Linked worktree move and manually-moved link repair have separate preview/apply controls shared with the SDK/ABI2. They retain local files/index and verify actual metadata/catalogue outcomes; repair audits all linked paths before Git can update their links. Runtime/GUI acceptance is pending. See Git worktrees.

Configured Git submodules now have a selected-repository catalogue and reviewed init/sync/recorded-commit update and separate preview/clone-and-stage addition, shared with the SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugin host. Separate deinitialization preview/action protects ignored/untracked files and open native documents while retaining the project gitlink/metadata and Git history. URL and tracking-branch editing now has a separate guarded preview/apply workflow, preserving existing metadata/index changes and actual checkout state. See Git submodules for guards, transport/ignored-file limits, actual outcomes and pending runtime acceptance. External providers keep their own actions; these new typed methods explicitly target built-in Git.

The panel now selects multiple/nested Git roots and manages linked worktrees through the shared native Engine and typed SDK. Automatic selection follows the active file; an explicit selector overrides it for the current workspace window. See Git repositories and worktrees for controls, guards, permissions and compile-only validation of this new milestone.

Text-hunk staging/unstaging is available in Version control > Hunks through the shared Diff view and vcs_hunks / vcs_apply_hunks MCP operations. Issued previews expire and reject changed index/worktree data or dirty buffers. Working files stay untouched. Added/deleted/binary/mode-changing files retain whole-file staging. See Development workflows.

The native Version control panel shares its services with MCP. Git is built in; external providers keep the versioned C ABI and declare supported actions. The bundled Subversion plugin supplies status/diff/history/blame, file add/revert and mapped-copy commit/update with a separately installed SVN client. See Subversion for scope and compile-only validation. A bundled Perforce provider also supplies checked-client status/review, single-file checkout/add/reopen/revert/submit/locks and guarded project sync. A bundled Mercurial provider supplies status/review, exact-file add/forget/revert, commit, clean update, bookmark/named-branch creation and configured-alias pull/push. It requires an installed Hg client; real-client and GUI validation remain pending. The bundled Diversion provider adds status/review, commits, file reset, branch creation, clean checkout/update and locks, preserving automatic tracking/sync without a staging or push/pull fiction. It requires a configured Diversion client; real client/agent/GUI acceptance remains pending. The provider contract also supports future independent systems and their own actions/menus.

The panel provides changes, whole-file staging/unstaging, commits, unified diff and blame review, structured history, local/remote branches, safe branch deletion, remote URLs, fetch/prune, push/tracking, fast-forward pull, merge and stashes. Rider Ctrl+K opens Changes; Ctrl+Shift+K opens Remotes and sync. The command palette also exposes Git branches/history/remotes/stashes/conflicts and file diff/blame.

Changing branches or merging requires saved live buffers and no tracked disk changes. Stashing requires saved buffers, and includes untracked files only when explicitly selected. Git itself prevents overwriting conflicting untracked paths. After a working-tree operation, changed clean buffers reload through the document service with new revisions and refreshed clangd overlays. Buffers edited during the operation are retained; deleted/unreadable files are reported as retained. Repository-wide changes require the selected Git directory to be its actual root. Document paths remain workspace-relative; unrelated repositories' dirty buffers are outside the selected Git action's preflight/reload scope.

Pull fetches then merges with --ff-only, rejecting divergence. Push never forces. Git uses its configured credential helpers, signing and hooks. Authentication dialogs, interactive rebasing, force operations and conflict-abort controls are not provided yet. Process calls use argv, bounded output and deadlines; network calls can take up to 180 seconds. Cancellation currently waits for native completion.

For a normal text merge conflict, Resolve conflict reads the index stages: base, ours and theirs. The panel shows neutral, read-only source views; edit the working file in its normal editor tab. Use ours/theirs updates the live buffer only, guarded by the displayed revision. Refresh conflict obtains current revisions. Save and mark resolved explicitly saves and stages the working file, rejecting remaining conflict markers and external disk changes. It does not commit the merge. Binary, oversized, deleted-working-file and complex rename/delete conflicts still need external Git tools; the three-way editor does not implement those workflows.

Git metadata/history/diff/blame/conflict reads are exposed through typed vcs_* MCP operations. These SDK operations explicitly target the selected workspace Git folder (repository, default "."; optional expectedRepository identity), accept only provider:"git" and keep their exact Git schemas/permissions. External providers use vcs_provider_action with its advertised actions and existing generic plugin/process/workspace/VCS permissions, including for reads. Generic provider calls wait up to 600 seconds for bounded sequential native preflight/network work. Writes require vcs.write; working-file mutations also require workspace.write. Network, hook-bearing working-tree operations and explicit conflict resolution require process.execute. Each schema documents its permissions and parameters. Process results contain exitCode/output/timedOut/truncated; clients must inspect exitCode, including merge conflicts. Working-tree results additionally report reloaded/retained paths. Native exceptions become failed Core jobs.

The opt-in native vcs CTest creates owned repositories and a local bare remote. It checks branches, reload/revision guards, dirty buffer/tree rejection, stash, fetch/pull/push, tracking divergence, history/blame and actual conflicting commits with revision-safe resolution. The official MCP integration exercises the same native service and permission checks. app/scripts/verify_vcs.py is the explicit GUI acceptance suite. New nested-repository/worktree assertions have been syntax-checked only; native and graphical runs remain suspended during the antivirus interruption. Tests never contact or modify a user remote. See Testing.

Project-specific provider selection is persisted with guarded writes in .cycode/vcs.json. The deepest root mapping for the active file drives native routing and the available GUI menus; generic MCP provider calls use the same selection. Typed SDK Git operations remain explicit as described above. Git is the built-in default. An extension can advertise its own checkout/changelist/lock-style actions and text parameters; Git-specific controls are hidden for other providers. Unavailable providers fail explicitly without a fallback write to Git. File actions validate workspace/mapping containment and declared required fields before calling the provider. See Plugin SDK for descriptors, status contracts and permissions.

Remaining workflows include arbitrary staging-line selection, interactive rebase and multi-commit/mainline replay, worktree pruning and arbitrary main/bare/custom-layout repair, submodule existing-repository adoption/permanent removal and recursive bulk actions, credential UI and additional third-party providers. Linked-worktree writes are limited to this workspace. The alternative provider used by existing native/UI tests remains a fixture. The bundled SVN, Perforce, Mercurial and Diversion plugins have separate runner/ABI regression sources; real clients/servers and graphical execution remain unverified.

pages.title: Workspace monitoring and path index
pages.html:
Workspace monitoring and path index#

The native Engine owns WorkspaceMonitor. Windows uses recursive ReadDirectoryChangesW, an overlapped worker, a 60 KiB notification buffer and 100 ms stop checks. An overflow advances both counters and forces reconciliation. No path-event queue or callback can grow without a bound. Shutdown cancels the pending read and joins its owner before releasing the directory handle.

The non-Windows implementation currently polls directory metadata once per second (up to 200,000 entries, 64 directory levels, no symlink traversal). Windows falls back to it if notifications cannot start or fail. Its backend/error is visible in workspace.poll. Only Windows native notifications have been executed locally; Linux/macOS polling is implemented but unverified. Polling a large tree has a cost; native Linux/macOS watchers remain planned.

The desktop reconciles in a background future every 500 ms. A clean document whose disk bytes changed reloads through the same expectedRevision guard as an explicit reload. The editor receives the new revision, retains its cursor and records the replacement through its existing Undo path. Dirty documents retain their live text and saved baseline. Removed, unreadable, oversized or invalid UTF-8 files retain their last valid buffer too. A visible warning accompanies diskConflict metadata. Saving still rejects external changes. An explicit discard/reload is required to replace a dirty buffer; no automatic last-writer-wins save is added.

Every two seconds a reconciliation also checks open documents, even if notifications were coalesced or the path is in an index-excluded directory. Directory notifications do not follow a symlink to grant new document access: Engine.resolve still checks canonical workspace containment before reading. Images and external read-only SDK sources retain their own reload lifecycle. Unsaved-buffer checkpoints are owned by a separate Engine worker; see Recovery. The watcher never treats checkpoint writes as project edits or automatically saves dirty buffers.

workspace.files builds a sorted ripgrep path snapshot off the UI thread, respecting the existing ignore rules and excluding .git, runtime, data and .cycode. The cache holds up to 200,000 paths; ripgrep output is bounded to 32 MiB/30 seconds. Structural events and .gitignore/.ignore modifications invalidate it. Changes to global Git excludes or .git/info/exclude require an explicit refresh. The cache is in memory; there is no claim of a persistent path or symbol index.

Clients request pages with offset (default 0), limit (1..20,000) and refresh (default false). Each response contains files, truncated, nextOffset, total and indexRevision. Continue at nextOffset until null; keep the same indexRevision or restart when the tree changes. Pages have an additional conservative 8 MiB JSON budget. truncated may mean another page exists or the overall snapshot exceeded its bounds. The desktop assembles pages asynchronously, retains a bounded tree and retries after a concurrent invalidation. Manual Refresh always rebuilds.

workspace.poll / workspace_poll returns watcher counters, the extension-registry revision, reloaded paths, conflicts, checkpoint health and watcher status. It only reloads clean buffers; it does not save or discard dirty edits. These methods use the same native service from GUI, CLI and CyToolsCore/MCP.

CTest workspace_monitor uses actual filesystem operations in an owned temporary workspace: clean edits, dirty conflicts, deletion/recreation, invalid content, Unicode paths, pagination and cache invalidation. It does not alter user projects.

pages.title: Workspace sessions
pages.html:
Workspace sessions#

The new Structure panel uses the existing panel visibility and docking metadata; its default is hidden. Its filter, ordering, follow-caret state and the palette's explicit symbol-server selection are current workspace view state and reset on workspace switch/restart. No symbol/node/result cache is persisted. See Symbol navigation.

The desktop remembers workspace-relative open files, the active tab, native editor cursor coordinates, document scroll anchors, word wrap, visible code folds, image viewing controls, recent files, panel visibility and the common ImGui docking/window layout. Options > Restore last workspace session controls reopening. Explicit command-line file/line selection takes precedence. Documents restore at most two per frame through the existing workspace/open guards; removed or inaccessible files are skipped.

The session also retains explicit Git repository selection and its observed marker identity. Automatic selection is stored separately from an explicit workspace root. An unavailable/replaced repository produces a warning and restores Automatic; other tabs/layout still restore. The optional versioned git record is bounded and rejects absolute/traversal/metadata/untitled paths or mismatched empty identity. Legacy records without it remain valid. This desktop preference does not change project VCS mappings or explicit SDK/plugin repository parameters. Filesystem/Git identity restoration and multi-instance GUI acceptance remain unexecuted under the native-test suspension; see Git worktrees.

Each workspace entry has a separate session directory beneath the application's data/settings/workspaces. Every activation owns a unique JSON record, INI file and nonblocking OS file lease. Two running instances never select each other's live session as a restore source or write the same layout file. The next instance uses the newest valid inactive record, including an abandoned crash record. A deliberately empty closed session supersedes older open-tab lists. Legacy shared INI files remain a one-time layout fallback.

Metadata checkpoints run on a background worker every five seconds after pending restoration finishes. Workspace switches and normal exit wait for the outstanding write and save the final metadata. Atomic writes compare the previous bytes and refuse external modifications. Record identity, relative paths, nesting and collection sizes are checked. Limits are 256 tabs, 100 recent files, 512 panels, 512 KiB layout and 2 MiB record; the newest 32 valid inactive records are retained. Live records are never pruned. Lock files retain their inode to preserve leases.

The app owns this metadata; CyUI still owns editor rendering and layout. No text, credentials, process state or native plugin objects are serialized. Registered SDK/debug source references and external image grants do not restore. Terminal processes, debugger sessions, complete editor Undo history, multiple cursor/ selection sets and horizontal text scroll do not restore. Legacy scroll metadata remains approximate; new records retain the top visible document line, so wrapping/ folding changes do not confuse a visual row with a source line. Untitled tab coordinates/window keys now restore when their draft is explicitly recovered through Recovery; text is not automatically reopened. See Untitled documents. Dirty text remains in the existing Recovery checkpoints and is only applied through that guarded recovery workflow; reopening a tab does not silently overwrite disk.

WorkspaceSession and NativeFileLease are UI-free native services. The desktop adapter captures and restores common editor/layout models without a second editor implementation. Debug launch-profile writes also use the same cross-instance lease around their disk-baseline check and atomic write.

Editor views#

Optional version-1 editor/image fields extend the existing version-1 record; older records remain readable. The shared CodeEditor still owns wrap, folding, rendering, cursor normalization and Undo. No vendor code or second folding model is introduced. Pending settings survive a checkpoint while a tab is hidden.

Wrap applies when the tab opens. Fold starts apply through the public backend API after its first visible render has discovered folding opportunities. The stored fingerprint is compared with the current live text before folding; changed source keeps wrap/cursor restoration without replaying stale fold starts. This uses Recovery's existing FNV-1a/length fingerprint for accidental-change detection, not authentication. The cursor retains the backend's normal behavior: making it visible may unfold a containing block. Explicit editor commands, navigation or input take precedence over a pending fold/cursor restoration. Explicitly recovered untitled documents use the same adapter and fingerprint guard; Recovery still owns the text transfer and Undo transaction.

Only fold starts represented by the backend's public IsLineFolded query are captured. Hidden nested-fold bookkeeping is not exposed; restoring that internal history is outside this integration. Limits are 4,096 starts per tab and 16,384 per session. Capture scans at most 200,000 source lines per document and 1,000,000 across a checkpoint, with 32 MiB of newly fingerprinted text. Fingerprints are cached by document identity and the native editor's text revision. If a capture exceeds these bounds, its folds are omitted and foldsComplete is false; wrap, cursor and anchor are retained. Non-workspace sources do not consume these capture budgets.

Image views#

The application-owned ImageView adapts CyUI's existing Canvas/ImageState. It stores pixelated filtering, Fit mode, or manual zoom plus the image-space point under the viewport center. Restoration waits for decoding and a visible viewport; manual framing uses that new viewport's dimensions, rather than old screen pixels or a monitor position. Pending settings survive asynchronous loading/checkpoints. If source dimensions changed, the image fits again while keeping the filter. Fit mode also follows viewport resizing; manual views retain their zoom/pan. Reload and explicit viewing controls supersede pending settings.

Camera metadata accepts finite zoom 0.001–1,000, center coordinates within ±10,000,000 image pixels, dimensions up to the existing 32,768-pixel bound, and strict boolean flags. Transient pan/crop gestures, texture IDs and decoded pixels are never serialized. External image grants and SDK/debug sources still do not restore. No file content is written by these settings.

Verification#

Windows production compilation and MSVC syntax-only checks cover the implementation and added contract sources. Native lease/concurrency tests and graphical restoration acceptance remain unexecuted during the antivirus interruption. Linux/macOS implementations have not been compiled or executed locally.

View-state assertions extend the existing core/workflow-UI/image test targets, without an additional runner. Only their MSVC /Zs syntax is checked at present; actual folding, Unicode anchors, asynchronous image/filter framing, user-input precedence, themes/densities/DPI and multi-instance restoration remain unexecuted. See Validation for the production build and source checks.
pages.text: Workspace sessions # The new Structure panel uses the existing panel visibility and docking metadata; its default is hidden. Its filter, ordering, follow-caret state and the palette's explicit symbol-server selection are current workspace view state and reset on workspace switch/restart. No symbol/node/result cache is persisted. See Symbol navigation . The desktop remembers workspace-relative open files, the active tab, native editor cursor coordinates, document scroll anchors, word wrap, visible code folds, image viewing controls, recent files, panel visibility and the common ImGui docking/window layout. Options > Restore last workspace session controls reopening. Explicit command-line file/line selection takes precedence. Documents restore at most two per frame through the existing workspace/open guards; removed or inaccessible files are skipped. The session also retains explicit Git repository selection and its observed marker identity. Automatic selection is stored separately from an explicit workspace root. An unavailable/replaced repository produces a warning and restores Automatic; other tabs/layout still restore. The optional versioned git record is bounded and rejects absolute/traversal/metadata/untitled paths or mismatched empty identity. Legacy records without it remain valid. This desktop preference does not change project VCS mappings or explicit SDK/plugin repository parameters. Filesystem/Git identity restoration and multi-instance GUI acceptance remain unexecuted under the native-test suspension; see Git worktrees . Each workspace entry has a separate session directory beneath the application's data/settings/workspaces . Every activation owns a unique JSON record, INI file and nonblocking OS file lease. Two running instances never select each other's live session as a restore source or write the same layout file. The next instance uses the newest valid inactive record, including an abandoned crash record. A deliberately empty closed session supersedes older open-tab lists. Legacy shared INI files remain a one-time layout fallback. Metadata checkpoints run on a background worker every five seconds after pending restoration finishes. Workspace switches and normal exit wait for the outstanding write and save the final metadata. Atomic writes compare the previous bytes and refuse external modifications. Record identity, relative paths, nesting and collection sizes are checked. Limits are 256 tabs, 100 recent files, 512 panels, 512 KiB layout and 2 MiB record; the newest 32 valid inactive records are retained. Live records are never pruned. Lock files retain their inode to preserve leases. The app owns this metadata; CyUI still owns editor rendering and layout. No text, credentials, process state or native plugin objects are serialized. Registered SDK/debug source references and external image grants do not restore. Terminal processes, debugger sessions, complete editor Undo history, multiple cursor/ selection sets and horizontal text scroll do not restore. Legacy scroll metadata remains approximate; new records retain the top visible document line, so wrapping/ folding changes do not confuse a visual row with a source line. Untitled tab coordinates/window keys now restore when their draft is explicitly recovered through Recovery; text is not automatically reopened. See Untitled documents . Dirty text remains in the existing Recovery checkpoints and is only applied through that guarded recovery workflow; reopening a tab does not silently overwrite disk. WorkspaceSession and NativeFileLease are UI-free native services. The desktop adapter captures and restores common editor/layout models without a second editor implementation. Debug launch-profile writes also use the same cross-instance lease around their disk-baseline check and atomic write. Editor views # Optional version-1 editor/image fields extend the existing version-1 record; older records remain readable. The shared CodeEditor still owns wrap, folding, rendering, cursor normalization and Undo. No vendor code or second folding model is introduced. Pending settings survive a checkpoint while a tab is hidden. Wrap applies when the tab opens. Fold starts apply through the public backend API after its first visible render has discovered folding opportunities. The stored fingerprint is compared with the current live text before folding; changed source keeps wrap/cursor restoration without replaying stale fold starts. This uses Recovery's existing FNV-1a/length fingerprint for accidental-change detection, not authentication. The cursor retains the backend's normal behavior: making it visible may unfold a containing block. Explicit editor commands, navigation or input take precedence over a pending fold/cursor restoration. Explicitly recovered untitled documents use the same adapter and fingerprint guard; Recovery still owns the text transfer and Undo transaction. Only fold starts represented by the backend's public IsLineFolded query are captured. Hidden nested-fold bookkeeping is not exposed; restoring that internal history is outside this integration. Limits are 4,096 starts per tab and 16,384 per session. Capture scans at most 200,000 source lines per document and 1,000,000 across a checkpoint, with 32 MiB of newly fingerprinted text. Fingerprints are cached by document identity and the native editor's text revision. If a capture exceeds these bounds, its folds are omitted and foldsComplete is false; wrap, cursor and anchor are retained. Non-workspace sources do not consume these capture budgets. Image views # The application-owned ImageView adapts CyUI's existing Canvas/ImageState. It stores pixelated filtering, Fit mode, or manual zoom plus the image-space point under the viewport center. Restoration waits for decoding and a visible viewport; manual framing uses that new viewport's dimensions, rather than old screen pixels or a monitor position. Pending settings survive asynchronous loading/checkpoints. If source dimensions changed, the image fits again while keeping the filter. Fit mode also follows viewport resizing; manual views retain their zoom/pan. Reload and explicit viewing controls supersede pending settings. Camera metadata accepts finite zoom 0.001–1,000, center coordinates within ±10,000,000 image pixels, dimensions up to the existing 32,768-pixel bound, and strict boolean flags. Transient pan/crop gestures, texture IDs and decoded pixels are never serialized. External image grants and SDK/debug sources still do not restore. No file content is written by these settings. Verification # Windows production compilation and MSVC syntax-only checks cover the implementation and added contract sources. Native lease/concurrency tests and graphical restoration acceptance remain unexecuted during the antivirus interruption. Linux/macOS implementations have not been compiled or executed locally. View-state assertions extend the existing core/workflow-UI/image test targets, without an additional runner. Only their MSVC /Zs syntax is checked at present; actual folding, Unicode anchors, asynchronous image/filter framing, user-input precedence, themes/densities/DPI and multi-instance restoration remain unexecuted. See Validation for the production build and source checks.

pages.title: CyCode
pages.html:
CyCode#

Documentation · Documentation en français

CyCode includes stable GitHub release checks, explicit Windows portable updates, resume/fresh downloads, SHA-256 verification and categorized EN/FR feedback. Download/staging space checks precede transfer, full fallback and preparation; separate byte/hash/staging phases and sampled rate/transfer-time estimates avoid confusing a complete transfer with an installable update. Interrupted files, history and recovery backups are retained, with reviewed reversible cache moves. Installation uses the ordinary save/close flow and all-instance ownership guards. Allocation-aware installation/recovery space checks complement verified rollback outcomes and guarded pending-marker removal. Recovery prepares and verifies every needed original copy before moving installed targets. Retries reuse verified prepared originals from the active transaction and retain changed earlier copies. The staged helper shows phase/count progress, accepts cooperative stop requests and offers a copied result report while retaining plan-bound receipts when possible. See Installation checks. An explicit detailed history inspection adds metadata-only installation/recovery results, shared text/category filters, dates, pages and copied selected reports, with visible scan limits and no payload verification claim. Actual HTTP/helper/filesystem/GUI and Linux/macOS acceptance remains pending. See Application updates, Download controls, Recovery and Storage.

Three connected occurrence milestones add actual document-highlight requests, read/write/text outlines independent of diagnostics, and a dockable inspector with kind filters, cyclic navigation and atomic multi-selection. GUI, SDK/MCP and ABI2 share the same guarded native owner (227 SDK operations). Existing search and lexical occurrence shortcuts remain; Rider adds Ctrl+Shift+F7 for explicit highlighting. Windows production/source/schema checks are recorded separately from pending server/GUI/platform acceptance. See Document occurrences.

The preceding source-navigation milestone added declaration, type definition and implementation to the existing definition/reference commands. A shared bounded native catalogue validates Location/LocationLink ranges and source ownership; the result dock provides cached filtering, keyboard selection, copy and guarded refresh/activation. GUI/MCP/ABI2 share the same service (226 SDK operations at that milestone), without a new dependency or CyUI module. Real server/GUI/platform acceptance remains pending; see Source navigation.

Three connected diagnostics milestones strengthen document lifetime/version checks, add severity filtering and selected-message details in Problems, and link compiler output rows to guarded workspace source locations. The native parser is shared with SDK/MCP build_location and ABI2 plugins (222 operations). No new UI module, dependency or executable target is added. Runtime acceptance remains pending; see Diagnostics and Compiler locations.

Native C++20 IDE foundation using CyUI and Dear ImGui, with SDL3 windowing/rendering, a syntax-aware text editor, cancellable ripgrep search, Git, native plugins, clangd completion/diagnostics, definition/reference navigation and a CyToolsCore MCP companion. Project license: GNU GPL v3 only, SPDX GPL-3.0-only. Copyright (c) 2026 Cyberalien; see COPYRIGHT.

Project tasks now have live output/status shared by GUI/MCP/plugins, readable Cargo compiler messages and captured cancellation IDs. Problems gains filtered keyboard navigation through current-file or reported workspace locations. Actual runtime acceptance remains pending; see Project output and Diagnostics.

The Build panel now follows explicit CMake/MSBuild/Unreal output during execution, with a bounded live tail shared by MCP and plugins. Runtime acceptance remains pending; see Live build output.

Unreal Editor output inspection now checks receipts, module build IDs and recorded project binaries before bound Run/Debug, with bounded reports and virtualized lists. Actual runtime acceptance remains pending; see Unreal outputs.

Unreal launch profiles now retain their build context and restore their options. Compilation before debugging uses the bound target/configuration and blocks automatic launch after concurrent profile/document changes or uncertain builds. Native configure/run/launch validate the binding; explicit detachment preserves manual profiles. Actual runtime/GUI acceptance remains pending.

The Unreal panel prepares editor, standalone game and uncooked-server profiles, including typed map/listen/port/resolution/log options and DebugGame. Reviewed settings save to the shared Debugger profile with a concurrent-change guard; Run/Debug retain native terminal/DAP ownership. SDK/ABI2/provider 1.5.0 share the same service. Actual UE/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Unreal launch profiles.

Unreal cook/package review now provides typed maps/container controls, separate staging/archive/logs, retained intents/results and common build cancellation, shared with SDK/ABI2 and the bundled Unreal provider. Actual UE/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Unreal automation.

The Replay view now reviews one cherry-pick/revert, continues resolved conflicts or quits tracking while retaining local work/index. History context actions, native guards, persistent intent and actual postflight are shared by SDK/ABI2. Actual Git/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Git replay.

An explicit Merge view now inspects actual conflicts/staged paths and reviews completion into an unsigned merge commit, or quitting merge tracking while retaining working files/index. Repository/state/message/hooks guards, persistent intent receipts and parent/tree/index postflight are shared with SDK/ABI2. Real Git/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Merge workflow.

Git working-file synchronization now previews and installs exact staged bytes or removes an absent-index local file, preserving the original in persistent project trash. Separate guarded Undo retains displaced bytes, and common resource events refresh affected image views. GUI/SDK/ABI2 share one owner; documents must be closed and real runtime/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Git working files.

Git conflicts now have a binary-safe stage catalogue, absent-side/deletion previews and explicit grouped index resolution for rename paths. GUI, SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugins share repository/index/preview guards and actual postflight checks. This stages reviewed versions while preserving working files and live buffers; it does not check out or physically rename/delete files. Real Git/GUI acceptance remains pending; see Git conflicts.

Git repository selection now restores through desktop sessions with an identity check. Linked worktrees have separate reviewed move and manually-moved link repair workflows, shared by the native UI, SDK/MCP and ABI2 plugins. Local files/index are retained; repair audits the entire linked set because Git can update other linking files. Real Git/session/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Git worktrees.

Git submodules now have a selected-repository catalogue and explicit init/sync/ recorded-commit update, plus a separate preview/clone-and-stage addition, through the common native, SDK/MCP and plugin service. A distinct reviewed deinitialization preview/action now removes a clean checkout while preserving the gitlink, .gitmodules and absorbed Git repository. Ignored/untracked files, hidden index flags, nested gitlinks and open native documents block that removal. Reviewed URL/tracking-branch editing now shares this service, preserving existing metadata edits/index state, reporting local overrides and hiding unsafe old values. Reviewed revisions, clean/open-document guards and optional clone/fetch protect the workflow; real Git/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Git submodules.

Run to cursor now arms a verified source breakpoint in a saved editor document, resumes once and restores the original breakpoint list at the next actual stop. It shares native, SDK/MCP and plugin ownership, with revisioned recovery for uncertain replies. Rider uses Alt+F9 and Visual Studio Ctrl+F10. Real adapter/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Run to cursor.

Set next statement now queries actual destinations in the selected frame source and applies an explicit adapter-supported move. It shares the native target catalogue implementation with step-in and waits for the actual relocated stop; this skips intervening code and does not run to the cursor. Real adapter/GUI acceptance is pending. See Set next statement.

Targeted step-in now reads actual adapter targets for the selected paused frame, lets the user choose a function and executes through the common DAP/SDK/plugin owner. Issued handles expire with the captured context or after submission; real adapter/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Targeted step-in.

Instruction breakpoints now have a shared native/SDK/plugin service and a disassembly-to-draft workflow, with conditions, disabled entries, revision guards and actual verification/uncertainty. Addresses remain session-only; real adapter/ GUI acceptance is pending. See Instruction breakpoints.

Debugger Execution controls now share optional line/instruction stepping, single-thread execution, reverse actions and selected frame restart with the Run menu, SDK and plugins. Availability depends on actual adapter capabilities; backend/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Execution controls.

Paused variable/expression editing and explicit memory writes now use the shared DAP owner, with captured-context guards, expected-byte checks and actual partial/unconfirmed outcomes. See Value and memory editing for the UI/SDK/plugin contracts and pending adapter/GUI acceptance.

Manual data breakpoints now use advertised adapter capabilities, paused target inspection, read/write modes and guarded full-list replacement. UI, SDK and plugins share actual verification and uncertain failure state. See Data breakpoints for limits and pending acceptance.

Java/Maven/Gradle debug targets now prepare a shared DAP launch through JDT LS with a separately installed Microsoft java-debug add-on. See Java debugging for setup and pending runtime acceptance.

Java also supports explicit JDWP attach to an existing local/remote JVM, with separate saved endpoint fields and shared inspection. Stop requests detach without terminating that JVM; actual network/runtime/GUI acceptance remains pending.

Manual Java Hot Code Replace now compiles the imported JDT workspace before requesting class redefinition, with session/document guards, matched cancellation and explicit unchanged/error results. Matching JDT output and VM support are required; actual JVM/GUI acceptance remains pending. See Java debugging.

Cargo tasks and Rust analysis can select a named installed Rustup toolchain without requesting installation. Existing native process owners and local preferences retain launch/cancellation/activation behavior. See Rust toolchains for setup and pending runtime acceptance.

Cargo task options can now be applied explicitly to Rust analysis, with a saved local snapshot or session-only configuration. The native server owner keeps raw settings separate and supports removing the override. See Rust analysis for mapping and pending runtime acceptance.

Language-server text-edit annotations now use the shared native preview/apply/undo path, with visible labels/file groups and per-plan required confirmations. The desktop, SDK and native plugins share those guards. See annotated changes for limits and pending acceptance.

Workspace sessions also retain wrap/visible folds, document scroll anchors and image zoom/center/filter settings through the common editor and CyUI canvas. Source fingerprints and image dimensions guard replay; new native/GUI acceptance remains pending. See workspace sessions.

Semantic coloring now negotiates full/delta server responses with bounded native bases, refresh/restart invalidation and full-request fallback. The existing desktop/SDK/plugin service and Unicode/revision guards remain shared. See semantic updates for limits and pending acceptance.

View > CMake preset actions adds reviewed CTest/CPack/workflow execution with the common build reservation, cancellation and SDK/plugin surface. Read-only inspection never runs project tools. See Preset actions.

Call/type hierarchy now shares actual LSP preparation/expansion, guarded issued sessions and per-call-site navigation across the desktop, real SDK and native plugin host. See Hierarchies for controls, limits and pending runtime acceptance.

File > New text document now creates an Engine-owned untitled draft. Save as writes a new workspace file while retaining the live document/editor identity and Undo; empty drafts use the existing guarded Recovery workflow. Three SDK/native-plugin operations share those services. See untitled documents for destination restrictions and pending native/GUI acceptance. Extensions also manages signed local packages, explicit publisher trust, updates/removal, retained-version rollback and guarded cleanup. The native service is shared with six SDK operations; installed versions apply to new processes, and workspace changes retain the process selection. Monocypher 4.0.3 supplies Ed25519/SHA-512. Native package and graphical acceptance is pending. Workspace tabs/cursors, recent files, panel visibility and docking layout now restore through independent per-instance metadata; text recovery remains a separate guarded operation. See workspace sessions. The debugger adds capability-gated function/exception breakpoints, paged scopes, register scopes, memory and disassembly views through shared native/MCP/plugin services. See advanced debugging. Maven/Gradle build/test/run use real Java launchers and runtime dependency models in the existing project-task panel. See JVM builds. These additions compile on Windows; their new native/GUI acceptance remains unexecuted during the antivirus interruption. Java debugging remains separate. HLSL/GLSL also have typed DXC/glslang build tasks, real-tool diagnostics and bounded DXIL/SPIR-V outputs. See shader compilation for tool requirements and the unimplemented GPU/Unreal shader environments. The bundled Subversion plugin adds SVN provider actions and shared review views through the same project/root mapping as Git. Install the SVN client separately; this addition is compiled on Windows but not runtime-validated. The bundled Perforce plugin uses the same native provider UI for checked-client review, checkout/changelists, one-file submit/revert, locks and guarded sync. It requires an installed P4 CLI; actual server acceptance is pending. The bundled Mercurial plugin adds JSON status/history, shared Diff/annotations, exact-file add/forget/revert, commit, clean update, bookmark/named-branch creation and configured-alias pull/push. Install Hg separately; Windows production compilation passed, real-client/GUI acceptance remains pending. The bundled Diversion plugin uses the same mapping/forms for status/review, commits, clean checkout/update, branch creation and locks. It follows Diversion's automatic tracking/synchronization model. Install and authenticate the client separately; real client/agent/GUI acceptance remains pending. See custom providers for the independent VCS SDK contract. The supplied logo and application/document icons are in ../icons/; keep this folder beside the executable. See branding for integration. Images open in dockable read-only tabs with background decoding, transparency, zoom/pan, actual-pixel view and reload. PNG, JPEG, static WebP, GIF first frame, BMP, TGA, composited PSD, Radiance HDR and binary PGM/PPM are supported. See image previews for controls, permissions and format limits. File → New project creates C/C++ CMake, Rust Cargo, C# .sln/.NET, standalone Java and web projects from exact file previews. Generated projects use the existing native build adapters. See project creation for tools, permissions and template limits. Installed ABI2 plugins can extend that wizard with declarative templates and typed options. The bundled Unreal extension adds a C++ game with its module and Game/Editor targets, using the existing UBT generation/build services. Type/symbol search, file structure, C++ rename previews and project-aware formatting use the same clangd service. Navigation can open registered Unreal/SDK sources in read-only tabs, with separate access checks from editable project documents. Shared language-server code actions provide issued fixes/refactorings, lazy resolution and preview/apply/undo through the native core and MCP. Alt+Enter / Ctrl+. opens the compiled GUI panel; its full desktop acceptance remains pending. Installed-tool detection, saved CMake profiles, target builds and compilation database synchronization with clangd are provided by the shared native core. Visual Studio solutions and Unreal .uproject files open directly. UnrealBuildTool generation/build/index operations share native services with MCP. Floating panels and documents use real SDL/OpenGL system windows.

XML .slnx solutions share the native hierarchy/configuration/MSBuild services. The CMake panel also selects configure/build presets, with shared MCP/plugin discovery, inheritance/path guards and actual CMake execution. See project formats for limits and pending runtime validation.

Plugins can subscribe to committed workspace/document/resource/build metadata through the shared native event journal, with manifest permissions, snapshot handshakes and error suspension. See workspace events. Versioned language diagnostics also feed the common editor's squiggles/tooltips; see editor diagnostics for revision guards and limits. ABI2 extensions can also contribute stdio-DAP adapters, selected in the Debugger's Launch configuration and shared with MCP/plugin requests. The host owns their processes and revokes sessions when a provider is disabled or changed. See plugin debuggers for options, permissions and pending runtime validation; the bundled Unreal extension adds a CodeLLDB entry.

Unsaved text buffers receive background recovery checkpoints every second. View > Recovery offers inactive checkpoints with a shared CyUI code preview, guarded restoration into memory and editor Undo/Redo. Project files are written only by explicit Save. See Recovery for quotas and limitations.

View > Files adds the common CyUI Assets browser, including empty directories. Project context menus prepare guarded file/folder creation, rename/move and deletion. Deletion uses persistent project trash; open buffers/window identities and text Undo are preserved. See file operations for restoration, shared MCP and plugin services, limits and the distinction from semantic refactoring.

Non-Unreal solutions and direct .vcxproj/.csproj projects use native MSBuild build, clean/rebuild/restore, configuration mappings, evaluated artifacts and explicit C++ index preparation. Windows C++ and SDK C# builds are exercised. See MSBuild.

Native interactive terminals and DAP debugging are integrated. PowerShell/cmd use ConPTY on Windows; POSIX PTYs are implemented for Linux/macOS but remain unverified. Source breakpoints, conditional/log breakpoints, threads/stack/locals, watches, expression evaluation, stepping, run and attach/detach share native services with MCP. See Run, terminal and debugging.

C#/.NET run/debug uses the same panels and MCP operations through a pinned NetCoreDbg adapter. Runnable managed assemblies and apphosts are detected from their metadata; portable PDB breakpoints, variables, watches, stepping and attach/detach are exercised on .NET 8. Roslyn language services are described in C#.

Git includes branches, remotes, fetch/pull/push, stashes, history/blame and a three-way text-conflict view with explicit resolution. See Version control. The repository selector follows the active file or an explicitly selected nested Git root; Worktrees adds guarded catalogue/create/lock/unlock/clean removal through the same native Engine and SDK. New native/GUI acceptance is pending; see Git worktrees.

Native plugins can declare host-version and OS/architecture constraints, checked before library loading. ABI2 activation notifications support stopping background work on disable and resuming per-instance state; enabled dormant dependents start when their dependency becomes active. See the plugin SDK.

View > Tests discovers and runs selected configured CTest tests with per-test results/output and process cancellation. Version control > Hunks stages/unstages issued text blocks. Global regex search includes unsaved buffers. ABI2 plugins can add host-owned LSP servers; Python/Pyright and GLSL Analyzer use the same native services. See development workflows for installation, controls, MCP/SDK contracts, exact limits and remaining scope.

Rust, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript (including JSX/TSX), HTML and CSS now have shared incremental syntax parsers and independent language servers. See language support for capabilities, prerequisites and remaining project/build/debug workflows. CyCodeReader shares their syntax parsers. Problems can remember language-server settings and activation choices per project, restore installed defaults, reload or forget saved settings. GUI, MCP and plugins share the native store with revision/file-lock guards. See language preferences for activation and validation limits. Cargo, npm and standalone Java projects have native build/test/run tasks and an integrated target/script panel. Cargo binaries use the existing native debugger. Cargo also exposes workspace/features/custom-profile and bin/example/lib/test/bench selection with package/kind executable guards. See Cargo workspaces for controls, path boundaries and pending expanded runtime acceptance. See Project tasks for exact scope and remaining adapters.

Build#

Build > Cancel build covers CMake, MSBuild and explicit Unreal operations, with shared MCP/plugin controls and operation IDs. See Build cancellation for scope and validation limits.

The companion CyCodeReader now has its own repository and build. It owns the shared editor, syntax palette and native file services consumed at the revision in editor-source.lock.json. The ordinary build produces only CyCode. Use --editor-root PATH with fetch_dependencies.py and build.py to select an explicit development checkout. --no-install retains outputs under runtime/ without copying a root executable.

Requirements: Python 3.11+ for build scripts, CMake 3.24+, a C++20 compiler, Git. The build fetches a checksum-pinned ripgrep binary into runtime/tools. Windows: Visual Studio 2022 C++ workload. Linux/macOS: Ninja and the SDL3 platform development libraries. The native application runs without Python; the optional integrated MCP service uses its private Python environment. The GUI requires an OpenGL 3.3 driver (3.2 on macOS).

CyUI is resolved at the exact revision in app/cyui-source.lock.json. The default build uses a separate dependency cache; an explicit clean checkout must match that revision. See modular CyUI integration for migrated views, module selection and remaining adapters:

Official CyUI source: MrMybal/CyUI, currently private. CyUI MIT license is also included as licenses/CyUI.txt.

sh
python app/scripts/fetch_dependencies.pypython app/scripts/build.py --no-install# Optional matching checkout: --cyui /absolute/path/to/CyUI

After a Windows Release build, create the allow-listed development ZIP with:

sh
python app/scripts/package_windows.py --build runtime/build-vs

The package has a source/dependency manifest and SHA256SUMS.txt. It excludes the private development runtime, user settings and downloaded dependency source trees; only the verified ripgrep binary and its notices are copied to tools/. The IDE detects that directory before its development runtime/tools location. The Microsoft Visual C++ 2022 x64 runtime and an OpenGL 3.3 driver remain prerequisites. The MCP SDK, language servers and debugger adapters need separate local installation.

Downloaded archives are pinned by revision and SHA-256 in dependencies.lock.json. The fetch script never modifies CyUI or CyToolsCore. Build output is under runtime/; the build script copies the desktop executable to the installation root. For a core/CLI/plugin build without CyUI: python app/scripts/build.py --core-only. Ordinary builds do not compile or launch native tests. See local testing for source-only checks, isolated test builds and the current antivirus interruption.

GitHub Actions needs a repository secret named CYCODE_READER_READ_TOKEN with read access to the private CyCodeReader source repository. The default workflow token cannot read another private repository. This secret is currently absent; the local validation recorded for 0.2.0 does not establish that the CI matrix passes. Never commit the token or include it in a release archive.

For the private MCP runtime, obtain the actual CyToolsCore 0.10.1 wheel:

sh
python app/scripts/setup_runtime.py --core-wheel /absolute/path/to/cytools_core-0.10.1-py3-none-any.whl

The default wheel location is the sibling CyToolsCore/dist checkout. This is a local development dependency, not an invented public package repository. No SDK source, environment or machine-specific D: path is copied into the repository.

Run#

Windows: CyCode.exe. Linux/macOS after compilation: ./CyCode.sh. Arguments: --workspace PATH, --open RELATIVE_FILE, --theme KEY, --language en|fr, --keymap rider|visualstudio|vscode. --line and --column select a one-based UTF-16 location in --open. For an automated render: --capture ABSOLUTE_FILE.bmp --theme navy. Use --show-cmake to open the CMake settings panel at startup. Use Ctrl+O for .sln/.uproject, or pass the project path directly. --show-unreal opens the Unreal panel. File > New window starts another independent instance. Drag document tabs or panels out to create native windows and dock them back. Closed panels reopen from View or the sidebar; layouts are stored per workspace. Graphite is the default neutral dark theme, with original vector file-type icons. The five original CyUI themes remain selectable. Default text size is increased 15%. Keyboard profiles and command overrides are under Options > Keyboard shortcuts. Ctrl+Shift+F searches the workspace, Ctrl+F the document, Ctrl+Alt+F file names; double Shift opens files/actions search. See Commands. In the Rider profile, Ctrl+N finds types, Ctrl+Alt+Shift+N finds symbols, Ctrl+F12 opens file structure, Shift+F6 previews a rename and Ctrl+Alt+L formats using the project's .clang-format. Rename previews show wrapped before/after code with subtle change backgrounds and readable syntax in both dark and light themes. Applying a rename updates live buffers; Save all explicitly persists them. See Semantic editing. Capture mode ignores the saved layout, applies explicit theme/language overrides, does not save preferences and does not start Python or clangd.

Check#

The default check launches no native executable:

sh
python app/scripts/verify_sources.pypython app/scripts/build.py --plan --no-install

Native binaries are opt-in: build.py --build-tests compiles them without running; build.py --run-tests also executes CTest serially and stops on the first failure. These use separate caches and do not copy over the root executable. The suite includes real language servers, debuggers and generated-program execution; it is currently suspended locally following reported Kaspersky deletions. See Testing before explicitly launching native integration checks. Set CYCODE_TEST_CLI to the absolute built cycode_cli path, then:

sh
python -m unittest discover -s app/tests -p test_mcp.py -v

Use the private runtime/python interpreter for those tests. They exercise the native process, SDK permissions, official MCP stdio transport and shared HTTP service. scripts/verify_gui.py renders all themes and EN/FR without editing project files. scripts/verify_navigation.py checks real desktop navigation, Unicode cursor positions and References renders in EN/FR and dark/light themes using owned temporary projects. scripts/verify_cmake.py --cli ABSOLUTE_CLI configures/builds an owned project and verifies restored profiles, Unicode paths and the CMake panel in all five themes. scripts/benchmark.py records repeatable search/index baselines, not performance promises. scripts/verify_shortcuts.py sends real key events to verify profiles, editing, chords and searches with a minimal Windows PATH. scripts/verify_unreal_completion.py checks automatic UHT preparation and actual Unreal completions in the native editor. scripts/verify_semantic.py exercises actual symbol navigation, multi-file rename, formatting/undo and refactoring renders in all six themes and French. scripts/verify_unreal_navigation.py opens AActor's engine header from the owned Unreal completion fixture as a read-only SDK document. scripts/verify_csharp.py exercises C# completion/insertion, project-reference navigation and Roslyn formatting through actual desktop commands and captures.

Architecture and scope#

  • Architecture
  • C# language services
  • Run, terminal and debugging
  • Toolchains and CMake
  • Solutions and Unreal Engine
  • Commands and keymaps
  • Plugin SDK
  • Workspace monitoring and paged file index
  • MCP integration
  • Implemented capability coverage
  • Validation
  • Roadmap
  • Third-party notices

CyUI and CyToolsCore must be made accessible with their licenses and fixed revisions before this repository can be built publicly. Do not publish runtime/, data/ or connection descriptors. Native plugins are trusted code, not sandboxed extensions.

They exercise the native process, SDK permissions, official MCP stdio transport and shared HTTP service. scripts/verify_gui.py renders all themes and EN/FR without editing project files. scripts/verify_navigation.py checks real desktop navigation, Unicode cursor positions and References renders in EN/FR and dark/light themes using owned temporary projects. scripts/verify_cmake.py --cli ABSOLUTE_CLI configures/builds an owned project and verifies restored profiles, Unicode paths and the CMake panel in all five themes. scripts/benchmark.py records repeatable search/index baselines, not performance promises. scripts/verify_shortcuts.py sends real key events to verify profiles, editing, chords and searches with a minimal Windows PATH. scripts/verify_unreal_completion.py checks automatic UHT preparation and actual Unreal completions in the native editor. scripts/verify_semantic.py exercises actual symbol navigation, multi-file rename, formatting/undo and refactoring renders in all six themes and French. scripts/verify_unreal_navigation.py opens AActor's engine header from the owned Unreal completion fixture as a read-only SDK document. scripts/verify_csharp.py exercises C# completion/insertion, project-reference navigation and Roslyn formatting through actual desktop commands and captures.
